items.title: Muffin - A Shared Memory Buffer for Asynchronous AI Agents
items.abstract: The rise of Agentic AI systems has changed the landscape of artificial intelligence by enabling strong reasoning capabilities through specialized multi-agent interaction with structured self-reflection. However, in target-driven reasoning tasks, single- and multi-agent systems are often on par in terms of performance gains. A major challenge is that failures often arise from an ineffective exchange of critical information during inter-agent interaction and coordination. Different from existing multi-agent debate paradigms that rely on synchronous turn-taking and sharing information across different agents, we propose an inter-agent protocol based on shared Memory bUFFer INference - referred to as MUFFIN - in an asynchronous agentic framework. In the first step, an orchestrator routes queries based on their reasoning demands and delegates demanding ones to a multi-agent setting, where a shared memory buffer provides asynchronous exchange of intermediate findings while an agent's private reasoning remains local. Our experiments show that our framework Muffin outperforms established competitors, achieving the best accuracy in 17 out of 20 of our benchmark settings, and provides a better quality-cost trade-off than multi-agent debate: Muffin improves accuracy by 19.2 accuracy points while using 77.4% fewer tokens, without requiring full-trace sharing.

items.title: Dynamics of random recurrent neural networks: colored noise and sublinear activations
items.abstract: We study the dynamics of recurrent neural networks with random couplings, sublinear odd activation functions, and temporally correlated noise. Using large N methods, we determine stationary correlations and distinguish the loss of local linear stability from the onset of chaos, characterized by a positive largest Lyapunov exponent. These thresholds delimit an intermediate regime in which local instability coexists with asymptotic stability under a common noise history. Their separation depends on both the noise correlation time and the asymptotic growth of the activation function. We show that internal noise with any finite correlation time cuts off the divergence of the network's intrinsic correlation time tau_corr at the edge of chaos; it exhibits a critical scaling tau_{corr,max} propto 1/sqrt{D_0}, where D_0 is the integrated noise strength. Static random input instead produces coincident thresholds and a divergent correlation time. We also calculate the frequency-dependent participation dimension from a four-point correlation function. Its zero-frequency value is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the network correlation time, predicting a smooth minimum at the weak-noise chaos threshold. Numerical simulations support the large-network predictions and reveal appreciable finite-size effects.

items.title: Music Between Two Minds: Individual Signatures, Shared States, and the Emergence of Creative Interaction
items.abstract: Some of the most valued forms of human creativity arise between people-in conversation, collaboration, and improvised music-yet how two minds jointly regulate the flow of novelty in real time remains unknown. Here we examined the information dynamics of interpersonal improvisation using 986 professional jazz improvisations. Pitch-based fluctuations of uncertainty and surprise behaved as signatures of individual identity: the two partners differed within 90% of takes, performers were identifiable from single solos and the separation between partners persisted undiminished across turns and takes. Rhythm-based fluctuations showed the reverse organization: partners were statistically indistinguishable within a take yet shifted together from take to take, and this shared state drifted gradually as each performance progressed, with each performer moving away from their own past at the same rate as from their partner's. Beyond joint drift, solo hand-offs revealed turn-by-turn complementarity: when one performer exceeded their own average surprise in the predictive dynamics of improvisation, the partner's next solo fell below their own, in both pitch and rhythm and in all duos. Improvising pairs thus neither fuse into one system nor remain two independent ones: they preserve individual melodic voices while sharing a rhythmic state, within which moment-to-moment push-pull continually rebalances their interaction. Individuality and togetherness thus coexist, carried by different musical dimensions, a measurable organization of creativity that emerges between minds.

items.title: Global Convergence of Detailed Balanced Mass Action Systems
items.abstract: We give a self-contained proof that, for a finite detailed balanced mass-action system with positive rate constants, each positive stoichiometric compatibility class contains exactly one positive equilibrium and every positive trajectory converges to it, together with a Lean 4 formalization of the complete argument from persistence to convergence. Boundedness and persistence come from the barrier argument of OpenAI (2026) for weakly reversible systems: an arbitrary-tolerance affine approximation yields a finite-minimum barrier whose superlevel sets confine trajectories and give one logarithmic bound for all solutions from a given initial state. The Horn-Jackson dissipation identity identifies the positive equilibria as an exponential family with parameters in the orthogonal complement of the stoichiometric subspace, which gives uniqueness in each class. A bounded-speed descent argument replaces LaSalle's invariance principle; it uses neither uniqueness of solutions nor continuous dependence on initial data, and it places every cluster point in that family. The route given here is direct and elementary, and its main theorem is checked by the Lean kernel against explicit definitions. The proofs, the Lean development, and the manuscript were produced in ClawsGO Science, an agent harness that packages a complete research environment: Claude Opus 5.5 made the research decisions, GPT 6 Astra carried them out, and the Lean kernel checked every formal step.

items.title: A Headwind-like Helium Outflow from TOI-3884b
items.abstract: Constraining atmospheric loss is crucial for understanding the evolution of planetary atmospheres. We report the detection of an evaporating exosphere from TOI-3884b, a super-Neptune in a polar orbit around an M4 dwarf star. We infer this evaporation from a 6.8$\pm$0.27\% excess transit depth in the He I 10830 Å\, line, observed during five transits of TOI-3884b with the Habitable Zone Planet Finder spectrometer. While we observe outflow signatures starting as early as 5 hours before the onset of the planet's optical transit, no significant post-transit tail is detected. Hitherto, such a pre-transit headwind without a significant post-transit tail has only been detected from HAT-P-67b, a hot Saturn orbiting an F-type star. This asymmetric outflow morphology supports irradiation-driven mass loss over core-heated mass loss, and we explore whether this could be caused by sub-Alfvén star-planet interaction. The detection of such complex outflow morphologies is now opening a new window, enabling us to test theories of star-planet interactions and planetary magnetic fields with observations.

items.title: The first selection of optimal targets for the Lazuli ExtraSolar Coronagraph's reflected starlight exoplanet campaign
items.abstract: Direct detection and characterization of exoplanet atmospheres via reflected starlight enables probes of composition of mature exoplanet systems (since flux is decoupled from age) at closer separations than via thermal emission (due to observations in visible wavelengths), and even probes of biosignatures. New and upcoming ground and space-based platforms are enabling these observations for the first time. Recently the 3-m Lazuli Space Telescope, from the Eric and Wendy Schmidt Observatory System, was announced, which will be equipped with the ExtraSolar Coronagraph (ESC) designed for reflected light gas giant exoplanet observations in visible wavelengths. In this paper we present 27 known giant exoplanets that make up the first target list for these observations. Our target list spans ages and temperatures of planets not probed before by direct imaging, but some of which will also be accessible to the \textsl{Nancy Grace Roman} Coronagraph instrument and the ELT-METIS thermal imager, providing comprehensive atmosphere characterization and synergies. We discuss the science enabled by ESC observations of our target list and enhancements provided by future astrometric and radial velocity measurements.

items.title: Network topology shapes consensus and vulnerability in LLM populations
items.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are deployed in interacting populations, their collective behaviour depends not only on the models but also on who interacts with whom. Studies of convention formation in LLM populations have mainly tested well-mixed interactions. We place policies extracted from four LLMs on fully connected, random regular, and heterogeneous networks, with $10^3$ to $10^5$ agents playing the naming game. Topology affects how quickly consensus emerges, sometimes whether it emerges at all, and, in rare cases, which convention wins. Sparsest networks slow consensus up to twelvefold. Yet, by preserving correlations between persistent neighbours, they restore consensus in some cases that fail to converge under well-mixed interactions. Networks also govern vulnerability to adversarial attack. We measure the critical mass of committed agents needed to overturn an established convention. Tipping thresholds follow the same ordering across models and conditions: hubs $\leq$ random $\leq$ low-degree nodes. On the most heterogeneous topology, median critical masses are 3%, 16%, and 35%, respectively; targeting hubs requires one-sixth as many committed agents as random placement. For most models, networked populations are easier to tip than well-mixed ones, so well-mixed estimates can overstate robustness. Assessing the safety of multi-agent AI requires mapping who interacts with whom.

items.title: Beyond city pairs: Higher-order information in urban growth across borders
items.abstract: We apply higher-order information measures to urban growth across borders and spatial units. We analyse 8,808 functional urban areas using gridded GDP estimates allocated from national accounts. Negative estimated O-information occurs in 29.93% of cross-border triplets and 2.00% of domestic triplets. This fifteen-fold contrast falls to fourfold at comparable dependence strength and persists under data-quality restrictions. Target-specific decompositions show how information overlaps or combines across cities. Administrative subdivisions have mean O-information within matched random-map ranges inside countries. These findings show why interpreting geographic dependence requires specifying comparison cities and spatial units, while economic connections remain to be established independently.

items.title: Spatial scaling of network length and shared-node density in bilayer distribution grids
items.abstract: Certain distribution networks are built in layers, each layer collecting a commodity from the layer above it and delivering it to the layer below. We propose a minimal model that gives the length of each layer per unit area from the local density of demand, here the population density. Starting from the Beardwood, Halton and Hammersley law for minimal networks, the length of a layer depends on the number of nodes it reaches and on the area occupied by the users. When two consecutive layers share this area, the gap between their two length exponents is fixed by the exponent of the density of their shared nodes, with no adjusted parameter. We test the model on the complete low and medium-voltage grid of metropolitan France, at the resolution of a population raster. The exponents are fitted by Poisson maximum likelihood on every pixel, with confidence intervals from a spatial block bootstrap. The length exponents imply an effective settled area that grows sublinearly with the density, and the gap between them agrees with the exponent of the substation density, counted independently. The agreement holds over the whole territory, so that the model can serve to estimate the length of such networks where only the density of demand is known.

items.title: Searching for substellar companion candidates with Gaia. V. M dwarfs within 15 pc studied with absolute astrometry, radial velocities, and direct imaging
items.abstract: In this work, we survey M-type stars within 15 pc observed by Gaia based on their colour, magnitude, and quality of astrometric data. We aim to detect new substellar companions using primarily Gaia astrometry and, when available, proper-motion anomaly (PMa) along with radial velocity (RV) and direct imaging (DI) data. We used the GaiaPMEX tool to search for bound companions around 582 M dwarfs. We identified all previously known stellar and planetary companions that were consistent with the Gaia excess signal. Then for all newly identified companions, we computed detection limits in the (mass, semi-major axis) parameter space using archival RV and DI data, to possibly rule out the presence of a stellar companion. The joint analysis of the parameter space allowed by astrometry and constrained by RV and DI provides tight constraints on the nature of the companion. We found 156 M dwarfs to have a bound companion within the Gaia sensitivity domain. The astrometric signals of 37 and seven of them are due to known stellar and substellar companions, respectively. We report 35 new substellar companions among which at least ten giant planets orbiting between 0.2 au and 2 au, with masses close to 1 M_Jup. We also report 77 substellar candidates, and provide detection limits using astrometry+RV+DI for 50 stars with known exoplanets and no significant Gaia excess noise. This work reveals a significant population of new substellar companions to M-type stars, challenging core accretion models. These results will be crucial inputs for estimating occurrence rates and studying the architecture of planetary systems around M dwarfs. Some new companions presented here, located beyond the water ice line, are prime targets for DI or coronagraphy observations with JWST or ELT.

items.title: Cross-Validation of Infrasound Detections and Fireball Observations from the Global Fireball Observatory
items.abstract: How do infrasound signals from fireballs relate to atmospheric entry conditions and the physical properties of their parents meteoroids? In this study, we investigate the detectability of infrasound generated by local-to-regional fireballs and use the associated signals to constrain meteoroid physical properties. Across Western Australia and California, the Global Fireball Observatory (GFO) recorded nearly 300 fireball events with well-constrained trajectories within 500 km of an infrasound array over an 11-year period. Of these, 20 fireballs were confidently associated with infrasound detections. For these events, we estimate energies, constrain source altitudes using atmospheric ray-tracing simulations, and investigate source mechanisms using a multi-diagnostic approach. In particular, we examine whether the recorded infrasonic signals originated from cylindrical line sources (ballistic shocks) or discrete fragmentation episodes. Our results show that infrasound-detected fireballs span a broad range of dynamical and physical properties. This variability indicates that infrasound detectability is governed by a combination of source characteristics, atmospheric propagation conditions, and source-receiver geometry, rather than any single entry parameter. Analysis of the fireball shock source mechanisms reveals an even contribution from both ballistic and fragmentation-related sources. These results also demonstrate the value of combining infrasound and optical observations for robust constraints on meteoroid shock generation processes.

items.title: Uncertainty estimation of incoming comet trajectories with a thermophysical non-gravitational force model for Comet Interceptor encounter planning
items.abstract: The European Space Agency Comet Interceptor mission is designed to fly-by an as-yet undetermined incoming long-period or dynamically-new comet, which will require an accurate prediction of its trajectory. Cometary orbits are perturbed from purely gravitational trajectories by non-gravitational accelerations (NGAs) stemming from their outgassing, however, and these must be taken into account in the navigation. We here test the ability of ground-based astrometry and standard NGA-fitting techniques to predict the position and velocity of incoming comets perturbed by a Monte Carlo sampled thermophysical acceleration model. We find that, due to the difficulties of predicting NGA evolution as well as the limitations of reasonably simulated astrometry, predicted accuracies are unlikely to meet the mission goals of 1000 km and 1 m s$^{-1}$ in position and velocity, sixty days before intercept. We instead recommend expanded uncertainties of $10,000$ km and several m s$^{-1}$. Our NGA fits struggle to reproduce the reference accelerations and trajectories when outgassing is rising steeply at a few AU-incoming, but with more observations up until perihelion, do eventually converge, leading to good estimates of many of the underlying acceleration parameters even for half an orbital arc.

items.title: Astrometric detection of rocky exoplanets from inexpensive space platforms
items.abstract: The detection of orbiting exoplanets by way of astrometric monitoring of the host star to reveal gravitationally induced reflex motion requires extreme precision and measurement stability when targeting Earth-mass objects. Despite this, astrometry is widely regarded as the most promising avenue for the most desired of all targets: true Earth analogue systems in the solar neighbourhood. Formerly thought to require flagship class investment, recently several smaller concepts such as the TOLIMAN and SHERA missions have shown that detections are possible, at least in principle, from more modest space platforms. A key enabling feature is that these missions exploit narrow-angle astrometry. Observing only multiple star systems where the target provides its own astrometric reference greatly alleviates the challenges confronted by traditional astrometry with its reliance on distant, faint field stars. This principle underlies the TOLIMAN mission, for which progress and status is reported. However, only a tiny handful of nearby star systems are suited to such a TOLIMAN-like architecture. This paper discusses speculative optical concepts featuring ultra-stable telescopes of modest (<0.5m) aperture designed for astrometric monitoring of isolated single stars at the micro-arcsecond scales required for the discovery of Earth mass objects orbiting sun-like stars in temperate orbits. In simulation, highly sought-after neighbourhood systems such as Epsilon Eridani and Tau Ceti can be exhaustively searched for rocky planets with dedicated observing campaigns spanning several years, all from relatively inexpensive orbital platforms.

items.title: Core-periphery structure induces double phase transitions in information cascades
items.abstract: Double phase transitions in spreading processes are commonly associated with additional dynamical or structural complexity. Here, we show that such transitions can emerge naturally in prevalent networks exhibiting a core-periphery (CP) organization. Specifically, we consider threshold-driven spreading on CP networks constructed from the stochastic block model, which is characterized by three parameters: the relative core size $r$, the CP coupling strength $μ$, and the fraction of intra-block link allocation $α$. We find that, by varying the allocation of links between the core and periphery, the system can generate a global cascade window in the parameter spaces, bounded by distinct phase transitions. At the upper boundary, where the periphery becomes sparse, the interplay between the structural inertia (resistance to state changes) of the core and the spreading constraints of the periphery can produce a double phase transition via a two-stage cascading mechanism. This double transition may change type from discontinuous-continuous to discontinuous-discontinuous as the model parameters vary in the limit of a vanishingly small initial seed. Our results reveal a simple structural route to double phase transitions of distinct types and highlight the role of CP structure in shaping threshold-driven spreading dynamics.

items.title: Detection of Solar-like Oscillations and Granulation at Infrared Wavelengths using JWST
items.abstract: Stellar oscillations and granulation are key probes of stellar convection, one of the most poorly understood processes in stars. Stellar models predict strong wavelength dependence of the amplitudes of oscillations and granulation, but hitherto both processes have only been measured at optical wavelengths. Here we present the first detection of oscillations and granulation at infrared wavelengths, using JWST time-series observations of the F6V main-sequence star WASP-121 that were obtained to study the atmosphere of an exoplanet. We find that the amplitudes of oscillations and granulation decrease with wavelength, consistent with expectations, but with a functional form that deviates from simple blackbody scaling. The detection opens the door to detailed tests of 3D convection models, facilitates the combined modeling of stellar and exoplanet signals in JWST passbands for exoplanet observations, and supports the predicted asteroseismic yields from the infrared time-domain data that will soon be obtained by the Roman Space Telescope.

items.title: Deep-Learning Identification and Global Characterization of Energetic O2+ Beams at Mars
items.abstract: Martian ionospheric ions can be accelerated away from Mars by the solar wind, contributing substantially to atmospheric ion escape. Here, we develop a U-Net-based image segmentation model to identify a distinct population of escaping planetary ions, energetic O2+ beams, from a decade of Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN (MAVEN) observations and perform an event-based statistical analysis of their global properties and dependence on external conditions. We find that O2+ beams are widely distributed throughout the Martian plasma environment, with a strong preference for the +E hemisphere, where the solar wind convective electric field points away from Mars. This pronounced spatial asymmetry indicates that the convective electric field plays a major role in beam formation. In the solar wind and magnetosheath, these beams are consistent with the plume. Their occurrence-weighted flux agrees with previous long-term plume estimates, whereas the flux during identified beam intervals is substantially higher. This highlights the advantage of our event-based approach in capturing the intrinsic properties of O2+ plumes. In the induced magnetotail, beam formation remains strongly associated with the convective electric field, while the Hall electric field can provide additional energization. The beam properties are primarily controlled by upstream solar wind conditions, with no apparent influence from solar extreme ultraviolet irradiance. These results might improve our understanding of ion escape at Mars. More broadly, we also demonstrate the potential of deep learning for identifying transient plasma populations from spacecraft observations.

items.title: Identification of TREK channels in mouse intracardiac ganglion neurons.
items.abstract: The intracardiac nervous system is a complex neural network formed by a diffuse plexus, the so-called intracardiac ganglion (ICG). These ganglia locally innervate and control heart function, but little is known about how ICG neuronal activity is regulated. Although various ionic currents have been characterized in cardiac tissue, the expression and role of TWIK-related K + (TREK) channels in ICG neurons remain unexplored. TREK channels, members of the two-pore domain potassium channel family, are essential regulators of neuronal membrane resting potential and excitability, with recognized neuroprotective functions. In this study, we have characterized different ionic currents present in mouse ICG neurons, including tetrodotoxin-sensitive Na + currents, delayed K + rectifiers, Ca +2 -dependent K + currents and A, H and M currents. Notably, we provide the first evidence of functional TREK channel expression in these neurons. Our findings suggest that TREK channels contribute to excitability control and cellular homoeostasis in ICG neurons, highlighting their potential relevance to cardiac physiology and disease. KEY POINTS: This study provides the first evidence of functional TWIK-related K + (TREK) channel expression in intracardiac ganglion (ICG) neurons. Comprehensive profiling of ionic currents shaping excitability in ICG neurons. Neuroprotective TREK channels might emerge as potential therapeutic targets for cardiac disorders.

items.title: Development and Validation of the 9-item Parkinson's Disease Screening Questionnaire.
items.abstract: We aimed to develop and validate a brief, self-administered questionnaire integrating motor and prodromal non-motor symptoms for screening Parkinson's disease (PD). We conducted a three-phase study. Phase 1 used a prospectively registered systematic review of 107 studies to generate a 52-item draft. In Phase 2, the draft was refined in 205 participants (122 with early PD and 83 healthy controls) using item-level areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUCs) and age- and sex-adjusted multivariable logistic regression. Phase 3 validated the 9-item Korean PD Screening Questionnaire (KPDSQ) in an independent cohort (n = 246; 122 PD, 45 essential tremor [ET], and 79 controls), and included a 4-week test-retest reassessment. The final 9-item KPDSQ comprises seven motor items (rest tremor, shuffling or short-step gait, slow daily activities, decreased arm swing, soft voice, masked face, and freezing of gait) and two non-motor items (hyposmia and dream-enactment behavior). At a cutoff of ≥2, sensitivity was 88.5% and specificity was 92.4% for distinguishing PD from controls (AUC = 0.970; 95% CI, 0.946-0.984; p < 0.001). At ≥3, the KPDSQ distinguished PD from ET (AUC = 0.774; 95% CI, 0.680-0.847; p < 0.001). Internal consistency was high (Cronbach's α = 0.800), test-retest reliability was excellent (ICC = 0.921), and scores correlated with MDS-UPDRS Part III scores in patients with PD (Spearman's ρ = 0.330; p < 0.001). The 9-item KPDSQ is a reliable, clinically valid screening tool combining motor and prodromal non-motor features. Prospective community-based validation is warranted.

items.title: The mechanism of Phosphatidylethanolamine-Binding Protein 1 in Neuro-Related Diseases.
items.abstract: Phosphatidylethanolamine-Binding Protein 1 (PEBP1), also known as Raf Kinase Inhibitory Protein (RKIP), is a widely expressed, highly conserved multifunctional signaling regulator that governs the activity of central signaling pathways including Mitogen-Activated Protein Kinase (MAPK), Nuclear Factor-κB (NF-κB) and G Protein-Coupled Receptors (GPCRs). We note that recent research has uncovered its role as a critical ferroptosis regulator, showing remarkably specific expression and function across different diseases. Here we systematically review the structure and function of PEBP1, focusing on its core mechanisms as a molecular hub in various neurological disorders. We also systematically integrate PEBP1's multiple roles across these disorders and explain its key position within neuropathological networks by coupling classical signaling pathways with the ferroptosis program. We further examine intervention strategies targeting its functional states and protein interaction networks, and then discuss its clinical translational potential as a therapeutic target, hoping to provide insights for investigations into disease-related mechanisms and the development of therapeutic strategies.Clinical trial number: not applicable.

items.title: Advances in neurological disease models and optimization of the laboratory animal environment for reproducible research.
items.abstract: Animal models of neurological diseases have evolved from phenotype-based systems to integrated platforms that link genetics, molecular signaling, synaptic physiology, neural circuits, behavior, and therapeutic responses. Simultaneously, increasingly precise phenotyping has revealed that experimental outcomes are strongly influenced by age, microbiological status, diet, housing, stress, previous experience, health status, and measurement methodology. This review considers these two developments to be complementary requirements for reliable experimental neuroscience. Studies on voltage-gated calcium channel mutants have shown that defined genetic alterations can produce age-dependent abnormalities in motor function, cognition, emotion, autonomic regulation, and seizure susceptibility. Studies on N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor-Calcium-calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII) signaling, epigenetic regulators, stress-related phenotypes, and fear memory circuits have further illustrated how animal models can be characterized across levels, from molecular mechanisms to neural ensembles and therapeutic rescues. Translation to common marmosets extends these approaches to primate sleep and epilepsy, while highlighting the effects of genetic diversity, spontaneous disease, handling, and colony management. In parallel, studies on germ-free animals, diet, the gut microbiota, barrier facilities, cage enrichment, telemetry, and veterinary monitoring have demonstrated that husbandry variables, rather than technical background, are biological determinants. Integrating rigorous disease model characterization with evidence-based husbandry, environmental control, and transparent reporting should improve the reproducibility and translational value of preclinical neuroscience research and the welfare of the animals used.

items.title: Psychosocial interventions for adult survivors and responders exposed to mass casualty events: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
items.abstract: This systematic review and network meta-analysis evaluated and ranked psychosocial interventions for reducing posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), depression, and anxiety among adults exposed to mass casualty events (MCEs). English- and Spanish-language databases were searched for randomized and nonrandomized trials comparing interventions with inactive (e.g., waitlist) or active (e.g., treatment-as-usual) controls. Primary outcomes were posttreatment symptoms of PTSD, depression, and anxiety. Risk of bias was assessed (Cochrane Risk of Bias 2, ROBINS-I), and random-effects network meta-analyses were conducted using standardized mean differences (SMDs), with ranking based on P-scores. Primary analyses excluded studies with a high or serious risk of bias. Fifty-four studies (N = 10,721) across 25 countries met the inclusion criteria. Compared with inactive controls, large effects for PTSD were observed for early eye movement desensitization and reprocessing (E-EMDR), SMD = 2.48; exposure therapy, SMD = 1.60; and cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), SMD = 1.40, with E-EMDR and CBT remaining significant versus active controls, SMDs = 2.36 and 1.28, respectively. For depression, exposure therapy, SMD = 1.36; interpersonal psychotherapy, SMD = 1.15; mind-body practices, SMD = 1.01; CBT, SMD = 0.85; and integrative therapies, SMD = 0.67, outperformed inactive controls, with exposure therapy, mind-body practices, and CBT remaining significant versus active controls. For anxiety, exposure therapy, CBT, and integrative therapies outperformed both control types, with less precise estimates. Exposure and CBT ranked highly across outcomes; E-EMDR ranked highest for PTSD. The findings support prioritizing trauma-focused interventions following MCEs while highlighting the need for additional comparative and long-term research.

items.title: When words reveal risk: a mixed-method study on autobiographical narratives of breast biopsy results disclosure as early markers of psychological distress.
items.abstract: Background: Autobiographical memory theory suggests that how stressful events are encoded and recalled, particularly in terms of centrality to identity, emotional intensity, and retrieval frequency, can influence mental health. In breast cancer care, the disclosure of biopsy results may represent a psychologically impactful moment, regardless of diagnosis type. Objectives: This mixed-method study aimed to determine whether and how narrative features of breast biopsy result disclosure, analysed by both content (what was said) and form (how it was said), are associated with psychological distress one month later. Method: Sixty-eight participants were interviewed ≥7 days after receiving a breast biopsy result. Psychological distress was assessed one month later using the Distress Thermometer (non-specific distress) and the Impact of Event Scale-Revised (post-traumatic stress symptoms; PTSS). Narratives were coded using a theory-driven framework assessing centrality, emotional intensity, and recall frequency, applied separately to content and form. Results: While controlling for self-reported dissociation, linear regressions showed that for content, centrality and emotional intensity were significantly associated with PTSS, whereas only emotional intensity was significantly associated with non-specific distress. No substantial evidence of an association was found between frequency and any psychological outcome. In terms of form, all three dimensions were significantly associated to PTSS, while frequency and emotional intensity were significantly associated with non-specific distress. Early narrative markers following breast biopsy result disclosure were associated with psychological distress one month later. Conclusions: These findings highlight how memory processes associated with medical stressors can shape psychological outcomes and support their potential as screening tools for early identification of at-risk individuals.

items.title: The potential of psychological intervention to decrease the risk of anxiety and depression in pulmonary fibrosis.
items.abstract: Emotional distress in pulmonary fibrosis remains under-recognised and poorly addressed. This study assessed changes in anxiety and depressive symptoms following an individualised psychological intervention. Single-centre, single-arm before-and-after observational study of an individualised psychological intervention delivered in routine ILD care, combining acceptance and commitment therapy, humanistic-existential techniques, and psychophysiological interventions. Anxiety and depressive symptoms were assessed with the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) before and after the intervention. Patient- and caregiver-reported experience measures (PREMs) were collected. Response was analysed across characteristics defined before any analysis of outcome data (age, sex, disease severity [ILD-GAP], frailty [CFS], time since diagnosis, and baseline HADS). Thirty patients were included (50.0% women; mean age 71.0 years). At baseline, 76.7% scored ≥8 on HADS-anxiety and 76.7% on HADS-depression, indicatingclinically relevant symptom risk. Six patients discontinued (lung transplantation, palliative care, or death; n = 2 each). Among 24 evaluable patients, mean HADS-anxiety decreased from 11.3 to 6.6 (mean difference 4.7; 97.5% CI 2.6-6.9; p < 0.001) and HADS-depression from 10.7 to 5.5 (mean difference 5.2; 97.5% CI 3.2-7.2; p < 0.001). HADS-anxiety score improved in 19 patients, was unchanged in 3 and worsened in 2; HADS-depression score improved in 20, was unchanged in 2 and worsened in 2. No patient worsened in HADS category. No differences in response were detected by age, sex, disease severity, frailtyor time since diagnosis. Patient- and caregiver-reported experience scores were high (totalscore 9.4 [SD 0.7] in patients and 9.5 [SD 0.7] in caregivers). In this uncontrolled study, an individualised psychological intervention was associated with reduced anxiety and depressive symptoms and a lower proportion of patients at risk of clinically relevant anxiety and depression in pulmonary fibrosis. These findings suggest the potential of psychological care within routine ILD follow-up and require confirmation in randomised controlled trials.

items.title: Emotion-diagnostic facial features guide social gaze across screen-based and interactive contexts.
items.abstract: During face perception, observers preferentially attend to features that signal emotional expressions (e.g. the eye region of angry and the mouth of happy faces), reflecting their importance for inferring others' emotional states. Since previous research has demonstrated these effects primarily in highly controlled laboratory paradigms, it remains unclear whether they generalize to real-life social encounters and whether individual differences modulate visual attention across settings. To address this gap, we directly compared gaze behaviour in 69 participants across two contexts: a computerized task with angry, happy and neutral facial expressions and a face-to-face interaction with an experimenter displaying the same emotions during a naturalistic conversation. Although overall face-directed gaze was markedly reduced in the real-life context, enhanced exploration of emotion-diagnostic facial features was consistently observed across contexts. Specifically in the naturalistic interaction, this effect was modulated by trait social anxiety, with highly anxious individuals focusing more strongly on emotion-diagnostic features than those low in social anxiety, indicating increased sensitivity to emotional cues during live interaction. Collectively, these findings suggest that while some aspects of social gaze generalize across controlled laboratory and real-life contexts, a comprehensive understanding of context-dependent gaze adaptation requires more interactive and naturalistic paradigms supported by mobile data-acquisition methods.

items.title: Informed decision making in cancer screening. Why we need a new definition and a new scale to measure it.
items.abstract: Informed decision-making (IDM) by individuals, taking into account both potential harms and benefits, is generally considered a necessary quality criterion for population cancer screening programmes. Over the years, the increased attention to potential harms of screening has been reflected in communications to potential participants, indicating a shift from persuasive messaging to communication aimed at IDM. However, to date, there is no agreed-upon definition and no agreed-upon and validated measure of IDM. Definitions are generally based on Rational Choice Theory, although this does not reflect how people make decisions in daily life. Most measures are neither based on solid theory nor validated. This lack of theoretically based and well-validated measures hampers studies assessing IDM as well as the development of interventions to foster IDM. In this paper we review the state-of-the-art of IDM in cancer screening. Additionally, we present an alternative theoretical framework for defining IDM and a new definition of IDM - one that addresses both the decision-making process as well as the conditions necessary for IDM. In addition, we developed and validated a new scale for measuring IDM reported in separate articles. This new scale may be useful for policy and practice in population cancer screening programmes.

items.title: Subjective alcohol response across drinking contexts: a systematic review with bayesian meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Rationale Alcohol subjective response (SR) predicts drinking behaviour and risk for alcohol use disorder, but there is limited consensus on how SR differs across contexts, research settings, and alcohol problem severity. Objectives This systematic review and meta-analysis examined how alcohol SR differs across (1) commercial (e.g., bar/club/restaurant) versus non-commercial (e.g., home) settings and (2) social versus solitary drinking contexts, and if these effects are moderated by (3) laboratory versus naturalistic study setting and (4) non-problem versus problem alcohol use. Methods Studies assessing alcohol SR across drinking contexts were systematically identified and synthesized. Outcomes included four SR quadrants (HIGH+, HIGH-, LOW+, LOW-) and alcohol reward (hedonic, motivational) and were analysed using random-effects Bayesian meta-analytic models. Results Across k = 15 studies, social and commercial contexts (versus solitary, non-commercial) were associated with enhanced HIGH + and alcohol reward (hedonic, motivational) effects, with potential LOW- attenuated effects. HIGH+ effects were stronger when drinking socially (versus alone) across research settings, with naturalistic environments possibly enhancing this effect. LOW- effects were potentially attenuated during social drinking only in naturalistic settings. Participants with problem alcohol use (versus non-problem) showed possible attenuation of LOW- effects while drinking socially (versus alone). Several planned analyses were limited by insufficient data. Conclusions Alcohol SR varies by context and may be underestimated in laboratory settings. Limited studies, including heterogeneous effects (e.g., LOW+), were identified, underscoring the need to refine laboratory context manipulations, integrate ecologically valid approaches, and address gaps in how contextual features, SR domains, and problem severity shape alcohol SR.

items.title: Effectiveness of digital health interventions for care integration in coronary artery disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Aim To assess the effectiveness of digital health interventions (DHIs) supporting care integration for coronary artery disease (CAD) in improving health outcomes compared to usual care. Methods For this systematic review, we searched MEDLINE, CINAHL, EBSCO Psychology and Behavioural Sciences Collection, Scopus, and Web of Science from 1 January 1995 to 5 November 2025. We included studies reporting primary data on DHIs supporting care integration for patients with CAD. Primary endpoints were all-cause mortality and readmissions, and CVD events. Secondary endpoints were the control of cardiovascular risk factors. We conducted random-effects meta-analyses in RevMan and assessed risk of bias with Cochrane's RoB tools. Results We included 72 studies (23,111 participants), assessing 45 in the meta-analysis. All DHIs supported person-centred care integration (n=72) while few DHIs addressed clinical care integration (n=22), professional integration (n=12) and functional integration (n=22). Compared to usual care, DHIs supporting care integration had significant reductions in the odds of CVD events (OR: 0.74 [0.59, 0.92], df=5, p=0.02), but not in all-cause mortality or readmissions. Conclusions Although this review shows that DHIs supporting care integration were associated with reduced CVD events compared to usual care, the current evidence remains concentrated primarily on person-centred care integration, with limited studies evaluating broader dimensions of care integration at organisational and systemic levels. These findings highlight the important evidence gaps of DHIs in supporting more comprehensive and system-level integration in cardiovascular care. Further research is necessary to understand the influence of DHI modality and function on effectiveness of care integration.

items.title: Dihydromyricetin as an Antibiofilm and Antibacterial Agent Against Streptococcus agalactiae.
items.abstract: Streptococcus agalactiae (Group B Streptococcus ) is a leading causative agent of sepsis, pneumonia and meningitis in neonates and is also a major pathogen responsible for bovine mastitis, posing a substantial threat to food safety and public health via the dairy production chain. The ability of S. agalactiae to form biofilms in the host enhances its resistance to conventional antibiotics and host immune defenses, thereby contributing to persistent and chronic infections. This study aimed to evaluate the antibacterial, antibiofilm, and combined antibacterial effects of dihydromyricetin (DMY) against the S. agalactiae strain GBS2 isolated from bovine mastitis. DMY exhibited significant antibacterial activity against GBS2, with a minimum inhibitory concentration and minimum bactericidal concentration of 0.5 mg/mL. Crystal violet staining and confocal laser scanning microscopy analyses demonstrated that DMY effectively inhibited and disrupted biofilm formation, resulting in looser and less dense biofilm structures compared to untreated controls. Furthermore, reverse transcription-quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) results revealed that DMY modulated the transcript levels of biofilm-associated genes ( csrR , srtA , fbsC , cpsE , and luxS ). Additionally, DMY markedly potentiated the antibacterial effect of penicillin G, ciprofloxacin, oxacillin, and vancomycin. These findings suggest that DMY could serve as a natural antibiofilm agent for controlling S. agalactiae contamination in the dairy industry, thereby contributing to the prevention of foodborne infections and reducing reliance on conventional antibiotics.

items.title: Maternal mental health and its intergenerational transmission in-utero: a scoping review.
items.abstract: Maternal mental health during pregnancy is important for maternal wellbeing and offspring development. Prenatal depression, anxiety, stress, and psychological distress have been associated with offspring emotional, behavioural, cognitive, and mental health outcomes, but evidence remains dispersed across conditions, outcomes, and proposed mechanisms. This scoping review synthesises empirical evidence on maternal mental health during pregnancy as a potential intergenerational exposure, including potential in-utero pathways.Five databases (MEDLINE, Scopus, PsycInfo, CINAHL, and Embase) were searched from 1995 to 24 February 2026, following PRISMA-ScR guidance. Eligible sources of evidence examined maternal mental health during pregnancy in relation to postnatal offspring outcomes. Data were extracted using a structured framework and synthesised narratively. Twenty sources of evidence met the inclusion criteria. Across diverse designs and populations, prenatal depression, anxiety, stress, and psychological distress were commonly associated with adverse offspring outcomes, including emotional and behavioural difficulties, neurocognitive impairments, and increased risk of psychiatric conditions from childhood to adulthood. Several primary studies reported associations independent of traditional birth outcomes, consistent with potential in-utero pathways. Plausible mechanisms included stress-related neuroendocrine processes, inflammation, and epigenetic regulation. However, heterogeneity in exposure measurement, outcome definitions, and follow-up periods limited comparability and causal interpretation.Maternal mental health during pregnancy may be an important early-life and intergenerational exposure associated with offspring developmental trajectories, but observational evidence does not establish causal in-utero transmission. Stronger causal inference, longitudinal data linkage, and incorporation of economic and policy-relevant outcomes are priorities for future research.

items.title: The Development and Preliminary Testing of a Dyadic Brief Shared Decision-Making and Motivation Interviewing Intervention for Early Adolescents with Asthma and Their Caregivers.
items.abstract: Introduction: Shared decision-making (SDM) interventions have been shown to improve asthma control in adults but are less studied in pediatric-caregiver dyads. Because asthma imposes a disproportionate burden on Black and Hispanic adolescents, we adapted an adult asthma SDM intervention to minoritized dyads. Materials and Methods: Focus groups informed adaptation of the intervention. Feasibility, for example, intervention fidelity, and clinical outcomes, for example, effect of the active intervention on shared decision-making (SDM-9) scores and Asthma Control Questionnaire (ACQ) scores were assessed. Post-trial interviews assessed acceptability of study components based on implementation metrics. Results: Nine focus groups were conducted with 25 adolescents (36% female; 84% Hispanic; mean age = 12.7 years) and 20 caregivers (95% female; 90% Hispanic; mean age = 39.8 years) to adapt the intervention to dyads. Sixty adolescents (aged 10-14 years; 53% female; 77% Hispanic; mean age = 11.3 years, caregivers (90% female; 77% Hispanic; mean age = 39.4 years), and dyads were enrolled in the trial. Clinician interventionists ( n = 7) were randomized to the active SDM or dose-matched attention control condition. Feasibility was demonstrated by high fidelity to intervention delivery, high retention of subjects, and high rates of data collection. No outcomes were significant for example, ACQ: β = 0.15, 95% confidence interval -0.22, 0.51, P = 0.43, although adolescents in the active arm reported higher SDM scores relative to controls ( β = 3.35 P = 0.14). Adolescents, caregivers, and clinicians completing posttrial interviews found the study acceptable. Discussion: The intervention was feasible and acceptable. Although no significant health improvements were detected, targets for future refinements, for example, in-person-only intervention delivery and enrollment of younger children, warrant testing to determine if a dyadic SDM may be a useful patient-centered strategy for underserved pediatric populations. Contribution to the Literature: While an SDM intervention was feasible and acceptable, refinements are needed to translate SDM improvements to behavior change that impact asthma outcomes.

items.title: Prevention and treatment of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women.
items.abstract: Postmenopausal osteoporosis is a major public health concern characterised by rapid loss of bone mineral density due to estrogen deficiency, leading to increased risk of fragility fractures. This article reviews current clinical strategies for the prevention and treatment of the condition in postmenopausal women. Primary prevention discusses lifestyle modification, including adequate dietary intake of calcium and vitamin D, regular weight-bearing exercise and cessation of smoking and excess alcohol consumption. For women at elevated fracture risk, pharmacological interventions are essential. Therapies include hormone replacement therapy (HRT), bisphosphonates, Selective Estrogen Receptor Modulators (SERMS) and RANKL inhibitors like denosumab, which function as antiresorptive agents to slow bone breakdown. For those with high fracture history, anabolic agents such as teriparatide or romozosumab are utilised. Early identification via personalised risk assessment, dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) screening and treatment where indicated is essential. Combining adjunctive lifestyle modification with pharmacological intervention offers a framework to maintain skeletal health, preserve independence and enhance long-term quality of life post menopause.

items.title: Leveraging Military-Civilian Partnerships in Crisis: A Case Study of the Las Vegas Response to COVID-19.
items.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed critical vulnerabilities in civilian healthcare surge capacity, highlighting the potential for military-civilian partnerships (MCPs) to augment public health emergency responses. The Las Vegas Military-Civilian Partnership (LV MCP), a unique collaboration, offers a case study of such integration. The objective of this study was to evaluate the impact of the LV MCP, specifically the workload of US Air Force (USAF) pulmonary and critical care medicine (PCCM) physicians, on the Las Vegas civilian healthcare system during the COVID-19 pandemic. This retrospective review analyzed USAF PCCM physician workload data at University Medical Center (UMC) of Southern Nevada from 2019 to 2023. Data included critical care encounters (CPT codes 99291 and 99292) and COVID-19 encounters (ICD-10 coding). Staffing of 5 USAF PCCM physicians was maintained, with 7 individuals rotating. We assessed changes in the volume of critical care and COVID-19-specific encounters managed by USAF PCCM physicians at UMC. Analysis indicated USAF PCCM physicians reported 19,155 encounters between 2019 and 2023. Encounters peaked at 4,648 in 2020, then declined to 3,155 by 2023. From 2019 to 2020, critical care encounters increased by 1,180, from 1,010 to 2,190. In 2020, 846 (38.6%) of the 2,190 critical care encounters were COVID-19-related. The highest workload occurred during 2020 and 2021, aligning with COVID-19 surges. Of the 2,914 COVID-19-related encounters, 1,892 (64.9%) were classified as critical care-reflecting strong response capability and return to baseline operations. The LV MCP is an effective model for military medical support during a protracted public health crisis. Its preexisting, integrated structure enabled a rapid and sustained surge response, significantly increasing critical care capacity in a medically underserved region without requiring ad hoc federal deployments or DSCA. This underscores the value of embedded military-civilian partnerships as a resilient, efficient strategy for future emergency preparedness, advocating comprehensive data collection to inform integrated responses.

items.title: Over-the-counter topical diclofenac in musculoskeletal pain: clinical value, access and responsible use.
items.abstract: Topical non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), including diclofenac, are established options for localized musculoskeletal pain, with guidelines supporting their use in knee osteoarthritis, broader osteoarthritis management and acute non-low-back musculoskeletal injuries. For selected indications, topical diclofenac can be highly effective and is generally well tolerated when used as indicated. It provides local analgesic and anti-inflammatory activity with substantially lower systemic exposure than oral NSAIDs, which may be particularly relevant for older adults and people with gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, renal or polypharmacy-related risk factors. As an NSAID, topical diclofenac should nevertheless be used in accordance with product labeling.These clinical benefits sit alongside environmental considerations. Diclofenac may enter wastewater via excretion, and for topical products, through handwashing, wash-off from treated skin, and improper disposal. National exposure estimates suggest that topical formulations can make an important contribution to diclofenac entering wastewater and surface waters, although estimates are setting-specific and depend on assumptions about use, wash-off and wastewater removal.This commentary considers the clinical value of over-the-counter (OTC) topical diclofenac alongside environmental evidence and uncertainties relevant to responsible use. Integrated evidence comparing analgesic options across clinical outcomes, patient safety, environmental burden and substitution effects remains limited, and the net consequences of treatment substitution cannot currently be reliably assessed. Some practical measures can reduce diclofenac release through specific point-of-use pathways, although their uptake and population level impact require further evaluation.Topical diclofenac therefore provides a useful case study for responsible, pharmacist-guided OTC self-care in musculoskeletal pain management. In the authors' opinion, the available evidence and remaining uncertainties call for proportionate stewardship: maintaining clinically appropriate OTC access to topical diclofenac while avoiding unnecessary use and supporting label-consistent treatment, patient education, and feasible measures to reduce avoidable environmental release, alongside formulation and delivery innovation.

items.title: Comprehensive approaches to Traumatic Brain Injury: bridging physical, emotional, and social dimensions for global health care.
items.abstract: Introduction Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) is a significant global health issue, affecting millions annually and resulting in physical, cognitive, emotional, and social challenges. While medical management, including neurosurgical interventions and rehabilitation, is well-documented, the emotional, psychological, and social dimensions of TBI remain underexplored. This gap in understanding hinders the development of holistic approaches to care. Method This article adopts an interdisciplinary approach, synthesizing existing literature to analyze the multifaceted impacts of TBI, as a narrative review rather than a systematic review; no formal search protocol, study screening, or quality appraisal was applied. Special focus is placed on the long-term consequences for individuals, families, and healthcare systems, with particular attention to the disparities faced by low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Result This narrative synthesis highlights the pervasive effects of TBI on quality of life, including persistent emotional and social challenges that are often overlooked in standard care practices. Drawing on this synthesis rather than on original data, we argue that current global health strategies inadequately address these dimensions, particularly in LMICs, where access to long-term rehabilitation and integrated care is limited and varies substantially across settings. Conclusion A more comprehensive approach to TBI management is essential, one that integrates physical, cognitive, emotional, and social dimensions. Addressing these aspects through improved global health strategies can enhance recovery outcomes and improve the quality of life for individuals with TBI and their caregivers, particularly in resource-constrained settings.

items.title: Safety and immunogenicity of the 24-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine in healthy Chinese adults: two single-center, randomized, double-blind Phase 1 and Phase 2 trials.
items.abstract: Background Conventional pneumococcal vaccines cover limited serotypes. This study evaluated the safety and immunogenicity of 24-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV24) in Chinese adults aged ≥18 years. Research design and methods Two single-center, randomized, double-blind Phase 1/2 trials were conducted. Two hundred forty Phase 1 participants were randomized with an overall allocation ratio of 1:1:1:1 to low/high dose PCV24, 23-valent pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine (PPSV23), or placebo. Nine hundred ninety‑two Phase 2 participants were randomized (1:1:1:1) to receive one of three PCV24 formulations (low-dose and low adjuvant, low-dose, high-dose) or PPSV23. Adverse events (AEs) within 30 days post-vaccination and study-wide serious adverse events (SAEs) were collected. Blood samples were tested for immunogenicity in Phase 2. Results Post-vaccination adverse reactions (ARs) within 0-30 days were primarily grade 1-2, with rare grade 3 events limited to the 0-7 days. No vaccine-related SAEs occurred over 6 months. Immunogenicity analysis confirmed that in all participants aged ≥18 years, the PCV24 high-dose group met non-inferiority criteria for IgG seroconversion of all 24 serotypes compared with PPSV23. Conclusions The PCV24 vaccine exhibits a favorable safety profile and robust immunogenicity in Chinese adults aged ≥18 years, supporting further efficacy studies in larger populations. Clinical trials registration www.clinicaltrials.gov identifier: NCT07025876; NCT07035054.

items.title: Digital Visibility and Vulnerability - Suicide Deaths Among Social Media Influencers in India.
items.abstract: Aim: To examine online media reporting of social media influencer (SMI) suicide deaths in India, focusing on socio-demographic characteristics, social media platforms used, reported reasons for suicide, and patterns of media coverage. Method: A Google search using the terms "social media influencer AND suicide AND India" was conducted on April 7, 2026, for the reference period January 1, 2020, to December 31, 2025. Of 258 retrieved links across 26 pages, 106 eligible reports describing 14 unique suicide deaths were included. Multiple reports for the same case were retained to assess reporting patterns. Data were extracted using a standardized template and analyzed descriptively. Results: Fourteen suicide deaths of SMIs were identified across 106 online media reports, most commonly from online newspapers (47.2%). Females accounted for 78.6% of deaths. All deceased SMIs were active on Instagram, with follower counts ranging from 7,900 to 700,000. Depression (42.9%) and cyberbullying (28.6%) were the most frequently cited reasons for suicide in media reports. Photographs of the deceased appeared in 70.8% of reports, predominantly for female influencers, and one death received exceptionally high coverage across 40 reports. Limitations: Reliance on online media reports, use of a single search strategy, and the small number of identified cases may limit completeness, accuracy, and generalizability. Conclusion: Media reporting of suicide deaths among SMIs in India appeared repetitive and frequently included photographs and speculative attributions regarding reasons for suicide. These findings highlight concerns regarding responsible suicide reporting and the need for more systematic research into suicide vulnerability within the digital creator economy.

items.title: What Have We Learned About Incentive Mechanisms?
items.abstract: This comment assesses the evidence from four papers on the development process for four breakthrough drugs or treatments. The comment notes that the papers show all the key breakthroughs in the development process were financed either through the National Institutes of Health or various foundations or charities, not drug companies looking to be compensated through patent monopolies. It argues that this evidence suggests patent monopolies are an unnecessary distortion that results in high drug prices and creates perverse incentives. Expanded public funding could replace patent monopolies, allowing new drugs to be sold at free market prices, ending the problem of high drug prices blocking access.

items.title: Concordance and discordance between policymaker and family physician experiences of the COVID-19-driven rise of virtual care in Nova Scotia.
items.abstract: Aim To describe and understand areas of concordance and discordance between the perceptions and experiences of family physicians and policymakers regarding the implementation and use of virtual care within the Nova Scotian primary care system. Background COVID-19 brought rapid change to primary care delivery and accessibility. Virtual care rapidly expanded, facilitating primary care access amidst public health restrictions. Health systems leaders facilitated access to virtual care, developed and implemented guidelines, and created new billing codes. Providers integrated virtual care and operation changes into practice. Methods Semi-structured interviews with family physicians ( n = 20), policymakers ( n = 9) and a family physician/policymaker ( n = 1) were conducted to understand virtual care implementation and outcomes in Nova Scotia, Canada, identifying benefits and challenges. Findings All participants discussed patient confidentiality concerns, overreliance potential, and virtual care to promote patient care access. Family physicians discussed provider privacy and burnout. Policymakers discussed virtual care increasing capacity for accepting new patients and challenges evaluating virtual care billing codes. Providers and policymakers shared concerns and policy directions for development and expansion of virtual care. As there is little research from policymaker perspectives on virtual care, reconciling these viewpoints is crucial for effectiveness and sustainability.

items.title: Ketamine Versus Electroconvulsive Therapy for Nonpsychotic Treatment-Resistant Depression: A Cost-Effectiveness Analysis.
items.abstract: Objective Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is a highly effective intervention for treatment-resistant depression; however, its use has been limited partly because of concerns about cognitive side effects. Evidence for the sustained (>1 month) efficacy of ketamine versus ECT for treatment-resistant depression has only recently been demonstrated. This study aimed to examine the cost-effectiveness-that is, the costs and benefits measured as quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs)-of racemic ketamine versus that of ECT for treatment-resistant depression. Methods Using a decision tree model, the authors examined the incremental QALYs and costs of ketamine in comparison to ECT over 29 weeks from both health care and societal perspectives in Canada. Deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were used to account for uncertainty. Results Compared with ECT, ketamine resulted in higher health-related quality of life (incremental QALY=0.024) and lower costs from both a health care (CA$-1,663) and a societal (incremental cost=-$3,413) perspective. In nearly all one-way sensitivity analyses, ketamine was found to be cost-effective relative to ECT. Conclusions Ketamine provided additional QALYs while saving costs relative to ECT for treatment-resistant depression. Health insurance plans that cover all costs of ECT should also cover all costs of ketamine treatment for treatment-resistant depression.

items.title: Outdated Product Labeling and Implications for Contemporary Standards of Care: The Example of Clozapine.
items.abstract: Discontinuation of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's clozapine risk evaluation and mitigation strategy program led to a package insert (PI) revision in June 2025. However, that PI update retained many elements that are inconsistent with modern clozapine prescribing, including rapid titration, twice-daily dosing at the start of therapy, and titration without regard to patient factors (e.g., ancestry, sex and gender, or smoking status). The revision also provided no guidance on monitoring for myocarditis or mitigating the primary causes of mortality-pneumonia and ileus. This discrepancy between the clozapine PI and evidence-based practices has caused clinicians to consider whether deviation from the PI presents a medicolegal risk and how to cope with outdated PI information for clozapine and other medications. This article reviews the relative weight of different forms of medical evidence in establishing the standard of care, illustrates through case law that a PI does not define the standard of care and is inadmissible in malpractice litigation without expert testimony, and provides guidance for clinicians on how to navigate outdated, non-evidence-based PI recommendations. The information in this article should reassure clinicians that using modern evidence-based care-not archaic PI recommendations-is the optimal choice when treating patients.

items.title: The average individual genome: a survey of nearly 1 million whole-genome sequences.
items.abstract: Background As whole-genome sequencing (WGS) is increasingly used in clinical and public health contexts, clearer expectations regarding the amount of variation present in the "average" human genome are required to contextualise findings. Methods We analysed WGS data from two large population cohorts: 490,541 individuals in UK Biobank (UKB) and 414,830 individuals in All of Us. Following variant and genotype QC, we aimed to assess the range of neutral and disease-associated variation across six genetically-inferred ancestry groups. Results The "average" genome contains ~4.3-5.3 million variants, of which ~1.5% are rare (within-cohort allele frequency 10,000 basepairs per genome, and rare autosomal copy number variants > 1 Mb present in ~ 1 in 41 (2.5%) individuals. On average, ~32-42% of variants per person are homozygous and individuals have ~4 unique runs of homozygosity > 1.5 Mb, with marked variation observed across ancestry groups. Of the ~21- 26,000 SNVs/indels per person in coding exons of MANE Select transcripts, ~48% are predicted to alter the protein, of which ~0.8% are high-confidence loss-of-function and ~0.1% have REVEL score > 0.7 suggestive of pathogenicity. Depending upon parental age, the average genome contains ~63 de novo variants, of which ~75-80% are paternal in origin. Considering only rare variants in GenCC-curated monogenic disease-associated genes, the average genome contains ~1-3 ClinVar pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants, ~2-5 high-confidence loss-of-function variants, and ~50 ClinVar variants of uncertain significance. Most ClinVar pathogenic variants are heterozygous in recessive disease genes, consistent with carrier status, and have multiple ClinVar submitters. Finally, applying polygenic scores (PGS) for 28 common diseases within UKB, we estimate that the average person is in the top 10% for ~3 conditions, and around 1 in 5 people are in the top 1% for at least one PGS. Conclusions The ubiquity of genetic variation in individuals has important implications for policy-makers considering genomic screening and clinicians counselling families. The continued underrepresentation of many global populations reflects a broader limitation of contemporary genomic research, underscoring the need for more inclusive datasets worldwide in order to enable equitable precision medicine.

items.title: Heated Arguments: Debates About Heat Wave Mortality and the Need to Act Nonetheless.
items.abstract: As the Earth heats up, heat waves have become an all-too-familiar threat to public health around the world. Heat-related mortality is on the rise. Heat waves have now attracted considerable attention from epidemiologists, sociologists, physicians, urban planners, and historians. This scholarship has been characterized by vigorous debate and fiercely contested narratives. This essay examines the controversies that have swirled around two prominent heat waves-Chicago in 1995 and Paris in 2003. Given the complexity of heat-related mortality, it is no surprise that researchers have argued about the nature of risk, the role of climate change, and the phenomena of mortality displacement. One risk, however, is that ongoing debate about the intricacies of epidemiology and sociology will foster confusion about the danger of heat waves and undermine the consensus that is needed to motivate action against the threat of heat. Scholars face a difficult challenge: how to acknowledge ongoing and healthy scientific debate while also recognizing that there are large areas of consensus that justify public health action. The health and environmental humanities, fields that have long been interested in questions of unstable and contested narratives, offer valuable perspective on meeting this challenge.

items.title: Circulating Immune and Cancer Driver Gene Biomarkers Precede Prostate Cancer Diagnosis by over 10 yr.
items.abstract: Background and objective Prospective proteomic and proteogenomic studies may enhance the understanding of proteins associated with prostate cancer (PCa) development. Methods In a case-cohort study within the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC), baseline plasma samples from 982 incident PCa cases and 1573 subcohort participants were profiled using the SomaScan 7k platform (over 6000 proteins). Associations were estimated using Prentice-weighted Cox models. The coprimary end points were incident overall PCa and aggressive PCa (n = 290). Findings were evaluated in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) study and supported by Mendelian randomization (MR) and exome gene-burden analyses. Key findings and limitations ACP3, FLT4, and KLK3 were associated with overall PCa risk (hazard ratio [HR] per 1 standard deviation [SD] increase were 1.20 [1.10-1.31], 1.26 [1.13-1.40], and 2.28 [1.96-2.65], respectively). Seven proteins were associated with aggressive PCa risk, with ANKRD1 consistently associated across multiple clinically relevant disease subtypes. Twelve proteins were associated with PCa diagnosed >15 yr after blood draw, including ANXA2, GZMK, and OSCAR. ACP3, ANXA2, APOC2, and KLK3 showed consistent associations in both EPIC and ARIC. Additionally, four proteins had support from MR analyses and eight from rare-variant burden tests. Circulating products of established PCa driver genes, including ERBB3, KRAS, and NRAS, were associated with future aggressive disease. Limitations include incomplete external replication and differences in end point availability across cohorts. Conclusions and clinical implications Prospective plasma proteomic analyses identified circulating proteins associated with future PCa risk, including proteins related to immune, adhesion, angiogenesis, and PCa driver-gene pathways. These findings identify candidate protein risk factors for overall and clinically significant PCa, and warrant further validation and mechanistic evaluation.

items.title: Acute heart failure in emergency settings.
items.abstract: Acute heart failure (AHF) represents a major cause of emergency medical care worldwide and continues to carry a substantial burden of morbidity and mortality despite advances in chronic heart failure management. Most patients with AHF present to emergency departments (EDs), where the first hours of care are critical to determine prognosis. Of these, some have been previously evaluated and treated by prehospital emergency medical services before ED arrival. This consensus document summarizes the current evidence and provides practical advice to emergency physicians for the diagnosis, treatment, and disposition of patients with AHF in these emergency settings (emergency medical services and ED). It emphasizes the importance of a rapid phenotypic classification into acute decompensated heart failure, acute pulmonary oedema, isolated right ventricular failure, or cardiogenic shock, as a key tool to guide early management and triage decisions. It reviews evidence on prehospital and ED management, including the use of biomarkers, imaging, ventilatory support, diuretic and vasodilator strategies, and early initiation or continuation of guideline-directed medical therapy. It also discusses risk stratification and disposition decisions supported by validated tools. Finally, it identifies major knowledge gaps and future research priorities, including pragmatic trials to assess prehospital interventions, biomarker-guided therapy, and early initiation of disease-modifying treatments. Ultimately, this consensus document is aimed to contribute to the improvement of outcomes in AHF.

items.title: A Simple Home-based Ring Test May Promote Early Diagnosis of Retinal Detachment, Retinal Vascular Diseases and Common Optic Nerve Disease.
items.abstract: Background and objective The purpose of this study was to evaluate a simple ring-based visual field screening test to determine whether, when used at home, the findings were similar to clinical evaluation in terms of visual field defects associated with retinal and optic nerve diseases. Patients and methods This was a prospective observational cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study. Consecutive patients presenting between May 2023 and February 2025 with acute vision loss, known history of retinal or optic nerve disorders, or symptoms of acute posterior vitreous detachment or floaters were enrolled. A total of 594 patients (667 eyes) were included. With the fellow eye occluded, patients viewed a 360° ring target and reported any missing or distorted segments. Ring-test findings were compared with clinical reference standards including dilated fundus examination, fundus photography, and Humphrey Visual Field (HVF) testing. Concordance between ring test defects and HVF defects was assessed based on location and orientation. Results Of a total of 667 eyes, 240 eyes underwent HVF testing. Among 88 eyes with HVF defects, the ring test identified 80 (sensitivity, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.83-0.96). Among 152 eyes without HVF defects, 149 were correctly classified (specificity, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.94-1.00). Ring test findings demonstrated strong spatial concordance with clinical pathology. Conclusions Concordance between ring test defects and HVF defects was high, with strong sensitivity and specificity for detecting mid-to-peripheral visual field defects in rhegmatogenous retinal detachment, retinal vascular occlusions, and certain optic neuropathies. Preliminary results of this initial proof-of-concept study suggest that the ring test has potential utility as a home-based screening tool to facilitate earlier awareness of vision-threatening conditions. Further studies are needed to evaluate its role in routine clinical practice.

items.title: Heart rate supports accelerometry as a reliable predictor of energy expenditure in bats.
items.abstract: Measuring the energetic cost of behavior is essential for understanding decision-making in wild animals. This is particularly true for bats, where life near their energetic ceiling has resulted in a diversity of behaviors to compensate for social and environmental unpredictability. Although GPS and tri-axial accelerometry have improved movement-based estimates of energy expenditure in the field, complex flight kinematics in bats may violate key assumptions accelerometry-based estimates rely on. To test whether energy expenditure is predicted by acceleration-based movement in bats, we deployed heart rate loggers alongside GPS with tri-axial accelerometers on free-ranging greater spear-nosed bats (Phyllostomus hastatus) in Panamá. We hypothesized that heart rate would positively reflect increases in vectorial dynamic body acceleration (VeDBA), a commonly used proxy for energy expenditure, and that including information on behavior would enhance this relationship. We also hypothesized that heart rate and VeDBA would reflect theoretical speed-power curves of flight. We found that VeDBA had a strong positive relationship with heart rate, and model accuracy improved when behavioral states of flying and not flying were defined. Additionally, incorporating behavioral duration and sequence number improved predictions, showing that temporal context and activity patterns further refine estimates of energy expenditure. The relationship between VeDBA and airspeed resembled the mechanical power curve previously estimated for P. hastatus, supporting the relevance of aerodynamic theory in interpreting bat energetics. Overall, acceleration-based estimates reliably predict energy expenditure in free-ranging P. hastatus, and incorporating behavior improves model accuracy and ecological relevance, providing a powerful tool for understanding energy allocation in wild bats.
