items.title: When brain networks crash: connectivity, slow-wave activity and neural replay in Alzheimer's disease.
items.abstract: Brain connectivity disruption is a hallmark of neurodegenerative disorders, including Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet how network breakdown gives rise to cognitive deficits remains unclear. Here, we review the evidence bearing on three interconnected processes that have been proposed to link molecular pathology to cognitive decline. First, we summarize evidence that misfolded proteins propagate along brain connectivity pathways, making the connectome the biological substrate for disease progression. Second, we discuss the divergent trajectory reported across the AD continuum, an initial compensatory hyperconnectivity followed by progressive hypoconnectivity and network collapse, together with the accompanying oscillatory changes (intrusion of slow-wave activity and suppression of fast oscillatory rhythms). Third, we examine the proposal that these oscillatory alterations compromise neural replay mechanisms, critical for memory consolidation, representing the potential link between network dysfunction and cognitive decline. By integrating evidence from human neuroimaging, electrophysiology, and animal models in the AD field, this framework offers new perspectives for therapeutic interventions targeting brain connectivity and replay mechanisms in neurodegenerative diseases.

items.title: Association Between Plasma N-Terminal Tau, Cognitive Decline, and Neurodegeneration in the ADNI Cohort.
items.abstract: Background and objectives Blood-based biomarkers offer a cost-effective, minimally invasive alternative to neuroimaging and CSF biomarkers. Newly developed fluid biomarkers, including the N-terminal tau fragment (NT1), show promise for identifying individuals at risk for Alzheimer disease (AD) and for monitoring disease progression. Here, we determine whether NT1 levels are associated with key clinical and biomarker measures in a large, well-characterized cohort. Methods Participants from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohort with available plasma NT1, β-amyloid (Aβ)-PET, MRI, and clinical measures (Clinical Dementia Rating) were included in this observational study. NT1 was measured using the Quanterix Simoa HD-X platform. PET, MRI, clinical, and other plasma measures were obtained using established ADNI procedures. A subset also had NULISA-based plasma measures of amyloid and tau and tau-PET assessed. Linear regression and linear mixed-effects models were used to assess cross-sectional and longitudinal associations between NT1 and clinical or biomarker measures, adjusting for relevant covariates. Multivariable-adjusted Cox regression was performed to evaluate the association between baseline NT1 levels and risk of clinically diagnosed mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or AD. Mediation analysis was conducted to examine whether hippocampal atrophy mediates the relationship between NT1 and memory decline. Spearman correlations were used to examine continuous relationships between plasma NT1 and continuous fluid and neuroimaging markers. Results A total of 755 participants (mean age: 72.9 [7.0], female: 375 [50%]) were included in the study. Plasma NT1 levels were elevated in MCI/AD individuals (B MCI/AD [SE] = 0.09 [0.022], p = 1.98 × 10 -4 ) and were cross-sectionally associated with worse memory performance (B [SE] = -0.25 [0.09], p = 0.005). Aβ moderated the association between elevated NT1 and greater cognitive decline across multiple domains (memory: B [SE] = -0.17 [0.074], p = 0.022; executive function: B [SE] = -0.24 [0.082], p = 0.004; language: B [SE] = -0.21 [0.075], p = 0.006). NT1 levels were negatively associated with hippocampal volume (B [SE] = -264.49 [125.99], p = 0.036) and predicted longitudinal atrophy (B [SE] = -42.00 [16.90], p = 0.013). Accelerated hippocampal atrophy largely mediated the association between higher baseline NT1 level and greater memory decline (B [95% CI] indirect effect = -0.082 [-0.135 to -0.03], p = 0.003, B [95% CI] proportion mediated = 70.1% [32.6%-155.3%], p = 0.004). Higher NT1 levels were associated with higher levels of plasma biomarkers, including NULISA-based brain-derived (BD) plasma pTau (BD-pTau181, BD-pTau217, BD-pTau231: p 's -6 ) and Simoa-Based pTau181 ( p -15 ) and neurofilament light chain ( p -7 ). Discussion Plasma NT1 may be useful in assessing amyloid-dependent cognitive decline and neurodegeneration.

items.title: Episodic Memory: Dynamic Modes for Constructing Episodes.
items.abstract: The capacity to re-experience a moment from one's past, known as episodic memory, is critical for our ability to navigate the present and plan for the future. This article reviews and synthesizes over a half century of behavioral and neuroscientific research that has shaped our understanding of how we remember past events. This work has revealed complementary truths about episodic memory: Episodic memories seem to be based on traces of experience, carrying objective information about specific moments in time, and on imaginative reconstructions, built on a scaffold of prior knowledge. We propose that the tension between these perspectives can be reconciled by conceptualizing episodic memory not as a readout from a static memory system but as the outcome of two neurocognitive modes- a generative mode that facilitates schema-based inference and prediction, and a contextual mode that binds memories to context-specific anchor points. Drawing from experimental findings and computational models, we describe how multiple memory modes arise from dynamic cortico-hippocampal interactions, allowing episodic memory to be at once precise and constructive.

items.title: Single-nucleotide polymorphism-directed design of allele-specific antisense oligonucleotides for spinocerebellar ataxia type 3.
items.abstract: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 3 (SCA3), also called Machado-Joseph disease, the most common form of autosomal dominant cerebellar ataxia, is caused by a CAG repeat expansion in ATXN3 . The mutant protein is prone to aggregation and exerts toxic gain-of-function effects, whereas the wild-type protein has important neuroprotective roles as a deubiquitinase. Current treatment strategies for SCA3 lack specificity for the mutant allele. Identifying genetic variants such as single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in linkage with the pathogenic CAG expansion offers a promising avenue to develop allele-specific therapeutic interventions, like antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs). To address this, we conducted allele-specific, targeted, multiplexed nanopore sequencing on 79 patients with SCA3 from Germany, UK, and Portugal. We identified almost 200 polymorphisms and grouped them into three haplotype blocks on the basis of linkage disequilibrium. These SNPs were strongly associated with the CAG expansion. Genotypic modeling of our subcohorts indicated that targeting only two SNPs from different blocks could enable allele-specific treatment of the majority of European patients with SCA3. We evaluated 17 candidate ASOs targeting SNPs from different haplotype blocks. Seven of these ASOs caused allele-preferential reduction of more than 65%. A single ASO application in two SCA3 iPSC-derived cortical neurons (AX1, AX2) achieved up to 90% reduction of mutant ATXN3. Toxicity assessments together with RNA sequencing analyses in AX1 did not indicate evidence of toxicity or widespread transcriptional perturbations. These findings highlight that characterizing heterozygosity rates offers valuable opportunities for selective ASO therapies. Our proof-of-principle targeting with ASOs demonstrates the feasibility of haplotype-informed allele-specific silencing in ATXN3 .

items.title: The association between orthorexia nervosa and social media use: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Orthorexia nervosa (ON) is a newly described mental disorder characterized by an extreme obsession with the consumption of healthy foods, resulting in anxiety and impaired functionality. This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to synthesize the association between social media use and orthorexic tendencies among adolescents and adults. PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Scopus, and PsycINFO were searched through January 2026. Original studies assessing the association between social media use and ON were included. Zero-order correlations between social media and orthorexia measures were pooled using Fisher's z under a random-effects (REML) model; heterogeneity, subgroup and meta-regression, sensitivity and publication-bias analyses were performed; certainty was rated with GRADE. Of 33 included studies, 22 contributed to meta-analysis of the correlation between social media use and ON symptoms, yielding a small positive pooled correlation (r = 0.20, 95% CI 0.15-0.25; I² = 84.3%; very low certainty by GRADE). This association remained stable across leave-one-out, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses (r = 0.18-0.20), and after adjustment for potential publication bias (bias-adjusted r = 0.17). A secondary analysis of two studies with reconstructable 2 × 2 data suggested greater odds of ON among heavier users (OR = 1.57, 95% CI 1.25-1.97). Pooled ON prevalence differed sharply with the diagnostic threshold (39.9% at the ORTO-15 cutoff below 35 versus 65.5% below 40), reflecting extreme heterogeneity (I² > 90%) across studies. Narrative synthesis indicated that the type of content consumed was more consistently associated with ON than platform or duration of use alone Social media use is associated with greater orthorexic tendencies. However, because all included studies were cross-sectional and overall certainty of evidence was very low, causality and directionality cannot be established and reverse causality remains plausible. Longitudinal and experimental research is needed to clarify the direction of this relationship.

items.title: BCG vaccination mitigates tau pathology and restores cognitive function in PS19 mice.
items.abstract: Retrospective studies in patients with nonmuscle invasive bladder cancer have reported a significant reduction in Alzheimer's disease incidence (12 to 78%) among Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) recipients versus controls. To investigate the underlying mechanisms, we evaluated BCG in the PS19 mouse model of tauopathy. We found that BCG administration reduced hippocampal phospho-tau and microgliosis while preserving neuronal markers. In vivo volumetric T2-magnetic resonance Imaging (MRI) demonstrated attenuation of brain atrophy accompanied by increased glutamate-weighted chemical exchange saturation transfer-MRI signals. Functionally, BCG-treated mice showed improved performance in the novel object recognition test, as well as improved body-weight maintenance and survival. Transcriptomic profiling of the hippocampus revealed near complete normalization of the PS19 disease-associated gene expression signature toward that of healthy controls. Flow cytometric profiling of brain myeloid populations demonstrated a reduction in activated resident microglia, but total microglia cells remain elevated. Moreover, an increase of trained immunity marker CD80 on the recruited peripheral myeloid cells ensues following BCG treatment. Consistent with this shift in myeloid state, primary brain myeloid cells from BCG-treated mice also exhibited enhanced phagocytosis of fluorescein isothiocyanate-labeled tau fibrils and increased lactate production. Together, these findings indicate that BCG induces systemic and central nervous system myeloid cell reprogramming that limits neuroinflammation, enhances tau clearance, and rescues cognitive and neurodegenerative phenotypes in a tauopathy model. BCG is a safe, readily available therapy that merits consideration as a preventive agent against dementia.

items.title: Neurophysiological dynamics related to perception, action, and language in schizophrenia.
items.abstract: Schizophrenia disrupts both how people perceive the world and how they express and act on their thoughts, yet these symptoms are usually studied separately. Using magnetoencephalography during multisensory and motor tasks, we tested whether reduced event-related beta-band (15 to 30 hertz) modulation, a signal implicated in predictive control, provides a candidate neural marker across these domains. Compared to healthy individuals, patients showed diminished beta changes during sensory processing and movement completion, suggesting reduced flexibility in updating internal models. This neural pattern covaried with audiovisual simultaneity-judgment behavior, disorganized natural speech, and greater clinical severity. These findings suggest that distributed beta modulation may serve as a candidate cross-domain marker associated with perceptual, motor, and language disturbances in schizophrenia, motivating future studies that directly test predictive updating mechanisms.

items.title: Differential sex-dependent responses of circulating steroid hormones and cortical gene expression in a traumatic brain injury model.
items.abstract: Accumulating evidence supports sex differences in traumatic brain injury (TBI) outcomes. However, the underlying processes that lead to sex differences are not well understood. TBI results in the initiation of molecular and cellular responses that facilitate the progression of neurodegeneration. Little is known about how the circulating hormone profile is altered in response to TBI and whether sex differences in endocrine responses might shape secondary injury pathologies. Using intact male and female mice in a preclinical TBI model, we assessed changes in plasma hormone concentrations and cortical gene expression at 24 and 72 hours after TBI. We demonstrate that males and females exhibit sex-specific alterations in circulating levels of testosterone, androstenedione, estradiol, and dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) in response to TBI. We also identified sex differences in the expression of genes that are involved in immune responses and tissue remodeling after injury. Moreover, we report divergent circulating hormone and gene expression correlations between sexes.

items.title: Predicting upcoming visual features during eye movements yields scene representations aligned with human visual cortex.
items.abstract: Natural scenes are complex arrangements of objects, surfaces, and backgrounds. For the brain's visual system to effectively operate, it needs to extract not only what objects are present but also their spatial and semantic relations. We hypothesize that such structures may be learned, in a self-supervised fashion, by exploiting temporal regularities of natural active vision: Each fixation reveals a glimpse that is related to the previous one via co-occurrence and saccade-conditioned spatial regularities. We instantiate this idea with glimpse prediction networks (GPNs), recurrent models trained to predict the embedding of the next glimpse along human-like scanpaths. GPNs are shown to successfully extract complex scene information, including object co-occurrences and spatial object arrangements, and integrate information across glimpses. GPN representations align strongly with human fMRI responses in mid- and higher-level visual cortex and match, often outperform, alternative state-of-the-art ANN models, establishing next-glimpse-prediction as a biologically plausible route toward brain-aligned scene representations.

items.title: Coordinated mosquito biting dynamics at the human skin interface.
items.abstract: The bite of a female mosquito is the critical point of pathogen transmission, yet the fine-scale biting dynamics on human skin remain unknown. Here, we combine high-speed videography, deep-learning-based tracking, and electrophysiology to analyze biting dynamics of the malaria vector Anopheles coluzzii in real time at the human skin interface. We uncover a previously uncharacterized synchronization of mouthpart and leg movements during probing and identify five distinct below skin sub-behaviors: piercing, vessel searching, blood ingestion, retraction, and withdrawal. We show that disruption of the orco and IR76b chemosensory genes can alter some components of normal biting but these effects are subtle, suggesting possible plasticity in direct-contact chemosensation and mosquito bite execution. Comparative analyses show genus-specific biting strategies between An. coluzzii and Aedes aegypti linked to distinct ways they find blood vessels. Our findings indicate that female mosquitoes exhibit a complex synchronization of body parts at the bite site via motor and chemosensory processes.

items.title: The successor representation in high-risk drinking and alcohol-related contexts.
items.abstract: The successor representation (SR) is a reinforcement learning strategy which has been suggested to underlie nuanced forms of habitual behavior, rendering it a candidate mechanism for mental health conditions thought to involve habitual control, such as addiction. However, paradigms used to assess habits in humans cannot detect SR use. Together with the fact that they are usually conducted in disorder-irrelevant contexts, this may explain why the evidence for a hypothesized shift from goal-directed to habitual behavior in addiction is inconsistent. Here, we tested whether individuals with high-risk (n = 260) compared to low-risk drinking behavior (n = 260) rely more on SR or a rigid goal-based dimension-reduced SR variant, particularly in alcohol-related contexts. An online multi-stage decision-making task performed in either a virtual bar or apartment context allowed us to dissociate (red)SR from model-based and model-free learning strategies by testing how well participants adapted their choices to different types of distal changes in the environment. Findings suggest that a particular type of SR, namely a (reduced) random-policy SR-like strategy, contributes to human behavior, but that high-risk drinkers do not differ from low-risk drinkers in their use of this strategy. Instead, both groups seem to rely less on what is likely a (reduced) random-policy SR strategy in alcohol-related contexts - and instead more on model-free control. Results suggest that the use of an adaptive, resource-efficient decision-making strategy is selectively downregulated in substance-related contexts. This study highlights the importance of considering contextual modulation and nuanced decision strategies in understanding habitual and goal-directed behavior in mental health conditions such as addiction.

items.title: Susceptibility of human neural stem cells to SARS-CoV-2: Entry mechanisms and glycocalyx influence.
items.abstract: Previous work demonstrated that ectodermal cells exhibit greater susceptibility to SARS-CoV-2 than endodermal and mesodermal cells, raising concerns about potential vulnerability of the developing nervous system. We hypothesized that neural stem cells (NSCs) derived from human ectoderm are susceptible to SARS-CoV-2. Using pseudotyped viral particles representing both wild-type and Omicron spike variants, we confirmed efficient transduction in NSCs, with Omicron variants preferentially utilizing endocytosis-mediated entry. Inhibition of endocytosis with filipin and OcTMAB significantly reduced viral entry across all spike variants. Low glycosylation levels on NSCs facilitated viral entry, and enzymatic removal of glycosylation increased their susceptibility. Ectodermal infection by SARS-CoV-2 raises serious concern for potential teratogenic effects on the nervous system, possibly causing latent or subclinical anomalies not immediately evident at birth. Therefore, future clinical studies and long-term surveillance of infants and children exposed in utero are necessary to investigate and identify potential neurodevelopmental deficits.

items.title: Developing a systems-based programme theory for reducing night-time interactive electronic device use and improving sleep among adolescents.
items.abstract: Background Adolescent night-time use of interactive electronic devices (IEDs) is increasingly linked to poor sleep, mental health challenges, and reduced academic performance. However, existing interventions often overlook the complex systems shaping these behaviours. This study presents a first-of-its-kind systems-based programme theory for CLOCK OFF - a peer influence intervention aimed at reducing night-time IED use and improving adolescent sleep - created through novel participatory mapping activities and analyses, which involved adolescents, parents and teachers. Methods We conducted five online participatory workshops with adolescents (aged 11-14 years), parents, and teachers across four United Kingdom schools, supported by desk-based research. Workshop activities were facilitated using StickyStudio software. Causal loop diagramming was used to identify system components and feedback loops influencing adolescent IED use and sleep. Causal loop diagrams (CLDs) were iteratively built using Kumu software, refined and validated through stakeholder input and network analysis. The final CLD informed the development of a systems-based programme theory. Results Thirty participants (23 adolescents, 7 adults) contributed to the systems mapping process. The final CLD comprised 68 factors (i.e., causal influences of night-time IED use) and 131 connections between these factors, spanning behavioural, educational, psychological, physiological, social, and technological domains. CLOCK OFF-related mechanisms were represented across a large proportion of the system's identified feedback structures. The programme theory diagram included 72 factors and 147 feedback loops, grouped into five subsystems. These subsystems highlighted the dynamic interplay between enjoyment, overstimulation, fear of missing out (FOMO), emotional regulation, and educational stress. Conclusions Participatory systems mapping with adolescents is a feasible and valuable method for surfacing complex behavioural drivers and informing intervention design. CLOCK OFF's systems-based programme theory offers a novel approach for understanding and addressing adolescent night-time IED use and sleep disruption. Findings support the need for multi-actor and peer-led, multi-level interventions embedded within broader systemic strategies.

items.title: Multimodal Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Relapse in Major Depressive Disorder.
items.abstract: Importance Early identification of patients at high risk of relapse is key to personalized preventive strategies in major depressive disorder (MDD). However, current predictive models do not adequately account for the multimodal factors contributing to MDD relapse and fail to provide clinically meaningful predictions. Objective To predict relapse within 2 years in patients with MDD by using a comprehensive machine learning pipeline that integrates an unprecedented set of multimodal data. Design, setting, and participants This naturalistic longitudinal prognostic study used data from the Marburg-Münster Affective Disorders Cohort Study, with baseline assessments collected from October 2014 to May 2019 and follow-up approximately 2 years later, between October 2016 and June 2021. Data analysis was conducted between July 2024 and June 2026. The study was performed at 2 sites in Germany (Marburg and Münster), with participants recruited from psychiatric inpatient and outpatient departments and the general population. Patients meeting diagnostic criteria for current or lifetime MDD without history of neurological or severe somatic conditions were included. Exposure Natural course of illness in patients with MDD. Main outcomes and measures Balanced accuracy (BACC) for binary prediction of relapse vs no relapse during 2-year follow-up served as the primary outcome. Baseline features comprised 9 modalities including clinical and psychometric data, 4 structural and functional magnetic resonance imaging modalities, genetics, neurocognition, blood markers, and gut microbiome. Results A total of 564 patients with a current or lifetime MDD diagnosis were included (367 female [65.1%]; mean [SD] age, 37.34 [13.38] years). A total of 270 patients relapsed during the 2-year follow-up, while 294 did not. Mean (SD) BACC for the prediction of relapse ranged from 47.21% (5.85%) to 64.43% (6.63%). The best-performing model was solely based on few clinical relapse risk factors, while multimodal data integration did not improve performance. Conclusions and relevance In this prognostic study, the models achieved moderate accuracy, yet the results suggest limited scope for guiding individual-level clinical decision-making. Predictive performance was largely driven by established clinical risk factors, indicating limited incremental value of multimodal measures when assessed at a single time point. Future advances may instead benefit from dynamic modeling approaches that more closely align temporally evolving multimodal markers with longitudinal clinical outcomes.

items.title: Naturalistic spatial education engages distinct neural processes for mental rotation, cognitive load, and linguistic demands.
items.abstract: Neuroscience studies typically isolate spatial cognition using simplified tasks targeting a single cognitive process. However, during formal spatial education, the brain rarely performs one cognitive operation at a time. Here, we used functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to assess neural systems involved in dynamically processing an educational spatial visualization lesson. We quantified lesson content using an instructional-design framework capturing variation in spatial complexity, cognitive load, and verbal density. We then characterized how instructional demands modulated brain function using content-evoked responses, functional connectivity, and network-centrality. Spatial transformations during instruction robustly recruited parietal and premotor regions, which were linearly modulated by spatial complexity. This parietal dominance aligns with theories that these areas encode geometric and quantitative dimensions. In contrast, domain-general frontal activity tracked overall processing demands, and language regions tracked verbal density. Activity also varied with learners' spatial abilities: higher spatial performers showed stronger modulation of parietal and premotor regions as spatial demands increased, and greater domain-general modulation across content types. Thus, the same circuitry representing spatial transformations during instruction also reflects individual variation in spatial cognition. Parietal regions showed the highest centrality and strongest within-network coherence, marking them as the central hub of the system, and distinguishing them from less central and less coherent domain-general regions. Together, the findings reveal how the brain dynamically decomposes complex spatial instruction, preserving parietal-centered spatial processing, while coordinating support from premotor, domain-general, and language systems. These findings begin to reveal how spatial cognition operates within the complexity of formal instruction.

items.title: Translational control of microglial metabolism, inflammatory responses, and survival by the eIF4E-binding proteins.
items.abstract: In Alzheimer's disease (AD), activation of the mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway promotes microglial neuroprotective functions by engaging multiple cell receptors. However, the relevant downstream effectors are not fully understood. mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1) promotes mRNA translation by phosphorylating and inactivating eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4E-binding protein 1 and 2 (4E-BP1/2), which are expressed in microglia. 4E-BP1 levels in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) are elevated in AD and correlate with markers of microglial reactivity and disease progression. Using linear regression analysis, we found that elevated CSF 4E-BP1 levels strengthen the association between soluble TREM2 levels and neurodegeneration in amyloid-positive individuals. To investigate the underlying mechanism, we performed in vitro experiments demonstrating that amyloid-β inactivated 4E-BP1 in murine microglia. The mTOR-mediated inactivation is highly dependent on Spleen Tyrosine Kinase (SYK) signaling and repeated exposure to amyloid-β impaired this process, whereas prolonged exposure increased 4E-BP1 levels in microglia. Deletion of 4E-BP1/2 resulted in increased mitochondrial mass and oxidative phosphorylation, reduced pro-inflammatory signaling, and protected microglia from amyloid-induced apoptosis. Thus, impaired 4E-BP1 inactivation-due to reduced mTOR signaling or excess 4E-BP1-disrupts immune resolution, leading to metabolic exhaustion and microglial cell death. We identify the SYK-mTORC1-4E-BP1 signaling axis as a key regulator of microglial mitochondrial biogenesis and immune resolution in AD.

items.title: Optogenetic reduction of theta oscillations induces remapping of time cells without memory impairment.
items.abstract: In a delayed alternation spatial working memory task, hippocampal time cells fire during specific moments of the delay period to form a sequential representation of the entire delay interval. The causal relationship between these sequences and working memory remains unclear. Similarly, hippocampal theta oscillations are thought to support working memory, primarily through the generation of time cell sequences. To causally examine these relationships, we optogenetically silence the medial septal GABAergic theta-generating circuit during the delay portion of a delayed spatial alternation task. With hippocampal theta oscillations substantially reduced, many time cells exhibit remapping, and new time cells are recruited. Despite partial remapping of time cell sequences, behavioral performance remains intact and trajectory-specific coding is preserved, suggesting that task-relevant information remains available under theta disruption.

items.title: Ex Vivo Assessment of Lamotrigine Clearance During Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy.
items.abstract: Continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) provides renal support for unstable ICU patients but significantly alters drug concentrations. For patients on long-term antiepileptics such as lamotrigine, CRRT may increase risk for breakthrough seizures due to subtherapeutic levels. Conversely, CRRT may aid in lamotrigine overdose. While partial clearance of lamotrigine by intermittent hemodialysis has been reported, CRRT clearance is not well studied. This study determined lamotrigine extraction by CRRT in an ex vivo system. Medication was administered at two concentrations: one therapeutic and one supratherapeutic to closed-loop, blood-primed, ex vivo CRRT circuits. Drug concentrations were measured in plasma, hemofiltrate (effluent), and matching control samples at specific time points. For each time point, percent recovery of lamotrigine was calculated, and differences between CRRT circuits and controls were analyzed using two-sample t-tests. Plasma lamotrigine concentrations decreased rapidly, with 10% (n = 3, SD = 4%) and 17% (n = 2, SD = 3%) recovery at four hours for therapeutic and supratherapeutic doses, respectively. Although lower starting concentrations trended toward greater clearance, differences were not statistically significant (P = .13). Control concentrations remained stable, with approximately 100% recovery. Lamotrigine concentrations were significantly affected by CRRT circuits. Patients receiving lamotrigine who require CRRT may need dosing adjustments to maintain clinical efficacy. Additionally, CRRT effectively clears lamotrigine, suggesting potential utility in overdose management.

items.title: The GBA1-related variant rs12411216 is Associated with Motor and Non-Motor Impairments and Unfavorable Progression in Parkinson's Disease: A Five-Year Longitudinal Study.
items.abstract: We investigated four regulatory single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) related to genes previously implicated in the autophagy-lysosomal pathway (rs76904798 and rs6581622 (LRRK2), rs356182 (SNCA), and rs12411216 (GBA1)) in order to assess their association with the clinical heterogeneity of Parkinson's disease. In a five-year observational study, 518 patients stratified by genotype were analyzed for cognitive, neuropsychiatric, motor, and other clinical signs.The rs356182 (SNCA) variant showed a modest association with disease traits, including significant associations with anxiety (HAMILTON scale). Conversely, the regulatory GBA1-related variant rs12411216 demonstrated a robust pleiotropic association with earlier disease onset, more severe motor impairment, and a broad spectrum of non-motor impairments, including anxiety, depression, impulsive-compulsive behaviors, and cognitive deficits. Longitudinal analyses revealed that patients homozygous for the rs12411216 AA genotype exhibited the most unfavorable progression across multiple domains, suggesting a faster neurocognitive decline.These findings suggest that the distinct pleiotropic effects of the GBA1-related variant rs12411216 contribute significantly to the clinical heterogeneity of PD by shaping unfavorable motor and neuropsychiatric progression trajectories. While the longitudinal design provides new evidence for genotype-dependent patterns, further functional studies are needed to confirm the proposed mechanistic link.

items.title: Putative Transcriptomic Endotypes Reveal Neuronal, Immune, and Metabolic Heterogeneity in Temporal Lobe Epilepsy with Hippocampal Sclerosis.
items.abstract: Temporal lobe epilepsy with hippocampal sclerosis (TLE-HS) is a biologically heterogeneous disorder in which neuronal loss, gliosis, neuroinflammation, and metabolic stress may coexist but are unlikely to be uniformly represented across all patients. To investigate this heterogeneity at the molecular level, we analysed publicly available hippocampal transcriptomic data from individuals with TLE-HS. Our analyses identified three transcriptomically defined putative endotypes within this shared neuropathological diagnosis. These states were associated with distinct molecular programs, including a neuronal/synaptic signalling-dominant profile, an immune- and glia-associated inflammatory state marked by cytokine and complement pathway activity, and a metabolically shifted state characterised by oxidative phosphorylation, reactive oxygen species signalling, and stress-response pathways. Cell-type-associated transcriptional signatures analysis and co-expression network organisation further characterised these transcriptomic endotypes, indicating that glial activation, inflammatory signalling, and mitochondrial/metabolic remodelling are differentially weighted across TLE-HS rather than uniformly present. These findings suggest that TLE-HS comprises partially distinct molecular contexts that may converge on a common histopathological endpoint. By characterising transcriptomically defined states within TLE-HS, this study highlights molecular heterogeneity within a shared histopathological diagnosis.

items.title: Parent-child discrepancies in health-related quality of life in pediatric celiac disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: To evaluate differences in health-related quality of life (HRQoL) between child self-reports and parent-proxy assessments in children and adolescents with celiac disease (CeD) using the CeD Dutch Questionnaire (CDDUX), and to describe disease-specific HRQoL patterns across the included populations. A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. Studies assessing HRQoL in pediatric CeD using the CDDUX questionnaire were identified through PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, and Cochrane Library databases. Pooled analyses were performed using random-effects models and expressed as ratios of means (RoM). Twenty-one studies from 14 countries, including 2,453 children with CeD and 2,257 parents, were included. Children consistently reported better HRQoL than perceived by their parents, with self-reported scores 7% higher overall. Differences were observed across all domains, particularly for "Diet". Overall, CDDUX scores indicated neutral HRQoL. Across studies, domain scores followed a consistent hierarchical pattern, with "Having CD" showing the lowest scores and "Communication" the highest. Marked geographic differences emerged, with the highest HRQoL scores reported in South America and the lowest in the Middle East and North Africa. Children with CeD reported higher HRQoL than their parents perceived, although the clinical importance of the pooled difference remains uncertain. The emotional burden of living with CeD represents the most affected dimension of HRQoL, while communication-related aspects are relatively preserved. Geographic variation emerged, however should be interpreted cautiously because comparability across language versions and cultural settings was not established. • Generic health-related quality of life questionnaires may underestimate the psychosocial burden associated with celiac disease; parent and child perceptions of disease burden frequently differ. • Parents consistently report lower health-related quality of life scores than children themselves, particularly in the "Diet" domain, while the"Having celiac disease" domain represents the greatest psychosocial burden worldwide.

items.title: Bioactivity profiling of linear venom peptides from Italian small wood-scorpion (Euscorpius italicus).
items.abstract: Background Rising host-expansion and the global spread of pest insects, confront agricultural sectors with substantial concerns. A promising source of potential lead compounds to target these growing challenges are animal venoms which abound with a huge diversity of bioactive peptides suited for both pest control and drug discovery. Arachnids in particular contribute substantially to the extreme diversity of highly adapted venom compounds, and for some of these, translational potential in pest control has already been demonstrated. Members of the Euscorpiidae family of scorpions are among the most successful groups of scorpions in Europe. Although they use their venom for hunting, none of their toxins has thus far been functionally evaluated as their low toxicity to humans has kept them out of the spotlight of venom research. We hypothesize that their venom peptides exert insecticidal activity which might be harnessed for pest control applications. Results Based on our hypothesis, we conducted bioactivity profiling of linear venom peptides derived from Euscorpius italicus, one of the most common euscorpiid species. In silico analyses revealed them as neutral to cationaic alpha helical peptides with high hydrophobicity. Functionally, our established profiling pipeline that combines in vivo and in vitro bioassays, reveals that one of the tested linear venom peptides, Ei1, causes mortality in Drosophila suzukii postinjection, as well as signs of neuroparalysis. Furthermore, Ei1 exhibits inhibitory effects on Staphylococcus aureus, while also affecting MDCK II cells and equine erythrocytes, implying functions in host defense. Conclusion This study reveals insights on properties of Euscorpiidae venom, their ecological values for predation and defensive function against microbial colonization of the venom glands - revealing further knowledge to the growing biodiscovery of animal venoms and potential agricultural functions as a biological insecticide. © 2026 The Author(s). items.title: Metagenomic detection and characterization of RNA viruses associated with Rhipicephalus linnaei (Audouin, 1826) ticks from the Amazon, Pará, Brazil.
items.abstract: In recent years, tick-borne viruses (TBVs) have gained significant prominence in public and veterinary health due to reports of fatal cases associated with vertebrates and the identification of a wide diversity of viruses in ixodid ticks through molecular techniques, particularly high-throughput sequencing. This study aims to investigate RNA viruses in Rhipicephalus linnaei ticks from two distinct regions of the state of Pará, in the Amazon, using a metagenomic approach. Specimens of Rhipicephalus linnaei were confirmed based on the COXI gene of their mitochondrial genome. We report the first record of Brown dog tick mivirus 1 (Mivirus rhipicephali; Family Chuviridae) and Brown dog tick phlebovirus 2 (Uukuvirus tobagoense; Family Phenuiviridae) in Brazil, as well as partial fragments of Uukuvirus tobagoense, Castanhal tick orthomyxovirus (Family Orthomyxoviridae), Guangdong tick quaranjavirus (Family Orthomyxoviridae), Alpharicinrhavirus taishun (Family Rhabdoviridae) and Zhangye Rhabd tick virus 1 (Family Rhabdoviridae). This research identified viruses with potential relevance to public and animal health and expands knowledge about the geographic distribution of viruses in tick populations, especially species of vector importance. In this context, studies on ixodid populations are essential to elucidate viral ecology, identify potential emerging agents and assess risks to public and animal health, contributing to the improvement of disease surveillance and prevention strategies.

items.title: Carbon flow to generalist predators shifts between plant- and fungal-derived resources in highly seasonal ecosystems.
items.abstract: Animals influence biogeochemical processes by consuming other organisms, transferring energy from basal resources up the food chain. Energy is routed through plant, fungal and bacterial channels, and the relative importance of these pathways can shift across space and time. Variation in these pathways may be particularly pronounced in highly seasonal environments where resource availability fluctuates throughout the year. Spatiotemporal variation in the transfer of plant- versus microbial-derived energy to higher trophic levels is poorly understood but can affect bottom-up and top-down processes. For example, seasonal shifts in herbivore versus microbivore availability (bottom-up) may alter prey choice by generalist-feeding predators and lead to changes in top-down predator control on primary production and decomposition. We tested how spatiotemporal variation in primary production influences the use of different energy channels by a widely distributed generalist invertebrate predator in the Arctic tundra. We sampled wolf spiders across four sites spanning a productivity gradient in the Alaskan Arctic during peak summer and on a weekly basis at one focal site throughout the growing season. Using essential amino acid (EAA) carbon isotope (δ 13 C) fingerprinting, we traced the flow of plant-, bacterial- and fungal-derived EAAs to spiders and quantified the use of plant- versus microbe-based energy channels between sites and across summer. Wolf spiders were associated with more plant- and less fungal-derived carbon assimilation when larger or collected from sites with higher normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI). Across the growing season, spiders shifted from primarily assimilating fungal-based resources in early summer to plant-derived resources in late summer, aligning with seasonal increases in NDVI. These patterns demonstrate spatiotemporal variation in carbon flow through different energy channels and suggest subsequent top-down predator effects may also vary with basal resource availability. Our findings also suggest wolf spider body size may predict whether predation indirectly influences primary production or decomposition. As climate change alters seasonality, resource dynamics and invertebrate body sizes, these insights provide a basis for predicting spatiotemporal variation in predator impacts on ecosystem processes. Finally, our work demonstrates the utility of compound-specific stable isotope analysis for integrating ecological and biogeochemical theory through the conceptual lens of zoogeochemistry.

items.title: Blood, ink, and flies: A case report on the house fly (Musca domestica) feeding on active tattooing wounds.
items.abstract: Cases of adventitious feeding on humans by non-hematophagous insects hold significant medical relevance, yet their occurrence during active body art procedures remains undocumented. This case report describes a persistent instance of opportunistic exsudatophagy by the house fly, Musca domestica Linnaeus, 1758 (Diptera: Muscidae), during a tattooing session on a healthy 32-year-old male client in Germany. Over a four-hour timeframe, four adult house flies entered the ground-floor studio through doors and windows opened for summer cross-ventilation. The insects exhibited highly persistent landing and feeding attempts directly on the freshly wounded tissue of the right lower leg, actively drinking a matrix of blood, plasma, and tattoo ink. Attraction intensified significantly once large-scale shading expanded the exuding epidermal surface area. Effective mechanical repulsion was heavily restricted by the client's enforced immobility required to ensure precise tattoo application. Following a routine aftercare protocol, the lesion healed completely without secondary bacterial infection. This report highlights a neglected hygienic hazard where the saprophagous and coprophilic ecology of synanthropic filth flies poses a mechanical vector risk for dermal pathogen inoculation, emphasizing the necessity of simple vector control strategies in tattooing facilities.

items.title: Plant-based meat alternatives can support reductions in agricultural land expansion and greenhouse gas emissions but entail micronutrient trade-offs.
items.abstract: Plant-based meat alternatives (PBMAs), designed to mimic the sensory properties of meat, may help reduce animal-sourced protein consumption and support a shift towards plant-based diets. Here we integrated PBMAs into a land-use model to assess their effects on nutrition, greenhouse gas emissions and food system sustainability. PBMA adoption not only substantially reduced agricultural land expansion and greenhouse gas emissions from the agriculture, forestry and other land use sector but also increased risks of micronutrient inadequacy. Across regions, PBMA diets exhibited diminishing marginal returns. Replacing ruminant meat alone achieved nearly half of the potential emission reductions while incurring relatively small nutritional costs. By contrast, broader substitution of livestock products delivered additional environmental benefits but markedly increased micronutrient deficiencies. Targeted policy support, sustainable land management and improved PBMA formulations will be essential to ensure equitable dietary transitions and progress towards global climate and sustainability goals.

items.title: Soil viruses as key regulators of the microbial carbon pump in deep soils.
items.abstract: Deep soils store over half of terrestrial organic carbon, yet the viral mechanisms governing carbon persistence in subsurface contexts remain unclear. Here, by conducting a soil profile survey (0-700 cm) across four agroecosystems and a global synthesis of subsurface metagenomes, we established the Deep Soil Viral Resources Database, comprising 50,949 viral operational taxonomic units and 3,902 auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs). Viral richness increased significantly with depth, accompanied by a shift towards lysogeny driven by declining carbon availability. The deep-soil virome carried AMGs and lysozymes involved in polymer degradation and cell endolysis. Viral endolysin significantly promoted necromass carbon accumulation, which contributed to increases in mineral-associated organic carbon. A synthesis of 138 global soil profiles further revealed a positive effect of viral abundance on soil organic carbon. Our findings establish a framework where viruses strengthen the microbial carbon pump in deep soils by facilitating host carbon scavenging via AMGs and promoting necromass formation via endolysin activity.

items.title: Drift, selection and recombination bias drive the evolution of a non-ribosomal peptide.
items.abstract: Non-ribosomal peptides play important roles in microbial ecology and medicine, for example as toxins and antibiotics such as penicillin. Like ordinary proteins, non-ribosomal peptides are subject to evolutionary change, which is driven by rampant recombinations of their synthetases. The evolutionary dynamics and causes of non-ribosomal peptide diversification are not well understood, because recombinations complicate phylogenetic analysis and statistical tests for natural selection and drift. Here we study the non-ribosomal GameXPeptides, which entomopathogenic bacteria use to kill their insect prey. We use recombination-aware phylogenetics, ancestral sequence reconstruction and statistical analysis of historical recombination patterns to retrace the evolution of GameXPeptides. This uncovers dozens of new GameXPeptides, including striking patterns of structural convergence. We provide statistical and experimental evidence that this diversity is shaped by selection, but also that GameXPeptides experience substantial genetic drift and biased recombination rates that limit the space of accessible peptide variants. Our work illuminates the complex interplay of adaptive and non-adaptive evolutionary forces acting on some of the most versatile chemical weapons in nature.

items.title: A rare deletion of IhUF3GT1 in the Ivy-leaf morning glory eliminates anthocyanin-based pigmentation.
items.abstract: Anthocyanin biosynthesis is a highly branched network with upstream mutations leading to the loss of many other branches beyond just anthocyanins like flavonols, isoflavonoids, and proanthocyanidins. Consequently, disentangling the specific effects of anthocyanins on plant fitness from those of other branches is difficult unless a mutant impacting the terminal step of anthocyanin biosynthesis can be found. We discovered an Ipomoea hederacea plant (Ivy-leaf morning glory) lacking anthocyanins due to a genetic deletion in the terminal step of the anthocyanin biosynthetic pathway. Anthocyanin loss follows a recessive, Mendelian inheritance pattern. Anthocyanin loss is perfectly correlated with a lack of expression of the anthocyanin biosynthesis gene IhUF3GT1 (anthocyanidin-3-O-glucosyltransferase). IhUF3GT1 is the gene most strongly and consistently differentially expressed between unpigmented and pigmented flowers in F 2 siblings. A deletion of half of the IhUF3GT1 gene, which includes the start codon is the genetic basis underlying a loss of IhUF3GT1 expression and, consequently, anthocyanins in unpigmented plants. The IhUF3GT1 deletion is rare and unique to the unpigmented line. Genome coverage analyses demonstrate that no other pigmented I. hederacea line (of 123 screened) has a loss-of-function mutation in IhUF3GT1. Furthermore, we confirm cosegregation of the IhUF3GT1 deletion with the unpigmented phenotype in F 3 progeny from a cross where all unpigmented plants are homozygous for the IhUF3GT1 deletion. Taken together, we describe the genetic basis of a novel unpigmented mutant in I. hederacea, creating a potentially important model for studying the fitness effects of anthocyanin loss.

items.title: Amazon carbon emissions driven by human actions amplified by droughts.
items.abstract: The Amazon carbon sink is weakening as deforestation 1-5 , rising tree mortality 6-8 and climate change disrupt the climatic conditions that sustain a humid tropical forest 9-11 . Forest loss reduces precipitation, increases temperatures and lengthens the dry season, driving higher carbon emissions 1-4,11,12 . Climate stress is stronger in more deforested regions, rendering forests progressively more flammable 1,9,13 . Large-scale climate events, such as El Niño, further amplify regional climate impacts 9,14-17 . Here we present an analysis of 15 years of Amazonian carbon fluxes derived from atmospheric CO 2 measurements. We determine a carbon balance of 0.32 ± 0.08 PgC yr -1 , with fires acting as the dominant source (0.40 ± 0.07 PgC yr -1 ) and forest uptake becoming increasingly unable to offset emissions. Furthermore, we investigate key drivers of the carbon emissions of Amazonia and identify three distinct year groups. Group 1 (2011-2014, 2017 and 2018) represents the role of the Amazon in the global carbon balance (0.11 ± 0.08 PgC yr -1 ) during wetter years with low human activity, such as deforestation, biomass burning and degradation. Group 2 (2019-2022) represents Amazon carbon emissions (0.43 ± 0.13 PgC yr -1 ) from human activities (mainly deforestation and degradation) during years with low climatic stress. Group 3 (2010, 2015, 2016, 2023 and 2024) has the highest carbon emissions (0.49 ± 0.07 PgC yr -1 ) and comprises warm and dry years (high climate stress), such as El Niño and the warming of the Tropical North Atlantic Ocean, associated with biomass burning.

items.title: Parasites in the meta-ecosystem landscape: hidden connectors and disruptors.
items.abstract: The meta-ecosystem framework explains spatial flows of organisms, materials, and energy across ecosystem boundaries. Parasites play crucial roles in these processes, yet they remain absent from meta-ecosystem models. Using examples from terrestrial and aquatic environments, we illustrate how parasitic organisms act as central connectors or disruptors of the flow of organisms, nutrients, and energy across ecosystem boundaries via four key mechanisms: parasite-induced host movement, behavioural changes that increase cross-ecosystem predation, host mortality, and parasite avoidance behaviour. These examples highlight the central role of parasites in driving and regulating nutrient and energy flow from catchment-to-coast, and we outline a pathway for improved integration of these parasite-mediated processes into the meta-ecosystem framework.

items.title: Microbial resistance from genotype to metabolic phenotype.
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses an escalating global threat, yet surveillance and mechanistic understanding remain anchored in individual resistance genes, an approach that is inadequate for capturing the ecological, genomic, and metabolic complexity through which resistance emerges and spreads. In this opinion article, we argue that genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) offer a principled framework for advancing AMR research beyond this gene-centric paradigm. Strain-resolved GEMs embed resistance determinants within metabolic networks, with the potential to generate quantitative, context-dependent phenotypic predictions, including minimum inhibitory concentrations and environment-conditional resistance, that sequence-based tools do not provide. Expanded GEM frameworks incorporating mobile genetic elements, horizontal gene transfer, and community-level interactions support ecology-aware resistance profiling. At the therapeutic level, whole-network modelling can identify metabolic vulnerabilities, synthetic lethal interactions, and microbiome-targeted strategies. Integrating GEMs with multiomics and data-driven approaches represents a critical step toward a mechanism-aware AMR platform connecting surveillance, diagnosis, and drug discovery.

items.title: Effect of visual and electrosensory deterrents on captive elasmobranchs.
items.abstract: Commercial gillnet fisheries interact with a wide range of elasmobranch species, many of which are incidentally captured as bycatch. Deterrent technologies have emerged as a potential approach for reducing interactions with threatened elasmobranchs. In this exploratory study, captive Giant Shovelnose Rays (Glaucostegus typus) and Brownbanded Bamboo Sharks (Chiloscyllium punctatum) were exposed to a static green LED light and a pulsed electrosensory deterrent attached to an experimental gillnet. The light deterrent initially reduced interactions by Giant Shovelnose Rays; however, this response diminished over time. Over a 10-min period, deterred Giant Shovelnose Rays showed a significantly greater distance of deterrence in both treatments compared to the control. There was also a significant difference in mean eye distance between the control and light treatments, but not in nose distance. In contrast, Brownbanded Bamboo Sharks exhibited no significant response to either deterrent. These contrasting responses may reflect differences in the sensory ecology of the two species, underscoring the importance of species-specific considerations in developing elasmobranch bycatch mitigation technologies. Given the promising outcomes reported for these deterrents in other studies, and the apparent variability in responses among elasmobranch taxa, further evaluation across a broader range of bycatch species is warranted.

items.title: A hypothesis-generating study of collateral reactivation: a reanalysis of Mycobacterium tuberculosis genomes from 119 recurrent tuberculosis cases.
items.abstract: Recurrent tuberculosis is traditionally classified as exogenous reinfection or endogenous reactivation. We previously proposed "collateral reactivation," in which distinct Mycobacterium tuberculosis subclones derived from a hypothetical original clone are involved in separate disease episodes, in contrast to traditional endogenous ("direct-descent") reactivation. To explore whether collateral reactivation occurs beyond the single case we previously reported, we reanalyzed publicly available whole-genome sequencing data from 123 recurrent tuberculosis cases. After curation, 119 cases (pairwise single-nucleotide variant [SNV] distance, 0-18) were classified as cases of collateral or direct-descent reactivation. In 21 cases (17.6%), a hypothetical original clone could be inferred, and these cases were classified as collateral reactivation. These cases showed a higher rate of SNVs/genome/year (median 3 vs. 0.4, p < 0.0001) and a higher proportion of drug resistance-associated SNVs (23.8% vs. 4.1%, p = 0.009) than direct-descent reactivation cases. These observations support the view that collateral reactivation is not restricted to the single case we previously reported, although mixed infection or exogenous reinfection caused by closely related strains cannot be excluded as alternative explanations. To determine whether collateral reactivation should be recognized as a concept distinct from direct-descent reactivation, future studies integrating whole-genome sequencing of single colonies, lesion-specific sampling, longitudinal sampling, deep sequencing, imaging, clinical follow-up, and epidemiological exposure information will be required.

items.title: Cucurbitacins as multitarget pharmacological modulators: chemistry, biosynthesis, molecular targets, regulated cell death, and translational challenges, with emphasis on cucurbitacin B and I.
items.abstract: Cucurbitacins are highly oxidized tetracyclic triterpenoids with context-dependent pharmacological effects. This review focuses primarily on cucurbitacin B (CuB) and cucurbitacin I (CuI)-the most extensively characterized family members-while surveying the wider structural diversity of the cucurbitacin family. We integrate their chemistry, biosynthesis, and structure-activity relationships with structural interpretations of molecular target engagement and translational feasibility. We highlight how the electrophilic α,β-unsaturated ketone, C-17 side chain, acetylation, and glycosylation may influence potency and selectivity. Mechanistically, we evaluate Janus kinase 2/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 signaling, ferroptosis involving solute carrier family 7 member 11 and glutathione peroxidase 4, PTEN-induced kinase 1-Parkin-dependent mitophagy, allosteric modulation of insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA-binding protein 1, and NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3 inflammasome inhibition. We consider anti-inflammatory and hepatoprotective effects, tumor-associated macrophage repolarization, and sensitization to immune checkpoint blockade. Experimentally determined protein structures inform proposed covalent and allosteric interactions, but these models require direct target validation and biomarkers. We distinguish compound-specific findings from family-wide interpretations. Effects may vary with compound, dose, and disease context. By connecting these pathways to wax gourd genomic resources and synthetic-biology approaches, we consider opportunities for sustainable cucurbitacin production. However, low aqueous solubility, rapid clearance, hepatotoxicity, and a narrow therapeutic index constrain clinical translation. We assess nanoparticle formulations, solid dispersions, and structure-guided analog development as possible solutions. Distinct from cucurbitacin B-centered reviews, this synthesis integrates structural pharmacology, regulated cell death, immunomodulation, and biosynthetic engineering within a research roadmap prioritizing target validation, biomarkers, and preclinical assessment.

items.title: Revisiting the Obesogenic Potential of Legacy Pollutants: Epidemiological, Toxicogenomic, and Benchmark Dose-Based Evidence.
items.abstract: Legacy pollutants remain detectable in human populations despite decades of regulatory control, yet whether they continue to pose biologically relevant health risks under contemporary exposure scenarios remains unclear. Here we integrated epidemiology, toxicogenomics, and benchmark dose (BMD)-based risk assessment to re-evaluate the obesogenic potential of legacy pollutants in 665 adolescents. Among 97 quantified environmental chemicals in serum samples, hexachlorobenzene (HCB) and pentachlorophenol (PCP) were consistently identified as the principal contributors to overweight/obesity by generalized linear and weighted quantile sum models. Toxicogenomics, molecular docking, and adverse outcome pathway analyses indicate that both chemicals converge on endocrine and metabolic disruption and oxidative stress through key regulators including PPARγ, INS, ESR1, TNF, and TP53. In vitro validation confirmed dose-dependent perturbations of obesity-related biomarkers, yielding biologically relevant points of departure through BMD modeling. Margin-of-exposure (MOE) analysis integrating these thresholds with human biomonitoring data revealed generally moderate-to-low risk for HCB, whereas approximately 4% of participants exhibited high-risk PCP exposure. These findings demonstrate that certain legacy pollutants remain biologically active and risk-relevant despite long-term regulation and highlight the value of integrating epidemiological evidence with mechanistic and quantitative toxicology for prioritizing chemicals of public health concern in the exposome era.

items.title: Laminin-α2 deficiency is associated with altered multiorgan redox signatures.
items.abstract: Muscle diseases often involve redox imbalance, driven by elevated ROS levels, impaired antioxidant defenses, mitochondrial dysfunction, and metabolic rewiring. In several muscular dystrophies caused by extracellular matrix gene mutations, increased oxidative stress in skeletal muscle is a defining feature. One such condition is LAMA2-congenital muscular dystrophy (LAMA2-CMD), resulting from mutations in LAMA2, which encodes the laminin-α2 chain. Although oxidative stress has been implicated in the muscle pathology in LAMA2-CMD, whether this effect extends beyond skeletal muscle remains unclear. Here, we used the dy W mouse model for LAMA2-CMD, which exhibits well-established muscle defects beginning at fetal stages, to investigate whether pathology is also present in other organs at disease onset. We found that Lama2-deficiency alters antioxidant responses in the fetal heart, kidney, and liver, with all three organs displaying increased NRF2 protein levels accompanied by organ-specific changes in selected NRF2 target genes. This phenotype is associated with alterations in mitochondrial markers in the kidney, not evident in the heart or the liver. To further understand the kidney phenotype, we isolated Lama2-deficient proximal tubule epithelial cells from fetal kidneys, which displayed defects in proliferation and mitochondrial metabolism in vitro, indicating a cell-autonomous effect. However, alterations in the NRF2 pathway were not detected, suggesting that its regulation may depend on the in vivo tissue context. Overall, this study provides the first evidence supporting a multi-organ involvement in laminin-α2 chain deficiency from the earliest stages of disease, extending the known phenotype beyond skeletal muscle. It further underscores the importance of laminin-α2 chain in maintaining tissue homeostasis and redox balance, offering new insights into systemic aspects of LAMA2-CMD.

items.title: Cold-season grazing better sustains ecosystem multifunctionality than warm-season grazing in Tibetan alpine steppe.
items.abstract: Grazing season profoundly shapes vegetation and soil properties in alpine grasslands, yet its effects on ecosystem multifunctionality (EMF) remain poorly understood. Here, we compared grazing exclusion (GE), moderate-intensity warm-season grazing (WG), and herder-managed cold-season grazing (CG) in a cold-season pasture of the alpine steppe on the Tibetan Plateau to evaluate how seasonal grazing influences species diversity, community biomass, soil physicochemical properties, and EMF. Relative to GE, WG reduced grass dominance but increased sedge and forb proportion, while also decreasing plant height and aboveground biomass (AGB), and lowered EMF. By contrast, CG was associated with higher plant diversity and significantly elevated soil total carbon (TC) while maintaining AGB at levels comparable to GE. Effect-size analysis showed that WG significantly reduced EMF relative to GE whereas the reduction under CG did not reach significance. Correlation and path analyses further indicated that, under WG, multifunctionality was chiefly associated with the biomass pathway, which was positive but insufficient to counterbalance the direct negative effect of grazing, whereas no significant plant diversity or soil nutrient pathway was detected. Under CG, EMF was jointly associated with plant biomass, plant diversity and soil nutrients. These findings highlight the critical role of grazing season in maintaining ecosystem multifunctionality in alpine steppe, suggesting that, in cold-season pastures of the central Tibetan Plateau, cold-season grazing represents a more sustainable strategy than warm-season grazing for balancing forage production and ecological conservation.

items.title: Occurrence of lipophilic marine algal toxins in surface sediments from representative polar seas and implications for toxigenic microalgae.
items.abstract: Phytotoxins produced by harmful algal blooms threaten marine organisms and human health, yet research on algal toxins in polar marine system remains extremely limited. In this study, liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry was used to systematically characterize the composition, concentration, spatial distribution, and potential sources of lipophilic marine algal toxins (LMATs) in surface sediments from Antarctic Prydz Bay and the Arctic Bering-Chukchi Seas. Only low levels of pectenotoxin-2 (PTX2) were detected in Prydz Bay sediments (mean ± SD: 6.649 ± 3.669 ng/kg; n = 8), providing evidence of sedimentary PTX2 occurrence. In contrast, eleven LMATs were detected in sediments from the Bering-Chukchi Seas, reflecting markedly higher LMAT chemical diversity. Notably, azaspiracids, PTX2-SA, and gymnodimine were recorded for the first time in this Arctic region. The mean ± SD concentration of ΣLMATs was 6313 ± 2842 ng/kg (n = 10), dominated by yessotoxin (YTX) and okadaic acid. ΣLMATs displayed pronounced spatial heterogeneity, with elevated levels concentrated in the southwestern portion of the study region near the Chukchi Peninsula, whereas the Bering Strait region showed low concentrations. Considering the observed LMAT diversity, documented YTX-producing taxa in the northwestern Pacific, and high-latitude records of Dinophysis and Azadinium/Amphidoma, the sedimentary LMAT assemblage may reflect contributions from multiple toxigenic microalgal sources. Because the vastness and harsh environmental conditions of polar oceans make comprehensive mapping of toxigenic microalgae difficult, sediment-derived LMATs provide baseline evidence of LMAT occurrence in high-latitude polar environments.

items.title: Review on algae-derived biopolymers to remove radionuclides from aquatic systems: sorption mechanisms, kinetics and stability.
items.abstract: The carboxyl, sulfate, phosphate and hydroxyl groups on algal biomass and its polysaccharides bind uranium, caesium, strontium and radium. The reported uranium capacities for brown macroalgae vary greatly depending on pH and pretreatment, ranging from roughly 150 to 560 mg/g. Green macroalgae and immobilized microalgae report much smaller uranium capacities, typically in the range of 75-290 mg/g. Certain microalgae remove 88-95% of dissolved 137 Cs within 48 h. However, these values mostly stem from acidic, single-solute batch experiments. When the same material is used to test actual effluents, removal rates drop, often dramatically. This review evaluates algae as a feedstock for functional polymers, combines capture mechanisms with the aqueous chemistry that governs them, and re-evaluates how isotherm, kinetic, and thermodynamic models are interpreted. The review then compares the quantitative and qualitative data regarding engineered hydrogels and composites, including their stability, regeneration, and response to competition from other ions. Finally, the loaded sorbent is viewed as secondary radioactive waste, and column operation, life-cycle burden, and traditional alternative options are placed within this context. Maximum capacity is less important than selectivity in real water and safe end-of-life management as critical evaluation criteria.

items.title: Phospholipid analogs and beyond: pleiotropic roles of betaine lipids in phycology, ecology, and biomedicine.
items.abstract: Betaine lipids (BLs) are a class of non-phosphorus glycerolipids widely found in microalgae, fungi, bacteria, mosses, and ferns. For decades, the central paradigm regarding the biological function of BLs has been their role in substituting for phospholipids under phosphate starvation-a crucial adaptive mechanism for survival in oligotrophic environments. However, accumulating evidence indicates that the functional diversity of BLs is far more extensive. Recent studies have demonstrated their distinct roles in fatty acid metabolism, adaptation to various environmental stresses, and ecological interactions such as symbiosis and predation. This review summarizes current insights into the pleiotropic roles of BLs in microalgal physiology and ecology, moving beyond their role as mere phospholipid surrogates. Furthermore, we highlight the recently discovered bioactive function of BL derivative in mammals.

items.title: A Qualitative Pragmatic Evaluation of Statewide Efforts to Promote Digital Access for Migrant and Seasonal Farmworkers in North Carolina.
items.abstract: Objectives Migrant and seasonal farmworkers face barriers to internet access, which impacts health. We sought to draw lessons and practitioner experiences from three digital accessibility programs for farmworkers in North Carolina (NC): (1) a project that provided technology and training to farmworker-serving community health workers and tablets to students from farmworker families; (2) a project that provided laptops to children of farmworkers; and (3) a state health department emergency pandemic response that provided internet access to farmworkers and community health workers. Methods We conducted 52 in-person, virtual, or phone interviews in English or Spanish with migrant and seasonal farmworkers ( n = 29), farmworker service providers ( n = 21), and employers or farm owners/managers ( n = 2) between August 2020 and February 2022. A team of four analysts used deductive and inductive thematic coding in NVivo 12. Results Our findings were captured in four themes: (1) pre-project challenges regarding internet accessibility and quality as well as access to technology and resources; (2) project-related experiences including recruitment, trainings, resources, and challenges; (3) benefits of the projects, including improved access to care and health information, communication, and self-efficacy; and (4) recommendations for training, resources, and relationship building, as well as persisting challenges. Conclusion Based on these findings, interventions to promote digital accessibility through internet access and education can benefit the health of farmworkers. Future program planners should consider lessons learned across three real-world implementation efforts in NC, addressing participants' recommendations for pairing training with internet access and seeking sustainable options for internet access through partnerships.

items.title: Diapause in Forest Insects: From Eco-Physiological Adaptations to Management Applications.
items.abstract: Forest insects worldwide face changing environments within a given year and across multiple years. Therefore, insects must match their life cycles with critical resources to maximize fitness and survival. A key strategy for life-cycle synchronization is entry into a special form of dormancy, called diapause. Diapause affects multiple life-history traits, including development, reproduction, movement, stress resistance, and energy storage. This review provides an overview and discussion of diapause expression for forest insects, focusing on ecologically and economically relevant plant-feeding species and highlighting specific, diapause-related features of forests. Diapause regulation and expression are highly variable across species and mainly help overcome unfavorable periods, synchronize life cycles with host trees and predators, and respond to scarce or irregular resources. Changing climatic conditions have direct and indirect effects on forest insect diapause, including temperature stress, energetic stress, and phenological mismatches. Knowledge of diapause regulation is essential for practical forestry to coordinate and evaluate management measures.

items.title: Contrasting resistance and recovery of co-occurring conifers to larch caterpillar defoliation in a Northeast China temperate forest.
items.abstract: Climate change has been linked to the intensification of forest pest outbreaks, posing a serious threat to non-coevolved tree species because of their potentially weak defensive capabilities. However, unlike broad-scale climatic disturbances such as drought and heatwaves, insect outbreaks are highly heterogeneous in space and among host species, and the response of occurring conifers to such outbreaks remains poorly understood. The core area of the Changbai Mountain Nature Reserve in northeastern China was severely defoliated in 2019 by larch caterpillars (Dendrolimus superans Butler)-a conifer-feeding defoliator that prefers larch but also attacks other conifers. In this region, a vegetation transition zone between the broadleaf-Korean pine and spruce-fir forests hosts multiple conifer species co-existing within short distances under similar defoliation intensities. We monitored 1,837 trees in 2019 (pre-disturbance), 2021 and 2024, and sampled needles of healthy individuals of each species in 2024 to obtain species-level proxies of intrinsic foliar traits. Results revealed that: (i) mortality of attacked Korean pine peaked within 2 years, with little subsequent increase, resulting in a cumulative mortality rate of 31.3%; in contrast, mortality of spruce and fir continued to increase until the fifth year, reaching a combined cumulative rate of 78.6%, while larch exhibited nearly 100% survival. (ii) a deciduous habit, low needle biomass allocation and low carbohydrate concentrations enhanced survival by reducing canopy regeneration costs. (iii) regarding radial growth responses, spruce showed stronger compensatory growth but weaker recovery ability than fir and Korean pine, likely due to its limited carbon and nutrient reserves. Considering these findings, prioritizing the protection of non-coevolved conifers is recommended to minimize biomass loss during pest outbreaks. This study also provides important insights for temperate and boreal conifer forest conservation, highlighting the high vulnerability of spruce-fir forests to larch caterpillar outbreaks.

items.title: Accessing invasion-competent Plasmodium vivax merozoites reveals antibody-dependent NK cell activation.
items.abstract: Malaria pathogenesis and clinical symptoms arise from blood-stage replication of Plasmodium parasites, which depends on rapid invasion of red blood cells by merozoites. Despite the central importance of this stage, direct functional studies of Plasmodium vivax ( P. vivax ) merozoites remain limited by the lack of continuous in vitro culture and restricted access to viable, invasion-competent merozoites from clinical isolates. Consequently, key aspects of P. vivax merozoite biology and immune recognition remain poorly defined. Here, we establish a robust platform enabling synchronized release and high-yield isolation of invasion-competent P. vivax merozoites from ex vivo cultures. Reversible inhibition of parasite egress using the PKG inhibitor ML10 enables synchronization at the segmented schizont stage, followed by rapid mechanical release of merozoites using a liposome-based extrusion approach. This workflow yields highly pure merozoites with recovery rates exceeding 75% while preserving structural integrity and invasive capacity. Leveraging this platform, we demonstrate that antibody-opsonized P. vivax merozoites activate human natural killer cells, revealing functional antibody-dependent immune responses.

items.title: The Pathomycosphere: A Spatially Defined Framework in Pathogen Ecology.
items.abstract: Fungal pathogens have historically been studied as autonomous agents, as self-contained units independent of their associated microbiota, with disease outcomes attributed to fungal virulence factors acting on susceptible hosts. However, many pathogenic fungi harbor bacterial associates that influence their ecology, persistence and virulence. The pathobiome concept addressed this limitation by framing disease as an outcome of multi-kingdom interactions. Yet most pathobiome studies rely on correlative analyses of microbial abundances with pathogens, lacking spatial resolution to identify which microorganisms physically interact with pathogenic structures. Conversely, the hyphosphere provides micrometer-scale spatial resolution but has been investigated predominantly in non-pathogenic fungi. Here, we propose the pathomycosphere as a spatially defined and experimentally tractable subset of the pathobiome: a hypha-associated microbial assemblage in which physical association with the pathogenic member, prolonged or transient has a consequence for the pathogen's biology, with pathogenicity residing in the fungus, an associated microorganism or their interaction. This framework bridges the pathobiome and hyphosphere concepts by anchoring disease-associated microbial interactions to hyphal interface, where mechanistic investigation becomes feasible. Pathomycosphere provides operational tractability to explore microbial partnerships contributing to pathogenesis, and positions fungal-associated bacterial consortia as important components of pathogen biology with relevance to disease ecology beyond agricultural systems.
