items.title: Perinatal health outcomes in relation to principal applicant and live-in caregiver status among economic class immigrants to Canada: A retrospective analysis of births from 1993 to 2017.
items.abstract: Objectives Economic class immigrants to Canada tend to have better health outcomes than other immigrant groups. However, variation may exist even within this population. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of data from the Migrant Maternal and Infant Morbidity and Mortality (MMIMM) dataset, which linked Canadian birth and infant death records (1993-2017) with maternal immigration records (1952-2017). All singleton births to economic class immigrant women at least 18 years of age at immigration were analyzed. Women were classified as principal applicants (PA), non-principal applicants (NPA), or former live-in caregivers (LIC); all analyses were stratified by marital status at landing. Outcomes examined included preterm birth (PTB), small- and large-for-gestational-age birth (SGA and LGA, respectively), stillbirth, and infant mortality. Risk ratios for adverse outcomes by PA and former LIC status were estimated with adjustment for parental, birth, and immigration characteristics. Results The cohort included 490,310 births (165,850 births to PAs, 267,200 to NPAs, 57,160 to former LICs). In adjusted analyses, among women who were single at landing, NPA had slightly lower rates of LGA (fully adjusted risk ratio (aRR) = 0.92, 95% CI 0.87-0.98) and stillbirth (aRR = 0.72, 95% CI 0.53-0.97) compared to PA, and former LICs had slightly elevated rates of PTB (aRR 1.05, 95% CI 1.00-1.11) and SGA (1.05, 95% CI 1.01-1.10). Conclusion These findings add to existing literature highlighting the vulnerability of live-in caregivers in Canada while shedding light on possible differences between principal and non-principal applicants.

items.title: Ontogenetic Variation in Plant-to-Plant Signaling Effects on Direct and Indirect Defenses in Wild Cotton (Gossypium hirsutum).
items.abstract: Various plant-related factors have been shown to influence volatile organic compound (VOC)-mediated plant-to-plant interactions, but effects of plant ontogeny have been rarely considered. Here, we tested if these interactions differ between two ontogenetic stages in wild cotton, Gossypium hirsutum. We used 2.5- and 4.5-month-old plants (seedlings and juveniles, respectively), arranged in triplets where one plant acted as an emitter and two as receivers (all plants within a cage were of the same developmental stage). Half of the emitters were subjected to herbivory by Alabama argillacea caterpillars, while the emitters of the other triplets were left unharmed. After 48 h of VOC exposure, we collected the VOCs from a subset of the emitter plants (for 2 h), and one receiver from each cage was removed to measure extrafloral nectar (EFN) production and to collect leaves for total phenolic analyses. The remaining receivers were subjected to herbivory to assess signaling effects on defense induction. Emitter seedlings released larger quantities of VOCs in response to caterpillar damage than juveniles, and ontogenetic stages also differed in the composition of the emitted VOC blend. Accordingly, we found trends for ontogenetic variation in signaling effects: seedling receivers exposed to damaged emitters tended to produce more EFN both prior to and following damage compared to those exposed to undamaged emitters, whereas juvenile receivers showed no EFN response to emitter damage. Similarly, seedling receivers exposed to damaged emitters exhibited higher phenolic concentrations, whereas no such signaling effect was observed in juveniles. These findings indicate that VOC-mediated signaling of defenses is strong in young cotton plants but weakens during development in pre-reproductive juvenile plants, and that this is reflected in both direct and indirect defense responses.

items.title: Volatile Insensitivity and Localized Alkaloids Support Commensalism in the Oxytropis sericea-Alternaria oxytropis Association.
items.abstract: The endophytic fungus Alternaria oxytropis is vertically transmitted through silky crazyweed (Oxytropis sericea Nutt.) and produces the neurotoxin swainsonine, yet its influence on host chemical signaling remains unclear. Here we characterize the floral and foliar volatile organic compound (VOC) profiles of endophyte-infected (E+) and endophyte-free (E-) O. sericea using dynamic headspace GC-MS on greenhouse- and field-grown plants - the first characterization of volatile profiles in this species. Endophyte infection had a negligible effect on VOC composition, explaining less than 1% of compositional variance in both greenhouse and field settings, with no compound differing consistently by infection status. Seven volatiles were reliably detected across both environments. The dominant axes of variation (PCA) instead reflected differences among individuals and between size-matched E+/E- plant across years. These accounted for most compositional variance (72.6% greenhouse, 64.9% field), and VOC profiles differed markedly between collection years, likely reflecting fine-scale environmental and physiological variation. Ancillary nectar assays and pollinator observations revealed no consistent differences between E + and E- plants, and seed set was unaffected regardless of endophyte status. Swainsonine in floral organs was roughly an order of magnitude lower than in leaves and near-trace in nectar, indicating that any localized chemical defense is likely decoupled from scent chemistry. Together, these findings position the Oxytropis-Alternaria association toward the commensal end of the symbiotic continuum: the fungus maintains vertical transmission while the host shows no detectable effect on volatile signaling, pollinator attraction, or reproductive output, despite the resources required to sustain fungal alkaloid biosynthesis. This system offers a tractable model for understanding how endophyte associations persist in the absence of measurable host benefit.

items.title: An integrated chemical and biomarker approach using Ucides cordatus (Crustacea; Decapoda) to assess trace element contamination and its biological impacts across two Amazonian estuaries.
items.abstract: In this study, an integrated chemical and biomarker approach was applied using the mangrove crab Ucides cordatus to assess trace element contamination and its biological impacts across two distinct Amazonian estuaries. Crabs were collected from São José Bay (A1-minimally impacted) and São Marcos Bay (A2-impacted by port activities) on the Amazon coast of Brazil. Simultaneously with crab sampling, physicochemical parameters and trace element levels in sediment and water samples were assessed. Biometric measurements included cephalothorax length and width, cheliped propodus length and width, movable finger length and width, and total weight. Two biomarkers, genotoxic responses (micronuclei) and histopathological lesions (gills and liver hepatopancreas), were measured. Abiotic parameters, such as pH, dissolved oxygen, and salinity, were similar between the two study areas (A1 and A2). However, the concentrations of trace elements (Zn, Fe, Al, and Mn) in the water were increased in A2. Biometric data revealed that crabs from A2 were significantly smaller and lighter (p < 0.05) than those from A1. Gill lesions (marginal canal deformation, pillar cell rupture, and necrosis) were frequently observed in crabs from both sites, with a higher prevalence in A2. Hepatopancreas histological alterations (e.g., necrosis) were significantly more common in crabs from A2 (p < 0.05). Genotoxic responses, such as pycnotic nuclei, were also significantly more frequent in A2 (p < 0.05). The results demonstrate that Ucides cordatus effectively reflects environmental contamination through measurable histological and genotoxic biomarkers, which is consistent with the chemical evidence of trace element pollution in estuarine environments.

items.title: Robustness of oxygen metrics to sampling frequency in a stratified lake.
items.abstract: Long-term lake monitoring often relies on monthly dissolved oxygen profiles, but the robustness of derived oxygen metrics to this temporal resolution is uncertain. We compared three years (2022-2024) of hourly sensor observations (high-frequency (HF)) with approximately monthly discrete profiles (low-frequency (LF)) from a small, dimictic subalpine lake. We evaluated volume-weighted oxygen concentrations, hypolimnetic oxygen depletion rates (ODR) and depth-specific counts of days with oxygen < 2 mg L⁻1. To isolate temporal sampling effects on ODR, we subsampled the HF daily record at 7-, 14-, 30- and 60-day intervals across all starting-day offsets within fixed annual fitting periods. LF profiles interpolated to daily resolution reproduced broad seasonal oxygen trajectories, but concentration differences persisted on matched sampling dates, particularly at 9 and 12 m. The mean within-year range width of signed ODR deviations from the full-HF reference was 8.0 percentage points at 7-day sampling, 20.5 at 14 days, 47.5 at 30 days and 48.6 at 60 days. Depth-specific low-oxygen-day counts were strongly correlated between datasets (Pearson's r = 0.933-0.977), but unequal observation coverage precluded unbiased estimates of annual duration. The results indicate that approximately monthly profiles can describe broad seasonal oxygen dynamics in this lake, whereas more frequent sampling reduces the sensitivity of ODR estimates to sampling timing.

items.title: Fungicide co-exposure influences ibuprofen accumulation, distribution and phytotoxicological responses in zucchini (Cucurbita pepo).
items.abstract: Pharmaceuticals introduced into agricultural soils through wastewater reuse and biosolids application may coexist with crop-protection products, yet the influence of fungicides on pharmaceutical uptake and phytotoxicity in crops remains poorly understood. This study investigated how benomyl, chlorothalonil, validamycin A, and probenazole affect ibuprofen (IBU) accumulation, translocation, and physiological responses in zucchini ( Cucurbita pepo cv. Soraya). IBU accumulated mainly in roots, and its distribution depended on fungicide identity. Compared with IBU alone, root accumulation was numerically higher under benomyl and significantly higher under validamycin A. Root-to-leaf translocation factors varied among treatments, but these differences were not statistically significant. These findings indicate treatment-dependent effects of fungicide co-exposure on IBU accumulation, particularly in roots, while evidence for differential root-to-leaf translocation remains inconclusive. Ibuprofen alone caused only minor physiological changes, whereas co-exposure, particularly with benomyl and chlorothalonil, reduced biomass and photosynthetic pigment concentrations and altered antioxidant and detoxification responses. The IBU+B treatment was associated with the highest lipid peroxidation. Molecular docking predicted a computationally plausible interaction between IBU and CpMLP-SY1, with AutoDock Vina scores ranging from -6.8 to -6.6 kcal mol -1 . Metabolic disturbances were strongest in roots and were dominated by amino acid biosynthesis and metabolism, particularly pathways involving branched-chain, aromatic and sulfur-containing amino acids, with additional alterations in secondary metabolism. These results indicate that fungicide co-exposure can influence IBU accumulation and plant responses in a treatment-dependent manner.

items.title: Multilayered network analysis reveals the centrality of newly discovered Nucleocytoviricota in wastewater treatment plant communities.
items.abstract: Viruses of the phylum Nucleocytoviricota are remarkable entities due to their exceptionally large genomes and complex gene repertoires, which blur the lines between viral and cellular life. Previous research has leveraged computational approaches to map their extensive diversity. Experimental work has, in parallel, begun to elucidate their intricate interactions with hosts, bacterial symbionts, co-infecting virophages, and other mobile genetic elements.Although unlikely to replicate all simultaneously within the same host cell, the convergence of these entities within a single environment creates a dense hub of potential interactions that calls for a holistic, topology-based analysis. Here, we recovered high-quality genomes of 61 Nucleocytoviruses, 15 virophages and 14 polinton-like viruses from deeply sequenced metagenomes of 23 Danish wastewater treatment plants, and integrated them into a multilayered interaction network together with microbial contigs. This network recovered putative interactions across multiple levels, including Nucleocytoviruses co-occurring with hyperparasitic elements, associations with abundant activated sludge bacteria, and read-level signals of integration events. We show that the giants among viruses act as centrality-inducing entities, elevating others into highly central positions within the community and therefore are key players shaping the microbial community structure, ecology and evolution in wastewater treatment plants.

items.title: Functional convergence despite taxonomic turnover across coral-associated microbiomes.
items.abstract: Coral-associated microbiomes are fundamental to holobiont health and resilience, yet their community structures often demonstrate high taxonomic variability across host species. Whether such variability results in functional instability or reflects pervasive metabolic redundancy remains unclear. Here, we investigated microbial taxonomic structure, functional potential, and community assembly mechanisms across 15 coral species using 16S rRNA gene sequencing and shotgun metagenomics. These communities exhibited extreme taxonomic heterogeneity, high beta-diversity, and the absence of a universally shared core genus, indicating strong host-specific filtering that dictates microbial membership. In contrast, Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes pathway-based functional profiles exhibited striking convergence across hosts, revealing a conserved metabolic landscape despite extensive taxonomic turnover. Mantel and Procrustes analyses identified a weak but significant correspondence between taxonomic composition and functional potential, a pattern consistent with functional redundancy across coral-associated microbiomes. Null model-based assembly analyses further revealed a decoupling between taxonomic and functional organization. Taxonomic structure was shaped by a host-dependent balance of stochastic and deterministic processes, whereas functional profiles were predominantly assembled through stochastic processes, maintaining consistently high functional redundancy across hosts. Metagenomic profiling uncovered a two-tier functional architecture underlying this stability: a conserved, high-abundance metabolic core enriched in carbon and phosphorus cycling and stress response functions that support microbial persistence in the coral microenvironment, together with lower-abundance host-specific metabolic modules involved in nitrogen and sulfur transformations that enable niche adaptation. Thus, functional requirements primarily govern the coral-associated microbiome rather than taxonomic identity. This synergy between conserved survival traits and flexible metabolic capacities maintains holobiont homeostasis despite extensive taxonomic turnover.IMPORTANCECoral reefs rely on complex partnerships between corals and their associated microorganisms to maintain health and withstand environmental stress. However, it remains unclear whether changes in microbial communities across different coral species lead to loss of important functions. In this study, we examined microorganisms associated with 15 coral species from the South China Sea and found that coral species hosted highly different microbial communities, while maintaining similar microbial functions. Our findings reveal that different microbial groups can perform similar ecological roles, allowing coral-associated communities to remain functionally stable despite changes in microbial membership. This functional flexibility may help corals maintain biological balance under changing environmental conditions and provides new insights into how coral holobionts preserve resilience in the face of ecological disturbances.

items.title: Competition-dominated microbial interactions and adaptive mutations enhance synthetic denitrifying community functions.
items.abstract: Understanding how interspecific interactions shape ecosystem functioning is a fundamental and longstanding question in ecology, especially along an evolutionary trajectory. Here, we used experimental evolution to evaluate how microbial interactions and adaptive mutations shaped community-level functions in synthetic denitrifying communities (SDCs) along a species richness gradient (one, two, and six species). Our results showed that competitive microbial interactions were observed and significantly (P < 0.05) enhanced denitrification rates in the six-species SDCs during experimental evolution. Genome and metagenome re-sequencing analysis revealed the highest fixed non-synonymous and frameshift mutations within the six-species SDCs, among genes involved in nutrient transport, DNA repair, and secretion pathways. AlphaFold2 protein structure prediction, molecular docking, and Evo 2 host fitness prediction indicated that the fixed mutations could improve host strain fitness, and partial least squares path modeling (PLS-PM) further revealed that interspecific competition accelerated adaptive mutations, thereby reinforcing community-level functions, indicating potential Red Queen dynamics. This study offers novel insights into our understanding of eco-evolutionary mechanisms linking species richness, microbial interactions, adaptive mutations, and community functions, with important implications for active nitrogen removal and greenhouse gas mitigation in diverse ecosystems. Microbial diversity is widely recognized as a key driver of ecosystem functioning, yet how species interactions shape ecosystem functions through evolutionary processes remains poorly understood. Using synthetic denitrifying communities with different levels of species richness, we show that interspecific competition can accelerate adaptive mutations and enhance community-level denitrification over evolutionary timescales. Communities with higher species richness accumulated more adaptive mutations, particularly in genes associated with nutrient transport, DNA repair, and secretion systems, ultimately improving microbial fitness and denitrification performance. Our findings provide direct experimental evidence that microbial competition can promote functional adaptation, consistent with the Red Queen hypothesis. This study advances our understanding of the eco-evolutionary mechanisms linking species richness, microbial interactions, adaptive evolution, and ecosystem functioning.

items.title: Unilateral cross-feeding constrains adaptive evolution, even in the producer without direct fitness effects.
items.abstract: Cross-feeding interactions are pervasive in microbial communities and profoundly shape community structure, stability, and function. While previous studies have explored how cross-feeding affects evolvability, this work has predominantly focused on bidirectional mutualistic interactions in engineered auxotrophic systems where both partners reciprocally exchange essential metabolites. However, most metabolic interactions in natural microbial communities are unidirectional, with organisms feeding on the metabolic waste products of other species. Our study addresses this gap by examining how a unidirectional cross-feeding interaction affects the evolutionary dynamics of both the producer (Acinetobacter johnsonii) and consumer (Pseudomonas putida) over 800 generations of experimental evolution. We found that co-culture constrained adaptive evolution in both species. Co-cultures exhibited lower πN/πS ratios (0.75 for P. putida; 1.04 for A. johnsonii) than monocultures (1.44 and 2.02, respectively), indicating stronger purifying selection against nonsynonymous mutations in the community context. Lineage tracking through whole genome sequencing of populations and clones revealed greater lineage diversity and complexity in monocultures, with more mutations showing significant parallelism across replicate populations. Additionally, P. putida evolved increased dependence on its partner; co-culture-evolved P. putida grew significantly worse than its ancestor when A. johnsonii was removed. These findings indicate that ecological interactions can reshape fitness landscapes and constrain adaptive evolution even when fitness benefits are unidirectional, with implications for understanding microbial community stability and predicting evolutionary dynamics in complex communities.

items.title: Heatwave-Resilient Cuticular Microbiota Protect the Leaf Beetle Plagiodera versicolora From Fungal Infection.
items.abstract: The increasing frequency and intensity of heatwaves-extreme thermal events characterized by prolonged supra-optimal temperatures-exert profound impacts on global ecosystem stability and species interactions. While the disruptive effects of thermal stress on host physiology and gut microbiota are well documented, the role of cuticular microbiota in host defense under heatwaves remains poorly characterized. Here, we show that the cuticular microbiota of the willow leaf beetle Plagiodera versicolora may serve as a thermostable protective barrier against the entomopathogenic fungus Beauveria bassiana. Using microbiota-manipulated larval models, we found that cuticular microbiota significantly bolstered host survival under both control (27°C) and simulated heatwave (32°C) regimes. High-throughput 16S rRNA sequencing revealed a dramatic microbial regime shift: Pantoea dominated at control temperatures, whereas Enterobacter proliferated and became predominant during simulated heatwaves. Both genera exhibited potent antifungal activity that markedly increased with rising temperature, suggesting a potential functional compensation property whereby thermally adaptive taxa may maintain host defensive capacity under climatic perturbations. Recolonization experiments confirmed that cuticle-isolated Enterobacter gergoviae and Pantoea anthophila are sufficient to reduce the increased fungal susceptibility of germ-free larvae. Mechanistically, these symbionts appear to inhibit fungal germination through direct antagonism and modulate host immune responses by upregulating antimicrobial peptide effectors while potentially reducing excessive immune recognition signaling. These findings highlight the resilience of cuticular defensive symbioses in the face of climate change and provide new insights into the adaptive mechanisms that sustain host-microbe-pathogen dynamics in a warming world.

items.title: Benzoic Acid Secreted From the Chickpea Root Promotes Persistent Colonisation by Specific Soil Microbes.
items.abstract: The plant root tip is highly sensitive to environmental cues and exerts sensory, chemical and movement responses. However, the microbial diversification at the root tip, and the nature of root-selection for microbes, are poorly understood. This study investigated root exudation and microbiome colonisation in the chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.) root tip and root base, in diverse soils. For the endosphere microbiome, deterministic effects were more important than stochastic processes in shaping the root tip microbiome, indicated by the stable endophyte composition independent of the soil microbiota background. A genotype with high secretion of benzoic acid (BA), was consistently colonised by 3 core ASV (Amplicon Sequence Variant) from the Burkholderia clade. Two of 98 isolated strains were confirmed as the culturable candidates of the core ASV, both of which were characterised by superior BA tolerance and the ability to utilise BA as a sole carbon source, demonstrated through high expression of BA degradation genes. Additionally, one IAA-producing coloniser specifically promoted the growth of its original host genotype across different soils, but provided no consistent benefits for other genotypes. Our results reveal the mechanisms by which soil microbes interact with root exudates of a host genotype to establish colonisation.

items.title: The characterization of municipal solid waste in a Ukrainian region during the war period: Reference values and a methodological review.
items.abstract: Ukraine's sustainable post-war transition toward resilient, resource-oriented waste management (WM) systems relies mainly on accurate data on municipal solid waste (MSW) generation and composition. This paper reviews methodologies and reference values for MSW composition in the Poltava region during the war period (2023-2024), combining (1) a systematic analysis of pre-war and wartime data from several Ukrainian regions and (2) four seasonal sorting analyses conducted in the Kotelva settlement, complemented by a simplified socio-demographic stratification approach using Austrian MSW data as analogies. The four seasonal sorting analyses applied two successive Ukrainian methodological frameworks, the latter supplemented by the Austrian and European waste classification approach. Existing Ukrainian data from different regions show wide ranges for key waste fractions, reflecting strong methodological heterogeneity-from purely normative, regulation-based estimates to seasonally stratified field campaigns. Wartime MSW in Kotelva was dominated by kitchen waste (mean 37.4 wt%), along with organic (other than food) waste (6.0 wt%), followed by inert construction waste (7.6 wt%), hygiene products (7.3 wt%), and textiles (5.9 wt%). Compared with 2020 pre-war data, a shift from glass to plastic packaging in the residual waste was observed. The study demonstrates that the current Ukrainian methodology only partially aligns with European practice, underscoring the need for a harmonized national framework. Moreover, a simplified comparative approach based on socio-demographic stratification was developed to pre-assess the MSW composition of Ukrainian settlements lacking basic WM data. The proposed approach may serve as offer a pragmatic interim tool for WM planning in data-poor Ukrainian regions to promptly support post-war circular-economy-oriented decision-making.

items.title: Natural recovery and gaming disorder: a case series.
items.abstract: Conceptualizations of recovery in gaming disorder (GD) remain relatively underdeveloped. While remission without formal treatment appears common in longitudinal data, the mechanisms through which it occurs have received little systematic attention. In contrast, natural recovery-the resolution of addictive problems without formal treatment-is well documented in substance and gambling research, where it has prompted broader reconceptualizations of how and where recovery unfolds. Using longitudinal qualitative data from Finland, Slovakia and South Korea, this case series examines how individuals who had previously experienced self-identified gaming-related problems reached recovery without successful intervention explicitly targeting their gaming behaviour. Six recurring recovery pathways were identified: axiological shift, social enforcement, gradual regulation, reflexive transformation, healing comorbidity and environmental transformation. Rather than centring on abstinence or direct symptom elimination, recovery emerged through reconfigurations of life structure, social roles and personal value hierarchies. In most cases, gaming did not disappear but was repositioned within a broader ecology of responsibilities and relationships. These findings suggest that natural recovery in GD may be better understood as a contextual and relational reconfiguration rather than solely as symptom reduction. The pathways identified here provide a conceptual stepping stone towards more comprehensive frameworks for understanding the recovery process in GD.

items.title: Experience-dependent shifts in behavioural decision-making following repeated captures in a wild mammal.
items.abstract: Live trapping is central to behavioural ecology, yet whether post-capture behaviour reflects consistent among-individual differences and how it is modified by repeated captures remain poorly understood. Here, we repeatedly captured wild individuals of the rodent Apodemus mystacinus and temporarily held them in a standardised wooden experimental box. We then allowed them to voluntarily exit the box near the capture location and continuously recorded their behaviour for 5 minutes. Using multilevel, multivariate and continuous-time multi-state models, we characterise the sequence of behavioural states from confinement to escape. We also test whether capture experience reorganises individual behavioural trajectories and whether individual characteristics, such as body mass and sex, mediate behavioural transitions across capture-recapture events. We show that there is among-individual variation in the measured post-capture behaviours and that repeated captures reorganise the structure and sequential organisation of behavioural responses after individuals exit a trap. Importantly, we also show that recapture experience and body mass are associated with an increased tendency towards rapid escape. In contrast, we find that sex has no detectable effects. Our findings highlight that behaviours expressed immediately after trap release do not represent individuals' undisturbed ecological baseline, but instead experience-dependent responses shaped by individuals' cumulative history of interactions with their environment.

items.title: Soil moisture enhances the vibrations induced by moving earthworms, especially of detritivores.
items.abstract: Earthworms (Lumbricidae) are moisture-loving soil-dwellers that can be categorized into two feeding guilds with distinct behaviours: detritivores and geophages. Detritivores feed on litter fragments and geophages on smaller litter particles mixed with soil. When earthworms move within and across soil layers to forage, soil characteristics might influence the scale of these movements and their detectability to predators. To investigate the extent to which the detection of earthworm movements and the vibrations they thereby generate is affected by soil moisture, we used an innovative method to detect and quantify vibrations of moving earthworms emitted through the soil. We designed a mesocosm experiment in which we recorded, with a geophone, the movement-induced vibrations of detritivores and geophages in drier and wetter soils. Earthworm vibrations were detected best at 200 Hz and were detected significantly more in wetter than in drier soils. Moreover, in wetter soils, vibrations induced by detritivores were detected more frequently and at higher intensities than those of geophages. These findings suggest differences in activity levels between detritivores and geophages, as a function of soil moisture content. The observed activity patterns are likely to have food web consequences because earthworm consumers relying on mechanoreceptors to detect prey might detect detritivores more often, specifically in wetter soils.

items.title: Modularity without convergence: integrated evolution of the salamander autopodium.
items.abstract: Morphological modularity is known to favour evolutionary diversification by enabling different body regions to vary in response to functional and ecological demands. Despite their remarkable diversity in limb morphology and ecology, amphibians-and salamanders in particular-remain significantly under-represented in empirical tests of modularity. Using geometric morphometrics and phylogenetic comparative methods, we investigate patterns of shape variation, integration and modularity in the salamander autopodium. We first validated a landmark-based method to outline foot shape, demonstrating that image orientation does not affect shape analyses and that species can be reliably distinguished. We then applied this approach to a larger comparative dataset encompassing 149 salamander taxa across major lineages and ecological strategies. Our findings demonstrate that the salamander autopodium is functionally modular: the distal region (digits and interdigital region) shows more evolutionary lability than the proximal pes, while remaining integrated within a coordinated evolutionary system. Furthermore, the combinations of allometric, ecological and life-history factors account for a small but significant percentage of shape variation, with a low evolutionary signal in foot shape. Our results suggest that modular organization of the salamander foot may allow for morphological variation while still being limited by a common evolutionary and developmental history. By focusing on an understudied group and morphological system, this study provides new insight on how modularity influences limb evolution in tetrapods.

items.title: A climate action intervention increases four psychological motivators, as well as climate advocacy, activism and civic participation.
items.abstract: Urgent climate action is needed to keep warming below 2°C and protect hundreds of millions from climate collapse. As part of a broader Registered Report series, this study examined whether a longitudinal intervention designed to strengthen psychological correlates of pro-environmental behaviour could motivate n = 31 university students in The Netherlands to take climate action. The intervention was delivered over six weeks through interactive lessons and activities informed by psychological theories and interventions. The goal was to increase pro-climate behaviours by targeting 12 psychological factors. Participants completed surveys assessing these correlates, as well as ecological momentary assessments of individual and collective pro-climate behaviours before and after the intervention, and after three months (14 days each). A control group was included ( n = 27). Results showed that 4 of the 12 psychological correlates increased significantly: emotional engagement, collective efficacy, the bottom-up theory of change (the belief that change can start from grassroots action and spread systemically) and climate appraisal. Three (except appraisal) remained elevated at the three-month follow-up. Civic engagement, advocacy and activism increased after the intervention in the experimental group relative to control group. The increase in activist behaviour was predicted by the development of a bottom-up theory of change.

items.title: Can consumers accurately identify loot boxes and loot box receipts?
items.abstract: Loot boxes are randomized rewards in video games. Meta-analyses suggest relationships between loot box spending and problem gambling symptomatology, and early longitudinal evidence suggests loot box purchasers migrate into conventional gambling at higher rates than non-purchasers. Regulatory responses vary across jurisdictions, and even in jurisdictions that have banned loot boxes, evidence suggests their presence in games remains common. Consequently, consumers are often responsible for regulating their own, and their children's, loot box purchasing. To effectively achieve this, consumers must first be able to identify loot boxes. Here, we investigated consumer accuracy in identifying critical features of loot boxes. Participants were tasked to identify basic facts about, pictures of, and receipts generated by loot boxes. Parents and non-gamers, compared with non-parents and gamers, respectively, were poorer at identifying loot boxes. Our results suggest that parents and non-gamers may be less equipped to make informed loot box purchasing decisions compared with non-parents/non-guardians and gamers, respectively. This may pose risks for parents and unaware incipient gamers. These are the first findings providing objective evidence about the relative ability of consumers to identify, and thus self-regulate purchases of, loot boxes and suggest that parents and non-gamers may require support to ensure informed purchasing decisions.

items.title: Psychological and behavioral correlates of food addiction symptoms in university students: the role of hedonic eating and food label attitudes.
items.abstract: Food addiction (FA) involves addictive-like eating and impaired control over palatable food consumption. This cross-sectional study examined FA correlates among 404 university students, focusing on palatable eating motives and food label reading attitudes. Sixty-six participants (16.3%) met the original Yale Food Addiction Scale (YFAS 1.0) threshold of at least three of seven DSM-IV-TR criteria plus clinically significant impairment or distress. Female sex, smoking, obesity, and a higher T-PEMS mean were associated with higher odds of meeting the threshold; the obesity estimate was imprecise because that subgroup was small. Model discrimination was acceptable in-sample (AUC = 0.746). The T-PEMS mean had a weak inverse correlation with label attitudes ( r = -0.143) that was not significant after adjustment (β = -0.10, p = 0.060; R 2 = 0.057). Findings support an association between palatable eating motives and FA but limited evidence for an independent label-attitude relationship. Longitudinal and multicenter studies are needed.

items.title: Boosting or Blocking Breastfeeding Confidence? The Role of Online Breastfeeding Content in Relation to Mothers' Breastfeeding Self-Efficacy.
items.abstract: Mothers increasingly go online to find answers to their breastfeeding concerns, read personal experiences, or connect with breastfeeding "mommy influencers." This study analyzes how the consultation of online platforms and breastfeeding-related posts is linked to mothers' breastfeeding self-efficacy, and whether this relationship is moderated by mothers' different motives (i.e., information-seeking, entertainment, or community building) for consuming such content online within a Dutch-speaking context. Drawing on Social Cognitive Theory and the Uses and Gratifications framework, an online survey (N = 354; M age = 31, 22) was conducted among Dutch-speaking mothers. Participants reported their exposure to online breastfeeding content from various resources (social media, "Mommy influencers," parenting community groups), their motives for consulting these different resources, and their breastfeeding self-efficacy. Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) reveals that online breastfeeding content consumption is not directly related to breastfeeding self-efficacy. However, an interaction effect was found with the information-seeking motive: mothers using online parenting platforms for informational purposes show a more negative association between online exposure to breastfeeding content and breastfeeding self-efficacy compared to mothers not using these platforms for informational reasons. These findings highlight the complex role of online breastfeeding content, suggesting that informational motives may shape mothers' self-efficacy differently.

items.title: Level of educational attainment and school dropout rates of people with disability in Denmark.
items.abstract: Aims Education is linked to health outcomes, and health selection processes may shape educational trajectories among people with disabilities. This study examines educational attainment and school dropout patterns among people with physical and mental disabilities. Methods This cross-sectional study used data from a nationally representative survey of Danish adults ( N =18,749). Participants included individuals with physical disability only ( n =4047), mental disability only ( n =888), and both physical and mental disabilities ( n =745). Results Compared with individuals without disabilities, those with disabilities had significantly lower levels of educational attainment and were less likely to participate in higher education. Participants with only physical disability (odds ratio (OR) 0.71, confidence interval (CI) 0.66-0.77), only mental disability (OR 0.64, CI 0.54-0.76), and both physical and mental disabilities (OR 0.46, CI 0.39-0.54) had lower odds of completing higher education compared with individuals without disabilities. A similar pattern was observed for dropout. Participants with physical (OR 1.47, CI 1.35-1.61), mental (OR 2.61, CI 2.22-3.07), and both physical and mental disabilities (OR 3.26, CI 2.78-3.84) had higher odds of dropping out. Moreover, early-onset disability (before age 25 years) was associated with lower odds of higher education completion compared with adult-onset disability (OR 1.16, CI 1.00-1.35). Conclusions Disability remains a major barrier to accessing and completing higher education, particularly when disability occurs early in life. Although higher education is free in Denmark and students with disabilities receive financial support, further measures are needed to close the educational gap .

items.title: EXPRESS: The Dynamics of Cue Integration in Metacognitive Judgments.
items.abstract: Learners form judgments of learning (JOLs) by integrating multiple cues. However, little is known about how cue integration might change over time. To examine this, we introduced a modified cue-integration paradigm in which one cue (the context cue) remained constant across sequences of trials varying in length, while another cue (the target cue) varied randomly. This design allowed us to examine how the consistency and variability of a cue affect its use for JOLs and that of other available cues. In three experiments, participants studied nouns with two cues manipulated per experiment (e.g., emotionality, concreteness). In all experiments, both cues influenced JOLs, and the target cue's influence remained stable across conditions, suggesting that learners used the two cues independently. In Experiment 1, the context cue's effect declined when its level was constant across multiple consecutive trials. This adaptation effect did not replicate in Experiments 2 and 3. Exploratory cross-experimental analyses showed stronger context cue effects immediately after than immediately before context cue levels switched. This hints at a transient increase in cue salience following a switch. Together, our findings show that learners flexibly respond to changes in cue consistency and variability while maintaining their overall cue integration strategy.

items.title: Psychological distress among nurses before and after COVID-19 vaccines: A repeated cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: BackgroundExtensive research conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic has consistently found significant levels of anxiety, perceived stress and depression among healthcare workers, particularly among nurses. Nevertheless, the effect of COVID-19 vaccine availability on the psychological distress of healthcare workforce remains unexplored.ObjectiveTo compare levels of anxiety, perceived stress and depression among Spanish nurses immediately before and after the full COVID-19 vaccination protocol which was conducted in Spain throughout 2021.MethodsWe employed a repeated cross-sectional design recruiting 439 and 410 Spanish registered nurses at the first (pre-vaccination) and second (post-vaccination) timepoints respectively. Data on psychological distress were collected via online surveys using the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS) and the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS).ResultsAfter vaccination nurses showed lower perceived stress and depression with a small effect size, but anxiety was not reduced. The magnitude of these effects was very small. Although in both timepoints psychological distress was higher in women, the initial differences between frontline and non-frontline professionals tended to disappear. Over the period studied, the proportion of nurses receiving psychiatric or psychological care increased from 7.7% to 20.4%, and half of those using psychotropic drugs had started treatment in the preceding year.ConclusionsThe psychological distress of nurses continued being a relevant problem even after COVID-19 vaccines became available. Policymakers and health systems must ensure adequate psychological support for nurses and a supportive work environment to improve their long-term resilience and well-being, regardless of the existence of effective vaccines.

items.title: Effectiveness of a continuous ergonomic program on workplace health and cognitive strain in university employees.
items.abstract: BackgroundUniversity staff are at high risk of musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) and mental workload due to prolonged static postures, poor ergonomic conditions, and high cognitive demands. These issues lead to significant health and productivity challenges, particularly in developing countries.ObjectiveThis study aimed to evaluate the impact of a participatory ergonomic intervention program on reducing MSDs and mental workload among university staff, and to enhance their awareness of ergonomic principles.MethodsA quasi-experimental design with pre- and post-tests was used, involving 60 participants divided into control and intervention groups. The intervention included 8 weekly training sessions on ergonomics, workstation adjustments, and the introduction of ergonomic equipment. Data were collected using the Cornell Musculoskeletal Discomfort Questionnaire (CMDQ) and NASA-TLX workload index, analyzed via paired t-tests and covariance analysis.ResultsThe intervention significantly reduced mental workload by 24.17% (p = 0.008), with the highest reductions in physical (46.58%) and mental (35.84%) dimensions. MSDs prevalence decreased notably in the back (50%), neck (39%), and wrists (39-61.6%). The control group showed no significant changes.ConclusionsBased on these results, continuous training and ergonomic adjustments are recommended, as they may help sustain the observed benefits over the long term. This approach has the potential to promote healthier work environments and could lead to enhanced productivity, although further longitudinal research is needed to directly confirm these broader implications.

items.title: Understanding the Complex Linkages Between Climate Change and Gender-Based Violence Globally.
items.abstract: Many determinants of gender-based violence (GBV) are sensitive to climate change. In this theoretical article, we offer a conceptual framework for analyzing how climate change can shape the incidence of GBV through five mechanisms: human physiology and psychology, economic insecurity and job loss, scarcity of natural resources, changes in migration patterns, and disruption of infrastructure and essential services. We argue that significant empirical gaps in the literature stem from over-reliance on household surveys using narrow measures of domestic violence in a non-representative set of contexts, and provide methodological recommendations for achieving a more expansive understanding of climate effects on GBV.

items.title: Perceived satisfaction with care, service atmosphere and mood fluctuations among patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorder in Italian mental health supported accommodations: a multicenter study.
items.abstract: Background Supported Accommodations (SA) are central to Italy's community-based mental health care for individuals with schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSD), offering structured, recovery-oriented environments. While symptom severity remains important, care environment and satisfaction strongly influence well-being. Mood fluctuations, a key aspect of daily functioning, have been underexplored in SA. Using the Experience Sampling Method (ESM), this study aims to examine the associations between perceived ward atmosphere, care satisfaction, and momentary mood in SA residents with SSD. Methods As part of the DiAPAson project, 68 residents with SSD were assessed also using ESM. Additional measures included psychopathology (BPRS, BNSS), functioning (SLOF, WHODAS 2.0), perceived ward atmosphere (WAS-P) and service satisfaction (VSSS-32). Descriptive analyses were conducted, and a structural equation model examined mood in relation to clinical, demographic, and environmental factors. Results Residents with SSD (29.4% female; mean age = 42.8 years) were mostly single (80.9%) and unemployed (79.4%), with a mean disorder duration of 19.2 years. Clinical assessments indicated moderate symptom severity and functioning. Structural equation modelling showed excellent fit (CFI = 1.000; RMSEA = 0.000; SRMR = 0.060). The latent variable Env-Perc, combining service satisfaction (VSSS-32) and perceived ward atmosphere (WAS-P), was the only significant predictor of momentary mood (β = 0.344, 95%CI: [0.084;0954], p = 0.033). Conclusions Perceived satisfaction with care and service atmosphere in SA contribute to promoting positive mood among individuals with SSD. Trial registration ISRCTN registry ID ISRCTN21141466, registration date 17 February 2020.

items.title: Webcams can be used to study eye movements during reading.
items.abstract: Eye movements have revealed a wealth of information about how readers process written language. Modern eye trackers can record eye movements in the lab with high accuracy. However, such equipment is expensive, and participant testing is labour-intensive. Kaduk et al. (Behav Res Methods 56(5):5002-5022, 2023) recently reported that webcam eye tracking may be a viable alternative, showing that webcams achieved correlations with laboratory eye trackers of ~0.83 during a free-viewing task. We conducted three experiments to test whether webcams can be used to study eye movements during reading. Participants read short sentences with a target word frequency manipulation while their eye movements were recorded with both an EyeLink system and a webcam in the laboratory (co-registration, Experiments 1 and 2) or online with their own webcam (online study, Experiment 3). In the lab, the webcam-based system recorded raw gaze positions that were highly correlated with the EyeLink (median r = 0.805), replicating Kaduk et al.'s results. We also found evidence for word frequency effects in the webcam data, but there was more noise than in the EyeLink data. In the online study, data quality was much poorer, but we still found reliable effects that were consistent with those observed in the laboratory. In summary, webcam-based eye tracking may be viable for studying reading, especially under laboratory conditions. However, obtaining useful data may require collecting many more observations when using webcams than with high-accuracy eye trackers.

items.title: Self-Care as a Self-Regulatory Process Linking Loneliness and Humor to Mental and Physical Health in Older Adults.
items.abstract: Psychosocial experiences such as loneliness and humor are associated with health in later life, but less is known about their relationship with everyday self-care. This study examined whether self-care was associated with mental and physical health beyond emotional loneliness and self-enhancing humor and whether self-care statistically accounted for indirect associations between these psychosocial factors and health-related quality of life in older adults. A cross-sectional community-based sample of 675 adults aged 60-99 years completed measures of emotional loneliness, self-enhancing humor, self-care, and health-related quality of life. Meaning and Life Purpose was examined separately as an exploratory predictor. Hierarchical regression models adjusted for age and sex were followed by bootstrapped indirect-effect analyses with 5000 resamples. Sensitivity analyses used overlap-reduced self-care scores to address potential conceptual and item-level overlap among measures. The self-care composite was strongly positively associated with both mental (r = 0.692) and physical health (r = 0.700; both p < 0.001). In hierarchical models, self-care added 13.7% and 15.3% of explained variance in mental and physical health, respectively, yielding final R2 values of 0.529 and 0.526. In the final models, self-care remained positively associated with mental (β = 0.515, p < 0.001) and physical health (β = 0.545, p < 0.001), while emotional loneliness remained negatively associated with both outcomes. Bootstrapped analyses showed significant indirect associations through self-care for emotional loneliness and self-enhancing humor in relation to both health outcomes. These associations remained statistically supported in conservative overlap-reduced sensitivity analyses. Exploratory indirect associations involving Meaning and Life Purpose were not robust to sensitivity analyses. Self-care was strongly associated with perceived mental and physical health and accounted for statistically supported indirect associations linking emotional loneliness and self-enhancing humor with health outcomes. The findings identify self-care as a potentially important behavioral intermediary in later life, while the cross-sectional design precludes conclusions about temporal or causal mechanisms. Longitudinal research is needed to determine the direction and developmental course of these relationships.

items.title: Evaluating methods for testing publication bias in meta-analyses with confounding covariates: A simulation study.
items.abstract: Selective publication of favorable results can bias meta-analytic estimates and threaten the validity of meta-analyses. Many methods that detect and adjust for publication bias perform poorly under substantial between-study heterogeneity. Heterogeneity complicates publication bias assessment because study characteristics may be associated with both effect size estimates and standard errors. These characteristics can induce an effect-precision association that regression-based diagnostics may misattribute to selective publication when such characteristics are omitted. However, it remains unclear how best to incorporate these confounding characteristics across methods and how their performance varies with confounding level, selective publication, residual heterogeneity, and the number of studies. To address this gap, I conduct an extensive Monte Carlo simulation evaluating Egger-type regression tests, residual-based tests, and a likelihood-ratio test of the three-parameter selection model (3PSM) under the one-step p value selection mechanism. Results show that when confounding covariates were ignored, Egger-type regression tests and residual analyses exhibited inflated Type I error rates, whereas the 3PSM likelihood-ratio test maintained near-nominal, albeit slightly inflated, Type I error rates across conditions. When confounding covariates were incorporated, Egger-type tests had well-calibrated Type I error rates, residual analyses based on residualizing effect sizes alone tended to be conservative, and the 3PSM test showed slight inflation. Nevertheless, 3PSM consistently yielded higher power than other methods. Overall, the findings suggest that Egger-type regression tests and 3PSM can be used as complementary analyses for assessing selective publication when confounding covariates are present.

items.title: Public responses to biodiversity loss terminology and crisis framing.
items.abstract: To avoid the technical term "biodiversity loss", public communications often refer to "nature loss" or "extinction of plants and animals" or apply crisis framing by stating "biodiversity crisis," "nature crisis," or "extinction crisis." To assess public responses to these terms, we conducted a randomized survey experiment with 7338 U.S. adults. Participants were randomly assigned to one term (biodiversity loss, nature loss, extinction of plants and animals, biodiversity crisis, nature crisis, or extinction crisis), either alone or in the context of an explanation and photos of plants and animals. With and without context, "biodiversity loss" and "biodiversity crisis" received the lowest ratings of familiarity, concern, perceived urgency, and conservation support. "Extinction of plants and animals" generally received the highest ratings. "Nature loss" performed similarly to this term when context was provided. Crisis framing had little to no effect. Terminology effects were strongest for political Independents. We discuss implications for public communications.

items.title: The prognostic value of physical functioning on survival in patients with nonsmall cell lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Background Physical functioning has emerged as a potentially valuable prognostic indicator in patients with nonsmall cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of objectively measured components of physical functioning on survival outcomes across treatment modalities. Methods Medline, Web of Science and Scopus were searched up to May 2025. Eligible studies included adult patients with NSCLC and assessed at least one objectively measured physical functioning indicator in relation to survival outcomes. Indicators were categorised using the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) framework into "body functions and structures", "activities" and "participation" and studies were stratified into "surgery" and "nonsurgery" groups. Meta-analyses were conducted when data permitted it. Results 58 studies (19 436 patients) were included. Most assessments were performed before treatment. In the surgical group, only "activities"-based measures were evaluated. A meta-analysis restricted to this group showed that survivors had substantially higher (functional) exercise capacity, measured through cardiopulmonary exercise testing and field tests (standardised mean difference 0.79). In nonsurgical cohorts, prognostic value extended across all ICF domains, with low handgrip strength (hazard ratio (HR) 1.27), low (functional) exercise capacity (HR 2.11) and physical inactivity (HR 2.86) associated with significantly higher mortality. Notably, no studies in surgical cohorts evaluated "body functions" or "participation". Heterogeneity and varying thresholds were noted across studies. Conclusions Objectively measured physical functioning is a significant prognostic indicator of survival in NSCLC. Routine assessment could enhance risk stratification and guide personalised care. Future research should address longitudinal changes, standardisation of measures and targeted interventions.

items.title: Altered language network microstructure links with impaired language function and development in very preterm/very low birth weight born adults.
items.abstract: Premature birth is associated with impaired language function. In premature-born children, language function has been linked with microstructural alterations of the language network.Whether these brain-language associations persist into adulthood remains unclear. We investigated the microstructural properties of major dorsal and ventral language pathways in very preterm/very low birth weight (VPT/VLBW) adults and their associations with language performance in adulthood and childhood. Sixty-three VPT/VLBW and eighty full-term-born adults (mean age 26.8 years) underwent diffusion-weighted imaging and language assessment. The arcuate fasciculus, superior longitudinal fasciculus, uncinate fasciculus and inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus were reconstructed using probabilistic tractography from which fractional anisotropy (FA) and mean diffusivity (MD) measures were extracted. Adult language function was assessed via the Regensburg word fluency test, rapid automatized naming and verbal IQ; childhood language was assessed at the mean age of 8 using the Kaufman Assessment Battery for children. We observed altered language network microstructure in VPT/VLBW participants, illustrated by lower FA and higher MD in the SLF and UF. These microstructural alterations were associated with language function in adulthood, but also with language development in childhood. We found that the association between tract microstructure and language abilities differed between groups. Our results demonstrate altered language network microstructure in premature born adults, which links with impaired language function and development. These findings extend previous work by comprehensively characterizing the adult dorsal and ventral language network and relating its microstructural properties to language function across development. The selective follow-up sample may limit generalizability to the broader VPT/VLBW population.

items.title: Statistical Learning of Feature-Spatial Mappings and Its Modulation by Cue-Induced Expectation.
items.abstract: Visual statistical learning enables individuals to extract regularities from the environment, thereby optimizing attentional allocation. Previous research has mainly focused on unidimensional location or feature probability learning, leaving unclear whether individuals can acquire multidimensional mappings between target features and high-probability spatial locations, and how cue-induced expectations modulate the neural expression of such mappings. We employed a location probability paradigm combined with multivariate pattern analysis (MVPA) and recorded EEG. Reaction times showed a significant gradient from the feature-matched high-probability location to the low-probability location, indicating successful acquisition of feature-spatial mappings under both cue conditions. The N2pc did not reliably differentiate the two high-probability location conditions, providing no detectable evidence of feature-dependent modulation of early lateralized selection. Predictive cues elicited brief pretarget alpha lateralization toward the cue-associated HPTL. Search-array-locked MVPA discriminated feature-matched from feature-mismatched HPTL trials under both cue conditions, with stronger decoding under predictive cueing. These findings show that learned feature-spatial regularities were expressed behaviorally and in distributed neural activity, and that predictive cues modulated their neural expression before and after search-array onset.

items.title: Co-developmental trajectories of internalizing symptoms and psychotic-like experiences among adolescents: The predictive role of sleep disturbance.
items.abstract: Background Internalizing symptoms and psychotic-like experiences (PLEs) are common among adolescents. However, few studies have explored the longitudinal co-development of internalizing symptoms and PLEs in this age group. Methods A total of 7529 adolescents (M age at baseline = 13.89 years, SD = 1.34; 50% girls) participated in this three-wave longitudinal study. A parallel-process latent class growth analysis identified joint trajectories of internalizing symptoms and PLEs, and multinomial logistic regression examined the effect of sleep disturbance. Results Three distinct trajectories were identified: a low-risk group (74.0%), a pure-internalizing symptoms group (13.5%), and a chronic co-occurring group (12.5%). After controlling for sample characteristics, negative life events during follow-up, and sleep duration, baseline sleep disturbance was significantly associated with both the pure-internalizing symptoms trajectory (OR = 3.41, 95% CI = 2.84-4.08) and the chronic co-occurring trajectory (OR = 3.69, 95% CI = 3.06-4.46). Conclusions These findings indicate that sleep disturbance independently associated with the heterogeneous co-developmental trajectories of internalizing symptoms and PLEs. Early assessment and treatment of sleep disturbance may be an important strategy for the prevention and intervention of psychopathology development.

items.title: Emotion regulation diversity and depressive symptoms in mid- to older adulthood: A longitudinal investigation.
items.abstract: Depression is associated with emotion regulation (ER) impairments. ER diversity has been proposed as novel measure of the diversity of the ER repertoire and has been linked to clinical depression status cross sectionally. A more diverse ER repertoire, particularly under stressful circumstances, may protect against depressive symptom elevation longitudinally. This study used a longitudinal design to examine the within- and between-person associations between ER diversity, stress, and depression in mid- to later life adults. ER strategy use, perceived stress, and depressive symptoms were assessed. A series of linear mixed effects models were fit. As expected, ER diversity did not systematically change over the course of 10 years. Importantly, perceived stress moderated the ER diversity - depression association between individuals. Specifically, for individuals experiencing moderate to high levels of perceived stress, higher ER diversity was associated with lower depressive symptom levels. This moderation effect was observed consistently across baseline age and was not influenced by aging longitudinally. Thus, a diverse ER repertoire under stress may protect against depressive symptom elevation in mid- to later-life adults.

items.title: Towards semantic brain-computer interfacing: The graded inventory of semantic triggers (GIST) paradigm.
items.abstract: Objective Semantic Brain-Computer Interfaces (sBCIs) aim to decode conceptual information directly from neural activity, enabling more efficient and natural communication for individuals with severe motor impairments. However, existing approaches are often confounded by stimulus-driven perceptual processes and lack a reliable means of tagging the moment of concept formation. We introduce the Graded Inventory of Semantic Triggers (GIST), a novel electroencephalography (EEG) paradigm designed to elicit semantic retrieval from graded verbal clues with precise temporal alignment. Approach: EEG data were recorded from 14 participants performing the GIST task across three semantic categories (food, musical instruments, and body parts). Target neural activity was aligned to each participant's self-reported moment of semantic retrieval (spacebar press), enabling response-locked analysis. Here, we propose a staged framework where the first comprises a Conformer-based encoder trained on pooled data using a hybrid contrastive objective that combines instance-level consistency and cross-participant class alignment with domain-adversarial learning to reduce participant-specific information. In the second stage, the frozen encoder is transferred to a held-out participant whose data played no part in Stage 1, and a support vector machine is calibrated on that participant's own labelled items under a nested leave-one-item-out protocol. Results: Above-chance semantic decoding was achieved in all three pairwise tasks. Mean accuracies were 73.4% (Body vs. Food), 70.7% (Body vs. Music), and 68.2% (Food vs. Music). Participant-level permutation tests were significant in 9/11 participants for Body vs. Food and 8/11 for each of the other tasks (p < 0.05). The pre-response interval at [-1.5s, -0.5s] was the most discriminative. Significance: The GIST paradigm enables controlled elicitation and temporal alignment of semantic processing while reducing perceptual confounds. Combined with cross-participant representation pretraining and participant-specific calibration, the results demonstrate above-chance decoding of semantic categories from EEG in individuals excluded from representation learning, supporting the feasibility of sBCIs.

items.title: Barriers and facilitators to informal caregiving in Rhode Island: A qualitative study.
items.abstract: Informal caregivers are instrumental in supporting the activities of older adults; however, caregiving can negatively impact caregivers' health. This qualitative study explored the experiences, support, and unmet needs of informal caregivers of older adults (n = 12) in Rhode Island. Interviews were audio recorded, transcribed and analyzed through a thematic analysis approach. Identified themes were categorized into three domains: 1) Health Services Challenges for Care Recipients, 2) Negative Impact on Caregivers, and 3) Caregiver Coping Strategies and Challenges. Results indicate that informal caregivers often struggled to access health services and experienced significant disruptions in their lives, ultimately taking a toll on their health and well-being. Finding meaning through caregiving for loved ones and home self-care practices, such as yoga, helped caregivers cope with personal challenges. Findings suggest the need for tailored interventions to better support caregivers throughout the caregiving process.

items.title: Altered interlimb coupling during unimanual and bimanual force control in aging and Parkinson's disease.
items.abstract: Bimanual coordination depends on the ability to flexibly regulate interlimb coupling while maintaining independent control of each limb. Aging and Parkinson's disease (PD) may disrupt this balance by altering sensorimotor regulation and shared neural input between limbs. This study examined force control, coordination dynamics, and physiological coupling during unimanual and bimanual isometric force tasks in healthy young adults (HYA), healthy older adults (HOA), and individuals with Parkinson's disease (PD). Participants completed 30 s unimanual and bimanual force tasks with target forces set at 20% maximal voluntary contraction (MVC). During unimanual tasks, participants produced the target force with one limb while the uninstructed limb rested on a force transducer. During bimanual tasks, both limbs produced the target force. Beginning 15 s after trial onset, visual feedback for the instructed limb in the unimanual tasks or one designated limb in the bimanual tasks was removed for 10 s. Behavioral measures included constant error (CE), coefficient of variation (CV), and interlimb force-force cross-correlation, while physiological coupling was quantified using EMG-EMG coherence between homologous first dorsal interosseous (FDI) muscles. PD participants demonstrated greater force variability, greater unintended force production in uninstructed limbs, and stronger interlimb force-force coupling relative to HYA and HOA participants, with group differences most pronounced during bimanual conditions. Whereas HYA and HOA participants generally increased force variability following removal of visual feedback, PD participants demonstrated reduced variability when feedback was removed. EMG-EMG coherence was elevated in PD across frequency bands and task conditions, while HYA and HOA participants demonstrated comparatively lower and more feedback dependent coherence patterns. Behavioral and physiological measures provided converging evidence of stronger and less adaptable interlimb coupling in PD. These findings indicate altered and less adaptable regulation of sustained force output in PD and are consistent with greater shared neural input to homologous muscles and reduced flexibility in the independent regulation of force across the limbs.

items.title: Pointing at communicative, cognitive, linguistic, and motor skills in preterm and full-term infants at 18 months.
items.abstract: Preterm birth represents a risk for vulnerability across neurodevelopmental domains. However, its impact on early communication and cross-domain associations remains underexplored. This study compared preterm and full-term infants at 18 months on communicative, cognitive, linguistic, and motor abilities, and examined associations between pointing and these skills. Thirty-nine preterm and 28 full-term infants participated. Pointing (hand, index), vocal productions (vocalizations, babbling, words), and expression modalities (unimodal gestural, unimodal vocal, bimodal gestural-vocal) were elicited using the "decorated room" task and coded with ELAN. Cognitive, language (receptive, expressive), and motor (fine, gross) abilities were assessed with the BSID-III. Preterm infants produced fewer index points, babbling, and bimodal expressions, and showed lower scores across all BSID-III scales. Only in preterm infants, index pointing significantly correlated with developmental scores, particularly cognitive and fine-motor ones. Findings highlight interconnected cross-domain developmental trajectories in the preterm population, with index pointing as a key developmental marker at 18 months.

items.title: Exploring pathways between childhood parental abuse and adulthood generalized anxiety disorder: The roles of neuroticism, extraversion, and conscientiousness.
items.abstract: Childhood parental abuse is an established risk factor for adulthood generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), but the personality mechanisms explaining this pathway are underinvestigated. Based on developmental psychopathology and triple vulnerability models, this study evaluated whether neuroticism, extraversion, and conscientiousness mediated the 18-year prospective paths from maternal and paternal abuse to adulthood GAD severity. Each abuse source was tested independently. Community adults (N = 3293) (M age = 45.61 years, standard deviation [SD] = 11.41, range = 20-86; 54.95% women; 89.7% non-Hispanic White) participated in three Midlife Development in the United States (MIDUS) study waves. A parallel latent variable mediation analysis estimated all three personality traits as mediators. Covariate-adjusted analyses controlled for age, sex, race, education, and body mass index (BMI). Random-intercept cross-lagged panel models (RI-CLPMs) and residualized-change models differentiated trait-level from within-person effects. Greater maternal, but not paternal, abuse significantly predicted higher neuroticism, which, in turn, significantly mediated the path to GAD symptoms (B = 0.051, p = .008). This effect remained significant after covariate adjustment and in unadjusted and covariate-adjusted RI-CLPMs (Bs = 0.074 and 0.060, ps < .001), though paternal abuse showed a smaller effect. Change-based mediation was attenuated (B = 0.007, p = .014). Conscientiousness and extraversion did not mediate any path. Neuroticism mediated the 18-year path from childhood maternal abuse to GAD symptoms, mainly via trait-level differences, but pre-existing personality differences are still potential confounders. Neuroticism-focused prevention approaches, possibly optimized via transdiagnostic strategies, require assessment.

items.title: Whole person health in epilepsy: prioritizing care-partner wellbeing.
items.abstract: The experiences of care-partners of people with epilepsy are complex and dynamic throughout the lifespan, yet their wellbeing remains insufficiently recognized within care systems. There is a public health need to examine and address the wellbeing of epilepsy care-partners. Utilizing the National Institute of Health (NIH) Whole Person Health framework, we present a narrative synthesis of often-overlooked challenges faced by epilepsy care-partners, along with potential strategies for improving their identification, measurement, support and advocacy. These considerations are essential to advancing a whole-person health approach that addresses the needs of both individuals with epilepsy and their care-partners as an interconnected dyad. We present a call to action for clinicians and systems of epilepsy care to invest in research and resources to improve health outcomes and wellbeing for care-partners of people with epilepsy; and to innovate epilepsy center care pathways that are inclusive of whole person health values and logic for epilepsy dyads.

items.title: Driving Simulation Methods for Assessing Post-Injury Driving Performance After Mild Traumatic Brain Injury: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Driving is a cognitively demanding task that involves the continuous integration of attention, executive control, visual processing, and motor coordination. Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) may disrupt these functions and affect driving performance during recovery. Driving simulation is increasingly used to examine post-mTBI driving performance, yet substantial heterogeneity exists in simulator platforms, task designs, and outcome selection. This scoping review characterized driving simulation methodologies used to assess post-mTBI driving performance and examined patterns of mTBI-related findings across reported outcomes. A systematic search of seven electronic databases identified 12 eligible publications between 2017 and 2026. Publications were synthesized by participant characteristics, time since injury, simulator platform, task demands, and outcomes. Across publications, mTBI-related findings were most frequently reported for vehicle control metrics, particularly lane position variability and speed regulation. mTBI-related differences were most often condition-specific, including differences during curves, hazard events, and manipulated cognitive load or dual-task conditions. Cognitive measures also demonstrated mTBI-related differences and associations to driving performance, particularly those assessing executive functioning and processing speed domains. Differences were observed across all post-injury intervals, including ≥ 15 days, with a small number of related publications reporting performance differences after symptom resolution. However, the predominantly cross-sectional evidence does not establish whether these differences persist over time within the same individuals. Findings suggest that driving simulation can provide a useful controlled method for examining functional driving performance following mTBI across varying road environments and task demands. Future work should prioritize standardizing simulator outcomes and validating simulator performance against on-road, naturalistic-driving, and crash-related outcomes.

items.title: Creating safer social media environments for body image: Evidence and research priorities for multilevel interventions.
items.abstract: Public, policy, and research interest is growing in interventions that create safer social media environments for body image. Although intervention efforts have primarily focused on helping individuals critically evaluate or manage social media, users' experiences are also shaped by parents, peers, influencers, advertisers, social norms, platform systems, and government regulation. This paper applies a social ecological framework to review emerging approaches across intrapersonal, interpersonal, organisational, community, and public-policy levels. At the intrapersonal level, media literacy, temporary reductions in use, and feed curation have produced mixed, though sometimes promising, effects. Evidence for interventions involving parents, educators, peers, and influencers remains limited, despite their potential to shape young people's social media practices and the content they encounter. Similarly, advertising labels have generally failed to protect body image, while more substantive changes to advertising content, platform design, recommendation systems, and social norms have rarely been evaluated. The effects of rapidly emerging policies and regulations on body image are also largely unknown. We identify priorities for developing and evaluating interventions at each level, including stakeholder co-design, ecologically valid trials, longer follow-ups, objective assessment of content exposure and engagement, and careful monitoring of unintended effects. Individual-level strategies remain important but cannot address the broader systems that produce and reinforce appearance pressures. Coordinated interventions across multiple ecological levels are needed to create meaningful and sustained improvements in social media environments.
