items.title: Awareness of anchoring: Intentional processes contribute to anchoring effects.
items.abstract: Judgments and decisions are highly susceptible to influence from reference points. Anchoring effects arise when a benchmark is provided prior to estimation of a target quantity, and are observed even when the anchor is ostensibly shown to be randomly generated. It is commonly assumed that anchoring is automatic and unavoidable, but very little research has directly investigated this assumption. We report five studies aiming to characterize individuals' awareness of anchors and their effects. High proportions of participants indicated that knowing an anchor would improve their estimates (Studies 1 and 3), and desired to view an ostensibly random anchor - indicating that they would use it to inform their own absolute estimates (Study 2). Anchoring was stronger for participants who indicated that they intended to use (Studies 2 and 3) or reported having used (Study 5) the anchor value to inform their estimate. We also replicated and extended a previous demonstration that anchors have a reduced effect when they are judged to be poor estimates of the target quantity (Studies 1, 3, 4). Although anchoring was not eliminated in participants who reported that they did not intend to use the anchor, or judged it to be a poor estimate, the results overall suggest a substantial explanatory role for intention and awareness in the generation of anchoring effects.

items.title: The unique contributions of negative emotionality and sleep problems to toddlers' physiological stress response.
items.abstract: Previous research has examined temperament and sleep separately with respect to their relationship to young children's physiological stress response; however, little research has jointly investigated these two constructs in relation to children's physiological stress response. Previous research also has not considered the potential contributions of individual components of children's negative emotionality to their stress response. In the present study, mothers reported on children's negative emotionality and sleep problems when children were 18 and 24 months old respectively. When children were 30 months old, saliva samples were collected prior to and after the stranger approach task to assess physiological stress response as measured by total cortisol secretion (AUCg) and cortisol reactivity (AUCi). Results showed that frustration was positively associated with AUCg. Frustration and sleep problems were also both positively associated with AUCi, and shyness was negatively associated with AUCi. No other dimensions of negative emotionality were related to AUCg or AUCi. These results highlight the unique contributions of toddlers' temperament and sleep difficulties to their stress physiology. Furthermore, these results highlight the importance of parsing out the individual components of negative emotionality when conducting temperament research on children's stress response.

items.title: Sleep in the first three years of life: Age-related patterns and predictors in a South African sample.
items.abstract: Sleep is integral to early neurodevelopment and health, yet most normative data derive from high-income, global North populations. Context-specific data from sub-Saharan Africa, and South Africa in particular, remain scarce. This study describes sleep patterns across the first three years of life in a South African sample and examines caregiver and child characteristics associated with variation in sleep outcomes. A cross-sectional online survey was completed by 340 South African caregivers of children aged 0-36 months. Sleep was assessed using items from the Brief Infant Sleep Questionnaire-Revised. Several sleep outcomes were examined across six age bands. One-way ANOVAs examined age-related differences, and multiple linear regression analyses identified caregiver and child correlates of sleep. Significant age-related differences were observed for total sleep duration, nighttime consolidation, and daytime sleep, with large effect sizes for daytime sleep. Bedtime, bedtime consistency, and sleep onset latency remained similar across the six age groups (0-3-25-36 months). Child age was the most consistent predictor of sleep outcomes. Caregiver unemployment was associated with shorter and less consolidated nighttime sleep. Second-born or later children showed more frequent night wakings and greater daytime napping. Intermediate temperament was associated with longer sleep onset latency. Age-related differences in sleep patterns during the first three years are broadly consistent with international findings, though aspects of sleep timing appear more contextually shaped. Findings provide preliminary data for South Africa and highlight the need for age-stratified, culturally sensitive sleep guidance and interventions.

items.title: Mental Health and Psychosocial Processes in Transgender and Gender Diverse Adults with Chronic Physical Illnesses: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Transgender and gender diverse (TGD) adults experience high rates of chronic physical illnesses (CPIs) and mental health difficulties, yet little is known about the psychosocial processes underlying this relationship. This scoping review aimed to map and synthesize the literature examining psychosocial factors associated with mental health among TGD adults living with CPIs. Following PRISMA-ScR and Joanna Briggs Institute guidelines, systematic searches were conducted in PubMed, PsycINFO, Scopus, and Google Scholar. Eligible qualitative and quantitative studies that investigated psychosocial processes and mental health outcomes among TGD adults with CPIs were included. Twenty-five studies met the eligibility criteria. Most were cross-sectional and focused on transgender women living with HIV. Minority stress-related experiences, including stigma, discrimination, trauma, and violence, were consistently associated with depression, anxiety, psychological distress, poorer quality of life, and reduced healthcare engagement. In contrast, social support, community connectedness, resilience, coping, mindfulness, and spirituality emerged as important protective factors. Few studies examined CPIs beyond HIV or biophysiological processes. Overall, the evidence highlights the central role of minority stress in shaping mental health among TGD adults with CPIs while revealing substantial gaps regarding diverse TGD populations, non-HIV chronic illnesses, and transdiagnostic and biopsychosocial mechanisms that should be prioritized in future research.

items.title: Parental Smartphone Use and Children's Emotional Well-Being in Everyday Family Life: Experience Sampling Study.
items.abstract: Over the past decade, smartphones have become an integral part of family life, shaping both daily routines and parent-child interactions. Although parental smartphone use in the presence of children is frequently framed as harmful through concepts such as phubbing and technoference, these constructs emphasize disruptive smartphone use and may bias interpretations toward negative effects. Moreover, most previous research has relied on cross-sectional self-report data, limiting insight into how parental smartphone use relates to children's well-being in everyday life. This study examined the associations between parental smartphone use in the presence of the child and children's affective well-being, as well as perceived threats to children's fundamental needs, using both self-reported and device-logged measures of smartphone use. Individual parents (N=131) participated in a 10-day daily diary study. Each evening, parents reported their smartphone use in the presence of a selected target child, their child's positive and negative affect, and perceived threats to their child's fundamental psychological needs. In addition, Android users who provided consent installed a mobile sensing app that continuously recorded objective smartphone use throughout the study period. Multilevel models were used to examine both within-person (day-to-day fluctuations) and between-person associations separately for mothers and fathers while controlling for day of study, weekday vs weekend, and daily working hours. Higher parental smartphone use was largely unrelated to children's affective well-being. However, mothers who, on average, reported greater overall smartphone use perceived greater threat to their child's fundamental needs. Similarly, on days when fathers reported using their smartphones more than usual, they also perceived greater threats to their child's fundamental needs. In regard to positive affect, no significant associations were found for children's positive affect perceived by their parents, indicating that parents who, on average, used their smartphones more frequently around their child did not report lower child positive affect. Regarding negative affect, fathers who reported higher overall smartphone use also reported higher child negative affect. Additionally, on days when mothers used their smartphone more than usual, they perceived their child as displaying more negative affect. None of these associations emerged when parental smartphone use was assessed using device-logged data. Taken together, these findings suggest that perceived child need threat may be linked to parents' subjective perceptions and interpretations of their smartphone use rather than to their digitally traced smartphone behavior. This discrepancy underscores the importance of distinguishing between subjective and objective assessments of parental smartphone use and highlights the need for future research that integrates children's perspectives and interactional context to clarify when and how parental smartphone use may impact children's well-being.

items.title: Multiple Sessions of Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation Combined With Squat Training Improve Lower-Limb Maximum Strength in Healthy Adult Men.
items.abstract: Yan, X, Zuo, Z, Nitsche, MA, Zhang, X, and Qi, F. Multiple sessions of transcranial direct current stimulation combined with squat training improve lower-limb maximum strength in healthy adult men. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study aimed to investigate the effects of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) combined with Squat training (ST) on lower-limb maximum strength in healthy adult men. Sixty men (age: 21.6 ± 2.1 years, height: 177.5 ± 5.3 cm, body mass: 73.1 ± 7.4 kg) were randomly assigned to 4 groups (tDCS + ST group, sham tDCS + ST group, tDCS + rest group, sham tDCS + rest group). The 6-week intervention program was implemented with biweekly sessions, totaling 12 treatment sessions, each separated by a minimum 48-hour interval. After the tDCS intervention, the ST groups performed squat exercises while the tDCS + rest and sham tDCS + rest groups sat quietly for 30 minutes. Lower-limb maximal muscle strength was measured at 4 distinct time points: preintervention (T0), 24 hours post-third week intervention (T1), 24 hours post-sixth week final session (T2), and 1 week post-entire intervention completion (T3). Key evaluation metrics were measured, including 1 repetition maximum (1RM) squat, knee extensor and flexor peak torque, and rectus femoris cross-sectional area (CSA). Significant improvements in 1RM, knee extensor strength, and nondominant rectus femoris CSA were observed in both tDCS + ST and sham tDCS + ST groups compared with the sham tDCS-only group (p < 0.05). No differences in knee strength, 1RM, or rectus femoris CSA were observed between the tDCS + rest and sham tDCS + rest groups. The results indicate that anodal tDCS combined with ST does not yield additional training benefits on lower-limb maximal strength in healthy adults when compared with ST alone.

items.title: Network Analysis of Depressive Symptoms Among Chinese Older Adults Across Different Intergenerational Support Patterns.
items.abstract: BackgroundIntergenerational support plays a crucial role in mental health in later life, yet both the heterogeneity of support patterns and the symptom-level interplay among depressive symptoms remain underexplored.MethodsUsing data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS 2020, N = 7,444), Latent Class Analysis (LCA) identified intergenerational support patterns. Network analysis and the Network Comparison Test (NCT) were utilized to estimate and compare depressive symptom networks (CESD-10) across subgroups.ResultsThree patterns emerged: Distant-Supportive (55.9%), Proximate-Interactive (24.2%), and Traditional Co-resident (19.9%). While "sadness" and "being bothered" were universal core symptoms, NCT revealed distinct structural disparities. The Proximate-Interactive group exhibited a uniquely strong "bothered-fearful" connection. The Distant-Supportive group showed pronounced "effort-cannot get going" pathways, whereas the Traditional Co-resident group displayed a stronger "bothered-trouble focusing" link.ConclusionsIntergenerational support patterns are not only associated with overall depression severity but also with differences in the network topology of depressive symptoms. Differentiated interventions tailored to specific family structures are essential for geriatric mental health.

items.title: An interpretable machine learning model integrating mucosal and cellular immunity to predict SARS-CoV-2 reinfection: a multicenter cohort study.
items.abstract: SARS-CoV-2 reinfection remains a significant public health challenge that requires accurate risk assessment across populations. Using prospectively collected data from two independent cohorts, we developed and externally validated an interpretable machine learning model for predicting symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 reinfection. The cohort comprised 1,156 adults from Wuxi and Nantong, China, with a median follow-up duration of 10 months. Reinfection occurred in 128 participants (11.1%). The model integrated eighteen clinical and immune features, and ultimately identified spike-specific nasal secretory immunoglobulin A (sIgA) and spike-specific CD4+ central memory T cells (TCM) as key predictors. Developed using the extreme gradient boosting (XGB) algorithm, the prediction model achieved an AUC of 0.835 in the internal validation cohort and demonstrated strong discrimination in the external validation cohort. SHAP analysis revealed that higher nasal spike-specific sIgA was associated with lower risk, while spike-specific CD4+ TCM cells exhibited a non-linear association with reinfection. This interpretable immune-based model provides a framework for immune-informed risk stratification, enabling better prediction and management of SARS-CoV-2 reinfection risk in settings with heterogeneous population immunity.

items.title: Transarterial endovascular treatment of tentorial dural arteriovenous fistulas: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: To quantitatively evaluate the efficacy and safety of transarterial endovascular treatment for tentorial dural arteriovenous fistulas through a systematic review and meta-analysis. A systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis were conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and Cochrane recommendations. PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched up to 10 December 2025, for studies reporting angiographic, clinical, and safety outcomes of transarterial endovascular treatment for tentorial dural arteriovenous fistulas. Pooled proportions with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using random-effects models, and heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic, τ2, and Cochran's Q test. Ten independent observational cohorts comprised 450 patients, with extractable transarterial data for 371 and outcome-specific denominators. Pooled proportions were 81.2% (95% CI, 67.2-90.1%) for complete angiographic occlusion, 89.6% (82.1-94.1%) for favorable functional outcome, and 14.5% (9.7-21.0%) for overall complications. Among 161 patients, one procedure-related death and five all-cause deaths were reported; corresponding pooled proportions were 4.7% (2.0-11.0%) and 8.8% (4.1-17.9%). Mortality estimates were influenced by continuity corrections for zero-event studies. Disease-related mortality could not be separately quantified. TAE was associated with high pooled occlusion and favorable functional outcome proportions, alongside clinically relevant complications. Overall confidence in the evidence is low because of observational designs and methodological limitations; no randomized trials were included. Comparative efficacy and safety remain uncertain.

items.title: A Target Product Profile Framework to Guide Patient-Centered Development, Regulatory Approval, and Market Access of Digital Therapeutics for Substance Use Disorders.
items.abstract: Background: Digital therapeutics (DTx) offer a scalable means of addressing persistent barriers to substance use disorder (SUD) care, including stigma, provider shortages, and geographic inaccessibility. SUD was the first therapeutic area in which the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) authorized a prescription DTx, establishing the regulatory classification under which a growing family of DTx has since reached the market. First-generation SUD DTx demonstrated clinical efficacy, opened regulatory and reimbursement pathways, and generated an empirical account of what successful translation requires beyond FDA authorization, namely, sustained engagement, clinical workflow integration, payer-aligned evidence, and affordability. Objective: The Target Product Profile (TPP), a planning framework long used in drug and vaccine development to align product design with regulatory, clinical, and market requirements from the outset, offers a practical mechanism for converting these lessons into prospective design decisions. Yet no TPP has been published for a DTx for SUD, and TPP development for therapeutic DTx remains fragmented, limited to general templates and isolated examples. As most companies do not publish their TPPs, our goal is to posit a working, public framework to guide developers. Methods: In this review, we synthesize FDA authorization summaries, regulatory guidance, implementation experience, and market-access literature to derive an evidence-informed TPP for SUD DTx, using opioid use disorder as an illustrative case. Findings and Conclusions: We specify minimum acceptable and ideal target profiles across eleven attributes and discuss how academic investigators and small businesses, already primary drivers of published TPP development, can use this framework to design DTx that reach the patients who need them.

items.title: Traditional, Complementary, and Integrative Medicine Use Among U.S. Children: National Health Interview Survey 2012 and 2022.
items.abstract: A recent report of traditional, complementary, and integrative medicine (TCIM) utilization by U.S. children found increased usage across 2007, 2012, and 2022 by age, sex, and race/ethnicity. Here, we examine cross-sectional changes between 2012 and 2022 in detail by TCIM approach and sociodemographic and health characteristics, including reports of asthma, depression, diabetes, and pain, in U.S. children aged 4-17 years. We examined overall TCIM use, use of practitioner-based TCIMs (TCIM directly provided by practitioners) and use of nonpractitioner TCIMs (TCIM not directly provided by practitioners). National Health Interview Survey (NHIS) in 2007, 2012, 2017, and 2022 asked questions on TCIM, but analyses were limited to 2012 and 2022 as they had the most comparable wording. Prevalence and variance estimates were calculated using Proc Survey Procedures in SAS software version 9.4 to account for NHIS's complex sample design. When using the TCIM approaches assessed in this study, we found that utilization among U.S. children increased from 6.4% in 2012 to 17.8% in 2022, largely driven by use of nonpractitioner-based TCIMs, which rose from 3.2% to 14.0%. Among those using practitioner-based TCIM, use specifically for pain management increased from 28.7% to 47.6%. In both years, children who were non-Hispanic, White, Female, from families with at least one college-educated adult, and reporting current depression or asthma were more likely to utilize any TCIM. Based on the TCIM approaches assessed in this study, U.S. children are increasingly utilizing TCIMs, particularly nonpractitioner approaches, mirroring similar increases in TCIM use by U.S. adults. Given the fast pace of TCIM adoption by children in the United States, future research examining the downstream impacts of these changes is warranted.

items.title: Disease-specific body composition patterns in children with cerebral palsy and spinal muscular atrophy.
items.abstract: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and cerebral palsy (CP) are severe neurological conditions characterized by neurodegeneration and non-progressive brain injury, respectively, both profoundly affecting the nutritional status in children. This observational study aimed to comprehensively assess and compare anthropometry and body composition across groups of children with SMA, CP, and healthy controls (HCs). We enrolled three age- and sex-matched groups of 40 children each: CP (Gross Motor Function Classification System IV-V), SMA (Types I-II), and HC. Anthropometry, skinfolds, and circumferences were collected, and relative z-score was calculated. Body fat percentage (BF%) was estimated using the Slaughter equation; fat mass index (FMI), fat-free mass (FFM), and FFM Index (FFMI) were calculated. One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) and robust linear regression were performed adjusting for sex, age, body mass index z-score (BMIz), epilepsy, feeding via, ventilation, and pharmacological treatment. BMIz was significantly lower in children with neurological impairment than in HC, with no difference between CP and SMA (HC: 0.04 [-0.5; 0.6]; CP: -1.8 [-4.3; -0.6]; SMA: -3.0 [-4.7; -1.2], p < 0.0001). After adjustments, SMA group showed 17.02% higher BF% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 8.27-25.78; p = 0.0003) and higher FMI (+1.37; 95% CI: 0.98-3.75; p = 0.001), compared to CP. When referenced to HC, FMI was higher in SMA and lower in CP. Lastly, SMA showed lower FFMI compared to both CP and HC. SMA is characterized by higher BF% and a marked deficit in FFM compared to CP, independently of BMIz, epilepsy, feeding via, and pharmacological treatment. Neurological impairments are associated with distinct body composition patterns, highlighting the need for personalized nutritional assessment.

items.title: Structural Ableism in Dentistry.
items.abstract: Ableism is a system of beliefs, norms and practices that privileges non-disabled bodies and minds while devaluing and disadvantaging disabled people. Disabled people experience persistent oral health inequalities, yet dentistry has largely framed disability as an individual clinical challenge rather than a structural question. In this critical commentary, we apply a structural ableism framework to dentistry and examine how dental education, research, policy and service delivery reproduce normative assumptions about bodies, communication, behaviour and eligibility for care. Drawing on a purposive, non-systematic body of scholarship from disability studies, public health and oral health, predominantly focusing on the UK context, we organise the discussion around six interconnected guiding principles: interrogating dentistry's role; resisting biomedical universalism; attending to cultural context; connecting ableism with other systems of oppression; examining upstream as well as proximate pathways; and dismantling institutional and epistemic ableism. We argue that inaccessible facilities, inflexible systems, exclusion from research and the positioning of disability as peripheral or 'special' are not merely separate access problems. They become structural ableism when they arise from, and are repeatedly sustained by, institutional rules, resource decisions and professional norms organised around a non-disabled ideal. We propose a framework for action spanning dental schools, services, policymakers, regulators, researchers, and journals. Progress requires structural as well as clinical change, developed with disabled people as partners and experts.

items.title: Cumulative work duration and multisystem health burdens among informal sandstone workers in Thailand.
items.abstract: BackgroundInformal sandstone workers are exposed to multiple occupational hazards, yet evidence on their combined multisystem health effects remains limited.ObjectiveTo examine associations of cumulative work duration, occupational factors, and health behaviors with musculoskeletal, respiratory, dermatologic, and auditory symptoms among informal sandstone workers.MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted among 92 informal sandstone workers in Northeastern Thailand. Data were collected using structured interviews covering demographic, behavioral, occupational, and health characteristics. Cumulative work duration was calculated from years of employment, months worked per year, and daily working hours. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with system-specific symptoms.ResultsMusculoskeletal symptoms were the most prevalent (89.1%), followed by respiratory (60.9%), auditory (47.8%), and dermatologic symptoms (41.3%). High cumulative work duration was significantly associated with musculoskeletal symptoms (aOR = 6.21, 95% CI = 1.02-37.76). Male workers had lower odds of respiratory symptoms compared with female workers (aOR = 0.20, 95% CI = 0.06-0.68). Higher noise sensitivity scores were significantly associated with auditory symptoms (aOR = 3.65, 95% CI = 1.73-7.70).ConclusionsCumulative occupational workload, sex differences, and noise sensitivity were associated with multisystem health symptoms among informal sandstone workers. Integrated occupational health interventions are needed to reduce long-term health risks in informal quarry settings.

items.title: Perception and satisfaction of injured workers toward rehabilitation services: A cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: BackgroundWork-related injuries pose significant physical, psychological, and economic burdens on workers, their families, and society. Rehabilitation and return-to-work (RTW) programs are essential for recovery and reintegration into the workforce. However, little is known about injured workers' perceptions of and satisfaction with rehabilitation services in Jordan.ObjectiveThis study aims to explore and compare the perceptions and satisfaction of injured employees with rehabilitation services offered by the Social Security Corporation (SSC) and evaluate their outcomes of returning to work (RTW).MethodsThis cross-sectional survey evaluated perceptions and outcomes of return-to-work and satisfaction of a random sample of injured employees in Jordan in 2022. Phone interviews were conducted by trained interviewers using a five-part questionnaire on injury and rehabilitation experiences. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and inferential tests, including independent t-tests, ANOVA, Mann-Whitney U tests, Kruskal-Wallis tests, and Spearman's rank correlation coefficient.ResultsA total of 400 injured workers were surveyed. The mean age of the respondents was 36.1 ± 10.3 years, with the majority being males (92.5%) and married (70.3%). Less than half (46.8%) received rehabilitative services. The type and cause of injury were strongly correlated with receiving rehabilitation (p < 0.001). The mean perception rating was 3.89 ± 0.49 (out of 5), and the mean satisfaction rating among those who underwent rehabilitation was 4.52 ± 0.53. Perception was significantly higher among higher-income workers and workers who had rehabilitation services. There was a positive correlation between perception and satisfaction (r = 0.328, p < 0.001). In general, 87.5% of those who were injured returned to work.ConclusionMost injured workers successfully returned to work and expressed generally positive perceptions of SSC rehabilitation services. Enhancing awareness among employers and employees about the value and benefits of rehabilitation could further improve understanding, engagement, and utilization of these services among injured workers.

items.title: Grading colorectal adenocarcinoma: interobserver agreement between American Joint Committee on Cancer and World Health Organization criteria and revisiting diagnostic challenges.
items.abstract: The current American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC8) manual grades colorectal adenocarcinoma (CRC) based on the percentage of gland formation. The World Health Organization 5th ed (WHO5) and 6th ed (WHO6) grade based on the least differentiated component; WHO6 specifies a minimum 0.196 mm2 area of the least-differentiated component away from the invasive front to merit a high-grade diagnosis. We studied the interobserver agreement and challenges among pathologists when grading CRC using the above grading systems. Five gastrointestinal pathologists reviewed 100 scanned CRC slides and graded each slide per the provided criteria in (a) WHO5, (b) WHO6, (c) AJCC8 and (d) their clinical practice. A post-survey questionnaire was also provided. The Fleiss multirater kappa among the five reviewers was similar using WHO6 (0.730, P < 0.001) and two-tiered (low vs. high) AJCC8 (0.731, P < 0.001) and was higher than WHO5 (0.655, P < 0.001) grading criteria; the agreement was substantial for all 3 grading systems. Significantly more tumours were called high-grade when using WHO6 (average: 34.4 cases) and WHO5 (average: 33.6 cases) as compared to AJCC8 (average: 11.8 cases) grading criteria (P < 0.01). All reviewers were unanimous in handling certain scenarios (e.g. discounting invasive front tumour buds with WHO grading), but were discordant on certain scenarios (e.g. assessment of stroma-rich areas). While inter-observer agreement improved with WHO6 versus WHO5, the persistent upgrading of tumours using the WHO scheme may affect treatment algorithms. Synchronization of grading criteria with validation in prospective studies with clinical outcomes is crucial.

items.title: Inverse Vaccine Nanomimics: In situ Antigen-Specific Immune Tolerance Induction for Durable Cardiac Repair Post-Myocardial Infarction.
items.abstract: Alleviating the inflammatory response by inducing immune tolerance to cardiomyocyte lysate antigens has been shown to be a promising therapeutic approach for treating myocardial infarction (MI). However, immune tolerance induced by allogeneic antigens is constrained by insufficient antigen specificity, safety risks, and transient therapeutic efficacy. Herein, we present an injectable hydrogel capable of environment-responsive, long-acting delivery of inverse vaccine nanomimics (IVNMs) to overcome these challenges. These IVNMs efficiently capture antigens released by dying cardiomyocytes through the orthogonal reaction between surface maleimide groups and antigen thiols and promote mannose-facilitated uptake by CD206-expressing immune cells, including dendritic cells (DCs). The antigens captured by IVNMs, together with the sustained release of rapamycin from IVNMs, promote the differentiation of DCs into tolerogenic DCs, leading to a persistent increase in regulatory T cells and the establishment of immune tolerance memory. In post-MI rat models, myocardial inflammation was markedly and persistently alleviated, accompanied by enhanced neovascularization and reduced fibrosis, contributing to a sustained cardioprotective effect.

items.title: Phenology drives rice-fall armyworm interactions and arthropod community dynamics through foliar volatile signaling.
items.abstract: Background Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are one of the key mediators of plant-insect interactions. Although several studies have examined the factors affecting volatile-mediated tritrophic interactions, the role of phenology in determining the effects of volatile emission is less understood, especially in rice. Currently, fall armyworm (FAW, Spodoptera frugiperda) is considered a minor pest in rice; however, changes in climatic conditions and the rapid emergence of pesticide resistance can quickly alter this status. To address this, we examined how plant phenology and FAW herbivory affect foliar volatile emissions and the associated arthropod community dynamics in rice. Results Among the phenological stages (n = 6 per treatment), the vegetative stage emitted significantly more day volatiles than the reproductive stage. FAW herbivory also induced volatile emission in rice. Furthermore, in the Y-tube olfactometer choice assays, FAW larvae preferred volatiles from the vegetative stage and undamaged plants. After normalizing volatile emissions by plant biomass, the most common volatile compounds emitted included diketone alcohol, ethylhexyl benzoate, and ethylhexanol. In the common garden experiment, more arthropods, regardless of their taxonomic status, were attracted to the vegetative stage, although they were not significantly attracted to FAW-damaged plants. In addition, Diptera was the most predominant order observed, irrespective of the treatments. Conclusion Our findings collectively show that phenology is the key driver in mediating volatile-mediated tritrophic interactions in rice. The observed phenology-driven changes in VOC emissions influence differences in arthropod attraction, suggesting ecological consequences in rice-FAW interactions and highlighting the importance of incorporating phenology into sustainable pest management strategies. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

items.title: Novel but stable endosymbionts have contrasting effects on aphid dispersal and plant feeding damage in the cereal pest Diuraphis noxia.
items.abstract: Endosymbiotic bacteria can affect many ecological attributes of their insect hosts, including (in herbivorous insects) how they interact with plants where they feed. This raises the issue of whether deliberate endosymbiont introductions could be used to decrease crop damage caused by insect pests. Here, we investigate how transinfecting Rickettsiella viridis and Regiella insecticola endosymbionts into a novel pest aphid host, the Russian wheat aphid ( Diuraphis noxia ), influences population growth, alate production, dispersal ability, and crop damage. Both the Rickettsiella (originating from pea aphids) and Regiella (from green peach aphids) were stably maintained in their new host where they had contrasting effects. Rickettsiella increased the severity of aphid feeding damage on wheat and barley, resulting in greater leaf loss, chlorotic streaking, and higher aphid populations, whereas Regiella reduced aphid population growth and the severity of feeding damage by aphids. Their effects on dispersal morphology also differed: Regiella had no detectable impact on alate incidence, while Rickettsiella consistently suppressed wing formation in small cages, and in larger mesocosms with multiple wheat plants this endosymbiont suppressed dispersal. Endosymbiont-mediated changes in feeding damage did not involve the main plant immune response pathways: transinfected and wild type aphids induced similar levels of jasmonic acid, jasmonic acid-isoleucine, and salicylic acid in plant tissues, even though these plant defenses were strongly activated during aphid feeding. Novel endosymbionts can therefore modulate the severity of plant feeding damage by aphids as well as influencing aphid dispersal. Potential applications in controlling pest D. noxia populations are discussed.

items.title: Differential impacts of early, extended-spectrum, and last-resort β-lactams on manure-derived microbiomes and resistomes in an in vitro model.
items.abstract: Understanding the environmental dissemination of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is crucial for mitigating its spread and reducing the clinical burden of resistant infections. In a previous study, we demonstrated that copiotrophic enrichment in a medium that stimulates the growth of gut-associated bacteria can reveal clinically associated bacterial populations and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) that are not detected through direct environmental sampling. In the present study, we applied this enrichment approach to poultry manure to examine how β-lactamase-resistant antibiotics (cefotaxime and meropenem) shape the composition and resistance profiles of copiotrophic, gut-like microbial community relative to an earlier β-lactam (ampicillin) and to antibiotic-free controls. Our results show that extended-spectrum and last-resort β-lactams induced more pronounced shifts in microbial diversity, resistome, and mobilome profiles compared to ampicillin. When focusing on specific taxa, such as clinically relevant enteric bacteria and both susceptible and β-lactam-resistant coliforms, differential responses were observed correlating to the antimicrobial range of action. Moreover, cefotaxime and meropenem exerted different effects on the relative abundance of enteric bacteria and plasmids harboring multiple ARGs. Together, these findings underline how the diversity of pathogen and AMR indicators in gut microbiomes may be shaped by different selective pressures imposed by β-lactamase-resistant antibiotics.IMPORTANCEThis study explores how different generations of β-lactam antibiotics shape microbial communities and antibiotic resistance in a gut-like in vitro system. Using a metabolically driven synthetic community derived from manure, we found that advanced β-lactams such as cefotaxime and meropenem led to stronger and more specific shifts in both community composition and resistance gene profiles compared to ampicillin. These results emphasize that the ecological impact of antibiotics depends not only on whether bacteria are inhibited but also on the spectrum of activity of each compound. In addition, the system we used provides a simple and controllable way to study interactions among antibiotics, microbial communities, and the resistome. Overall, this work offers a clearer ecological view of how clinically important antibiotics may influence microbiomes and the spread of antibiotic resistance genes.

items.title: Adolescent Digital Engagement and Well-being Patterns Among Spanish Youth: A Data Note on Social Media Use, Mental Health Perceptions, and Digital Well-being (SMARS, 2024)
items.abstract: The rapid proliferation of social media platforms among adolescents has generated significant concern about its implications for mental health and digital well-being. In Spain, where social network use is near-universal among minors, this intersection is especially acute given the country’s high rates of psychological disorders among young people. This article describes a dataset generated within the National R&D&i Project “Adolescent Recipients and Creators of Mental Health Content on Social Media” (SMARS, ref. PID2022-141454OB-I00). The dataset provides a comprehensive, multidimensional quantitative record of the digital lives of 1,043 Spanish adolescents aged 12 to 18, collected through a structured online survey administered between April 24 and May 6, 2024. It captures detailed information on platform usage patterns (TikTok and Instagram), content consumption preferences across 20 categories, social perceptions of digital technology impact, and validated digital well-being self-assessments. The instrument incorporates an adapted Social Perception Scale (α = 0.89) and a three-factor Digital Well-being on TikTok Scale (α = 0.79–0.83), validated through Exploratory Factor Analysis. This dataset offers a reusable, platform-specific resource for interdisciplinary research in communication, psychology, sociology, and digital health, enabling comparative studies, gender-differentiated analyses, and evidence-based digital literacy program development.

items.title: Empowerment of Islamic Religious Education Teachers through Generative AI Training for the Development of Islamic Value-Based Learning Media at SMP Negeri 35 Medan
items.abstract: The development of artificial intelligence (AI) technology, particularly Generative AI, has created new opportunities for developing innovative, interactive, and contextual learning media. However, many Islamic Religious Education (IRE) teachers still have limited competencies in utilizing this technology as a learning medium while maintaining Islamic values. This Community Service Program (PKM) aimed to improve the competence of IRE teachers at SMP Negeri 35 Medan in utilizing Generative AI to develop creative, effective, and Islamic value-based learning media. The program employed a Participatory Action Learning approach consisting of needs identification, educational sessions, practical training, mentoring, and evaluation. The training involved demonstrations and hands-on practice using various Generative AI platforms, including ChatGPT, Canva AI, Gamma AI, and Microsoft Copilot, to develop teaching materials, presentations, assessment questions, and visual learning media based on Islamic values. The results indicated an improvement in participants' understanding of Generative AI, enhanced skills in developing digital learning media, and increased awareness of the ethical use of AI from an Islamic perspective. The teachers were able to produce learning media that were more engaging, interactive, contextual, and supportive of the implementation of the Merdeka Curriculum. This program contributed positively to improving teachers' digital literacy while strengthening the integration of technology and Islamic values in the IRE learning process.

items.title: MEASURING CONSCIOUS LEADERSHIP: DEVELOPMENT OF THE TOTAL LEADERSHIP INDEX AS A 100-POINT EXECUTIVE MATURITY ARCHITECTURE
items.abstract: Leadership assessment often oscillates between subjective reputation, outcome-based appraisal and broad competency or style measures. These approaches are valuable, but they do not consistently reveal how senior leaders regulate pressure before decision, sequencing, reflection and institutional speech. This conceptual paper develops the Total Leadership Index (TLI) as a 100-point executive maturity architecture comprising four equally weighted pillars: Decision Stillness and Pressure Containment; Timing and Sequence Discipline; Structured Reflection and Root-Cause Honesty; and Governed Speech and Institutional Consequence. Each pillar contains five behaviorally anchored indicators scored from 0 to 5, producing twenty indicators and a total score from 0 to 100. The model complements personality inventories, transformational, ethical, authentic and servant-leadership scales, competency frameworks, 360-degree feedback and performance scorecards by adding a pre-decisional, evidence-governed maturity lens. Distinctive design features include evidence-before-number scoring, a pillar-profile interpretation rule, an evidence-confidence overlay, multi-source moderation, maturity bands, a provisional balance rule and red-flag safeguards. The paper proposes six testable propositions and a staged validation agenda involving expert content review, item development, exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, reliability, criterion and incremental validity, measurement invariance and longitudinal intervention studies. Practical illustrations show how TLI may support executive coaching, succession, crisis review, board oversight and public-sector governance. No empirical findings are claimed; the framework is advanced as a falsifiable research architecture whose weights, thresholds and predictive utility require cross-sector and cross-cultural testing.

items.title: Nationwide prevalence of high-risk human papillomavirus and cervical cytology findings in Chile: a registry-based study (2019-2024).
items.abstract: Cervical cancer, primarily caused by high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV), remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related death in women globally. No nationwide analysis has integrated molecular HPV testing and cervical cytology using registry-based data. The aim of the present study was to provide the first nationwide registry-based estimate of HR-HPV positivity and age-specific cervical cytological abnormalities within the Chilean National Cervical Cancer Screening Program. A retrospective descriptive analysis was conducted using nationwide aggregate data from the Chilean Ministry of Health (MINSAL), covering the nationwide cervical cancer screening network. A total of 506 712 cervical samples tested for HR-HPV (2020-2024) and 4 055 738 adequate Papanicolaou (PAP) tests (2019-2024) were analyzed. The HR-HPV positivity between 2020 and 2024 was 13.02% (95% confidence interval: 12.93-13.11%), with annual values of 12.34, 12.73, 13.27, 13.47, and 12.85% in 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024, respectively. The highest HPV prevalence was observed in G1 (30-44 years), ranging from 15.39 to 16.26%, compared with 8.95-10.55% in G2 (45-64 years) and 5.46-13.30% in G3 (≥65 years). Among all HPV-positive women, HPV-16 accounted for 19.57% of infections, HPV-18 for 6.39%, and pooled HR-HPV types for 74.03%. Regarding PAP results, 95.63% of adequate tests were classified as negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy, while low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL) (NIE I) was found in 0.77%, high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL) (NIE II) in 0.33%, and severe HSIL (NIE III) in 0.26% of cases. This nationwide registry-based study establishes the first comprehensive baseline of HR-HPV positivity and cervical cytology in Chile. The predominance of non-16/18 h-HPV infections reinforces the importance of broad-spectrum extended HPV genotyping surveillance and provides a benchmark for evaluating the long-term impact of HPV vaccination and implementation of primary HPV screening.

items.title: Digital Mental Health Supports for Young People
items.abstract: Young people across the island of Ireland are navigating rising levels of psychological distress in a context marked by long waiting lists, fragmented services, and persistent inequities. Digital mental health supports offer a promising way to expand access, but international and local evidence shows that these tools are often underused when they are not co-produced with young people or tailored to diverse cultural and social realities. As part of the larger Atlantic Futures project, this all-island research study set out to address that gap by engaging young people—particularly those experiencing marginalisation—and the staff who support them to identify needs, evaluate digital tools, and generate evidence to guide implementation. Drawing on scoping reviews, surveys, creative workshops, a co-designed Google Site, and an acceptability and implementation study with a combined number of approximately 150 marginalised young people in the ROI and NI, the project found low awareness of existing digital supports among young people but interest in accessible, relatable, and youth-centred tools. Young people emphasised anonymity, immediacy, and autonomy as key advantages of digital supports but stressed that credibility, cultural relevance, and simplicity are essential for sustained engagement. Tools backed by trusted institutions (e.g., HSE, Action Mental Health) and those reviewed by peers were perceived as most reliable. Youth participants consistently rejected overly clinical, complex, or “school-like” designs, favouring platforms that are intuitive, strengths-based, and personalised. Across methods, young people described mental health challenges rooted in structural pressures—academic stress, financial strain, stigma, discrimination, and rural isolation. Marginalised groups, including Traveller youth, migrants, LGBTQ+ young people, and those with disabilities, reported additional barriers to help-seeking. Digital tools were seen as valuable complements to traditional services, particularly where waiting lists, geography, or stigma limit access. However, young people were clear that digital supports cannot replace human connection; instead, they should form part of blended, flexible pathways that integrate online and offline care. Consultation with service providers echoed these insights, highlighting the need for evidence-based tools, strong data protection, simple navigation, and organisational training to support implementation. They also identified literacy, digital skills, and privacy concerns as barriers for young people, reinforcing the importance of low-threshold, anonymous, and accessible design. The findings from an all-island policy dialogue with key policymakers, service providers and young people underscored the absence of a unified all-island governance framework for youth digital mental health and called for coordinated, youth-led approaches to accreditation, implementation, and participation. Overall, the project demonstrates that co-produced, equity-orientated digital mental health supports can meaningfully enhance access and engagement for young people across Ireland. To maximise impact, future efforts should prioritise youth participation, cultural competence, implementation planning, and cross-sector collaboration. Digital supports must be embedded within broader mental health systems—not treated as standalone solutions—to ensure that all young people can access timely, relevant, and trustworthy care.

items.title: Joints, Camera, Action! Co-Generating 3D Motion and Video for Arbitrary Rigs
items.abstract: Video generation models can now depict remarkably realistic motion. Yet it is unclear how to use this motion beyond pixels: to animate a specific 3D asset and replay the animation in its 3D scene. For instance, a video model can show a monkey jumping over a crossbar, but it cannot return that jump as replayable 3D motion placed in the 3D scene. Here we present a model that directly co-generates the video and 3D motion for any supplied rig, along with a camera that registers this motion to the scene. Prior video-motion models either handle only human skeletons, often adding billions of parameters, or triangulate 3D motion from generated 2D pose maps. We instead keep 3D motion in a separate model that supports arbitrary skeletons, and connect it to a pretrained video model through a small set of cross-attention layers. This separation lets the motion model first learn how skeletons move from motion-only data, which is easier to obtain and augment than paired video. Additionally, our model learns to locate each joint in the video frames, which lets us recover the camera and place the 3D motion in the scene. To train across many skeletons, we use a generative video editor to place animated 3D assets in scenes suited to their actions, curating the edits so their known motion remains valid. Together with human and robot video, this yields nearly 200K training pairs. Our evaluations demonstrate that our model animates diverse rigs from text more faithfully than video-first pipelines, and its motion responds to the surrounding scene. It also turns video into rig motion, rig motion into video, and enables keyframe-based control of the 3D motion. Videos and additional results are available on our project page: https://research.nvidia.com/labs/par/projects/jca/.

items.title: GBClaw: An agentic AI framework for atomistic grain boundary research and mechanistic discovery
items.abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems hold immense potential for automating complex workflows in materials discovery and design, but extending them to domain-intensive mechanistic investigations remains challenging. Here, we present GBClaw, an agentic AI framework for investigating the structure and deformation of general grain boundaries (GBs). Although general GBs constitute the vast majority of real-world interfaces in polycrystalline materials, they remain understudied because their structural complexity and interfacial mismatch complicate experimental and modeling research. GBClaw integrates large language models (LLMs) into a modular architecture comprising an orchestrator, specialized agents, domain-specific tools, simulation interfaces, and hierarchical memory. Through dynamic replanning and iterative workflow refinement, the framework effectively connects systematic simulations with targeted mechanistic analysis. Applied to 14 general asymmetric tilt GBs in nickel, GBClaw characterized interfacial defect structures and identified diverse deformation modes across these incommensurate boundaries. Comparing boundary sliding with and without secondary GB misfit dislocations revealed substantial differences in shear strength, underscoring the critical role of defect hierarchies in sliding resistance. Furthermore, researcher-guided follow-up calculations traced an anomalously high shear resistance to metastable boundary structures. This work demonstrates that combining agentic AI with domain expertise bridges high-throughput computational screening with deep physical understanding of complex material interfaces.

items.title: UniWALM: Unified World Action Language Model for Embodied Robot Control
items.abstract: Motivated by the human ability to integrate experience across language, perception, and action, we introduce UniWALM, a unified world-action-language model that learns video, action, and language in a single shared representation, where each modality is both a conditioning signal and a supervision target. We ask: can jointly generating language enrich this shared representation, improving manipulation and supporting memory-dependent behavior? Unlike prior approaches that attach a reasoning or vision-language model to a video-action backbone and run them as distinct stages, UniWALM unifies all three modalities inside a single mixture-of-transformers backbone whose per-modality diffusion heads co-denoise synchronously, decoding subtask and textual memory in the same pass as action with no separate planning stage; the generated language is re-consumed on the next step, closing a language-as-memory loop without an external planner or memory bank. To keep the action stream reliable under this richer objective, we further introduce Flow Matching with Correction (FMC), a training objective that teaches recovery from perturbed action trajectories at no inference-time cost. UniWALM consistently improves over same-backbone baselines (e.g., FastWAM) on compositional pick-and-place (MolmoSpaces) and across the memory-dependent subset of RMBench, where it reaches 34.5% without any pretrained language or reasoning model and exceeds Mem-0's keyframe-equipped setup (28.5%) using only a single anchor frame. On a real-world Find-the-Item task, generating textual memory lifts success from 11.1% to 61.1%, while state-of-the-art VLAs stay at or below chance (<=33.3%).

items.title: Industrial ReMEmbR: Scaling Spatiotemporal Memory to Robot Fleets
items.abstract: Warehouse robot fleets continuously observe operational conditions, but preserving these observations as reusable semantic memory incurs substantial computation, communication, and storage costs. For example, explaining recurring aisle blockages can require reviewing video from multiple robots across several shifts. We present IndustrialRemembr, a shared spatiotemporal memory system that extends NVIDIA ReMEmbR to robot fleets and reduces server-side computation by generating scene descriptions only on demand. On each robot, an NVIDIA Jetson encodes video clips into retrieval embeddings with Cosmos-Embed1, vision tokens with Cosmos3-Edge, and reconstruction latents with the Wan2.2 VAE, without uploading raw camera frames. The encoding models are re-used to detect people in image patches, zeroing them out to support PII abstraction for GDPR-compliant deployments. We split Cosmos3-Edge at its vision-language boundary, placing the vision encoder on the robot and the language decoder on an on-premises server. A Nemotron agent retrieves memories by content, position, and time and queries the decoder using cached vision tokens. This design eliminates caption generation at write time, while cached-token decoding reproduces the unsplit model's output in all 450 tested decodes.

items.title: MindView: Benchmarking Generative Multi-View Spatial Intelligence
items.abstract: Spatial intelligence has recently been assessed through generative tasks such as spatially grounded image editing, yet language-guided generation of spatially consistent views from partial multi-view observations remains underexplored. We introduce MindView, a benchmark for generative multi-view spatial intelligence with 1,500 samples from 513 scenes across three indoor datasets. Its seven tasks form two families: geometry-dominant tasks specify changes in camera position and orientation, while semantics-dominant tasks require inferring target viewpoints by grounding referred objects and interpreting spatial relations and reference-frame cues. Evaluation of eleven generators reveals substantial room for improvement on MindView. A paired context analysis further shows that all eleven generators obtain lower overall scores under the expanded context setting. These findings motivate us to investigate whether task-specific supervision can improve target-view generation and whether models can use additional multi-view evidence effectively. We therefore fine-tune BAGEL on the MindView training dataset, improving its overall score by 24.3 points and yielding gains across all seven MindView tasks. Beyond these generation gains, the fine-tuned model also yields higher scores on three spatial-understanding benchmarks without training on their annotations, suggesting that learning to generate spatially grounded views may benefit spatial understanding. To improve evidence utilization under expanded context, we propose MindCue, a training-free spatial evidence selector guided by a target-view hypothesis. MindCue reverses the drop in overall score under expanded context and outperforms the standard-context baseline. Overall, MindView provides a concrete testbed for generative multi-view spatial intelligence.

items.title: Adaptive Multi-Token Prediction: How far should we go?
items.abstract: Multi-token prediction (MTP) can accelerate language-model decoding by drafting several tokens and verifying them in a single target-model pass. However, the best speculation horizon changes with context: longer drafts offer greater amortization when reliable, but can waste compute on suffixes discarded after a rejection. Unlike autoregressive drafting, where a stopping rule can decide token by token, MTP must fix the horizon before drafting, as all heads fire in the same forward pass. We therefore formulate horizon selection as an online control problem, using verification feedback to learn how far the draft can be trusted in each context, and introduce Adaptive Multi-Token Prediction (AMTP): a lightweight controller that requires no retraining and leaves the exact verifier unchanged. To guide horizon selection, we characterize the expected number of tokens committed at each horizon via acceptance survival, the probability that a draft prefix is fully accepted. Before each round, AMTP predicts how far the draft is likely to survive and picks the horizon with the highest expected tokens per second, learning freely from every verification pass. Theoretically, we show that any online learner's prediction error translates into throughput regret against the best horizon for each context, and in turn into a bound on wall-clock completion time. With online gradient descent, this regret is sublinear. Across five draft-target pairings built on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with Medusa heads, Meta's MTP models, and Qwen3-4B-Inst-2507-MTP, evaluated on AIME 2025 and GSM8K, AMTP decodes up to 4.1x faster than standard decoding and matches or outperforms the fixed window in 8 of 10 settings, with throughput gains of up to 10%.

items.title: Semantic Observability for Autonomous Systems Diagnostics
items.abstract: Modern distributed microservice deployments generate massive volumes of heterogeneous, multi-format observability logs across physically and logically partitioned infrastructure. Isolating root causes during cascading failures remains an arduous task for Site Reliability Engineers (SREs), bottlenecked by manual keyword filtering and disjointed temporal correlation across monitoring dashboards. We introduce Semantic Observability, an autonomous multi-agent framework that unifies disparate log streams into a dynamic, queryable Property Graph Database. By modeling physical infrastructure topologies, logical software dependencies, and chronological event sequences as attributed nodes and directed relations, it bridges the semantic gap inherent in flat, unstructured log repositories. Building on this unified substrate, we deploy a stateful multi-agent system orchestrated through Directed Cyclic Graphs (DCGs). The system autonomously navigates the topology, applying causal graph algorithms and temporal back-traversal to isolate the precise blast radius of anomalies. The pruned subgraph is then interpreted by a Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning engine to generate contextualized, code-level Root Cause Analyses (RCA) and actionable remediations. This paper establishes the foundational system architecture, formal relational ontology, and multi-agent control loops of Semantic Observability. We show conceptually how the framework eliminates ambient telemetry noise, reduces Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR), compresses LLM token consumption, and prevents structural hallucinations. We also specify an open-source validation framework on standard benchmarks (LogHub and Train-Ticket), laying the groundwork for a forthcoming companion paper on exhaustive quantitative evaluation and production benchmarking.

items.title: Benchmarking Arabic Dialects for Math Problems
items.abstract: Mathematical reasoning remains underexplored for low-resource languages, including Dialectal Arabic. To bridge this gap, we introduce the DAR-MGSM (Dialectal Arabic Multilingual Grade School Math) Benchmark, the first manually curated benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning in Dialectal Arabic. DAR-MGSM consists of math word problems (MWPs) requiring multi-step reasoning and covers five major Arabic dialects alongside Modern Standard Arabic (MSA). The benchmark comprises two parallel versions: translated-only and translated & culturally localized. The latter version adapts entities and references to regional varieties. We evaluate eleven Arabic-centric and multilingual large language models on DAR-MGSM. The results show that the performance generally declines on the localized version, highlighting the challenges introduced by culturally grounded adaptations. However, the magnitude of this effect varies across models, with Arabic-centric models exhibiting different levels of sensitivity to localization. A mechanistic interpretability analysis shows that translated and localized variants of the same MWPs often induce distinct internal reasoning trajectories, even when aggregate accuracy remains similar. Overall, our results show that mathematical reasoning performance depends on both linguistic variety and cultural context.

items.title: Value-Rich, Differently Organized: Measuring Value Expression and Organization in AI-Generated Debates
items.abstract: Current evaluation of LLM-generated debate largely focuses on argumentative quality, leaving the value structure of generated arguments underexamined. We introduce a diagnostic metric framework for comparing how values are expressed and organized in human-reference and AI-generated debates. The framework separates value expression, the range of recognizable values a debate invokes, from value organization, how those values are distributed and sustained across turns. Grounded in Schwartz's Basic-10 value theory, it represents debates as multi-level value distributions over argumentative units, utterances, stances, and full debates, enabling metrics for value coverage, alignment, diffusion, and cross-turn dynamics. Across multiple generation systems, AI-generated debates are broadly value-expressive, often activating as many or more value dimensions than matched human references, but they organize these values differently. Their utterances are more locally value-diffuse, and source-blind judges distinguish value clarity from value focus. These findings show that debate evaluation should consider not only value presence, but also value organization. Code and supplementary materials are available at https://github.com/Maoyuan-li/Value-Expression-and-Organization.

items.title: Turning TS2Vec into a Foundation Model for Time Series Classification
items.abstract: TS2Vec is one of the strongest self-supervised methods for time series classification, introduced in 2022. It is designed to be trained anew on every dataset: self-supervised pre-training followed by linear probing. Since then, the field has shifted towards foundation models that reuse one encoder across datasets. Yet TS2Vec offers a compact convolutional architecture that operates directly on temporal samples and accepts variable-length inputs without resampling. We ask whether these properties can be retained when the encoder is pre-trained only once, and show that they can: TS2Vec can essentially be turned into a foundation model. Three changes suffice: pre-train on a synthetic corpus, feed the encoder a raw amplitude view and an instance-normalized shape view of the input through two small stems, and distill one specialist encoder per view into a single encoder. The result, TS2Vec-FM, is a 1.6M-parameter dilated convolutional network that, kept frozen, reaches 83.3% on UCR-128 and 75.3% on UEA-27 under linear probing, within 0.3 pp of MantisV2, the current state of the art, and above TS2Vec trained separately on each target dataset. What we find most interesting is how different TS2Vec-FM is from other foundation models in design: near-parity is reached without attention, without a patch tokenizer, and without intermediate-layer extraction, using an "old-school" convolutional encoder and a two-layer MLP stem.

items.title: Evolving Agent Interfaces
items.abstract: Computer-use agents are limited by the interfaces humans give them. An agent may type a spreadsheet cell by cell when a single line of code would do, or print all two thousand lines of a file through a shell to find one function. Both the interfaces and the knowledge of when to use each are built by hand, which cannot keep pace with new applications, workflows, and models. We argue that interface design should itself be an agent capability. We introduce Agent S4, an autonomous computer-use scientist that builds Evolving Agent Interfaces from task experience. A meta-agent examines task agents' trajectories on synthetic training tasks, without success labels, and constructs and revises interfaces and usage knowledge in a repository. Population-based evolution then selects which repositories to develop further by their performance on validation tasks the meta-agent never sees, favoring changes that generalize beyond the seen tasks. On OSWorld V2, Agent S4, with Qwen3.8-27B and the evolved repository of interfaces, sets a new state of the art in open-source computer-use agents, reaching 21.3% binary score, 3.8 times the same model with fixed interfaces. This is above both GPT-5.5 (13.0%) and Claude Opus 4.8 (20.6%), at about 4.3% and 1.5% of their respective costs. On ScienceBoard, the evolved interfaces improve the success rate from 41.4% to 58.6% with the same model. These results suggest that useful interfaces can be evolved from experience, making autonomous interface design a source of improvement complementary to advances in models and harnesses. We open-source our code at https://github.com/simular-ai/agent-s.

items.title: What Do RTL Repair Benchmarks Actually Measure?
items.abstract: RTL repair benchmarks should measure whether a model can fix broken RTL given a specification. To this end, we construct and hash-bind RTLRepairDataset, 5,784 (broken, fixed) training pairs; RTLRepairBench, 459 held-out cases with 374 syntactic and 85 behavioral mutations; and an evaluation harness supporting simulation and formal equivalence. We then use this infrastructure to identify two measurement confounds. First, simulation and formal scoring give opposite signs for the apparent effect of providing a specification in one evaluated cohort; reset-aware rescoring attributes almost all of the simulation-formal disagreement to reset and first-cycle comparison semantics. Second, on 274 mined model failures, the specification-only minus specification-conditioned recovery point estimate ranges from -8.5 to +18.3 percentage points across six models. Thus, a conventional repair score need not isolate whether the model used the faulty RTL. We translate these findings into evaluation controls: report initialization, reset, first-cycle, and unknown-value semantics; disclose oracle coverage and undecided cases; and include a specification-only baseline. Together, the resources and audit provide both a benchmark for behavioral repair and a protocol for diagnosing what contributes to its measured score. We release the benchmark, the training set, construction code, sanitized aggregate evidence, and reproduction materials at https://github.com/Evaaaz/RTLRepairBench.

items.title: Capable Teacher, Myopic Scorer: Reward-Free Teacher Repair for Agentic On-Policy Distillation
items.abstract: Agentic on-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student agent on its own trajectories while a teacher scores every token. A natural explanation of where it goes wrong is compounding error: the student's mistakes carry its trajectories beyond the region where the teacher is reliable, so recent methods keep training inside that region, through episode-length curricula, teacher-guided turns, prefix replay, or teacher intervention where the two disagree. We show this explanation is incomplete. From the states where the student departs most from the teacher, the teacher's own takeovers still finish the task, yet the student trained on its token scores keeps running out of turns. We attribute this to the myopia of next-token scoring. The teacher rates each token without seeing where the episode ends, so its scores let through the safe, delaying moves that outcome-based RL would punish with zero reward, a penalty agentic OPD lacks. We call this difference between what the teacher does and what it scores the rollout-scorer gap. We propose Rollout-to-Scorer Distillation (R2S), which repairs the scorer before distillation by mining high-disagreement states from the untrained student, running teacher takeovers from them, keeping the states where enough takeovers pass a reward-free check such as consensus or an LLM judge, and fine-tuning the teacher to give its takeover-informed scores on every assistant token from the divergence turn onward, without the takeover in context. The repaired teacher is frozen as the sole scorer for standard OPD, requiring no task reward during repair or training. Across three environments, two teachers and four students, R2S outperforms three state-of-the-art agentic-OPD methods in all twelve teacher-student-environment cells, by 12.8 success points on average over the best of them in each cell. Project page: https://tree-shu-zhao.github.io/r2s/.

items.title: SceneRig: An Agentic System for Simulation-Ready 3D Scene Reconstruction from Single Images
items.abstract: Simulation is a powerful tool for robotics, but building diverse, simulation-ready scenes at scale remains difficult. Reconstructing scenes from single images is a promising alternative, but visual similarity alone is insufficient: objects must also be recovered, accurately placed, and physically grounded. Existing methods that rely on post-hoc physics settling often misplace objects, producing scenes that look correct but behave poorly under manipulation. We present SceneRig, an agentic system that turns a single image into an editable, simulation-ready scene. SceneRig combines geometric, visual, and physical tools to reconstruct a faithful 3D scene. An agent then performs edit-and-validate loops inside a physics simulator to achieve physical stability. Across diverse inputs, SceneRig improves instance segmentation, object-centric appearance, and 3D placement while keeping the reconstructed scenes physically stable. Furthermore, SceneRig is effective for downstream robotics: its scenes predict real-robot policy outcomes more accurately than the baseline method and more reliably support replay of recorded manipulations without trajectory adaptation.

items.title: Beyond the Sequentiality Bottleneck: A Hybrid Diffusion-Autoregressive Framework for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning
items.abstract: Autoregressive models (ARMs) face a "Sequentiality Bottleneck" in reasoning, while diffusion language models (DLMs) offer parallelism but lack semantic coherence. To addresses both limitations, we propose Collaborative Reasoning Asymmetric Learning (CoRAL), a hybrid framework via an Asymmetric Planner-Executor (APE) architecture: a DLM Planner generates K diverse reasoning trajectories in parallel, while a large ARM Executor selects the optimal plan and synthesizes the final answer. To train the Planner effectively, we introduce Reward-Guided Denoising for CoT (RDC), which integrates outcome-based rewards into the diffusion process to steer it toward goal-directed reasoning. Experiments on vision-language benchmarks show that CoRAL significantly outperforms prior diffusion-based methods and achieves competitive performance against strong ARMs, achieving both superior efficiency and quality.

items.title: Spatially Informed and Direction Sensitive Representation Learning for Spatial Transcriptomics
items.abstract: Cellular states are shaped by both intrinsic gene expression programs and the spatial microenvironment in which cells reside. Spatial transcriptomics makes this context measurable, but effective representation learning requires capturing both spatially informative molecular signals and intercellular organization. Existing approaches address these challenges only partially: conventional gene selection can overlook spatially structured signals, while methods for encoding cell-cell relationships often either reduce a cell's microenvironment to proximity alone, discarding direction, or rely on absolute coordinates tied to an arbitrary tissue frame. Consequently, cells with similar neighbor distances but distinct spatial organization may receive overly similar representations, despite experiencing different biological contexts that shape their cellular states. We introduce Tessera, a spatial representation learning framework that addresses both molecular selection and cellular context. Tessera combines spatially informed gene selection with a geometric inductive bias that contextualizes each cell within its local tissue environment. By modeling relative cell-cell relationships, Tessera is translation-invariant while preserving direction, allowing neighboring cells to contribute differently according to their spatial context and cellular state. Across held-out tissues and technologies, Tessera outperforms existing spatial foundation models in representation quality and generalizes zero-shot to contexts up to $16\times$ larger than those seen during training.

items.title: Sage-A1.5: From Long-Horizon Execution to Scientific Exploration with Capability Composition
items.abstract: In this report, we introduce Sage-A1.5, a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model that builds on A1 to advance long-horizon problem solving through adaptive capability composition. Compared with A1, Sage-A1.5 learns not only to solve individual tasks, but also to organize work and revise its approach during execution. Sage-A1.5 highlights three improvements: agentic orchestration, verification, and open scientific discovery. First, agentic orchestration extends single-agent execution through task delegation and parallel collaboration among subagents with isolated contexts, enabling complex tasks to be decomposed and addressed concurrently and supporting efficient execution while reducing interference across concurrent subagents. Second, agentic verification strengthens long-horizon reliability through progress checking, evidence validation, and reflective strategy revision, allowing the agent to recognize unproductive search paths and pursue alternative approaches. Third, open scientific discovery extends agentic capabilities beyond answering predefined questions to conducting exploratory research, connecting scientific inquiry with interactive analysis and inspectable research artifacts. We showcase these capabilities through complicated agentic tasks and multidisciplinary scientific applications. Besides, we hope Sage-A1.5 provides the community with an accessible foundation for open scientific discovery, offering a practical path from long-horizon task execution to collaborative, verifiable, and inspectable scientific exploration.

items.title: Evolving Semantic Indexes for Generative Retrieval
items.abstract: Generative retrieval (GR) casts search and recommendation as autoregressive generation of discrete semantic identifiers (SIDs). SID design largely determines GR quality, but its discrete, interdependent components (SID construction, collision handling, decoding, and training) cannot be optimized end-to-end with gradients and remain largely hand-designed. We introduce a framework that improves these components through LLM-driven evolutionary program search, to our knowledge the first application of this approach to GR. A locally served, open-weight 31B model mutates executable GR components, so no proprietary LLM API is used, and a 1M-parameter proxy decoder provides fast feedback in place of repeatedly training the 1B target generator. Across 21 SID programs on NQ320K, proxy and target Recall@100 show strong rank correlation (Spearman $ρ= 0.90$). Guided by this proxy, evolution improves the seed GR on NQ320K, MSMARCO300K, and a multilingual e-commerce dataset under a fixed training recipe. On NQ320K, jointly evolving SID construction and collision handling improves Recall@1 from 55.8% to 59.3% and Recall@100 from 85.8% to 90.6%. A component study shows that proxy reliability depends on what is evolved: improvements transfer reliably for the semantic index but not for the generator's training objective or the full pipeline. LLM-driven evolutionary search is thus a practical tool for GR design, provided proxy reliability is established for the chosen search space.
