items.title: An automated, open-source pipeline for anti-virulence compound discovery: multi-target molecular docking with Z-score specificity filtering
items.abstract: Background: Salmonella infections pose a severe threat to global public health and livestock production, while the antimicrobials used to control them drive the emergence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Anti-virulence compounds are an attractive alternative, and structure-based virtual screening is an efficient route to find them. In practice, however, docking screens rank candidates by absolute predicted docking score, so their output may be dominated by uninhibited ligands that bind many unrelated protein surfaces. Open software that selects on binding specificity rather than on absolute docking score is not readily available to microbiologists. Results. We present an automated, open-source pipeline that couples multi-target molecular docking to a two-tier statistical specificity filter. The pipeline retrieves and curates compound libraries from PubChem by chemical abstracts service (CAS) numbers, with automatic desalting and size-based exclusion of polymers. Also, it builds three-dimensional ligands at a user-defined protonation state with Open Babel. It docks every ligand against every member of a protein panel with Smina, centering each search box on a pocket detected by fpocket and converts the resulting absolute docking score matrix into per-compound Z-scores, retaining only pairs that are both a strong absolute docking score (≤ −8.0 kcal mol⁻¹) and selective by standardized relative docking score (Z ≤ −1.5, cross-panel standard deviation > 1.5). Applied to 381 generally recognized as safe (GRAS) food additives and the Salmonella-associated structures, it returned 22 compound-target pairs. Riboflavin ranked highest, with S = −10.3 kcal mol⁻¹ and Z = −2.6 against the type III secretion system (T3SS) chaperone SigE. Conclusions. Ranking on standardized relative docking score rather than on absolute docking score gives a transparent way to remove uninhibited binders from a virtual screen. The pipeline is modular, configurable for any ligand library and protein panel, and openly released. The candidates it returns are computational predictions and require experimental validation.

items.title: Between the Spectrum and Mental Health: A Narrative Review of the Relationship between Autism Spectrum Disorder and Neuropsychiatric Comorbidities
items.abstract: Individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) present a high prevalence of neuropsychiatric comorbidities, particularly anxiety disorders, depression, and Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). These conditions substantially intensify the clinical, functional, and psychosocial challenges associated with the autism spectrum across the lifespan. This study aimed to analyze, through a narrative review of the literature, the association between ASD and these comorbidities, as well as their impacts on mental health, daily functioning, and overall quality of life. The literature search was conducted in the PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases, prioritizing recent and methodologically relevant studies addressing this topic. The findings indicate that symptomatic overlap between core ASD features and co-occurring psychiatric disorders complicates early identification, differential diagnosis, and clinical management. This overlap often leads to delayed treatment and suboptimal outcomes, underscoring the need for integrated, developmentally sensitive, and personalized diagnostic and therapeutic approaches. In addition, the literature highlights significant structural barriers, including a shortage of trained specialists, limited access to multidisciplinary services, and the lack of targeted public policies, all of which hinder the provision of adequate care for this population. In conclusion, multidisciplinary interventions, combined with social inclusion strategies, community-based support, family and caregiver guidance, and the promotion of neurodiversity, are essential to improve emotional well-being, functional autonomy, and quality of life for individuals with ASD. Such efforts also have a positive impact on families and caregivers, contributing to more equitable and effective mental health care.

items.title: Cost-Effectiveness Analysis of Ivonescimab Plus Chemotherapy versus Tislelizumab Plus Chemotherapy as First-Line Treatment for Advanced Squamous Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Chinese Healthcare Perspective
items.abstract: Abstract Background Ivonescimab is a novel bispecific antibody targeting programmed death-1 (PD-1) and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), showing promising antitumor activity in combination with chemotherapy for advanced squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients who previously untreated as first-line treatment. However, the cost-effectiveness of this regimen remains unknown. Methods A partitioned survival model with three health states was developed based on the HARMONi-6 clinical trial to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of ivonescimab plus chemotherapy (Ivo-Chemo) versus tislelizumab plus chemotherapy (Tis-Chemo) from the Chinese healthcare perspectives. Clinical efficacy was estimated using reconstructed individual patient data from the trial. Costs and utilities were derived from the literature and public databases. The primary outcome was the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) per quality-adjusted life-year (QALY) gained. One-way, and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were conducted to assess model uncertainty. Results In the base-case analysis, Ivo-Chemo was associated with a total cost of $50,959.04 and accrued 2.77 QALYs over the 15-year time horizon, compared with $27,589.99 and 1.77 QALYs for Tis-Chemo. The ICER was $23,366.05/QALY in China, lower than the respective willingness-to-pay (WTP) thresholds ($41,859.05). One-way sensitivity analysis identified the cost of ivonescimab, patient weight and utility of progressed disease as the most influential parameters. Probabilistic sensitivity analysis demonstrated a high probability of cost-effectiveness, at 99.83% in China. The subgroup analysis indicated that there was potential cost-effectiveness regardless of the patient's programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression level or the presence of liver metastasis. Conclusion Ivonescimab plus chemotherapy was likely to be cost-effective at current pricing and WTP thresholds in China.

items.title: Spatiotemporal Clustering of Tuberculosis Incidence and Identification of Hotspots in Bobonaro Municipality, Timor-Leste: A Five-Year Ecological Study (2021–2025)
items.abstract: Abstract Background : Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major public health challenge in Timor-Leste, with important geographic variation in disease burden. Identifying spatial patterns at the sub-municipal level may support geographically targeted surveillance and control. Methods: We conducted an ecological spatiotemporal study using aggregated notifications of new pulmonary TB cases from 50 sucos in Bobonaro Municipality from January 2021 through December 2025. Annual TB incidence rates were calculated per 10,000 population using annual suco population estimates. Empirical Bayes smoothing was applied to reduce instability associated with small-area populations. Global Moran's I was used to assess annual spatial autocorrelation using a first-order queen contiguity spatial-weights matrix with row standardization. Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA) with false discovery rate (FDR) correction were used for years with significant global spatial autocorrelation. Getis-Ord Gi_ analysis was used as a complementary hotspot assessment. Results : A total of 1,440 new TB cases were notified during 2021-2025. Municipal crude incidence ranged from 18.9 to 38.6 per 10,000 population, with the highest incidence in 2023. Global Moran's I showed no statistically significant evidence of spatial autocorrelation in 2021 (I=0.152, p=0.051), 2022 (I=0.094, p=0.202), or 2025 (I=0.123, p=0.102). Significant positive spatial autocorrelation was detected in 2023 (I=0.239, p=0.003) and 2024 (I=0.251, p=0.002). LISA identified three significant Low-Low (LL) clusters in 2023 located in Lebos, Lontas, and Guda, and one Low-High (LH) spatial outlier in Male-Ubu. In 2024, one High-High (HH) cluster was identified in Bobonaro, together with three LL clusters in Gildapil, Lontas, and Deudet. Conclusion : TB incidence in Bobonaro Municipality revealed temporal heterogeneity in spatial dependence, with significant global clustering concentrated in 2023 and 2024. Local spatial analysis can support identification of priority areas for surveillance and targeted TB-control activities. Spatial clusters should be interpreted as geographic associations in reported incidence rather than direct evidence of transmission between neighboring sucos.

items.title: Socioeconomic status and high impact chronic pain among adults in the United States: analysis of the 2016 National Health Interview Survey
items.abstract: Abstract Background: High-impact chronic pain(HICP) is chronic pain that limits life activities, affecting about 8% of adults in the United States(U.S.). Nonetheless, determinants of HICP are not fully understood, particularly regarding socioeconomic status(SES). It is important to clarify the relationship between SES and HICP. Objective: To assess the impact of SES on the presence of HICP among adults in the U.S. Methods: This was a cross‑sectional analysis of the 2016 National Health Interview Survey(NHIS) data targeting adults aged ≥18 years in the U.S.. Participants presenting HICP were compared to participants presenting no HICPto describe the relationship between SES and HICP. HICP was defined as pain occurring regularly during the past 3 months which limits life activities. The NHIS dataset provided information on sociodemographic characteristics, socioeconomic characteristics, and the possible presence of HICP in each individual. Data collected were analysed using SPSS software V27.0 where crude and adjusted odds ratios (OR) were derived and used to statistically describe the association. Associations were considered statistically significant when the 95% confidence interval did not include 1. Results : A total of 32,980 participants were included, with females (18,010; 54.01%) and adults within 18-64 years old (75.72%) comprising the majority. The prevalence of HICP was 9.42%. After adjustment, lower SES remained independently associated with higher odds of HICP. items.title: Study protocol for a hybrid type III effectiveness-implementation evaluation of the Detecta-APS strategy for organized breast and cervical cancer screening in Brazilian primary health care
items.abstract: Abstract Background: Organized breast and cervical cancer screening is a key strategy to expand access to early detection, reduce inequalities, and decrease mortality. In Brazil, however, the prevailing model remains opportunistic, with weaknesses in the systematic identification and monitoring of the target population, as well as limitations in follow-up. To address these challenges, coordinated actions will be implemented to support the transition from opportunistic to organized cancer screening in the North and Northeast regions of the country. These actions comprise DETECTA-APS, a multifaceted implementation strategy designed to support primary health care teams and evidence-informed decision-making for cancer screening. The present protocol was developed to: (1) analyze barriers and facilitators to the implementation of organized breast and cervical cancer screening; (2) evaluate the effectiveness and implementation outcomes of the DETECTA-APS strategy, and its effects on cancer screening practices; and (3) inform iterative, context-sensitive adaptations of the DETECTA-APS strategy to address implementation determinants and improve outcomes. Methods : This study protocol a hybrid type III effectiveness-implementation evaluation uses a multi-methods design involving patients, health professionals, managers, and the implementation team. Qualitative methods will be used to identify implementation determinants, guided by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR). Effectiveness and implementation will be assessed using a combination of quantitative (pre-post evaluation) and qualitative methods, guided by the RE-AIM framework, CFIR, with adaptations mapped using FRAME-IS. Participatory methods will then be employed to inform necessary adjustments to the DETECTA-APS strategy. Discussion: Reporting this study protocol is important for ensuring transparency, methodological rigor, and reproducibility in the evaluation of complex implementation strategies in primary health care within the public health system. The protocol outlines a structured and context-sensitive approach to examining barriers and facilitators to the organization of breast and cervical cancer screening, assessing the implementation process of the DETECTA-APS strategy, and informing context-sensitive adjustments to improve access, follow-up, and care organization. The findings will provide evidence to inform decision-making by health managers and policymakers regarding the implementation of organized screening strategies, considering regional specificities prior to scale-up.

items.title: Spatio-Temporal Patterns and Distribution Characteristics of Human Brucellosis in Xinjiang, China, 2018–2024
items.abstract: Abstract Background Human brucellosis remains a significant public health concern in Xinjiang, China, where spatial heterogeneity and complex ecological factors contribute to its persistent burden. Understanding the spatiotemporal dynamics of the disease is critical for optimizing prevention and control strategies. Methods The analyses included temporal trend assessment using the Theil–Sen slope estimator and Mann–Kendall trend test, global and local spatial autocorrelation analysis, hot spot analysis, and standard deviational ellipse analysis to characterize spatial distribution patterns and epidemiological features. Results The incidence of human brucellosis showed a significant overall upward trend despite interannual fluctuations, reaching a peak in 2023 and remaining at a relatively high level in 2024. Local spatial autocorrelation revealed persistent high–high clustering in northern and eastern Xinjiang and low–low clustering in southern Xinjiang. Hot spot analysis identified localized high-incidence areas with temporal variation, mainly concentrated along the northern slopes of the Tianshan Mountains, the Ili River Valley, and the Altay region. Standard deviational ellipse analysis indicated changes in spatial dispersion and directional distribution over time, while the weighted mean center remained in northern Xinjiang. Conclusion Human brucellosis in Xinjiang showed a significant overall upward trend and persistent spatial heterogeneity during 2018–2024, with hot spots mainly concentrated in northern Xinjiang. These findings support region-specific surveillance and targeted interventions for brucellosis prevention and control.

items.title: Determinants of Complementary Food Handling Practices in Conflict-Affected Tigray, Ethiopia: A Qualitative Exploration
items.abstract: Abstract This study aimed to determine complementary food handling practices among mothers/caregivers of children aged 6–59 months in conflict-affected Tigray, Ethiopia: The role of structural conditions, WASH Insecurity, and health-system factors. This is community-based exploratory qualitative study was conducted from March to April 2026 to explore factors shaping safe food-handling practices among mothers/caregivers of children aged 6–59 months in conflict-affected Tigray, Northern Ethiopia. A total of eleven in-depth interviews (IDIs), three focus group discussions (FGDs), and ten key informant interviews (KIIs) (41 individuals) were conducted with mothers or caregivers. The purposive sampling technique was used to include study participants based on their potential relevance in delivering a wealth of information. Thematic analysis were used to code and grouped into related families and synthesize the qualitative data. Discussions and interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed into the local language "Tigrigna," then translated into English and thematically coded using ATLAS-ti v.7.5.4 software. Mothers/caregivers actively want to practice proper hygiene of food preparation and handling for children and be completely educated on the risks to prevent cross-contamination. However, they acute lack of clean, safe water, lack the material resources, such as refrigeration, separate kitchens, soap, and affordable fuel, and reducing the time and capacity they can dedicate to meticulous, hygienic infant feeding practices, to put into practice. Therefore, mothers are forced to rely on dangerous proxy-feeding habits, such as storing leftover foods without refrigeration and based on sight and smell to see if food has spoiled and use unclean, unsafe water. The majority of health care providers (HCPs), especially general public health, family health, and health officers, have some knowledge of safe food handling practices, recognize its importance, and provide specific components of safe food handling practices interventions. However, these services are often delivered in a fragmented manner. Complementary food handling practices among mothers/caregivers of young children in conflict-affected Tigray are formed by a complicated matrix of structural, environmental, and socio-political determinants. While mothers/caregivers own baseline knowledge regarding food hygiene, their ability to execute safe practices is systematically constrained by severe WASH insecurity, poverty, and displacement. Handling strategies such as using wood ash for cleaning, relying on ambient-temperature food storage, and avoiding food waste at all costs represent rational adaptations to severe resource scarcity. Addressing food safety in post-conflict and humanitarian settings requires moving beyond individual behavior-change education toward structural enabling strategies that restore the physical, economic, and institutional environments necessary for safe child care.

items.title: Exploring the Underlying Causes and Contextual Determinants of Suicide Among Adolescents Under 19 Years of Age in Dezful, Iran: A Qualitative Study (2024–2025)
items.abstract: Abstract Background Suicide is a major global public health concern and one of the leading causes of death among adolescents worldwide. Despite the increasing prevalence of suicidal behaviors among young people, limited evidence exists regarding the contextual and sociocultural factors influencing adolescent suicide in southwestern Iran. This study aimed to explore the underlying causes and contexts of suicide among individuals under 19 years of age in Dezful, Iran. Materials and Methods This qualitative study was conducted in 2024–2025 using purposive and convenience sampling methods. Thirty-one participants were recruited, and data were collected through in-depth semi-structured interviews. All interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed manually using an inductive–deductive thematic analysis approach. Data collection continued until thematic saturation was achieved. Measures to ensure rigor and trustworthiness were applied throughout the study. Results Nine major themes emerged from the analysis: family violence and domestic adversities, identity crises, poverty and economic hardship, psychiatric disorders and emotional distress, substance abuse, emotional trauma and maladaptive interpersonal relationships, sociocultural pressures and social harms, spiritual and religious crises, and structural and systemic challenges. The findings revealed that adolescent suicide is a complex and multidimensional phenomenon shaped by interacting psychological, familial, social, economic, and cultural factors. Conclusions The findings underscore the urgent need for comprehensive and culturally sensitive suicide prevention strategies targeting adolescents. Policymakers and healthcare authorities should strengthen educational, psychosocial, economic, and legal support systems to create safer and more supportive environments for young people and reduce the burden of adolescent suicide.

items.title: Physical Activity Among Muslim Women in Majority and Minority Settings: A Systematic Review of Barriers and Facilitators
items.abstract: Abstract Purpose Physical activity (PA) is central to health and wellbeing, yet the physical activity participation of Muslim women remains understudied in the global public health literature. This mixed-methods systematic review aimed to assess the perceived barriers and facilitators to PA among Muslim women in Muslim-majority and Muslim-minority settings. Methods A systematic search of EBSCO, PubMed, and Google Scholar identified qualitative and quantitative studies (2000–2024) involving Muslim women aged 18 years and older, quality-appraised using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP) for qualitative designs and the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) for quantitative studies. Qualitative findings were analysed thematically and mapped onto the five levels of the Socioecological Model (SEM) to examine cross-level interactions; quantitative results were synthesised narratively. Results Eleven studies (nine qualitative, two quantitative; N = 816 women aged 18–55) across eight countries were included. Three themes were identified: modesty, visibility, and the absence of safe space; gatekeeping by family and community; and infrastructure, climate, and policy neglect, operating through compounding SEM-level mechanisms. Facilitators included religious motivation, health awareness, family support, and culturally tailored programming; barrier-facilitator configurations varied between Muslim-majority and Muslim-minority contexts. Conclusions A context-sensitive, multi-level, tailored approach is essential to promote physical activity among Muslim women. Faith-sensitive, gender-segregated initiatives that simultaneously address structural, organisational, and community factors offer the most promising pathway for equitable participation and wellbeing.

items.title: Metagenomic Characterisation of Antimicrobial Resistance Gene Profiles in Shrimp Farm, Pond Microbiomes From the Southern Coastal Areas of Kerala, India
items.abstract: Abstract Aquaculture is the fastest growing animal protein production sector in worldwide and Asia contributing annually with about 90% of the global seafood production. Penaeus monodon commonly known as the giant tiger prawn is a marine crustacean that is widely reared for food. The global rise in antibiotic resistance vitalised by indiscriminate antibiotic usage presents a significant public health challenge. The detrimental impact of antibiotic resistance includes the persistence of antimicrobial residues in fish and the surroundings. It gradually leads to the accumulation of resistance genes with the consequent contamination of the environment and the human food chain. There is a scarcity of data regarding the antibiotic resistance of shrimp aquaculture farms and ponds in Kerala. In the present study the metagenomic analysis revealed the occurrence of AMR genes across the southern coastal areas of Kerala, India. The pooled shrimp gut, water and sediment samples were subjected to metagenomic analysis. The antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes were determined by various databases like RGI (Resistance Gene Identifier) and the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD).In addition to this, KEGG and COG databases revealed the important biochemical pathways, cellular functions and specific protein ortholog of bacterial and archaea genomes of the studied locations. The outcomes imply noticeable regional differences in presence of AMR genes in the shrimp gut, sediment and water samples of the different southern coastal areas of Kerala.

items.title: Equity and access in maternity care during Kenya’s transition from free maternity care to social health insurance: a mixed-methods study in Homa Bay County
items.abstract: Abstract Background Social health insurance is promoted as a pathway to universal health coverage, yet its equity effects during implementation remain poorly understood. We examined Kenya's 2024 transition from free maternity care (Linda Mama) to the contributory Social Health Insurance Fund (SHIF), focusing on maternal healthcare access in Homa Bay County. The study was nested within a larger maternal health research programme (C-it DU-it) established before SHIF, providing a rare opportunity to examine the major health financing reform as it unfolded. Methods Using a convergent mixed-methods design, we combined longitudinal survey data from 300 pregnant women followed from first antenatal care (ANC) contact to six weeks postpartum, including patient cost surveys at three ANC visits and one postnatal visit, as well as interviews and focus group discussions involving 124 pregnant and recently postpartum women recruited separately from the survey cohort, alongside healthcare providers, community health workers, and policymakers. Results SHIF enrolment increased from 46.0% (138/300) at first ANC to 84.5% (234/277) by six weeks postpartum, indicating many women gained coverage only after early pregnancy care. Enrolment was lower among adolescents and unemployed women, reflecting barriers related to identification documents, digital registration, premium payments, and gendered decision-making. Enrolled women were more likely to complete four ANC visits (75.5% vs 41.9%), receive recommended ANC tests (46.6% vs 27.9%), and deliver in a public facility (79.1% vs 51.2%). However, out-of-pocket payments persisted regardless of enrolment, while many lower-level (Levels 2–3) facilities were excluded from SHIF reimbursement eligibility, undermining financial protection and access in rural areas. Conclusions SHIF's early implementation reproduced, and in some cases amplified, existing inequities in maternal healthcare access, particularly for adolescents, women lacking identification documents, and users of lower-level facilities. Achieving equitable maternal coverage under SHIF will require not only enrolment, but timely and continuous coverage, effective reimbursement of lower-level facilities, and monitoring of exclusion, enrolment timing, and continuity. Without these safeguards, health financing reforms risk widening existing inequities.

items.title: Evaluation of the cervical cancer surveillance system in Kigali City, Rwanda: a descriptive cross-sectional study, January 2023–June 2025
items.abstract: Abstract Background Cervical cancer remains a major public health problem, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Rwanda has strengthened cervical cancer prevention through HPV vaccination, screening, and digital surveillance systems. However, the performance of the cervical cancer surveillance system in Kigali City has not been systematically evaluated. This study assessed the performance of the cervical cancer surveillance system in Kigali City, Rwanda, from January 2023 to June 2025. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional evaluation was conducted using the CDC Updated Guidelines for Evaluating Public Health Surveillance Systems. Primary data were collected from 41 purposively selected healthcare providers using a structured questionnaire, while secondary data were extracted from 19923 cervical cancer screening records. The system was assessed across seven attributes: simplicity, flexibility, acceptability, timeliness, stability, usefulness, and data quality. Descriptive statistics were used to calculate attribute-specific performance scores, classified as fair (50–69%), good (70–79%), or very good (≥80%). Results Among 19,923 women screened, 13,693 (68.7%) underwent HPV DNA testing and 6,230 (31.3%) underwent VIA. Overall, 728 (3.7%) women had positive screening results. HPV positivity was 14.7% among women tested for HPV, while VIA positivity was 11.7% among women screened by VIA. Only 34.1% of HPV-positive women returned for VIA triage. The surveillance system demonstrated very good performance in usefulness (91%), data quality (88%), timeliness (87%), stability (85%), and acceptability (84%), while simplicity (76%) and flexibility (71%) were rated as good. Overall, the surveillance system demonstrated good to very good performance across all evaluated attributes. Conclusions The cervical cancer surveillance system in Kigali City demonstrated good to very good performance, particularly in usefulness, data quality, timeliness, stability, and acceptability. However, the high loss to follow-up among HPV-positive women and moderate system flexibility may compromise its effectiveness. Strengthening follow-up mechanisms, standardizing case definitions, improving the system's adaptability, and enhancing the training and capacity of healthcare providers could improve surveillance performance and support Rwanda's cervical cancer elimination goals.

items.title: Avoiding Data Leakage in Machine Learning Models for Diabetes and Hypertension Classification Using Routine Occupational Health Screening Data
items.abstract: Abstract Background and Aim: Reliable clinical prediction using machine learning requires leakage-free model development, yet this critical methodological concern is often overlooked. Type 2 diabetes and hypertension represent major public health challenges in Iran, and early identification of at-risk individuals using routine workplace health screening data could enable cost-effective prevention. This study had a dual objective: first, to develop and validate machine learning models for identifying diabetes and hypertension using routine occupational health screening data; and second and more critically to demonstrate how the inclusion of outcome-defining predictors (fasting blood glucose and blood pressure) artificially inflates model performance through data leakage, a methodological pitfall often overlooked in clinical prediction studies. By comparing 'full' models (with all predictors) against 'clinically meaningful' models (excluding outcome-defining variables), we provide empirical evidence of the magnitude of this bias and offer a transparent framework for avoiding it in similar studies. Methods A retrospective cross-sectional analysis was conducted on 370 health screening records. Five algorithms Decision Tree, Ridge Classifier, Logistic Regression, XGBoost, and Random Forest were developed and compared. Two modeling strategies were implemented: (1) a full model including all predictors, and (2) a clinically meaningful model excluding outcome-defining predictors (fasting blood glucose and blood pressure). The dataset was split into 80% training and 20% testing sets. Five-fold cross-validation was used for hyperparameter optimization, and SMOTE was applied solely to the training set to address class imbalance. Performance was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, AUC-ROC with 95% CI, calibration plots, and Brier scores. Feature importance was assessed using SHAP values. Results The prevalence of diabetes and hypertension was 18.4% (68 cases) and 20.5% (76 cases), respectively. In the clinically meaningful models that excluded outcome-defining predictors (fasting blood glucose and blood pressure), discrimination performance was moderate, with Random Forest achieving an AUC-ROC of 78.34% (95% CI: 72.15–84.92) for diabetes and 76.81% (95% CI: 70.23–83.45) for hypertension. In contrast, when these predictors were included in the full models, performance was artificially inflated (Random Forest AUC-ROC: 96.22% for diabetes and 94.59% for hypertension), confirming substantial data leakage. XGBoost performed comparably in both approaches. SHAP analysis identified age, BMI, waist circumference, and psychological distress (GSI) as the most important non-outcome predictors. Conclusion After excluding outcome-defining predictors to prevent data leakage, machine learning models particularly Random Forest and XGBoost showed moderate but clinically realistic discriminative ability for identifying diabetes and hypertension using routine screening data. Psychological variables contributed meaningfully to prediction, supporting integrated physical and mental health screening in occupational settings. External validation in independent cohorts is required before clinical implementation.

items.title: Epidemiological and Nutritional Factors Associated with Tuberculosis in the Kamina Health Zone, DRC
items.abstract: Abstract Introduction Tuberculosis remains a major public health problem, particularly in low-income countries, where malnutrition and certain socio-epidemiological factors increase the risk of disease. This study aimed to identify the epidemiological and nutritional factors associated with tuberculosis in Kamina. Methods A case-control study was conducted from February to September 2024 in three diagnostic and treatment centres. The cases comprised 41 patients with tuberculosis, matched with two controls without tuberculosis each (n = 82). Data were collected using structured questionnaires and KoboToolbox/ODK. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 23 and included the chi-square test, odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and multivariable logistic regression, with statistical significance set at p Results The mean age of cases was 29.4 ± 14 years, and most were male (75.6%). Epidemiological and nutritional factors significantly associated with tuberculosis were low educational attainment, current smoking, contact with a person with tuberculosis, and the absence of an adequate diet. The predictive model showed good performance, with an ROC area under the curve of 0.83. Conclusion This study highlights the importance of epidemiological and nutritional factors in tuberculosis risk. Identifying these local factors may help guide context-appropriate prevention and nutritional care interventions.

items.title: Prediction of growth and nutritional status using circumference measurements among preschool children in Jalpaiguri West Bengal India
items.abstract: Abstract Introduction: Undernutrition remains a major public health challenge among preschool children in low- and middle-income countries. Conventional anthropometric measures are widely used to assess nutritional status due to simple, non-invasive, and low-cost alternatives. However, population-specific cut-off values, particularly for chest circumference, are largely unavailable among Indian preschool children. Aim: The present cross-sectional study assessed the utility of head circumference (HC), chest circumference (CC), and mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) for predicting undernutrition and derived optimal cut-off values among 1,240 preschool children (625 boys and 615 girls) aged 2-5 years from ICDS centres in Jalpaiguri district, West Bengal, India. Anthropometric measurements were recorded following standard protocols, and nutritional status was evaluated using WHO 2006 Z-score criteria. Results: Binary logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analyses were employed to determine predictive accuracy and optimal cut-offs using the Youden Index. The prevalence of undernutrition ranged between 13.79% for wasting, 24.43% for stunting, 25.00% for underweight, 25.32% for low HC for age, and 25.40% for low MUAC for age, with higher deficiency observed among girls. All circumference measures increased significantly with age and exhibited sexual dimorphism. The CC emerged as the strongest predictor of underweight and stunting, while MUAC demonstrated superior accuracy in identifying wasting. Optimal cut-off values ranged from 45.5-47.9 cm for HC, 48.0-49.3 cm for CC, and 13.4-14.0 cm for MUAC. Conclusion: These findings highlight the effectiveness of circumference-based anthropometric measures as reliable screening tools for undernutrition. HC, CC, and MUAC can serve as practical screening measures for childhood undernutrition. CC may complement MUAC, particularly for identifying underweight and stunting.

items.title: Optimizing the Chain of Survival: European OHCA Outcomes and Reporting Standards—A Scoping Review
items.abstract: Background: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains a major public health challenge across Europe. While prehospital emergency medical services (EMS) vary widely, the degree to which regional infrastructure, dispatch guidance, and community responder frameworks influence clinical outcomes when mapped against standardized reporting templates remains insufficiently synthe-sized. This scoping review evaluates European OHCA evidence across standardized Utstein re-porting domains to analyze prehospital system factors, responder interventions, and clinical out-comes. Methods: Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines and Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology, a systematic literature search was performed across PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science (January 2021–March 2026). From 8,882 records identified, 2,126 full-text articles were evaluated using a Population, Exposure, Outcome (PEO) framework. Data were synthesized across four core Utstein domains. Results: Forty three primary studies (N = 43) were included. System Factors demonstrated that prolonged ambulance response intervals severely diminish survival, particularly in sparsely populated rural sectors. Dispatch Protocols highlighted that rapid dispatcher recognition signifi-cantly increases telephone CPR instructions and community resource activation. Under bystander a prominent gap was identified between public AED availability and actual lay bystander deployment (< 5%). Dispatched Volunteer Community Responders (VCR) and First Responders (FR) achieved median arrival time-gains of 4–5 minutes; however, survival benefits were descriptively observed primarily when early arrival facilitated ultra-early defibrillation or high-quality CPR. Clinical Out-comes confirmed that 30-day survival and favorable neurological recovery (CPC 1–2) remain highly variable, heavily constrained by reporting heterogeneity. Conclusions: Strengthening early links in the chain of survival—specifically dispatcher recognition, app-alerted volunteer dispatch, and public defibrillation—is consistently associated with improved clinical survival. Universal adoption of the updated Utstein 2024 reporting template is essential to eliminate reporting heterogeneity and enable meaningful cross-system benchmarks across Europe.

items.title: Real-World Effectiveness of Direct-Acting Antivirals in Mexican Patients with Chronic Hepatitis C: A Multicenter Study by Cirrhosis Status
items.abstract: Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection remains a major global health burden, potentially leading to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) have improved treatment outcomes, achieving high sustained virologic response (SVR) rates. However, real-world evidence from Mexico remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate DAA effectiveness in Mexican patients with chronic HCV infection and compare outcomes according to cirrhosis status. A retrospective, multicenter cohort study was conducted across five public healthcare institutions in Mexico. We included 253 patients who received DAA therapy. The primary outcome was SVR, defined as undetectable HCV RNA after treatment. Clinical, demographic, and treatment-related variables were analyzed, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Overall, SVR was achieved in 94.5% of patients. Among those with cirrhosis (54.1%), the SVR rate was 95.6%, compared with 93.1% among those without cirrhosis (p = 0.536). Patients with cirrhosis were older and had longer treatment durations, while baseline viral load and genotype distribution were comparable. Treatment completion was high (94.1%), with low discontinuation rates and no significant differences by cirrhosis status. DAAs were highly effective in Mexican patients with chronic HCV infection, regardless of cirrhosis status. Expanding access to diagnosis and treatment is essential to reduce disease burden and achieve hepatitis C elimination goals.

items.title: Availability and Access to Cardiovascular Medicines in Mozambique: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are a leading cause of mortality worldwide, with more than 80% of deaths occurring in low- and middle-income countries. In Mozambique, non-communicable diseases account for approximately 28% of deaths, with CVDs contributing substantially to this burden. Despite the country’s hierarchical health system and the World Health Organization target of 80% availability of essential medicines, access to cardiovascular medicines remains poorly documented. This scoping review mapped the availability, prices, affordability, physical access, and health-system barriers affecting access to essential cardiovascular medicines in Mozambique. The review followed the PRISMA-ScR guidelines and the Arksey and O’Malley framework. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were systematically searched without publication-year restrictions. Eligible studies assessed the availability, stock-outs, prices, affordability, or health-system barriers related to cardiovascular medicines and diagnostics in Mozambique. Study selection and data extraction were independently performed by multiple reviewers. Consistent with the scoping review design, formal risk-of-bias assessment was not undertaken. Fifteen studies met the inclusion criteria. Essential cardiovascular medicines showed persistently low availability, with mean availability of approximately 21% across public hospital pharmacies, private retail outlets, and private hospitals, substantially below the WHO 80% target. Public facilities consistently provided only a limited range of older first-line medicines, while second- and third-line medicines, statins, digoxin, direct oral anticoagulants, and diagnostic reagents were frequently unavailable. When public stocks were depleted, patients relied on private-sector purchases, where generic medicines cost an average of 4.51 times international reference prices. Long-term secondary prevention could require 14.0–17.8 days of wages per month for low-income workers. These barriers were associated with low hypertension awareness, treatment, and control, substantial target-organ damage, high stroke case-fatality, and poor anticoagulation control. Access to cardiovascular medicines in Mozambique is severely constrained by low availability, frequent stock-outs, and unaffordable private-sector prices. Strengthening medicine selection, supply-chain management, financial protection, and decentralized protocol-based care is essential to improve equitable access to cardiovascular treatment.

items.title: From evidence to impact: reflections on the SPECTRUM Consortium’s work on the commercial determinants of health
items.abstract: The SPECTRUM Consortium (Shaping Public hEalth poliCies To Reduce ineqUalities and harM) was a UK Prevention Research Partnership-funded, multi-university, multi-agency consortium that worked between 2019 and 2025 to shape public health policy and practice on non-communicable disease prevention and the commercial determinants of health (CDOH), focusing on tobacco, alcohol and foods high in salt, sugar and fat. Guided by a Theory of Change and an associated Impact Framework, SPECTRUM organised its work around three interconnected impact pathways: Engagement and Knowledge Exchange, SPECTRUM Research, and Research Landscape. This article reflects on the Consortium’s experience of pursuing impact across these pathways, using the Impact Framework to structure both an account of activities and outputs and a critical assessment of what worked well, what fell short, and what this suggests for future research consortia. Effective strategies included embedding knowledge brokers within policy organisations, sustained co-production with public involvement panels and citizens’ juries, and the development of shared analytical tools and conceptual models that strengthened the emerging field of CDOH. Persistent challenges included the absence of systematic monitoring and evaluation of impact, uneven integration across work packages, and tension between the pace of policy windows and the time needed for rigorous research. Reflecting across all three pathways, the Consortium found that the Theory of Change worked well as a tool for aligning stakeholders at the outset but was underused as an instrument for ongoing evaluation once the programme was under way. The experience points to the value of treating impact frameworks as evolving hypotheses rather than fixed blueprints, and of investing deliberately in structural mechanisms, such as embedded knowledge brokers and dedicated evaluation capacity, rather than relying on individual researcher effort alone to sustain the relationships and systems through which policy-relevant, cross-disciplinary research on CDOH generates impact.

items.title: Palliative Care in Surgery: Updated Research Priorities from the Surgical Palliative Care Research Expert Consensus Conference.
items.abstract: Background Surgical palliative care (SPC) research has advanced since the 2017 research agenda, but persistent gaps in patient selection, intervention delivery, and outcome measurement limit implementation across evolving surgical care settings. Study design In November 2025, a national consensus conference convened 28 SPC experts and researchers. Through iterative discussion and consensus-building during the meeting and subsequent months, participants updated research priorities across the surgical continuum and health system context. Full methodology and participant attributes were described in Supplemental Materials https://links.lww.com/JACS/A821. Results The updated agenda identified 11 research gaps across 3 priority areas: patient selection; interventions, care processes, and competencies; and outcome measurement. Priorities were mapped at 2 levels: surgical episodes, encompassing patient-, family-, and provider-level factors, and health systems, encompassing organizational and structural factors affecting SPC delivery. The agenda prioritizes identifying which patients benefit from SPC and when; broadening SPC beyond traditional populations; defining primary SPC competencies and the role of specialty consultation; improving communication of surgical intent, trade-offs, and preference-sensitive decisions; integrating and sustaining SPC across heterogeneous systems and care transitions; transforming clinical cultures; and developing patient-centered, context-specific surgical and systems-level outcomes. Emerging electronic health record, natural language processing, and large language model approaches may support scalable patient identification, intervention delivery, and outcome measurement, while requiring attention to bias and task-dependent performance. Conclusions SPC research should move beyond narrow proof-of-concept settings toward pragmatic, scalable approaches that define who should receive SPC, what should be delivered, and how success should be measured across diverse surgical environments.

items.title: Advancing colorectal cancer management through clinical proteomics: from genotype to proteotype toward clinical translation.
items.abstract: Introduction Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the leading causes of cancer death worldwide, with outcomes depending on the stages at diagnosis. Genomic and transcriptomic classifications are largely inferential because the genotype-phenotype relationship is non-linear and is influenced by post-translational regulation, protein turnover, and the tumor microenvironment (TME). Proteomics measures this functional layer directly. Areas covered This review surveys proteomic technologies for CRC emphasizing mass spectrometry, affinity- and aptamer- based multiplex platforms, post-translational modification proteomics, spatial proteomics, AI-driven structural and predictive analysis, and multi-omics integration. Each platform is evaluated based on clinical questions, the supporting evidence and the barriers to implementation. Literature was drawn primarily from PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus (2020-2026), emphasizing advanced and translational applications. Expert opinion Alongside approved blood cfDNA and stool-RNA molecular tests, proteomics is a functional complementary technology that may improve biological interpretation, assay triage and treatment response prediction, although prospective clinical utility remains to be established. The decisive barriers are standardized biospecimens, validation evidence, clinical utility data and interoperable public data sharing.

items.title: Cobertura da triagem neonatal biológica no Brasil e fatores associados, 2014-2023: estudo de séries temporais
items.abstract: Biological newborn screening (BNS), known as the “heel prick test,” is a vital public health strategy for the early diagnosis of treatable congenital diseases. This ecological time-series study analyzed BNS coverage in Brazil between 2014 and 2023 based on data from DATASUS. Trends were assessed using Prais-Winsten regression, and the correlation between coverage and indicators such as adequate prenatal care, hospitalizations in children under 1 year of age, mortality, and HDI was verified. National coverage increased from 73.75% to 83.28% (APC = 1.06%). The South region had coverage above 90%, whereas the North had coverage below 70%. There was a strong correlation between coverage and adequate prenatal care (r = 0.93) and a moderate correlation with hospitalizations and neonatal mortality. HDI was not significantly associated. Despite the progress, regional inequalities persist. These findings highlight the need for targeted policies, better integration of health services, and equity-oriented strategies to achieve universal BNS coverage in Brazil.

items.title: Digital media engagement and its relationship with depression severity
items.abstract: Introduction Throughout the pandemic, social media became the new newspaper, and the widespread information created a vulnerable state for the user. The study's goal is to determine the presence of depression in the Czech Republic's local population as well as how the use of media correlates with depression in the Czech population. Methodology A web-based interviewing technique was employed. A longitudinal study method was employed, and the data were collected in 5 waves. In each wave, the population varied in number: 2,192 (2020), 2,164 (2021), 1,717 (2022), 1,707 (2023), and 2,072 (2025), and listwise 1,120 participants participated in all 5 waves. The trend analysis of depression using PHQ-5 and MUQ was calculated for the years (2020–2023 & 2025). Results Total PHQ mean scores rose progressively from 7.41 ( SD = 3.02) in 2020 to 8.60 ( SD = 3.58) in 2025. Correlation analyzes revealed distinct, wave-dependent patterns across media engagement dimensions. Component 2 (Interactive Content and Reader Comments) demonstrated the most consistent positive correlation with depressive symptoms across all waves ( r = 0.233 to 0.305, p < 0.01, moderating it r = 0.147, p < 0.01 in 2025). Component 3 (Emotional Impact and Media Stress) was positively correlated with depression during active crisis years ( r = 0.069 to 0.125, p < 0.01 from 2020 to 2023) but exhibited a negative correlation in 2025 ( r = −0.268, p < 0.01). Component 1 (Economic Reporting and Serious News) maintained weak or non-significant associations throughout the study period ( r = 0.011 to 0.055). Conclusion The results indicate that Emotional reactivity is significantly correlated with media-related depression, while interactive content has a variable multiplier effect, and analytical news has a low direct effect. Public health interventions should prioritize emotional regulation, media literacy, and affective platform design to curb population-level mental health declines.

items.title: A novel Artificial Intelligence enabled framework for automated audio visual speech in noise evaluation
items.abstract: Presbycusis, or age related hearing loss, affects over 430 million individuals worldwide. Despite the widespread use of hearing aids, users frequently report persistent difficulties in noisy, multi talker environments. A critical discrepancy exists between conventional audio only (AO) clinical assessments and the complex, multimodal nature of real world communication. This research addresses this gap through the development and validation of a novel AI powered audio visual speech in noise (AVSIN) evaluation framework designed to simulate ecologically valid communicative scenarios. To facilitate the development of this framework, essential resources were established in the form of two custom designed audiovisual corpora: a structured dataset of IEEE sentences and a naturalistic, free flowing conversational corpus. These datasets served as the foundational ground truth for both perceptual assessments and the training of machine learning models. Validation of the AVSIN framework was conducted through extensive intelligibility testing with normal hearing and hearing aid users. Results indicated a statistically significant improvement in speech recognition thresholds (SRT) in AV conditions compared to AO, with an absolute AV benefit of 7.1 dB (p < 0.001). To automate this evaluation, a novel deep learning (DL) based intelligibility metric was developed. This model demonstrated superior predictive accuracy, achieving a predicted intelligibility score of 58.0% that was identical to the human ground truth (58.0%). This performance significantly surpassed conventional metrics such as STOI, which underestimated intelligibility at 46.9%. Beyond intelligibility, the framework integrates an objective assessment of cognitive load (CL). A multimodal fusion approach was implemented, combining pupillometry with non invasive radio frequency sensing. This combination provided a robust indicator of CL, with the fusion model achieving a strong overall Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.84 between the physiological modalities. To further align the framework with patient needs, data driven social media analysis was employed to map population level sentiment. This spatio temporal analysis validated the clinical relevance of the framework by quantifying real world patient sentiment regarding service disruptions and hearing technology limitations. In conclusion, this thesis presents a unified, interdisciplinary platform that successfully bridges the gap between subjective clinical testing and real world utility. By integrating deep learning predictions, physiological sensing, and ecological datasets, the AVSIN framework establishes a robust standard for the next generation of user centred, multimodal hearing assessment.

items.title: From AI-Assisted Performance to Independent Thinking: A Framework for Developing Higher-Order Thinking with Generative AI in Higher Education
items.abstract: In an AI-supported task, a student may explain a weak comparison once it has been identified, yet fail to notice a similar problem without a reminder. A decision about further help therefore needs evidence about what the student did without being prompted. We examine such decisions in English-medium university argumentation and evidence evaluation. The framework brings together English-language work on scaffolding, learner-generated reasoning, metacognitive calibration, and cognitive offloading. We distinguish help that supplies a reason from help that initiates a check. Readiness to work without the first does not establish readiness to work without the second. Coding examples and boundary cases make evidence about these functions interpretable, while six conditional propositions connect reconstruction and regulation to adaptation and transfer. A proposed experiment gives every group comparable diagnostic practice but varies whether teachers use its results to adjust assistance. This comparison isolates the value of using the evidence from learning through the diagnostic task itself. We relate the account to four GenAI approaches and illustrate it with a hypothetical sociology lesson. Help may be retained or restored when a new task requires it. The framework and coding rules need validation, particularly beyond the language and disciplinary settings considered here.

items.title: Paradigma Belajar dan Pembelajaran: Tinjauan Teoritis dan Psikologis
items.abstract: This study examines learning and instructional paradigms from a theoretical and psychological perspective. The aim of the study is to understand how classical and modern learning theories can be integrated with students' psychological aspects, resulting in a more comprehensive learning paradigm. The research method used is a literature study by analyzing various academic literature related to learning theories (behaviorism, cognitivism, humanism, and constructivism). The results show that each theory has a significant contribution to educational practice, but also has limitations when applied partially. Behaviorism emphasizes behavioral reinforcement, cognitivism emphasizes internal mental processes, humanism emphasizes personal needs, while constructivism emphasizes the active involvement of students in constructing knowledge. In addition, psychological factors such as intelligence, attention, interest, talent, motivation, attitude, and readiness have been shown to significantly influence learning effectiveness. The integration of learning theories and psychological understanding allows for the creation of a learning paradigm that is more adaptive, humanistic, and relevant to the demands of the digital era. Thus, this study confirms that learning success is determined not only by theoretical foundations, but also by the psychological condition of students and the educator's strategy in creating a conducive learning atmosphere.

items.title: The Association Between Socioeconomic Status and Academic Achievement Mediated by Psychological Factors
items.abstract: This narrative literature review proposes an integrative dual-pathway model to explain how socioeconomic status (SES) shapes academic achievement through interacting psychological mechanisms. Drawing on allostatic load theory, central executive functioning, self-efficacy, and learned helplessness, the model identifies two interconnected routes: a cognitive depletion pathway, in which allostatic load overburdens the prefrontal cortex and constrains limited working memory resources; and a motivational pathway in which low self-efficacy and repeated failures develop into learned helplessness that undermines motivation for learning. Crucially, these pathways do not operate independently but dynamically reinforce each other. Cognitive depletion undermines motivational beliefs, while diminished motivation reduces cognitive engagement, forming a self-reinforcing downward cycle. This integrated framework offers a more ecologically valid understanding of educational inequality than single-factor explanations. Practical implications suggest that educators should implement integrated interventions that simultaneously reduce extraneous cognitive load (e.g., scaffolded instructional sequences) and foster self-efficacy (e.g., process-oriented feedback) to break this bidirectional cycle. As the proposed model remains theoretical, future empirical research using longitudinal and experimental designs is required to validate its causal pathways and inform evidence-based educational policies.

items.title: From AI labels to trust: cognitive pathways linking authenticity judgments, risk perception, and trust in AI-generated videos
items.abstract: Background The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) has raised concerns regarding the authenticity and trustworthiness of synthetic media. Although AI disclosure labels are increasingly used as transparency mechanisms, the cognitive processes through which these cues influence trust formation remain unclear. Objective This study aimed to develop and test a cognitive pathway model explaining how AI disclosure labels, authenticity judgments, perceived risk, cognitive processing styles, and literacy factors shape trust toward AI-generated videos. Methods A 2 × 2 between-subjects experiment was conducted with 617 participants randomly assigned to four conditions involving AI-generated instructional videos with different AI label and video quality combinations. Participants evaluated authenticity, systematic and heuristic processing, trust, perceived risk, adoption intention, sharing intention, AI literacy, and media literacy. Regression, bootstrapped mediation, and moderation analyses were performed. Results AI disclosure labels significantly reduced perceived authenticity but did not directly affect trust, adoption, sharing intention, or perceived risk. Trust formation occurred through cognitive pathways: systematic processing increased trust, whereas heuristic processing reduced trust. Authenticity enhanced trust and lowered perceived risk, with perceived risk mediating the authenticity–trust relationship. Trust positively predicted adoption and sharing intentions, while AI and media literacy moderated selected relationships. Conclusion Trust in AI-generated videos was not directly determined by transparency labels alone. Instead, the observed associations among authenticity judgments, perceived risk, information processing, and trust were consistent with a multi-stage cognitive interpretation, although the cross-sectional post-exposure measurement of these constructs does not establish their temporal or causal sequence.

items.title: Social support processes link gratitude and well-being across cultures and over time
items.abstract: Abstract Strong evidence shows that gratitude enhances well-being, though the mechanisms driving these effects are unclear. Here, we test the idea that gratitude may enhance well-being by (1) attuning people to the support that they receive and boosting perceptions of social support and (2) promoting support provision. Using data from over 148,000 participants across two studies, we explore the mechanistic roles of perceived social support and support provision in linking gratitude to well-being. With both cross-sectional and longitudinal data, we find that social support processes—especially perceived social support—partially mediate the link between gratitude and well-being. Moreover, we find evidence of weaker associations between gratitude and social support provision in more collectivistic countries. This suggests that gratitude’s consequences for social support processes—and their implications for well-being—may depend upon local cultural norms about community and social support.

items.title: The rise of super-emotional intelligence
items.abstract: The debate about the future of artificial intelligence (AI) runs along a single axis: cognitive capability and its projected culmination in superintelligence. We argue that this framing leaves a complementary axis unexamined and propose the goal of Super-Emotional Intelligence (SEI): systems that perceive, model, regulate, and respond to affect better than skilled human experts, while remaining human-centered. SEI is a performance construct realized by a functional architecture, not a claim about machine experience, and we give measurable criteria for each of its four capacities. Today's affect-aware AI, from multimodal emotion recognition to empathic chatbots, recognizes, or simulates emotion at or below human level and is judged against human ceilings. Three things would set SEI apart: perception that adds peripheral and contactless physiological channels, none of them emotion-specific, but some, like the vestigial ear muscles, resolving affective processing at the timescale of the events that evoke it; a generative model of affect grounded in active inference rather than pattern matching; and functional allostatic self-regulation. The decisive gap in current systems is architectural. A sensed state conditions a prompt, but nothing carries a state estimate across turns, models the effect of the system's own responses, or selects actions under an explicit objective. We specify such a closed loop, state the conditions under which it is stable and steerable rather than manipulative, propose a preregistered validation plan whose failure would falsify our claims, and treat governance as a design constraint of the loop rather than an afterthought.

items.title: The Mechanisms Through Which Social Media Marketing Influences Purchase Intentions among Generation Z Consumers
items.abstract: As the Z-generation (born between 1997 and 2012) is gradually reaching adulthood, this group has become the main driving force in the current and future global consumer market. Understanding how social media marketing influences their purchasing decisions is a key market direction that the industry is focusing on. This article systematically examines the mechanism by which social media marketing affects the purchasing intentions of the Z-generation, with a particular focus on the roles and pathways of key opinion leaders (KOLs), key opinion consumers (KOCs), and live-streaming sales. The study reveals that social interaction and trust building are the core psychological mechanisms driving purchasing intentions - the professionalism and social appeal of the merchants' agents stimulate the audience's emotional attachment and imitative behavior, which in turn positively influence the brand purchase intention. The high-traffic content produced by these agents aligns with the values of the Z-generation, providing the emotional compensation that this group finds difficult to obtain in school and at home, thereby inducing impulsive consumption. At the same time, the trust relationship driven by social interaction is inherently fragile. Account scandals or trust breakdowns can quickly erode the accumulated consumer credit and company marketing assets. Based on this, this article proposes references from three aspects: content design, long-term trust relationship building, and values-driven marketing, to construct a research report on the consumption tendencies of the Z-generation.

items.title: Editorial: Psychological dynamics in knowledge management: cognitive, emotional, and social influences
items.abstract: Liu, Yang, and Gao (2026) extend this cognitive lens from the individual mind to the information environment. Their study of online emergencies shows how anchoring, representativeness, and availability heuristics shape cognitive bias through adaptive expectations and implicit attributions, with meaningful differences across demographic groups. In digital knowledge environments, therefore, the problem is not only whether information reaches people, but how context frames what appears credible, memorable, and actionable. KM must concern itself with the quality of sensemaking, not merely the quantity of information circulated.From cognition, the collection moves naturally to the emotional and relational conditions of knowledge sharing. Zhang and Xu (2024) show that psychological capital is connected to knowledge sharing through emotional intelligence and psychological safety among e-commerce practitioners. Their findings position hope, optimism, resilience, self-efficacy, emotional regulation, and interpersonal safety not as peripheral "soft" variables, but as resources that help determine whether knowledge is exchanged. Bai (2025) adds a leadership perspective, demonstrating that transformational leadership supports employee career growth partly through knowledge sharing, while self-efficacy and psychological capital shape the strength of these relationships. Together, these studies make a clear point: people share what they know when they feel capable, supported, and safe enough to do so.The next contributions ask what happens when knowledge must be mobilized under pressure. Wu, Lai, and Li (2025) show that pilots' personal knowledge management capability is positively associated with career resilience, with safety behavior acting as a partial bridge between knowledge capability and resilient functioning. Their nonlinear findings for safety climate and work pressure are equally important: supportive conditions can strengthen adaptation, but "more" is not always "better." Knowledge becomes valuable when it is translated into disciplined action within an appropriate psychological and operational climate.At the team level, Yang and Suntrayuth (2025) make this translation especially visible. Drawing on knowledge creation and dynamic capability perspectives, they show that team knowledge dynamics contribute to resilience through communicative, leadership, interpretive, and analytical capacities. Knowledge creation alone is insufficient; teams must discuss, interpret, judge, and enact what they know. Resilience, in this sense, is an emergent achievement of collective cognition and coordinated action.Wang, Zhang, and Zhao (2025) then carry the argument to the organizational level. Their study of technology-oriented small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) identifies a learningresilience pathway through which strategic human resource management supports innovation. Organizational learning builds knowledge; resilience enables adaptation; together they help convert human resource practices into innovation. Yet the inverted U-shaped role of environmental dynamism reminds us that psychological and knowledge capabilities are always contingent. When turbulence becomes excessive, established routines and capabilities may no longer be enough.Across these seven papers, three themes converge. First, psychological dynamics are not antecedents sitting outside KM; they are part of the mechanism through which knowledge is acquired, interpreted, shared, and applied. Second, KM is best understood as a multilevel process: cognitive control and personal resources scale into interpersonal exchange, team sensemaking, resilience, learning, and innovation. Third, context matters. Task demands, leadership, psychological safety, safety climate, digital information fields, human resources (HR) systems, and environmental dynamism can enable knowledge to become action-or distort and constrain that translation.The agenda opened by this Research Topic is therefore both practical and intellectually demanding. Future work should connect levels of analysis more deliberately, combine selfreport evidence with longitudinal, behavioral, neurocognitive, and digital-trace methods, and examine whether psychological mechanisms travel across occupations, cultures, and technologies. This is especially important as artificial intelligence (AI) becomes embedded in knowledge work: the central question will not only be what AI can capture or generate, but how human attention, emotion, trust, agency, and social interaction shape what people accept, share, challenge, and ultimately use.The enduring message of this collection is simple: knowledge does not manage itself. Between information and intelligent action stands the human mind in a social world. Understanding that space is essential if KM is to become more adaptive, resilient, and genuinely useful.

items.title: Epistemic trust, mentalizing and extremist attitudes in a German community sample
items.abstract: Introduction While extremist attitudes, here conspiracy mentality, antisemitic attitudes, and the ideological support of violence, are typically studied in political or sociological psychological contexts, their investigation in relation to clinical psychological concepts may offer additional insight with respect to underlying psychological mechanisms. In this study, we aimed to explore the relation between self-reported extremist attitudes and epistemic trust, mistrust, and credulity, as well as mentalizing. The different epistemic stances as well as difficulties in the ability to mentalize are assumed to represent non-pathological individual variations in psychological vulnerability and resilience. Methods This questionnaire study investigates the relationship between levels of epistemic trust, mistrust, and credulity, assessed via the Epistemic Trust, Mistrust and Credulity Questionnaire, mentalizing deficits assessed via the Mentalization Questionnaire and endorsement of extremist attitudes (antisemitic attitudes assessed via 2 items of the model questionnaire on right-wing extremism by the German Federal Agency for Civic Education, conspiracy mentality assessed via the Conspiracy Mentality Questionnaire, and violence supporting attitudes assessed via the Violent Extremist Attitudes Scale) in a German community sample (N = 566). Due to scarcity in empirical research on these concepts, we took an exploratory approach to investigate potential associations using structural equation modeling. Self-indicated presence of a mental disorder and participants` gender were integrated into the model. Results Epistemic mistrust and all extremist attitudes were positively related via mentalizing deficits; as was the marginally significant negative association between epistemic trust and conspiracy mentality. No other indirect effects of epistemic trust or credulity on extremist attitudes reached significance. Presence of a mental disorder was associated with epistemic credulity, epistemic mistrust, and mentalizing deficits, but not with extremist attitudes. Female gender was associated with higher epistemic trust and lower antisemitic attitudes as well as lower endorsement of violence supporting attitudes. Conclusion Exploratory findings should inspire future longitudinal or experimental research on the investigated constructs to identify whether they might be promising candidates to reduce extremist attitudes in the general population. Moreover, gender-specific mechanisms seem of relevance and need to be further explored.

items.title: The Influence of Cultural Differences on the Neural Mechanisms of Risky Decision-Making
items.abstract: Risky decision-making is an important cognitive process involved in financial, health-related, social and everyday decisions. Previous research suggests that individuals from different cultural backgrounds may differ in risk preference, information processing, and the evaluation of probability and potential outcomes. However, cultural differences cannot be understood solely through behavioral outcomes because similar choices may result from different cognitive and neural processes. This paper reviews research on the relationship between culture, risky decision-making, and the neural systems involved in risk processing. Existing evidence suggests that culture may influence risky decision-making by shaping information processing, self-construal, and the subjective evaluation of probability, reward and loss. These influences may further affect how common neural systems involved in value evaluation, reward processing, uncertainty and cognitive control process information. However, culture should not be viewed as a deterministic factor because substantial individual differences exist within cultural groups. Overall, cultural experience appears to function as an important modulator of the cognitive and neural processes underlying risky decision-making.

items.title: СОЦІАЛЬНО-КОГНІТИВНІ НАСЛІДКИ РІЗНИХ ТИПІВ ЦИФРОВОЇ АКТИВНОСТІ: РИЗИКИ ТА РЕСУРСИ САМОРЕГУЛЯЦІЇ
items.abstract: Вступ. У статті розглянуто проблему впливу цифрових технологій на соціально-когнітивний розвиток особистості в умовах тотальної цифровізації. Актуальність зумовлена стрімким зростанням часу взаємодії з цифровими пристроями, раннім початком їх використання та суперечливими даними щодо наслідків цього впливу. Мета роботи − проаналізувати особливості впливу цифрових технологій на соціально-когнітивний розвиток особистості (переважно дітей, підлітків та молоді) з урахуванням типу цифрової активності, вікового періоду залучення та ролі рефлексивних стратегій саморегуляції. Наукова новизна полягає в авторському теоретичному узагальненні диференційованого характеру впливу цифрових технологій. Виокремлено три взаємопов’язані групи чинників: 1) тип цифрової активності (активна, цілеспрямована взаємодія сприяє розвитку окремих когнітивних функцій, тоді як пасивне споживання фрагментарного контенту пов’язане зі зниженням когнітивних показників); 2) віковий період залучення до цифрового середовища; 3) наявність рефлексивних стратегій саморегуляції, які виконують компенсаторну функцію. Запропонована рамка має характер теоретичного узагальнення. Висновки. Аналіз літератури свідчить про амбівалентний вплив цифрових технологій: активне цілеспрямоване використання може сприяти розвитку окремих когнітивних функцій, тоді як пасивне споживання фрагментарного контенту пов’язане зі зниженням показників довільної уваги, робочої пам’яті та здатності до глибинного читання. Одним із можливих механізмів є нейропластичність та особливості дофамінової системи винагороди, однак більшість даних мають кореляційний характер. Рефлексивні стратегії саморегуляції можуть компенсувати негативні ефекти, хоча їх ефективність потребує подальшого вивчення. Найбільш перспективним напрямом вважаємо лонгітюдні дослідження довгострокових наслідків різних типів цифрової активності.
