items.title: Delivering a high-dose walking booster program after stroke: a multimethod study of therapists' beliefs and experiences nested within a randomized trial.
items.abstract: Background High-dose motor training is rarely implemented later after stroke. This study explored intervention therapists' beliefs and experiences delivering a high-dose walking booster program (HiWalk) within a Phase II trial. Objective The objectives of this study were to (i) describe the beliefs intervention therapists held about a high-dose walking booster program prior to delivery, (ii) report facilitators and barriers to delivery, and (iii) to describe the strategies intervention therapists used to maintain training intensity during the program. Methods A multimethod design examined intervention therapists' perspectives of delivering a high-dose walking booster program to stroke survivors who were more than 6-months post-stroke. Pre-program surveys assessed beliefs about high-dose motor training. Observational audits evaluated program delivery. Semi-structured interviews, informed by the Theoretical Domains Framework (TDF), identified facilitators and barriers to program delivery. Survey and observational audit data were descriptively analyzed, and qualitative data were analyzed thematically. The HiWalk Trial was registered on January 10, 2023 (registration number ACTRN12623000316606). Results All therapists who delivered the HiWalk program ( n = 6) participated. Before delivery, intervention therapists believed high-dose training was important (98.5/100, SD 2.5) but were less confident that stroke survivors could complete 3 hours of training per day (74.8/100, SD 25.8). Audit observations indicated that, on average, observed intervention sessions met protocol expectations. Key facilitators included training (TDF Skills), team support (TDF Social Influences), and resources (TDF Environmental Context and Resources). Barriers were beliefs about stroke survivor capability (TDF Beliefs about Capabilities) and resource limitations (TDF Environmental Context and Resources). Conclusions Intervention therapists can deliver a high-dose walking booster program within a clinical trial when supported by training, resources, and team collaboration. Findings inform future trial design and clinical practice translation.

items.title: Using 360-video to investigate visual exploratory activity in 7v7 and 9v9 sided games in women's soccer.
items.abstract: Immersive technology such as 360-video offers opportunities to analyse visual exploratory activity (VEA) under varying task constraints in controlled experimental settings. The study aimed to investigate the effect of pitch location and sided‑game format on VEA and verbal action responses in 360-video. Nineteen sub-elite female soccer players (21 ± 4 years) viewed 40 soccer videos in a head-mounted display. Footage was recorded using a stationary GoPro 360 Max camera at eye height in defensive and attacking central midfield locations. VEA was measured as the number of "scans" away from the ball across 32 analysed trials. Upon receiving a pass in 360-video, participants simulated and verbalised an action to continue play. A 2 × 2 repeated‑measures ANOVA showed a significant main effect of pitch location ( p = 0.016), with higher scan frequencies in defensive (0.31 ± 0.15 scans/s) than attacking midfield (0.29 ± 0.15 scans/s), with no significant effect of sided‑game or interaction effect ( p > 0.05). Findings demonstrate players had significantly higher scan frequencies in defensive central midfield compared with attacking central midfield, with the most verbal actions per trial in the 9v9 attacking midfield condition. Future research should assess agreement between VEA measured in 360-video and on-field activities.

items.title: Maternal Factors Modifying the Link Between Genetic Risk for Autism and Developmental Milestones.
items.abstract: Although common genetic liability-quantified through polygenic risk scores (PRS)-accounts for substantial variance in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) liability, how prenatal environmental exposures interact with genetic predisposition to shape developmental outcomes remains poorly understood. Using the data from Autism Genetic Resource Exchange (AGRE), we examined whether maternal prenatal factors moderate the association between ASD PRS and developmental outcomes, including language delay, motor delay, and core ASD traits. In exploratory gene-environment interaction analyses, amniocentesis was a candidate positive moderator of the association between PRS and both language and motor delay, such that higher polygenic liability was associated with a greater likelihood of these delays among prenatally exposed children. First-trimester vaginal bleeding showed a similar positive interaction estimate for motor delay. Maternal use of over-the-counter (OTC) medications during pregnancy-predominantly acetaminophen, reported by 59.9% of OTC users-was associated with an inverse interaction estimate, corresponding to a decreased association between polygenic liability and language delay among exposed children. These observations suggest that several prenatal factors may modify the association between common genetic liability and developmental outcomes among autistic children and should be considered hypothesis-generating until replicated in larger, population-based cohorts. Replication in independent samples, together with analyses that address selection and confounding, will be required before these candidate gene-environment interactions can be interpreted as reflecting specific developmental mechanisms.

items.title: Cost-effectiveness of iStent-based trabecular micro-bypass stenting combined with cataract surgery in mild-to-moderate open-angle glaucoma: a systematic review of analytic perspectives and time horizons.
items.abstract: Background Glaucoma remains a major cause of irreversible blindness and was estimated to affect 64.3 million people worldwide in 2013. Despite growing clinical use of minimally invasive glaucoma surgery (MIGS), reimbursement and uptake remain constrained by uncertainty about long-term cost-effectiveness. iStent-based trabecular micro-bypass implantation is commonly performed at the time of cataract surgery in patients with mild-to-moderate open-angle glaucoma, yet its economic value has not been synthesised systematically across healthcare systems. Objective To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of iStent trabecular micro-bypass implantation performed concurrently with cataract surgery for mild-to-moderate open-angle glaucoma, and to examine how the analytic perspective and time horizon adopted in the underlying models relate to the decision the evidence is intended to inform. Methods A systematic review was performed of published model-based economic evaluations. Eligible studies used a formal decision-analytic model, reported quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), and evaluated an iStent device implanted concurrently with cataract surgery. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library and Web of Science were searched on 27 July 2026 without date, language or publication-type restriction. Incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs), QALYs, analytic perspectives, time horizons, discount rates and probabilistic results were extracted with a page reference for each value. Reporting was appraised item-by-item against CHEERS 2022. Findings were synthesised narratively; no quantitative pooling was attempted. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020. Results Of 418 records identified and 293 after de-duplication, eight economic evaluations from eight countries met the eligibility criteria. All eight compared the device added to cataract surgery against cataract surgery alone; seven used a cohort Markov model and one an individual-patient microsimulation. Six adopted a payer or health-system perspective and two a societal perspective; five used a lifetime horizon, one 35 years and two 15 years. No evaluation adopted a provider perspective or a base-case horizon shorter than 15 years. All eight reported a favourable base-case result in the mild-to-moderate target population: reported ratios included €1,154 per QALY in France, €12,676 in Spain, €13,037 in Italy, €10,955 to €15,673 in Germany, JPY 1,430,647 in Japan and A$2,430 in Australia, together with two instances of dominance. Six of the eight were funded by the device manufacturer. Incremental QALY gains were small throughout, between approximately 0.005 and 0.17, so the reported ratios are highly sensitive to small changes in the denominator. One study did not report a price year and for a second it could not be verified; no study reported a pre-specified health economic analysis plan, and none modelled long-term structural change in medication prices, prescribing practice or competing alternatives. Conclusions The included peer-reviewed models generally project that adding an iStent-family device to cataract surgery can be cost-effective over long horizons. That projection depends on sustained medication reduction, on extrapolated glaucoma progression and on local device and treatment costs. Direct evidence that the modelled long-term clinical benefit is realised in practice and offsets the acquisition cost remains limited: the evidence base is small, concentrated in industry-funded analyses of a single device family drawing largely on the same two-year pivotal trial, and built on incremental QALY gains close to zero. All included evaluations adopt a payer, health-system or societal perspective over 15 years or longer, and none addresses whether the marginal cost of adding a stent to an already-scheduled cataract procedure is justified within an annual operating budget. This is a gap in the included QALY-based cost-utility literature; the review was not designed to identify provider-perspective budget-impact analyses outside these eligibility criteria. Trial registration Not applicable. This study is a systematic review of published economicevaluations; no clinical trial registration was required. The review was not registeredprospectively in PROSPERO.

items.title: Theta-Band Temporal Interference Stimulation Modulates Food Reward Prediction Error Encoding in Individuals with Elevated Food Addiction Symptoms.
items.abstract: Prediction error (PE) signals support feedback evaluation and adaptive updating, and are closely linked to medial frontal theta dynamics, particularly within dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC)-centered networks. However, evidence linking these oscillatory mechanisms to the modulation of PE encoding remains limited. Here, we tested whether theta-band modulation of a dACC-centered medial frontal network altered trial-level PE encoding during food-reward processing. In a single-blind, sham-controlled pre-post design, individuals with elevated food addiction symptoms performed a food incentive-delay task while undergoing electroencephalographic recordings combined with theta-band temporal interference stimulation. Single-trial analyses revealed that feedback-related negativity (FRN) amplitudes varied as a function of both behavioral and model-derived prediction errors. Critically, theta-band modulation altered FRN-PE coupling, with the effect most pronounced for unfavorable outcomes, whereas anticipatory activity remained unchanged. These findings support the hypothesis that theta-band modulation can alter feedback-related PE encoding within this population and task context.

items.title: Sex Education in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: A Qualitative Analysis of ChatGPT-3.5 Responses to Adolescents' Questions on Romantic Relationships and Sexuality.
items.abstract: Large language model chatbots, such as ChatGPT, have garnered increasing attention in the field of education, due to its versatility, processing speed, and widespread accessibility. However, its application to sexual education remains understudied, highlighting the need for more research into its potential to support informed decision-making among youth. The current study aimed to document ChatGPT-3.5 responses to adolescents' questions about romantic relationships and sexuality, using a more-than-human netnography approach. To obtain these responses, 393 anonymized emails written in French and English from adolescents aged 14 to 16 were collected from a recognized youth support organization. Data were obtained through ChatGPT-3.5 from January 14 to 31, 2024. The analyses focused on identifying content violations and describing the response formats, followed by a conventional content analysis of ChatGPT-3.5 recommendations. Overall, 17.8% of the emails were flagged as potentially violating ChatGPT-3.5's content policy. Responses were provided in two formats: (1) structured text or (2) continuous text that both included an introduction clarifying the question, normalizing the experience, and/or validating emotions; a list of recommendations; and a conclusion promoting support seeking, and/or a positive outlook. The recommendations aimed to encourage adolescents to embrace authenticity and personal agency, practice self-care and build self-confidence, engage in open communication, develop meaningful relationships, and seek support when needed. The findings highlight ChatGPT's potential to contribute to comprehensive sex education for adolescents seeking information.

items.title: The landscape of gene loss and missense variation across the mammalian tree informs on gene essentiality.
items.abstract: Patterns of gene and sequence preservation across species provide insight into gene essentiality under natural selection. Here we developed two interspecies constraint metrics across 462 mammalian species: Gene Identity Score of Mammalian Orthologs (GISMO), which quantifies gene loss weighted by evolutionary distance to humans, and GISMO-mis, which measures missense constraint using the ratio of missense to synonymous variation across mammals. Both metrics are strongly correlated with human loss of function, missense and dosage constraint derived from large-scale sequencing studies, yet are largely independent of coding sequence length. GISMO and GISMO-mis identify essential genes missed by existing human-only metrics, particularly short genes. Genes in the most constrained deciles are enriched for rare variant associations in disorders linked to reduced fecundity, including schizophrenia, autism and neurodevelopmental disorders, and show strong enrichment for common variant heritability. These deciles also exhibit reduced copy number variation, consistent with dosage sensitivity. In addition, GISMO improves prioritization of recessive disease genes and captures signatures of homozygous selection across the mammalian tree. Taken together, GISMO and GISMO-mis leverage deep mammalian evolution to provide complementary, length-robust measures of gene essentiality that strengthen disease-gene prioritization and illuminate the selective forces shaping human biology.

items.title: Dysregulated cholesterol trafficking through ABCA1 drives neurodegeneration in Parkinson's disease.
items.abstract: Although brain cholesterol dysregulation is implicated in Parkinson's disease (PD), targeting cholesterol synthesis has shown limited efficacy. Here we identify ATP-binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1) as a critical regulator of cholesterol homeostasis in PD. We show that ABCA1 expression is elevated in the substantia nigra of postmortem PD brains and in a PD mouse model, with regional analyses revealing preferential alterations in nigral and striatal circuits. Mechanistically, astrocytic ABCA1 drives excessive cholesterol efflux in mice, promoting neuronal cholesterol overload. In neurons, ABCA1 localizes to lysosomes, where it facilitates cholesterol import, leading to cholesterol accumulation, autophagy impairment and α-synuclein pathology. Genetic silencing of Abca1 in either astrocytes or dopaminergic neurons attenuates neurodegeneration and behavioral deficits in vivo. Furthermore, we identify magnesium citrate as an ABCA1 inhibitor and show that it reduces dopaminergic neuronal loss in a PD mouse model. Our findings identify an ABCA1-dependent cholesterol pathway underlying PD pathogenesis and support ABCA1 inhibition as a potential disease-modifying strategy.

items.title: Early lineage divergence segregates sensory and motor-associative identities in the thalamus.
items.abstract: The thalamus integrates sensory, motor and associative functions through distinct nuclei, yet the developmental principles driving their specification remain unclear. Here we generate a spatiotemporal single-cell multiomic and spatial transcriptomic atlas of the embryonic mouse thalamus, combined with barcoding-based lineage tracing. We identify two major glutamatergic lineages, sensory-related and motor-associative, each governed by different gene regulatory programs and temporal dynamics. These lineages arise from spatially and molecularly distinct progenitor domains, revealing an early segregation of functional identities. Within the sensory lineage, we resolve branching sensory trajectories leading to first-order visual and somatosensory neurons, both emerging from a shared higher-order-like state. Using in silico predictions and in vivo perturbation, we identify Sp9 as a key regulator of visual thalamic fate. Together, our findings define the molecular architecture and developmental trajectories that underpin thalamic modality specification, providing a framework to understand how functional circuits emerge in the mammalian brain.

items.title: Neural mechanisms underlying metacognitive processes in sequential decision-making.
items.abstract: Self-monitoring in decision-making is a hallmark of self-improvement in cognitive processes. To enhance outcomes in future decisions, individuals must accurately assess the correctness of prior choices and apply the information to control subsequent decisions. Although metacognition encompasses monitoring and control functions, the neural mechanisms underlying these processes and their relationships remain unclear. Furthermore, while the prefrontal cortex (PFC) is implicated in both functions, their distinct neural substrates and interrelations require further elucidation. In this study, we employed a sequential perceptual decision-making task with confidence ratings to examine how initial confidence influences subsequent decisions while recording neural activity using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). Subjects (female and male) performed a visual discrimination of two different-sized stimuli and subsequently rated their decision confidence. Behavioral results showed that subjects were more likely to change their choices between initial and subsequent decisions according to confidence levels. A signature of confidence (confidence magnitude) in initial decisions was observed primarily in the anterior medial PFC (amPFC). In contrast, the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC) exhibited higher neural activity related to changes of their initial choice at subsequent decisions. Furthermore, the pregenual ACC (pgACC) was associated with both processes, and it exhibited effective connectivity with the amPFC and dACC. These findings suggest that the medial PFC plays a role in integrating metacognitive monitoring and subsequent control in the sequential decision-making processes. Significance Statement Metacognition, encompassing monitoring and control, is fundamental to self-regulation and sequential decision-making. Despite their distinct roles, the neural mechanisms of how monitoring connects to subsequent control remain unclear. Using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), we reveal distinct yet interconnected medial prefrontal regions that support metacognitive processes. Specifically, the anterior medial prefrontal cortex encodes confidence in initial decisions, while the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex supports changes of mind. Effective connectivity analysis indicates that the pregenual anterior cingulate cortex integrates these processes. These findings advance our understanding of medial prefrontal mechanisms underlying adaptive self-regulation, with implications for addressing disorders characterized by impaired behavioral control.

items.title: Tumor innervation in non-central nervous system tumors: origins, mechanisms, and phenotypic plasticity.
items.abstract: The peripheral nervous system has emerged as an important regulator of solid tumor biology. We synthesize recent advances in cancer neuroscience, focusing on three interconnected themes: the cellular origins of tumor-associated nerves, the molecular mechanisms that govern neural recruitment and remodeling, and the resulting phenotypic plasticity within the tumor microenvironment. Tumor innervation arises through axon extension from pre-existing nerves, recruitment of neural precursors, and neuron-like transdifferentiation of non-neuronal cells. These processes are driven by neurotrophic factors, axon guidance cues, extracellular vesicles, and stress-associated pathways. The functional consequences of innervation are context-dependent, with sympathetic, parasympathetic, and sensory inputs exerting distinct effects across tumor types and stages. We conclude by outlining key challenges and future directions for therapeutic translation.

items.title: ASFNR Clinical State of Practice Statement on Imaging of Chronic Subdural Hematoma.
items.abstract: Background The efficacy of middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAE) for chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH) has heightened interest in imaging biomarkers that may reflect neomembrane activity, predict recurrence, and identify patients most likely to benefit from treatment. Characterization of hematoma internal architecture, referred to as the imaging phenotype, may provide indirect information regarding the biological activity and maturation of the neomembrane. However, imaging phenotype has not been incorporated into randomized trials or validated treatment-selection algorithms, and standardized definitions and reporting remain lacking. Methods The American Society of Functional Neuroradiology Clinical Practice Committee developed this State of Practice statement through expert consensus and review of the available literature. Key message Noncontrast CT (NCCT) remains the primary imaging modality for cSDH assessment. Hematoma burden should be characterized by maximum thickness measured perpendicular to the inner table, midline shift, and, when appropriate, volume. Volume may be estimated using the ABC/2 formula, whereas segmentation is more accurate for irregular, crescentic, or multiloculated collections when available. Internal architecture should be described using the Nakaguchi framework of homogeneous, laminar, separated, and trabecular phenotypes, with mixed or transitional features explicitly reported. Advanced techniques, including dual-energy CT, photon-counting CT, MRI, and arterial spin labeling, may provide information regarding membrane activity but are supported by limited, largely single-center evidence and currently have a problem-solving rather than routine role. Standardized reporting and prospective validation are needed before imaging phenotype or advanced-imaging biomarkers can guide treatment selection.

items.title: Obesity-induced oxidative stress and cGMP depletion suppress cerebellar α2,3-Na<sup>+</sup>,K<sup>+</sup>-ATPase activity in female mice.
items.abstract: Obesity is a major metabolic disorder linked to neuroinflammation and cognitive decline. Beyond hypothalamic alterations, emerging evidence indicates that extra-hypothalamic regions, including the cerebellum, are vulnerable to obesity-induced neurotoxicity. This study investigated whether high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity causes cerebellar oxidative stress, impairs Na + ,K + -ATPase (NKA) activity, and triggers molecular features resembling brain aging in female Balb/C mice. Chronic 10-week HFD intake established a marked obese phenotype, characterized by increased adiposity, fasting hyperglycemia, hyperlipidemia, and elevated serum TNF-α. In the cerebellum, obesity induced a selective, expression-independent reduction in α2,3-NKA isoform activity, accompanied by a marked depletion of tissue cGMP levels. This functional impairment was driven by an oxidative microenvironment, evidenced by elevated H 2 O 2 and TBARS levels and increased 4-HNE accumulation. Concomitantly, obese animals mounted an adaptive antioxidant response characterized by increased GST, GR, and GPx activities, reduced glutathione (GSH) consumption, and ERK1/2-mediated nuclear translocation of Nrf2, alongside structural membrane lipid remodeling (elevated cholesterol and reduced phospholipids). In summary, chronic obesity induces robust lipoxidative stress and suppresses cerebellar cGMP signaling and α2,3-NKA activity in female mice, recapitulating key molecular hallmarks of natural brain aging.

items.title: Machine learning of connectome-wide functional connectivity in spinal muscular atrophy.
items.abstract: While traditional view posed SMA as a pure motor neuron disorder, accumulating evidence pointed to the broader involvement of central nervous system. This study aimed to combined connectome-wide resting-state functional connectivity with machine learning algorithms to investigate the underlying brain mechanisms in SMA and capture the potential neuroimaging biomarker. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging were acquired from 43 SMA (26 SMA type 2 and 17 type 3) and 45 healthy controls (HCs). Connectome-wide functional connectivity, defined based on the Automated Anatomical Labeling 116 atlas (AAL116), combined with machine learning algorithms including logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM) and random forest (RF) were conducted for SMA vs HCs and SMA type 2 vs 3 classification. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) algorithm was used to quantify the contribution of individual connections. Connectome-wide functional connectivity allowed individual classification of SMA and HCs with stable performance across machine learning models. The majority of the most discriminative functional connectivity involved the high-level associative regions and cerebellum, subserving sensory and motor processing. Furthermore, the functional connectivity between right superior parietal gyrus and right inferior temporal gyrus was positively correlated with motor function. In conclusion, our study provided connectome-wide evidence that functional connectivity patterns involving high-level associative cortices and the cerebellum could distinguish SMA from HCs using machine learning. The identified connectivity features offer new insight into the distributed brain pathology of SMA beyond the traditional classical motor neuron view, and may serve as promising neuroimaging marker for this disease.

items.title: UBL3 Modification Reduces Nuclear POLE Levels to Potentiate Antitumor Immunity in Aero-upper Digestive Squamous Cell Carcinomas.
items.abstract: While immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have revolutionized treatment of the patients with aero-upper digestive squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs), including esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) and lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC), only a subset of patients benefit from ICIs, therefore entailing exploration of the mechanisms to regulate treatment responsiveness. POLE, as a subunit of DNA polymerase ε, possesses 3'-5' proofreading activity, and its mutations have been associated with favourable response to ICIs in several solid tumors. However, post-translational modification (PTM) of POLE and its impact on the therapeutic efficacy of ICIs are unknown. Here, this study demonstrates that ubiquitin-like protein 3 (Ubl3), whose expression is markedly downregulated in SCCs, covalently binds to Pole, reduces nuclear Pole levels, triggers DNA damage, and activates cGAS-STING signaling pathway. Notably, Ubl3 modification of Pole significantly primes the local immune microenvironment to mitigate the growth of murine aero-upper digestive SCC cells and boost the efficacy of αPD-1 treatment in vivo. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis further revealed that UBL3 expression is positively correlated with better clinical outcomes in a cohort of ESCC patients receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy combined with αPD-1. Together, our findings unravel UBL3 modification as a novel PTM mechanism governing subcellular location of POLE and its influence on immunotherapy responsiveness, thus making UBL3 modification as a promising immunomodulatory approach to enhance immunotherapy efficacy in patients with aero-upper digestive SCCs.

items.title: Resting-state fMRI biomarkers of surgical outcome in temporal lobe epilepsy: Network reorganization, rsfMRI-based prediction models, and cognition - A systematic review.
items.abstract: Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is a network disorder extending beyond the structurally defined epileptogenic zone. Resting-state functional MRI (rsfMRI) may provide information on brain network alterations relevant to seizure outcome and cognitive risk after epilepsy surgery. We reviewed rsfMRI studies in TLE surgical cohorts to evaluate postoperative network changes, preoperative predictors of seizure outcome, and associations between functional connectivity and cognition. This systematic review followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO. Fifteen studies were included, comprising 474 TLE patients who underwent resective epilepsy surgery and had at least 1 year of follow-up. Studies were reviewed for patient population, surgery, rsfMRI methodology, networks or regions, outcome definition, postoperative network changes, and cognitive assessments. Despite heterogeneity in patient selection, surgery, rsfMRI analysis, and outcome definition, studies consistently reported reduced DMN-related connectivity in TLE compared with healthy controls. Postoperative functional connectivity in seizure-free patients shifted toward healthy controls patterns in few studies. Preoperative rsfMRI-based prediction models showed promising accuracy for predicting seizure outcome but were generally developed in small cohorts and lacked external validation. Evidence relating rsfMRI to cognition was limited, but implicated thalamic, ascending reticular activating system, and thalamo-occipital connectivity in attention, language, and executive functions. RsfMRI is a promising research biomarker for network-level risk stratification in TLE surgery, particularly for seizure outcome prediction and postoperative network reorganization. Current evidence remains insufficient for clinical implementation. Future studies require larger homogeneous multicenter cohorts, standardized acquisition and preprocessing, consistent outcome definitions, systematic postoperative rsfMRI, neuropsychological assessment, and external validation of prediction models.

items.title: Interpersonal neural synchrony and parent-child behaviors during naturalistic interactions: A systematic review.
items.abstract: Interpersonal neural synchrony (INS), defined as the temporal alignment of neural activity between socially interacting individuals, has been proposed as an index of parent-child interaction quality. However, its relationship with moment-to-moment adjustment of parent-child behavior remains insufficiently understood. This systematic review examined associations between INS and observable behavior during naturalistic parent-child interactions, the factors influencing these associations, and the methods used to investigate them. Following PRISMA guidelines, systematic searches of Scopus, PubMed, and ScienceDirect identified 15 peer-reviewed empirical studies involving children from preschool age to early adolescence. INS-behavior associations were heterogeneous across studies. Higher INS was most consistently associated with mutual engagement, shared positive affect, and supportive parenting, whereas findings concerning reciprocity, responsiveness, and child agency were more context-dependent. Time-resolved analyses further indicated that INS fluctuated in relation to specific behavioral events and revealed temporally asymmetric patterns in which parent or child neural activity preceded that of the interaction partner. However, these patterns do not establish causal directionality and may partly reflect shared exposure to task-related or interactional inputs. Task structure and the availability of direct social cues appeared to shape INS-behavior associations, while parental stress and child social functioning emerged as potential sources of variability in INS. Methodologically, the findings highlight the value of combining micro- and macro-level behavioral coding with time-resolved and directionality-sensitive analyses, alongside stronger controls for spurious synchrony and common inputs. Given the limited number and methodological heterogeneity of available studies, the findings should be regarded as preliminary and primarily hypothesis-generating.

items.title: From Blue Dye to Multimodal-Guided Surgery: The Evolution of Sentinel Lymph Node Mapping in Vulvar Cancer - A Narrative Review.
items.abstract: The surgical management of inguinofemoral lymph nodes in early-stage vulvar cancer has progressively shifted from complete lymphadenectomy toward selective sentinel lymph node (SLN) biopsy, reducing treatment-related morbidity while preserving oncologic safety. This narrative review summarizes the historical, technical, and clinical evolution of SLN mapping, from vital blue dyes to radiotracer-based validation and contemporary multimodal image-guided approaches. A literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus was performed through May 2026, including landmark prospective studies, multicenter validation trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, guidelines, and studies evaluating indocyanine green (ICG) and hybrid radioactive-fluorescent tracers. Early blue dye studies established the feasibility of lymphatic mapping, whereas technetium-99m, lymphoscintigraphy, and gamma-probe guidance provided the reproducibility required for prospective validation. GROINSS-V I supported safe omission of complete inguinofemoral lymphadenectomy in carefully selected SLN-negative patients, complemented by diagnostic validation in GOG-173; subsequent evidence linked SLN tumor burden to prognosis and enabled risk-adapted management of positive nodes. ICG-based near-infrared fluorescence has emerged as a valuable tool for real-time visualization and may improve intraoperative guidance. However, most comparative studies have evaluated fluorescence after radiotracer-based localization or defined the SLN according to technetium uptake, limiting conclusions regarding stand-alone interchangeability. Current evidence therefore supports ICG primarily as an adjunct within multimodal mapping rather than as a validated replacement for technetium-99m. Future progress should focus on standardized fluorescence protocols, rigorously sequenced ICG-first validation, hybrid radioactive-fluorescent strategies, and integration of imaging-derived and artificial intelligence-based tools into individualized groin management.

items.title: Repeated ketamine administration induces cross-tolerance to sodium salicylate but not to morphine in male rats.
items.abstract: Cross-tolerance profiles provide critical insights into shared neurobiological substrates among analgesics. This study evaluated whether repeated sub-anesthetic ketamine administration induces cross-tolerance to morphine or sodium salicylate. Thirty-six adults male Wistar rats (180-200 g, n = 6/group) received either normal saline or ketamine (10 mg/kg, i.p.) once daily for 8 consecutive days. Antinociceptive thresholds were assessed daily using the hot-plate test (52 ± 0.5 °C) at 45 min post-injection and expressed as the percentage of maximum possible effect (MPE%). On day 9, acute cross-tolerance challenges were conducted using morphine (10 mg/kg, i.p.) or sodium salicylate (300 mg/kg, i.p.). Serum malondialdehyde (MDA) levels and superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity was measured on day 8 to evaluate systemic oxidative status. Repeated ketamine administration produced a progressive decline in MPE%, demonstrating marked antinociceptive tolerance by day 8. On day 9, morphine maintained full antinociceptive efficacy in ketamine-pretreated rats, indicating no cross-tolerance. Conversely, sodium salicylate-induced antinociception was significantly blunted, confirming cross-tolerance. Biochemically, ketamine pre-treatment did not elevate serum MDA and preserved SOD activity substantially better than morphine. In conclusion, repeated sub-anesthetic ketamine administration induces antinociceptive tolerance and selective cross-tolerance to sodium salicylate, while sparing morphine responsiveness. These behavioral adaptations parallel a favorable redox balance, highlighting distinct pharmacodynamic mechanisms governing ketamine interactions with opioid versus non-opioid regimens.

items.title: Maternal high-fat diet and metformin treatment affect palatable diet preference and central reward system gene expression in rat offspring in a sex-specific manner.
items.abstract: Maternal metformin (MT) treatment improves the metabolic phenotype of high-fat (HF) diet-exposed offspring, but its effect on offspring's palatable food preference remains unclear. We assessed HF diet and sucrose preferences in adult offspring from Sprague-Dawley rat dams fed a control diet, an HF diet with or without MT treatment. Additionally, we measured the mRNA expression of sweet taste perception-related genes in taste buds and dopamine- and opioid-related genes in the central reward system. In adult males, maternal HF diet increased HF food preference and decreased dopamine-related gene expression in the reward system. Furthermore, maternal MT treatment decreased low-concentration sucrose preference, and reduced opioid-related gene expression in the reward system. Maternal HF diet elevated sweet taste perception-related gene expression in taste buds, while maternal MT treatment reversed these changes. In adult females, neither maternal HF diet nor MT treatment affected HF food preference. However, maternal HF diet decreased low-concentration sucrose preference and reduced the expression of sweet taste perception-related genes, while maternal MT treatment did not reverse it. At weaning, maternal MT treatment generally decreased dopamine- and opioid-related gene expression in the central reward system across both sexes. Notably, this early-life central reward transcriptional suppression persisted into adulthood in males but not in females. Our results indicate that maternal HF diet and MT treatment influence HF diet and low-concentration sucrose preferences in adult offspring in a sex-specific manner, which may be associated with altered gene expression in the central reward system and the peripheral taste perception pathways.

items.title: Systemic oxidative stress in patients with Alzheimer's disease.
items.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder and oxidative stress (OS) is believed to play a role in disease pathogenesis. However, reliable OS markers are lacking. In this study we aim to assess OS in AD by evaluating free thiols, which serve as key indicators of the systemic redox status. SCD (subjective cognitive decline), MCI (mild cognitive impairment), AD, and other dementias (Non-AD) were recruited. Comorbidity data were collected and free thiols were measured in plasma. Additionally, phosphorylated-Tau (pTau217), amyloid-beta ratio (Aβ42/40), Glial Fibrillary Acidic Protein (GFAP), and neurofilament light (NfL) levels were used to investigate correlation with free thiols. Further, associations between free thiols and disease severity in AD were calculated. Three hundred and ten patients were included (SCD 109, MCI 51, AD 125, Non-AD 25). Free thiols were significantly lower in AD compared to SCD and MCI (p<0.01). Free thiols correlated negatively with pTau217, NfL and GFAP, also within AD (p<0.01 for all). Additionally, free thiols significantly negatively correlated with Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MOCA) scores (N=210, p<0.001). Multiple linear regression showed that type 2 diabetes and age were significant predictors for free thiols (B=1.01, β=0.266, p<0.001; B=-0.040, β=-0.273, p<0.001, respectively). After adjusting for these covariates, free thiols remained significantly lower in AD compared to SCD (p<0.05). Increased systemic OS, reflected by lower free thiols, is observed in plasma of AD patients, supporting a key role for OS in AD-pathophysiology and highlighting free thiols as potential therapeutic targets and possibly complementary biomarkers for clinical diagnostics.

items.title: Sex-divergent neurovascular and cognitive effects of chronic cerebral hypoperfusion.
items.abstract: Chronic cerebral hypoperfusion is the leading risk factor for the development of vascular dementia and is associated with white matter damage and cognitive impairment. Here, we assessed sex differences in vascular and neural pathology and cognitive impairment in the asymmetric carotid arterial stenosis (ACAS) mouse model of chronic cerebral hypoperfusion. Thirty days of ACAS significantly reduced cerebral blood flow, increased microvascular permeability as evidenced by extravasation of IgG and fibrinogen into brain parenchyma, and impaired MCA vasodilation. ACAS also induced white matter damage in the hippocampus and corpus callosum, with greater damage in the corpus callosum of females compared to males. Spatial memory impairments on the Barnes maze were significantly greater in ACAS males than in females. Finally, miRNA analyses revealed upregulated angiogenic miRNA in the hippocampus and cortex in ACAS females and upregulated neuroinflammatory miRNA in the hippocampus and cortex in ACAS males. Together, these findings indicate that the ACAS model produces robust neuropathology and sex differences in spatial memory and miRNA profiles.

items.title: Risk Factors and Clinical Outcomes of Reocclusion after Endovascular Treatment for Acute Ischemic Stroke: An Updated Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis and Meta-Regression.
items.abstract: Background Early reocclusion after endovascular treatment (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is underrecognized; its determinants and impact remain poorly defined. Methods Random-effects meta-analysis of early reocclusion after successful EVT (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library through January 2026). Crude odds ratios (ORs) were pooled and certainty rated with GRADE. Post hoc sensitivity analyses included only same-site reocclusion definitions. Results Ten studies (3,381 patients) were included; 244 (7.2%) reoccluded. Reocclusion was associated with lower 90-day functional independence (OR 0.25, 95% CI 0.17-0.38) and higher mortality (OR 1.86, 1.29-2.68), both moderate certainty. Reocclusion was more frequent with large-artery atherosclerosis (OR 2.24, 1.41-3.55; same-site 3.04, 1.73-5.33) and less frequent with cardioembolism (OR 0.40, 0.28-0.57) and atrial fibrillation (OR 0.39, 0.26-0.59), mutually confounded associations reflecting one embolic-versus-atherothrombotic axis. Prestroke antiplatelet therapy (OR 0.43, 0.28-0.67) lost significance under the same-site definition (0.60, 0.31-1.16). Exploratory data (two cohorts) linked eTICI 2c-3 reperfusion with less reocclusion (OR 0.44, 0.28-0.69). No study reported when etiology was adjudicated; the atherosclerosis association may be partly outcome-induced. Conclusions Early reocclusion is uncommon but carries a substantial prognostic penalty. Its determinants appear to lie in the vascular substrate rather than thrombectomy technique; prospective studies with uniform same-site definitions and systematic follow-up imaging are needed.

items.title: Meta-Analytic Evidence of Clinical, Cognitive, Biological and Treatment Characteristics of Bipolar Spectrum Disorder in Children and Adolescents: Results From an Umbrella Review.
items.abstract: Objective To comprehensively synthesize the meta-analytic evidence regarding bipolar spectrum disorder (BSD) in children and adolescents. Method PRISMA-compliant umbrella review (PROSPERO:CRD420250651065) across multiple databases to identify meta-analyses involving children and adolescents with BSD. Literature search, screening, data extraction, and quality assessment (via AMSTAR-2) were performed independently. Findings were synthesized and grouped according to key clinical, cognitive, biological and treatment domains. Results Fifty-two meta-analyses were included (k=754, N=59,967, age=13.0 years, 44.8% female participants). Most reported symptoms were increased energy (79%, 95% confidence interval (CI)=61-93%), irritability (77%, 95%CI=64-88%), and mood lability (76%, 95%CI=55-92%). Psychiatric comorbidities were common, with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder being most frequent (53%, 95%CI=36-70%). Treatment delay was longer in children and adolescents than in adults with BSD (SMD=0.39, 95%CI=0.15-0.64). 26.2% (95%CI=24.4-28.0) of children and adolescents with BSD attempted suicide at least once, with higher risk vs. children and adolescents with depression (OR=1.59; 95%CI=1.24-2.05) and adult-BSD (OR=1.68, 95%CI=1.29-2.18). Compared to healthy controls (HCs), children and adolescents with BSD showed neurocognitive impairments. Abnormalities in neuroimaging markers were significant in children and adolescents with BSD vs. HCs, children and adolescents with depression and adult-BSD. Second-generation antipsychotics (SMD=0.68, 95%CI=0.51-0.86) and mood stabilizers (SMD=0.61, 95%CI=0.40-0.82) were superior for mania vs. placebo. Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) was associated with improvements in manic and depressive symptoms. Conclusion BSD in children and adolescents is linked to illness severity, cognitive deficits, and neuroimaging abnormalities, requiring integrated pharmacological and psychosocial interventions (e.g. CBT). SGAs effectively treat mania, but options for depression remain limited. More prognostic and long-term studies are needed.

items.title: Clinical and genetic correlates of a circadian subtype of depression in the Australian Genetics of Depression Study.
items.abstract: Although commonly accepted depressive subtypes reflect phenotypic differences, there has been minimal progress in identification of discrete pathophysiological pathways, biomarkers or differential therapeutic approaches to effectively guide clinical management. To test the biological validity and clinical utility of a circadian subtype of depression on the basis of clinical course, differential medication response (self-reported) and genetic risk profile. Cross-sectional data were drawn from the nationwide Australian Genetics of Depression Study. Participants were classified as having a 'circadian' or 'non-circadian' subtype of depression on the basis of meeting criteria for at least three binary circadian-associated features: social jetlag, seasonality, delayed sleep midpoint, evening chronotype, morning tiredness and hypersomnia. Clinical course characteristics were compared. Associations with response to commonly prescribed antidepressants and polygenic risk scores for mental disorders and sleep, circadian, metabolic and inflammatory traits were investigated using logistic regression models. A total of 2604 participants (23%; 80% female; mean age 37.87 ± 13.62 years) had a circadian subtype. They reported an earlier age at onset (P < 0.001), more severe clinical features including (hypo)manic-like and psychotic-like experiences, suicidality, psychological distress and somatic complaints (all P < 0.001), weight gain during depressive episodes (P < 0.001), poorer response to selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (odds ratio 0.88 [95% CI 0.82, 0.94]) and serotonin-noradrenaline reuptake inhibitors (odds ratio 0.89 [95% CI 0.83, 0.97]), and more side-effects compared with those with a non-circadian subtype. Having a circadian subtype was associated with higher polygenic risk scores for attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (odds ratio 1.11 [95% CI 1.06, 1.17]), major depression (odds ratio 1.11 [95% CI 1.06, 1.16]), anxiety (odds ratio 1.10 [95% CI 1.04, 1.15]), bipolar disorder (odds ratio 1.09 [95% CI 1.04, 1.14]), body mass index (odds ratio 1.09 [95% CI 1.05, 1.14]), triglycerides (odds ratio 1.10 [95% CI 1.06, 1.16]), interleukin-6 (odds ratio 1.08 [95% CI 1.03, 1.13]), higher insulin resistance (odds ratio 1.08 [95% CI 1.04, 1.13]), later sleep midpoint (odds ratio 1.15 [95% CI 1.10, 1.21]), insomnia (odds ratio 1.08 [95% CI 1.03, 1.13]) and later chronotype (odds ratio 0.68 [95% CI 0.65, 0.71]). These findings support the face validity and potential clinical utility of a circadian subtype of depression as a clinical profile. Pending independent replication, investigation of its biology and predictive utility are warranted.

items.title: More than just accuracy: A pathway-level framework for implementing blood and digital biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease care.
items.abstract: Blood biomarkers are transforming Alzheimer's disease diagnostics by enabling a scalable, minimally invasive assessment of pathology. Food and Drug Administration clearances and European market certifications of different plasma tests mark a shift toward biological diagnosis in routine care. However, clinical implementation is not guided by diagnostic accuracy alone but will depend on improved patient-centered and pathway-level outcomes, including diagnostic confidence, the appropriate use of CSF and PET assessments, time to diagnosis, amyloid-targeting treatment eligibility assessment, and trial recruitment. Digital biomarkers may complement blood tests by providing repeated measures of cognition, speech, and mobility. Yet, their evidence base remains more heterogeneous regarding construct validity, supervision requirements, device dependence, adherence burden, cultural portability, interpretability, and regulatory classification. This review defines how combined blood-digital workflows could be evaluated beyond accuracy, including the context of use, downstream decisions, ethical aspects, governance, and post-market monitoring, ultimately aiming to translate biomarker innovation into meaningful benefits for patients and health systems.

items.title: Recanalization After Acute Cervical Artery Dissection: A Multicenter International Study.
items.abstract: The rates and factors associated with complete recanalization after cervical artery dissection (CeAD) have not been comprehensively quantified in large cohorts. We sought to determine the 6-month rate of complete recanalization in CeAD, clinical and imaging factors associated with recanalization, and risk of recurrent ischemic stroke based on recanalization status. This was a planned subanalysis of the Antithrombotic Treatment for Stroke Prevention in Cervical Artery Dissection study, a multicenter retrospective cohort including patients with imaging-confirmed CeAD diagnosed between January 2015 and June 2022 at 63 sites worldwide. For this analysis, we included 1,095 patients with single-vessel CeAD causing stenosis at presentation who had available follow-up vascular imaging at 6 months after CeAD. The primary outcome was complete recanalization within 6 months after CeAD. Clinical and imaging variables, as well as recurrent stroke, were compared between patients with and those without complete recanalization. Factors independently associated with complete recanalization were identified using multivariable logistic regression. Time to complete recanalization was analyzed using an accelerated failure time Weibull model. Among 1,095 included patients (median age 45 years; 46.7% female), 634 (57.9%) achieved complete recanalization by 6 months. In multivariable analysis, each additional year of age was associated with lower odds of complete recanalization (odds ratio [OR] 0.97 per year; 95% CI 0.96-0.98; p < 0.001). Diabetes (OR 0.46; 95% CI 0.27-0.81; p = 0.006), active smoking (OR 0.69; 95% CI 0.50-0.95; p = 0.025), and complete occlusion at presentation (OR 0.44; 95% CI 0.32-0.59; p < 0.001) were independently associated with lower odds of complete recanalization. Complete occlusion at presentation was associated with both longer time to, and lower rates of, complete recanalization. We observed no effect of antithrombotic regimen (antiplatelet therapy vs anticoagulation) on complete recanalization. Incomplete recanalization was associated with a nonsignificant numerically higher proportion of recurrent stroke (5.4% vs 3.5%; p = 0.064). Almost 60% of patients with CeAD achieved complete vessel recanalization by 6 months. Older age, diabetes, smoking, and complete occlusion at presentation were independently associated with incomplete recanalization. Further study is required to determine whether these findings may help guide tailored imaging surveillance and secondary prevention strategies.

items.title: Differential Trajectories of Brain Atrophy in Multiple Sclerosis, MOGAD, and AQP4 + NMOSD: The Role of Disease Activity in MOGAD.
items.abstract: Background and objectives Multiple sclerosis (MS), myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD), and aquaporin-4 antibody-positive neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (AQP4 + NMOSD) are inflammatory demyelinating disorders with distinct mechanisms of tissue injury. MS is characterized by diffuse neurodegeneration, whereas damage in antibody-mediated diseases is considered attack related. In MOGAD, the relationship between disease activity and brain atrophy remains unclear. We aimed to compare longitudinal trajectories of global and regional brain atrophy across MS, MOGAD, and AQP4 + NMOSD and investigate whether atrophy in MOGAD is associated with disease course and lesion dynamics. Methods In this retrospective multicenter Magnetic Resonance Imaging in Multiple Sclerosis (MAGNIMS) study, patients fulfilling the following criteria were enrolled: (1) age 18 years or older, (2) MS/MOGAD/AQP4 + NMOSD diagnosis, (3) ≥2 same-scanner brain MRIs ≥6 months apart and ≥3 months postattack, (4) concurrent Expanded Disability Status Scale, and (5) disease course information. White matter lesions were segmented using the Lesion Segmentation Toolbox. Longitudinal brain volumes were quantified on lesion-filled T1-weighted images using Sequence Adaptive Multimodal SEGmentation (SAMSEG) with a within-subject template approach. In MOGAD, lesion dynamics were classified as stable/new lesions/lesion resolution. Linear mixed-effects models adjusted for age, sex, baseline volume, and center estimated atrophy rates. Results Overall, 489 participants from 15 centers were included (98 MS [mean age 39.79 years, 68.37% female], 72 MOGAD [42.14 years, 66.67%], 41 AQP4 + NMOSD [51.25 years, 87.80%], and 278 healthy controls [42.94 years, 61.87%]). The mean follow-up was MS: 2.44 ± 1.55 years, MOGAD: 2.57 ± 1.85, and AQP4 + NMOSD: 3.22 ± 2.42. Compared with controls, MS showed accelerated global brain atrophy (β = -2.027 cm 3 per year, 95% CI -3.430 to -0.623). MOGAD demonstrated white matter volume loss (β = -0.989, 95% CI -1.889 to -0.090) and ventricular enlargement (lateral: β = 0.219, 95% CI 0.089-0.350; third ventricle: β = 0.009, 95% CI 0.003-0.015). AQP4 + NMOSD showed pallidal volume reduction (β = -0.008, 95% CI -0.014 to -0.001). Within MOGAD, relapsing patients (62.5%) exhibited greater third ventricular expansion than MS (β = 0.009, 95% CI 0.001-0.017). MOGAD with new lesions (22.22%) had greater ventricular enlargement than controls (lateral: β = 0.359, 95% CI 0.147-0.572; third ventricle: β = 0.016, 95% CI 0.006-0.025), MS, and AQP4 + NMOSD. Discussion Each inflammatory demyelinating disease exhibits a characteristic pattern of brain atrophy. In MOGAD, neuroaxonal loss seems associated with inflammatory activity and lesion accrual, supporting an event-driven pattern of tissue injury rather than diffuse neurodegeneration. Limitations include small NMOSD sample, heterogeneous follow-up, and potential scanner-related variability.

items.title: CX3CL1 (fractalkine)-CX3CR1 interface drives CD8⁺ T cell-induced neurodegeneration in human brain organoids.
items.abstract: Immune-neuron interactions play a critical role in neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer's disease (AD), but how CD8⁺ T cells contribute to brain pathology remains poorly understood. Amyloid-β (Aβ), a hallmark of AD, is known to trigger neuronal stress and inflammation. Here, we established a human cortical organoid (hCO) model to investigate CD8⁺ T cell responses to Aβ-induced neurodegenerative stress. Aβ exposure increased neuronal expression of CX3CL1 (fractalkine), which engages its receptor CX3CR1 on CD8⁺ T cells. Transwell migration assays showed enhanced recruitment of CX3CR1⁺ CD8⁺ T cells toward Aβ-treated hCOs. In parallel, Aβ upregulated IL-15 expression, a cytokine that supports CD8⁺ T cell activation. The infiltration of CD8⁺ T cells led to neuronal injury, marked by MAP2 loss and cleaved Caspase-3 activation, accompanied by an increase in gene signatures for cell death and inflammation. Exposure to the conditioned medium of activated CX3CR1 high CD8⁺ T cell recapitulated this damage, and the neutralization of CD8 + T cell cytokines and cytotoxic molecules rescued the phenotype. These findings identify the CX3CL1-CX3CR1 axis and CD8⁺ T cell effector programs as drivers of neurotoxicity and establish brain organoids as a platform to study immune-driven neurodegeneration.

items.title: Multiple sources contribute to predictive tactile attenuation in the mouse whisker system.
items.abstract: The brain predicts action outcomes using interacting neuronal systems that integrate sensory feedback, movement, and rewards. In the mouse whisker system, we investigated whether two presumed predictive mechanisms jointly attenuate ascending tactile signals during movement. To this end, we employed an open-loop whisker-reach task that monitored facial nucleus motor activity and presented experimental tactile consequences while measuring tactile attenuation in the barrel cortex. Experimentally manipulating sensory consequences revealed two distinct systems. Sensory gating, a previously documented but functionally unclear mechanism of tactile attenuation, appeared graded but persisted during and after movement. In contrast, a second system was found to be temporally precise, generate suppression when stimuli are omitted, and capable of being learned within hundreds of trials. We label it state estimation as its characteristics-active suppression of expected tactile input-aligns well with the classical reafference principle, previously overlooked in the whisker system.

items.title: Improving optogenetic control over G<sub>i/o</sub>-coupled receptor signaling by optimized GIRK channel expression.
items.abstract: Stimulation of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) that couple to G i/o leads to the activation of G protein-activated inward rectifier K + (GIRK) channels and membrane hyperpolarization in excitable cells. GIRK channel availability can determine the success of optogenetic silencing strategies based on G i/o -coupled GPCRs. To selectively enhance G i/o -mediated GIRK currents, we created expression cassettes that coupled the activity of a GIRK subunit to the light-activated G i/o -coupled GPCRs Opn4L (an opsin also known as melanopsin), longwave-sensitive opsin Opn1, parapinopsin, or Opn7b. We used the GIRK1 F137S mutant because of its fast activation, generation of large currents, and formation of homomeric channels, which reduced the size of the expression cassette. We demonstrated that light-mediated activation of GIRK1 F137S through the opsins induced robust GIRK currents in HEK293 cells, cardiomyocytes, and cerebellar Purkinje neurons. Moreover, coupling GIRK1 F137S activation to the promiscuous Opn4L changed the net effect of G protein signaling from G q/11 -mediated excitation to G i/o -mediated inhibition in cerebellar Purkinje neurons and cardiomyocytes. Thus, our tools optimize the use of GIRK activity in the optogenetic control of the G i/o pathway in excitable cells.

items.title: Characterizing Features of Vulnerability in Narrative Production of Cantonese-Speaking School-Aged Children With Developmental Language Disorder.
items.abstract: Purpose Narratives show vulnerability in children with developmental language disorder (DLD) cross-linguistically. However, certain narrative measures revealing significant deficits in English and European DLD literature have been studied primarily in preschoolers, with limited evidence in school-aged children and no data in Cantonese. We examine features of vulnerability in narrative production of school-aged children learning a major Chinese language, Cantonese. Method Twenty-five children with DLD ( M age = 9;7 [years;months]) and age-matched typically developing (TD) peers ( M age = 9;8) were assessed using the Cantonese Multilingual Assessment Instrument for Narratives (MAIN) in story retelling and storytelling. Their narrative competence across macrostructure, microstructure, and internal state term measures were analyzed at group and individual diagnostic accuracy levels. Results Both expressive macrostructure and microstructure showed significant TD/DLD group differences, indicating story structure (SS), story complexity (SC), syntactic complexity, and grammaticality are vulnerable in monolingual Cantonese-speaking school-aged children with DLD. No significant TD/DLD group differences were registered in number of different words, mean length of utterance, productivity measures (total number of utterances, total number of words), or internal state terms. For diagnostic accuracies, SS and syntactic complexity reached acceptable sensitivity (91.7% and 83.3%, respectively) but limited specificity (41.7% and 70.8%, respectively); SC and grammaticality showed marginal sensitivity and specificity (both 70.8%). Conclusions This study confirms SS, SC, grammaticality, and syntactic complexity-but not productivity-as features of vulnerability in narrative production of Cantonese-speaking school-aged children with DLD. The exploratory diagnostic accuracy results support using narrative measures in combination with other assessments for diagnosis. Future studies should examine younger and larger samples to further document these vulnerability features and evaluate the clinical utility of narrative measures at earlier developmental stages.

items.title: ClC-7 links PIKfyve inhibition to Rab-dependent LRRK2 activity at lysosomes.
items.abstract: Increased activity of leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) confers Parkinson's disease risk. LRRK2 dynamically localizes to lysosomal membranes in response to various stresses, yet the mechanisms by which distinct lysosomal perturbations are communicated to LRRK2 remain unclear. Here, we show that inhibition of the lysosomal lipid kinase PIKfyve promotes LRRK2 recruitment and signaling through a pathway that requires the lysosomal chloride/proton antiporter ClC-7. ClC-7 in turn controls the accumulation of multiple Rab GTPases on lysosomes. LRRK2 signaling under these conditions requires its established Rab-binding surfaces, with Rab12 contributing significantly to this response. This pathway operates independently of CASM. In contrast, lysosomal stresses that induce CASM require both Rab-binding sites on LRRK2 and GABARAP for robust LRRK2 signaling. These findings identify ClC-7-dependent lysosomal remodeling and Rab accumulation as key features linking PIKfyve inhibition to LRRK2 signaling and reveal that distinct lysosomal stresses engage different combinations of Rab and GABARAP inputs to activate LRRK2.

items.title: Endothelial neo-antigen expression initiates CD8⁺ T cell-driven CNS vasculitis amplified by peripheral immune challenge.
items.abstract: Primary central nervous system (CNS) vasculitis is a rare and devastating inflammatory cerebrovascular disease for which pathogenic mechanisms remain poorly defined, largely due to limited access to human tissue and the absence of validated experimental models. Here, we present a mouse model of CNS-restricted vasculitis based on inducible, endothelial-biased neoantigen expression, termed brain endothelial ovalbumin (BrEndO). In BrEndO mice, tamoxifen-induced ovalbumin (OVA) expression in cerebral endothelial cells (ECs) elicited a controlled endogenous CD8+ T cell response at the blood-brain barrier that remained clinically restrained. In contrast, peripheral immune activation through infection with OVA-expressing Listeria monocytogenes or systemic PD-L1 immune checkpoint blockade converted this regulated response into severe, CD8+ T cell-driven CNS vasculitis with vascular injury and parenchymal infiltration. Transcriptomic profiling of inflamed cerebral microvessels and spatial transcriptomic analyses demonstrated shared inflammatory and immune activation signatures between BrEndO mice and human primary CNS vasculitis brain biopsies. These findings identify antigen-specific endothelial immune recognition as a regulated process whose breakdown precipitates CNS-restricted vasculitis and establish BrEndO as an experimentally tractable platform to investigate mechanisms and modifiers of immune-mediated cerebrovascular inflammation.

items.title: Social vulnerability as a key dimension of frailty in Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia.
items.abstract: Objectives Frailty and social vulnerability are two dynamic and multidimensional constructs able to capture susceptibility to adverse health outcomes related to physical decline or arising from weakened social connections, support, and resources. While the burden of physical frailty in dementia has been well established, the impact of disadvantageous social conditions is less known. In this study, we investigated these dimensions in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD) with the aim of describing possible common and individual trajectories. Methods 47 individuals living with AD and 24 with FTD, as well as 66 healthy control (HC) subjects, were included. An ad hoc developed 60-item bidimensional Frailty Index (FI) questionnaire was administered to explore the two dimensions. Global (gFI), physical (pFI) and social (sFI) FI scores were derived and compared among groups with ANCOVA, including age and education as covariates. Pearson's correlation analyses explored the relationship between FI scores and clinical-neuropsychological measures. Results No group effect was observed for pFI. Both patient groups showed significantly higher gFI and sFI levels compared to HC. sFI positively correlated with disease severity and cognitive patterns in both dementias. Conclusion Our findings point to an urgent need for person-centered care strategies that extend beyond biomedical models. Deficits in social connections and support represent a primary and common underpinning of vulnerability in dementia populations. A timely periodic evaluation of non-physical determinants of vulnerability may contribute to a better and earlier detection of maladaptive trajectories with a consequent beneficial effect on the well-being and burden of the patient-caregiver dyad.

items.title: Methodological concerns limiting the detection of treatment effects in the OSAN trial of blue-blocking glasses for mania.
items.abstract: Background This correspondence is a commentary to the recently published report from the OSAN trial by Fiedorowicz et al. but with applicability to the broader research involving blue-blocking glasses and patients in a manic episode. Method Clinical studies on dark therapy are still rare, and we read with great interest the report from the OSAN trial published in Journal of Affective Disorders the 1st of April 2026. Results The sample was significantly higher in manic symptoms, more medicated and less adherent to the intervention than in preceding studies on effects of dark therapy for mania. Efforts to comply with the gold standard of blinding of raters may have come with the cost of underestimating the symptom level. Extended intervention period (2 weeks) may have caused the extensive loss to follow up (35/42 (83%) at 2 weeks). Several issues with the statistical methods and data reporting make the results difficult to interpret. Conclusions The statistical power of the OSAN trial may have been substantially reduced by attrition and multiple sources of variance to the data. The results from the trial should be interpreted with caution.

items.title: The impact on scoliosis development and the need for bracing after posterior fossa decompression for Chiari Malformation type I and de-tethering for tethered cord syndrome: a retrospective study of 171 patients.
items.abstract: Purpose Scoliosis is frequently associated with CM1 and TCS, but its course following neurosurgical treatment remains incompletely understood. The aim of this study was to describe scoliosis development following posterior fossa decompression for CM1 or de-tethering for TCS. A secondary aim was to describe postoperative brace treatment and its association with scoliosis progression. Methods This was a retrospective study including children operated consecutively from the age of one to eighteen years for CM1 or TCS. We included patients with and without preoperative scoliosis who had a last follow-up from five years of age at earliest. Scoliosis patients were categorized based on type of scoliosis and braced patients were analysed based on compliance. Results We identified 293 patients and 171 (58%) were included. The cohort consisted of 100 females (58%) and the mean (SD) age at neurosurgery was 9.1 (4.3) years. There were 73 out of 171 (43%) who were operated for CM1 and 98 (57%) had been operated for TCS. The mean age at last follow-up was 12.4 (4.2) years and the median (25th, 75th percentile) follow-up was at 31 (14, 54) months. Scoliosis progression was seen in 21 (37%) patients. De novo scoliosis was seen in 5 (4%) patients. Patients compliant with postoperative bracing progressed less frequently than non-compliant patients (p = 0.025). Conclusion Scoliosis progression remains common following neurosurgery. Continued scoliosis surveillance is warranted, while postoperative bracing requires further prospective evaluation.

items.title: A biopsychosocial perspective on obesity and eating disorders: A narrative overview and exploratory study of ghrelin, LEAP2, trait impulsivity, and eating psychopathology.
items.abstract: Dysregulated eating in obesity and eating disorders (ED) is associated with complex relationships between peripheral hormonal signals and neurobehavioral characteristics. Ghrelin and its endogenous antagonist liver-expressed antimicrobial peptide-2 (LEAP2) have been implicated in the regulation of energy homeostasis and food intake, while trait impulsivity has been proposed as a transdiagnostic characteristic associated with dysregulated eating. This study aimed to integrate narrative evidence with exploratory empirical data to examine associations between ghrelin, LEAP2, and trait impulsivity in women with obesity, with and without ED, and to explore their associations with food addiction (FA) and eating psychopathology. A total of 164 adult women (67 with obesity, 35 with obesity + ED, 62 healthy controls) completed anthropometric assessments, fasting ghrelin and LEAP2 determinations, and psychometric measures of trait impulsivity, FA, and eating psychopathology. Group comparisons and exploratory structural equation modeling (SEM) were used to explore associations between endocrine and behavioral variables. Women with obesity (with or without ED) showed significantly lower ghrelin levels than controls, while LEAP2 concentrations did not differ between groups. Trait impulsivity and FA scores were higher in the obesity + ED group. Within this subgroup, SEM analyses identified positive associations of trait impulsivity and FA with eating psychopathology, while LEAP2 was positively associated with trait impulsivity and FA scores. Previous research has pointed to potential associations of ghrelin and LEAP2 with obesity and ED, as well as with behavioral characteristics related to dysregulated eating, although the available evidence remains limited and heterogeneous. In our study, ghrelin was lower in women with obesity, whereas LEAP2 did not differ between groups. The observed associations involving LEAP2 emerged only in the exploratory SEM analysis and should therefore be interpreted cautiously. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not provide evidence of mechanistic or causal relationships. Further research in larger and longitudinal samples is needed to replicate these findings and clarify the relationships among endocrine and behavioral factors.

items.title: Lyme Disease and Other Tick-Borne Infections.
items.abstract: Purpose of review The neurologic manifestations of selected tick-transmitted infections in North America and Eurasia were reviewed. Recent findings Both Powassan virus in North America, and Tick-Borne Encephalitis (TBE) virus in Eurasia can cause encephalitis, often with significant neurologic morbidity. Lyme disease, Ehrlichia chaffeensis (the cause of human monocytic ehrlichiosis [HME]), and Borrelia miyamotoi infections can cause meningitis (the third primarily in immunocompromised individuals). Patients with Lyme disease may also develop cranial neuropathy, and/or radiculoneuropathy. Tick-borne infections are being increasingly recognized in North America and Eurasia. While many tick-borne infections can cause headaches, lethargy or other non-specific symptoms, these are generally not evidence of nervous system infection - i.e., neuroinvasive disease. The latter is less common but may occur in infections due to Powassan and TBE viruses, in HME and in Lyme disease. Patients with symptomatic nervous system infection due to Powassan or TBE virus are at high risk of developing significant neurologic impairment and sequelae.

items.title: Therapeutic potential of varenicline in neuropsychiatric disorders: insights into its molecular mechanisms.
items.abstract: Neuropsychiatric disorders pose significant health challenges. Current drug therapies are often inadequate, highlighting the urgent need for new and effective treatments. The α4β2 nicotinic receptor has been implicated in the pathophysiology of various neuropsychiatric disorders. In this context, varenicline, its selective agonist, has garnered increasing attention for its potential therapeutic effects across a range of neuropsychiatric conditions. Emerging preclinical evidence suggests that varenicline may exert neuroprotective effects through modulation of pathways that include synaptic plasticity and synaptic proteins, neuroinflammation, microglial activation, apoptosis, and autophagy. However, direct target engagement for many of these pathways has not yet been established. In this review, we provide a comprehensive review of the cellular and molecular mechanisms by which varenicline might be expected to exert therapeutic effects in a range of neuropsychiatric disorders. Most previous reviews of varenicline have concentrated on its use as a smoking cessation aid or on its potential to treat individual diseases. The current review takes a different approach, focusing at the molecular level on the various pathways that are affected in different diseases, and discussing within each section the evidence that currently exists in relation to each of these in studies conducted in rodent models and in clinical trials. The review seeks to provide insight into the potential benefits and drawbacks of using a single compound to treat a variety of disorders, and to highlight areas for future research.

items.title: Sleep Spindles and Slow Oscillations as Potential Biomarkers and Therapeutic Targets in Mild-to-Moderate Alzheimer's Disease.
items.abstract: Purpose of review This review critically evaluates evidence on sleep spindles (SP), slow oscillations (SOs), and their coordination in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease (AD), focusing on their relationships with cognition, AD biomarkers, and their therapeutic potential. Recent findings Longitudinal studies associate greater SP and/or SO activity with better cognition and favourable amyloid and tau profiles after clinical onset. Spindle and SO coupling may index network integrity. Preserved NREM sleep oscillations are associated with lower orexin concentrations and weaker adverse relationships between orexin and cognitive and neuropsychiatric outcomes. Closed-loop acoustic stimulation and slow-oscillatory transcranial direct-current stimulation can modify SO activity, spindle activity, and coupling, although cognitive and biomarker benefits remain uncertain. Spindle-SO activity, including their temporal coupling, are associated with cognition and AD biomarkers across the disease continuum. Closed-loop acoustic and electrical stimulation can modify these oscillations, but biomarker-characterized trials in MCI and AD are needed to determine whether treatment produces durable cognitive and biomarker benefits.

items.title: Surgical timing in patients with cocaine-induced midline destructive lesions: when and how.
items.abstract: Purpose Cocaine-induced midline destructive lesions (CIMDL) may cause progressive septonasal and palatal destruction, but the optimal timing of reconstruction remains undefined. Because relapse is common, particularly within the first year, premature surgery may lead to failure and, in advanced cases, severe complications. This work synthesizes the available evidence and expert opinion to guide surgical timing and practical management. Methods We performed a narrative evidence-based review of studies addressing cocaine relapse, abstinence verification, and reconstructive or prosthetic management in CIMDL, integrated with multidisciplinary expert consensus. Key relapse data were drawn from large longitudinal cohorts, including national treatment and follow-up studies and analyses of continuing care and initial abstinence. Results Relapse risk remains clinically significant throughout the first 12 months after treatment, with weekly-use relapse rates of approximately 20-24% at 12 months. Beyond 12 months, increases appear smaller in longitudinal cohorts. Early sustained abstinence is protective, with at least 12 weeks of abstinence during treatment associated with substantially lower relapse rates. As self-report is often unreliable, repeated toxicology testing combined with serial endoscopic assessment offers objective monitoring, facilitates shared review with patients, and may improve adherence. Reconstructions beyond simple septal perforations are usually staged, and relapse during treatment can irreversibly compromise outcomes. Conclusions Based on relapse dynamics and expert consensus, reconstruction in CIMDL should be deferred until at least 12 months of toxicology-verified abstinence within a multidisciplinary pathway including structured monitoring, optimized prosthetic care, staged surgery, and prolonged postoperative surveillance.
