items.title: Mapping and analysis of the knowledge graph on the current status and key issues in global research on Norovirus infections in children over the past 28 years.
items.abstract: Background Norovirus (NoV) is a major pathogen responsible for acute gastroenteritis and outbreaks of diarrhea in humans. Children, due to their underdeveloped immune systems and higher risk of exposure, constitute a population with a relatively concentrated incidence of infection and disease burden. In recent years, research on NoV infections in children has been growing globally; however, there remains a lack of systematic quantitative analysis regarding the evolution of research themes, models of international collaboration, and future development directions in this field. Therefore, this study employs bibliometric methods to conduct a visual analysis of the knowledge structure, research hotspots, and development trends in the global field of NoV infection research in children, providing a reference for future scientific research and the formulation of prevention and control strategies. Methods This study retrieved literature on pediatric NoV infections published between January 1998 and December 2025 from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) database. Using CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and Bibliometrix software, we conducted a visual analysis of annual publication trends, countries/regions, institutions, authors, journals, keywords, and references to reveal the research trajectory, knowledge base, and cutting-edge directions in this field. Results This study included a total of 2,161 relevant publications. The results show that research on NoV infections in children worldwide has generally followed a steady upward trend, with activity remaining high in recent years. The United States, China, and Japan are the leading contributors to research in this field, with the United States exerting significant influence through international collaboration. The University of Tokyo, Emory University, and Chiang Mai University are the research institutions with the highest number of publications. Vinje, Jan; Ushijima, Hiroshi; and Khamrin, Pattara were the most prolific core authors, while Atmar, Robert L.; Lindesmith, Lisa C.; and Patel, Manish M. demonstrated strong academic influence. Keyword analysis revealed that research in this field primarily focuses on viral molecular characteristics, epidemiological features, and clinical manifestations in children, and is gradually expanding toward disease burden assessment, global prevention and control strategies, and vaccine development. Conclusion Global research on NoV infections in children has evolved into a Multi-Disciplinary research framework driven by virology, epidemiology, clinical medicine, and public health. Current research focuses primarily on molecular epidemiology and genetic diversity, as well as epidemiological characteristics and outbreak transmission mechanisms, while the assessment of disease burden and the optimization of global prevention and control strategies are gradually emerging as key future research directions. In the future, international collaboration, multicenter surveillance, and interdisciplinary research should be further strengthened to advance research on pediatric NoV infection from describing disease characteristics toward precision surveillance, proactive prevention, and comprehensive control and prevention measures.

items.title: Ensuring equitable emergency, critical and operative care.
items.abstract: Conditions requiring emergency, critical and operative (ECO) care account for a substantial proportion of preventable mortality and disability worldwide, yet ECO systems remain fragmented and underdeveloped in many settings. Recent global policy advances, including the adoption of the World Health Organization (WHO) Global Strategy and Action Plan for Integrated ECO Care by the World Health Assembly, provide an important opportunity to strengthen these systems. However, implementation must prioritise equity. ECO care spans a wide spectrum of complexity and cost, from basic triage, oxygen therapy and essential operations to advanced intensive care and specialised surgery. Given finite resources, health systems should first ensure universal access to foundational ECO care: early recognition of illness, basic airway and oxygen support, essential medications, monitoring, infection prevention, and timely referral. Approaches such as Essential Emergency and Critical Care (EECC) offer a feasible, highly cost-effective minimum standard of care, and prioritising such foundational ECO care is both an ethical imperative and the most effective pathway to achieving equitable population-level health gains.

items.title: Evidence for Embedding Smoking and Vaping Cessation Support in Primary Care: A Scoping Review.
items.abstract: Background Smoking is a leading preventable cause of disease, with vaping creating new public health concerns. This review synthesised evidence on interventions and strategies to integrate cessation care into primary healthcare. Methods We conducted a systematic scoping review of PubMed and EMBASE for studies published between 19 September 2020 and 19 September 2024. Eligible studies evaluated smoking and/or vaping cessation interventions or implementation strategies in primary care settings in high-income countries (Australia, Canada, EU, UK, USA). Two reviewers independently extracted data on study characteristics, intervention types, outcomes, and abstinence verification. Results Of 2166 records screened, 30 empirical studies were included. Most focused on smoking cessation, with only two addressing e-cigarette users. The strongest evidence supported multi-component interventions combining behavioural counselling and pharmacological treatments. Implementation strategies included electronic health record prompts, cost-free pharmacotherapy, financial incentives, and integration of cessation support into low-dose computed tomography screening or post-spirometry feedback. Evidence for the effectiveness of provider education was inconclusive. Conclusions The evidence supports several interventions and implementation strategies for integrating smoking cessation into primary care, though data on vaping cessation are limited. These findings will inform the development of targeted approaches to enhance cessation support in primary healthcare.

items.title: The L.I.F.T. Project-the 6 Intervention Mapping Steps to Create a Faith-Based HIV Health Education Intervention in the U.S. South.
items.abstract: Memphis, TN ranks first in the U.S. for HIV incidence and is designated as a high priority geographic area by the U.S. Ending the HIV Epidemic (EHE) Initiative. National EHE goals call for active engagement of all community sectors, including faith-based organizations, to promote HIV testing and prevention. Given Memphis' high density of predominately Black Churches and faith-centric culture, these institutions serve as a strategic platform for culturally tailored behavioral interventions. This study details the 6 behavioral intervention mapping (IM) steps used to plan, implement, and evaluate Leading by Igniting Faith and Education to Tackle Stigma (L.I.F.T.)-a faith-based HIV health education curriculum addressing HIV testing and prevention discrepancies in high HIV-incidence areas. IM is a systematic approach, useful for involving faith communities by providing a theory-informed scaffolding to address HIV disparities via community education programming.

items.title: Re-Evaluating Predictive Performance in the Clinical Risk Analysis Index of Frailty.
items.abstract: Objective To examine whether the Risk Analysis Index (RAI), last calibrated in 2010-2014, requires scoring system changes to remain an effective measure of surgical frailty. Summary background data The RAI is among the most validated and widely used measures of surgical frailty. However, like any clinical prediction model, the RAI's scoring system might be prone to algorithmic drift that could invalidate continued use. Methods Retrospective cohort study of patients evaluated in outpatient surgery clinics at Veterans Health Administration (VHA) or University of Pittsburgh Medical Center (UPMC). All-cause mortality was measured 180 days after frailty assessment using the RAI-clinical questionnaire (RAI-C). Results In 410,715 patients from UPMC and 190,044 patients from VHA, the existing RAI-C scoring system demonstrated strong discrimination (c = 0.868 95% CI [0.864-0.872] for UPMC, 0.827 [0.822-0.832] for VHA) which improved modestly after recalibrating parameter weights (c = 0.872 95% CI [0.868-0.876], for UPMC, 0.839 [0.834-0.845] for VHA). Calibration improved slightly, especially at the extremes where the model tends to underpredict mortality, but little change was observed in the range around the threshold of frailty. Of note, the scoring weights associated with a cancer diagnosis demonstrated some multicollinearity-driven instability, but cancer remained the largest contributor to total score. Decision curve analysis demonstrated that reclassification of just a single additional patient as frail would require screening 1400-6000 patients with the recalibrated system, depending on the threshold score defining frailty, and after accounting for the harms of false-positive classification, weighted proportional to the odds at each threshold probability. Conclusions The RAI scoring system remains robust after a decade of widespread use without evidence of meaningful algorithmic drift. The minimal incremental improvement associated with recalibration does not justify the resources required to disseminate and implement a revised scoring system.

items.title: Association of serum element levels with cardiovascular diseases and type 2 diabetes mellitus risk in a Kurdish population of western Iran.
items.abstract: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are a significant public health concern globally. Among the most prevalent NCDs the study aims to explore the association of some elements with the the likelihood of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D) development. In this cross-sectional case control study, 300 individuals with CVDs (n = 110), T2D (n = 70), and a control group (n = 120) from the Ravansar Non-Communicable Disease (RaNCD) cohort in western Iran were examined. The RaNCD cohort is part of the PERSIAN cohort study, consisting of 10,000 adults. Participants aged 35-65 were stratified into three clusters based on their health status. Various elements, including aluminum (Al), calcium (Ca), magnesium (Mg), phosphorus (P), manganese (Mn), potassium (K), cobalt (Co), lithium (Li), boron (B), molybdenum (Mo), and vanadium (V) in the blood serum was performed using the ICP-MS method, and data were analyzed using multivariable techniques, including logistic regression and clustering analysis. Our analysis revealed a notable association between most elements and the risks of CVD and T2D in the logistic regression model after adjusting for age and gender. Specifically, increased odds ratios of CVD and T2D were identified for higher Ca, Mn, Mg, Li, V, Al, P, and Mo levels. In the T2D group, four clusters were identified: Al-B, Mn-Co-Mo, K-P, and V-Li-Ca-Mg. In the CVD group, five clusters were observed: K, B-Co-Mo, Li-Mg, Ca-P, and Mn-Al-V. The study provides valuable insights into the role of some essential elements in the development of CVDs and T2D. The key elements that are most linked to the elevated risk of CVDs and T2D include calcium, manganese, molybdenum, vanadium, lithium, aluminum, phosphorus, and magnesium. Further exploration of the intricate relationships between elements and disease risk could enhance our understanding of preventive strategies and personalized interventions for individuals at risk of CVDs and T2D.

items.title: Age-specific survival after breast conservation versus mastectomy for ductal carcinoma in situ of the breast.
items.abstract: Breast conservation for invasive breast cancer is associated with better survival and fewer complications than mastectomy, which is especially relevant for older patients. It is unclear whether this can be extrapolated to ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS). This population-based cohort study used data from the Breast Cancer Database Sweden (BCBaSe 3.0) to compare overall survival (OS), breast cancer-specific survival (BCSS) and local recurrence (LR) probabilities in three different age groups (< 60, 60-69, 70 + years) of women with primary DCIS undergoing breast-conserving surgery with radiotherapy (BCS + RT), mastectomy without radiotherapy (Mx-RT), or breast-conserving surgery without radiotherapy (BCS-RT) during 2008-2019. Complete cases (CC) and multiple imputation (MI) analyses were applied. In 7165 women, treatment was BCS + RT (53.3%), BCS-RT (13.4%), or Mx-RT (33.2%). Estimated 10-year OS was 90.4% (95% CI 89.3-91.5) and BCSS 98.8% (98.3-99.2). After adjustments for patient and tumour factors, including socioeconomic status and comorbidity, Mx-RT was associated with a higher overall mortality than BCS + RT in CC (HR 2.10; 95% CI 1.20-3.67) but not in MI analyses (HR 1.29; 0.95-1.76). In age 70 + years, however, the overall mortality was consistently increased (CC: HR 2.48; 1.09-5.62, MI: HR 1.89; 1.23-2.90). Also BCS-RT was associated with a higher overall mortality than BCS + RT (CC: HR 2.68; 1.34-5.34, and MI: HR 1.72; 1.23-2.39). The 10-year LR probability was low (7.2%, 95% CI 6.3-8.0). Compared to BCS + RT, Mx-RT was associated with a lower (HR 0.18, 95% CI 0.11-0.28) and BCS-RT with a higher LR risk (HR 1.79; 1.31-2.46), especially among ages 70+. BCS + RT in DCIS appears safe. Acknowledging potential selection bias, BCS + RT may be associated with favourable overall survival outcomes in older women despite a higher risk of local recurrence.

items.title: Extreme temperatures and the epithelial barrier theory.
items.abstract: Extreme temperatures are now recognized as significant global health threats, driving morbidity and mortality across diverse diseases by compromising epithelial barrier integrity and causing periepithelial inflammation. The epithelial barrier theory posits that environmentally induced barrier dysfunction, driven by modern industrial and urban exposures, leads to compromised surfaces of the exposed tissues accompanied by epithelial activation and barrier dysfunction, microbial dysbiosis, loss of commensal bacteria, opportunistic pathogen colonization, bacterial translocation, inflammation and immune dysregulation. While toxic chemical exposures have been the primary focus of barrier research, temperature extremes-now intensified by anthropogenic warming, altered weather patterns and regional climatic variability-may similarly disrupt epithelial structure and function. Heat and cold can alter tight-junction regulation, induce mitochondrial and endoplasmic reticulum stress, oxidative stress, apoptosis and modify cytokine and chemokine profiles, thereby weakening barrier defenses and enhancing susceptibility to pollutants, allergens and pathogens. These effects may be amplified by co-exposures such as humidity fluctuations, UV radiation, wildfire smoke and increased pollutant loads associated with floods, droughts and other environmental catastrophes. Shifts in the exposome, including contamination of water systems and food chains, further link temperature-related barrier injury to rising rates of noncommunicable diseases (NCDs). Clinical and epidemiological evidence supports associations between heat waves and disease exacerbations, between cold exposure and infectious or allergic responses, and between altered weather patterns and growing prevalence of NCDs. This review synthesizes mechanistic, environmental and epidemiological data to highlight extreme temperatures as critical drivers of epithelial barrier dysfunction and global disease burden.

items.title: Association between ambient temperature and acute kidney injury: a nationwide space-time-stratified case-crossover study in Japan.
items.abstract: Background Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a severe condition characterized by a sudden decline of kidney function with a high mortality rate and healthcare costs. While extreme heat is a recognized risk factor for AKI, the effects of both heat and cold exposure across different demographics remain unclear. Objective To examine the association between ambient temperatures and AKI emergency hospitalizations, with a focus on age and sex differences. Methods Using a nationwide database, we identified 119,027 AKI emergency hospitalizations from 2011 to 2019. A space-time-stratified case-crossover study with conditional quasi-Poisson regression analysis was applied to estimate region-specific relative risk (RR) of AKI emergency hospitalization over lag days 0-13. Pooled RRs were calculated using random-effects meta-analysis. Analyses were stratified by age (younger, 15-49; middle-age, 50-64; and older, 65+ years old) and sex. Results Both extreme cold (first percentile) and heat (99th percentile) were associated with an increased risk of AKI emergency hospitalizations, with cumulative RRs of 1.24 (95% CI 1.09-1.40) and 2.21 (95% CI 2.00-2.43), respectively. Heat-related susceptibility was highest in younger (RR 4.24, 95% CI 2.93-6.15) and middle-aged men (RR 4.20, 95% CI 3.46-5.10), while in women it occurred in the older group (RR 1.87, 95% CI 1.64-2.14). Cold-related susceptibility was highest among older males (RR 1.28, 95% CI 1.06-1.53) and females (RR 1.29, 95% CI 1.04-1.58). Significance Extreme temperatures elevate AKI risk, with distinct age- and sex-specific vulnerability patterns. These findings highlight the need for targeted prevention strategies during temperature extremes, particularly protecting younger and middle-aged men from heat and older adults from cold exposure. Understanding the biological and social mechanisms underlying these demographic differences is essential for developing effective public health interventions in a changing climate IMPACT STATEMENT: This nationwide study reveals that both extreme heat and cold significantly increase acute kidney injury (AKI) emergency hospitalizations in Japan, with distinct age- and sex-specific vulnerability patterns. Younger and middle-aged men face a fourfold higher risk during heat exposure, while older adults of both sexes are most vulnerable to cold. These findings expand beyond heat-focused research and demonstrate the need for demographically targeted prevention strategies. As climate change intensifies temperature variability, these demographic-specific patterns highlight the need for tailored public health interventions to protect kidney health and reduce preventable AKI hospitalizations.

items.title: High-risk antimicrobial resistance genomic traits in multidrug-resistant Salmonella across China's food chain: projections to 2050.
items.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is rising globally, yet factors shaping its genomic evolution remain poorly understood. We investigated how socioeconomic, climate, and health factors are associated with AMR spread in multi-drug resistant (MDR) Salmonella enterica across China's food chain, mapped hotspots and forecasted genomic trait prevalence to 2050. We analysed 2,536 MDR genomes from 15 provinces over 16 years, covering patients, food and non-food workers, meat, livestock, and environmental sources. A machine learning framework integrated genomic surveillance with risk assessment to identify high-risk AMR traits (clinically relevant, MDR, mobile). Regression models linked trait prevalence to socioeconomic, climate, health, and antimicrobial consumption data, informing projections to 2050. Eighty-four high-risk traits, including carbapenem, colistin, and β-lactam resistance, are projected to rise, with antibiotic use, population growth, healthcare spending, and urbanisation. Projections were trait-specific: bla CTX-M-64 and bla TEM-1 may increase up to 20%, while bla CTX-M-65 and bla CTX-M-14 remain below 5%. A mechanistic shift in fluoroquinolone resistance is projected: mutation-based resistance (gyrA 87) declines while plasmid-mediated genes (qnrB17, qnrS1) rise. Food workers emerged as a potential reservoir, showing higher trait prevalence than food sources, uniquely carrying last-resort antibiotic-resistance genes (bla TEM-30 , bla NDM-5 , bla CTX-M-64 ). Integrating genomic with socioeconomic surveillance could shift AMR interventions from reactive to preventive.

items.title: Food insecurity in the development of metabolic diseases.
items.abstract: This Review discusses the current evidence on the relationship between food insecurity, obesity, metabolic syndrome and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), and identifies potential interventions to mitigate the effect of food insecurity on these conditions. Studies in adults (mainly cross-sectional) have consistently found associations between food insecurity and several cardiometabolic diseases, including obesity (mainly among women), hyperlipidaemia, metabolic syndrome, hypertension, cardiovascular disease and T2DM. These associations represent plausible causal relationships given that food insecurity can be a powerful psycho-emotional stressor that can cause distress, anxiety and depressive symptoms across the life course; poor dietary quality can increase the risk of metabolic syndrome and T2DM through increased visceral adiposity and insulin resistance, inflammation and an unhealthy microbiome; and food insecurity can cause healthcare behavioural trade-offs such as prioritizing purchasing food over medications for T2DM prevention or management. Community-based, healthy lifestyle promotion, early-life nutrition and Food as Medicine programmes could mitigate the negative effect of food insecurity on T2DM risk and metabolic health. There is a need to rigorously evaluate the results of promising large-scale interventions on food insecurity and cardiometabolic health outcomes.

items.title: Recovering anaerobic bacterial genomes in saliva, tumour and blood whole genome sequencing data from patients with prostate cancer.
items.abstract: Microbial constituents in the gastrointestinal tract, the urine and prostate tissue are being linked with clinical differences in prostate cancer, and a recent meta-analysis has linked periodontal disease to this cancer. Several hypotheses exist regarding how specific bacteria can contribute towards the development of prostate cancer. Recovering microbial genomes, and their genomic features, from clinical samples and investigating fine-scale taxonomy is a critical first step in investigating causality. Here, we describe the microbial diversity of samples associated with prostate cancer. Metagenomic assembly of non-human reads from the PanProstate Cancer Group, derived from blood, saliva samples and prostate tissue whole-genome data (N = 247), successfully reconstructed 249 highly complete bacterial genomes, predominantly from oral samples. Our data, reveals eighteen bacterial species from the oral cavity without species level classification, while demonstrating a wide range of known species. This approach enables us to gain additional insights of the microbes in cancer patients at no additional sequencing cost and has the potential to reveal new links that could improve our understanding of cancer initiation and development.

items.title: The tumor macroenvironment as cancer metabolism's next frontier.
items.abstract: The deregulated utilization of nutrients by tumors, first observed over a century ago, is recognized as a hallmark of cancer and continues to be exploited clinically to image neoplastic disease. Despite this historic focus on cancer cells and, more recently, their neighbors, metabolic reprogramming is not limited to the tumor microenvironment. Tumors also have the capacity to rewire the metabolism of cells throughout the body, including those at distant sites, often referred to as the tumor macroenvironment. Alterations in the metabolism of noncancerous tissues outside the local tumor ecosystem are gaining attention, but their origins and consequences remain incompletely defined. A deeper understanding of these changes may reveal previously unrecognized signatures of disease and unexplored opportunities for therapeutic intervention.

items.title: The content and reporting completeness of physical therapist-led interventions for glenohumeral osteoarthritis: a systematic review.
items.abstract: Objectives This study synthesised the content and reporting completeness of published physical therapist-led interventions for glenohumeral osteoarthritis (GHOA). Methods This systematic review undertook electronic database searches in PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane, CINAHL and PEDro (until June 2025) for any peer-reviewed articles/studies describing physical therapist-led interventions across non-surgical and perioperative settings for adults aged 45 years and over with GHOA. The content and reporting completeness were synthesized using the 22-item Template for Intervention Description and Replication for rehabilitation interventions (TIDIeR_Rehab). Results Overall, 134 articles/studies describing 156 physical therapist-led interventions were included, comprising mostly case series designs (n=47, 35.1%) or narrative reviews (n=38, 28.4%). Of the remaining 49 articles/studies, only 11 were studies reporting RCT results and three were protocols of RCTs in progress. Intervention content varied considerably, and the overall completeness of intervention item reporting was poor (only 18%). Interventions in non-surgical contexts commonly included strengthening exercises (n=33, 53.2%), range of motion (ROM) exercises (n=23, 37.1%), and electrotherapy modalities (n=16, 25.8%). Sling immobilisation was most reported in postoperative interventions (n=64, 72.7%). Many different proposed mechanisms of action were reported (n=49, 31.4%); but all were biomechanically orientated. Conclusion Very few high-quality empirical studies evaluating physical therapist-led interventions for GHOA have been published. We found substantial heterogeneity in the content of published physical therapist-led interventions, and the reporting completeness was generally poor. This suggests considerable uncertainty regarding best practice physical therapy for GHOA in terms of intervention content. Future high-quality empirical research is needed, preferably using RCT designs that include clear descriptions of interventions.

items.title: Barriers and enablers to engagement with green social prescribing in primary care: a scoping review using the socio-ecological model.
items.abstract: Background Green social prescribing (GSP) connects individuals with nature-based interventions (NBIs) through healthcare providers, link workers, and social and community networks. While evidence supports the health benefits of NBIs, further research is needed to understand the factors that influence engagement. Aim To explore barriers and enablers to GSP and NBIs for prescribers, service users and community providers. Design & setting A scoping review in primary care and community settings. Method We systematically searched Medline, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, and SCOPUS from 2019. We assessed quality using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme and the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. We mapped data to the socioecological framework during synthesis. Results Out of 4864 screened records, 45 studies from 11 countries were included. GSP and NBIs face micro-level barriers such as knowledge gaps, cultural and social issues, time and cost constraints and perceptions of adverse weather; meso-level and macro-level challenges include unequal access, underfunded NBIs, an emphasis on biomedical models, safety concerns, limited training, and insufficient policy support and leadership. Engagement was enabled by flexible, person-centred approaches, tailored NBIs with clear pathways, including link workers, strong cross-sector partnerships, community co-design, and public health campaigns. Conclusion Promoting engagement with GSP and NBIs requires a multi-level approach that addresses systemic barriers through collaboration between prescribers, third-sector organisations and policymakers. Investment in workforce training and sustainable funding models is critical to support long-term success in primary care and community settings. Addressing health inequalities by improving access for people in areas of high socioeconomic deprivation remains a priority.

items.title: Efficacy and Feasibility of Just-in-Time Nudging in Reducing Evening Snacking Measured by Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Micro-Randomized Study.
items.abstract: Aims This study aimed to determine whether in people with Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), a digital nudge delivered by a smartphone app soon after dinner reduces subsequent snacking events as measured by continuous glucose monitoring (CGM). Methods Participants: Adults with T2DM, managed with diet or stable oral antidiabetic medication for at least 3 months, and who habitually snacked after dinner on ≥ 3 nights/week. Design Pictographic nudges were co-designed with consumers. After-dinner snacking behaviours were confirmed during a 2-week Lead-In phase by CGM. Thereafter, eligible participants were micro-randomized daily (1:1, MRT phase) to either a pictographic nudge delivered-in-time (Intui Research) or no nudge for a second 2-week period. The primary outcome was the difference in incremental area under the CGM curve (net-iAUC) between nudging days and non-nudging days during the period 90-min post-dinner until 4 AM. Results Sixty-six participants completed the Lead-In phase and 56 completed the MRT phase with available CGM data. CGM data were collected over 911 nights during the Lead-In phase and 780 nights during the MRT phase, with a total of 410 digital nudges sent. Over the entire 2-week period there was no effect of nudging on the primary outcome (net-iAUC). However, secondary analyses showed that there was an initial nudge effect that faded over time. Similar results were observed for snacking behaviour and CGM time-in-range. Conclusion This study provides preliminary feasibility of delivering just-in-time nudges in adults with T2DM, with no overall glycaemic benefit. Exploratory early effects warrant confirmation and investigation of strategies to sustain efficacy. Trial registration ACTRN12622000531718.

items.title: Stratum Corneum Biomarkers for Differentiating Irritant and Allergic Contact Dermatitis.
items.abstract: Background/objectives Occupational hand dermatitis (HD) comprises irritant and allergic contact dermatitis (ICD and ACD), which share clinical features, often overlap, and may coexist with atopic dermatitis (AD), complicating diagnosis. The objective of this study is to explore whether stratum corneum (SC) biomarkers discriminate ICD from ACD. Patients We recruited 126 patients from the Occupational Dermato-allergology Clinics of the Amsterdam UMC. Methods SC samples were collected from lesional HD skin and patch test reactions to nickel, chromium, methylisothiazolinone, sodium lauryl sulfate (irritant), and control sites. Thirty-three biomarkers were analyzed. Random forest and penalized regression models were trained on the patch test dataset and validated in HD; an additional model was trained and validated in HD. Exploratory analyses evaluated discrimination among individual allergens and between AD, ICD and ACD. Results The patch test model showed good discrimination between ICD and ACD (mean AUC 0.85, 95% CI 0.82-0.87), driven primarily by skin barrier-related biomarkers. In HD, performance declined (mean AUC 0.51, 95% CI 0.26-0.76); sensitivity for ACD was 88%. Model trained and validated within HD achieved mean AUC of 0.60 (95% CI 0.57-0.64). Discrimination between individual allergens yielded mean AUC of 0.75 (95% CI 0.72-0.77). Conclusion SC biomarkers discriminated ICD from ACD good in acute patch test, but showed limited discrimination in HD, reflecting differences between acute and chronic inflammation.

items.title: Combined Anterior-Posterior vs. Posterior-Only Fusion in Adult Spinal Deformity Radiographic, Clinical, and Mechanical Outcomes With Longitudinal Mixed-Effects Analysis.
items.abstract: Study DesignRetrospective cohort study.ObjectivesTo compare radiographic, clinical, and mechanical outcomes of posterior-only versus combined anterior-posterior fusion in adult spinal deformity (ASD) patients undergoing long-segment thoracolumbar fusion with pelvic fixation.MethodsConsecutive ASD patients undergoing instrumented fusion ≥7 levels with pelvic fixation at a single center (2016-2023) were stratified by surgical approach. Longitudinal radiographic changes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models with difference-in-differences (DiD) estimation. Mechanical complications were evaluated with Kaplan-Meier survival and Cox proportional hazards analysis.Results207 patients were included (posterior-only, n=115; combined, n=92). Mean age was 62.1 ± 11.1 years (77.8% female), with mean follow-up of 46.2 ± 21.2 months. The combined approach demonstrated significantly greater DiD estimates for lumbar lordosis (-7.8° to -9.2°, all p<0.001), relative pelvic version mismatch (+3.4° to +4.2°, all p<0.001), and GAP score (-1.8 to -2.1, all p<0.001) at all postoperative timepoints. DiD estimates were stable across three covariate specifications. Rod fractures occurred in 14.8% of posterior-only versus 3.3% of combined patients (p=0.008), with superior rod fracture-free survival in the combined cohort (log-rank p=0.019). In the primary Cox model, the combined approach showed a non-significant trend toward lower rod fracture hazard (HR 0.35, 95% CI 0.10-1.24, p=0.10). Patient-reported outcomes improved comparably in both groups.ConclusionsIn long-segment ASD fusion with pelvic fixation, the combined anterior-posterior approach was associated with greater sustained sagittal correction and lower rod fracture rates, while both approaches provided comparable clinical improvement.

items.title: Experiences and Challenges of Home Blood Pressure Monitoring Among Patients with Uncontrolled Hypertension: A Qualitative Study.
items.abstract: IntroductionHome blood pressure monitoring (HBPM) is recommended for hypertension management. However, patients' experiences and challenges with HBPM, particularly among those with uncontrolled hypertension, remain poorly understood. This study aimed to explore how patients with uncontrolled hypertension experience and perform HBPM, and the challenges they encounter.MethodSeventeen adults aged ≥21 years with uncontrolled hypertension were purposively recruited from three public primary care clinics in Singapore. A qualitative descriptive-interpretive study used in-depth, semi-structured, audio-recorded face-to-face interviews until data saturation. Interview transcripts were analysed thematically. The qualitative data were managed using NVivo version 14.ResultsMost participants owned an HBPM device, yet their practices varied widely. Patients engaged in selective monitoring, measuring blood pressure mainly when symptomatic or close to clinic visits. Many adapted HBPM routines to fit competing life demands, resulting in irregular timing and frequency. Selective recording of readings, including omission of higher values, was frequently reported. Documentation preferences differed by digital literacy, with older patients preferring paper records. HBPM was often perceived as a healthcare provider (HCP) assigned task rather than a self-care behaviour. Limited and inconsistent guidance from HCP contributed to confusion and reduced motivation.ConclusionAmong patients with uncontrolled hypertension, guideline-concordant HBPM was shaped by practical barriers, uncertainty about correct monitoring and documentation, and the extent of HCP engagement. Participants' selective monitoring and recording practices highlight the need for clearer patient education, consistent provider feedback, and tailored documentation approaches to support more reliable use of HBPM in primary care.

items.title: Interactions Between Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon Exposure and Epigenetic Regulatory Genes in Embryonic Arrest.
items.abstract: Embryonic arrest poses a significant clinical challenge, yet the interplay between environmental toxicants and epigenetic modifiers remain poorly understood. This is the first study to systematically investigate whether genetic variants in N6-methyladenosine (m6A) methylation enzymes mediate the toxicity polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in early pregnancy loss. In a case-control study of 151 embryonic arrest patients and 151 controls, we quantified PAH-DNA adducts and m6A regulators (methyltransferase-like 3 [METTL3] and AlkB homolog 5 [ALKBH5]) in villus tissues. Three key single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in METTL3 and ALKBH5 were genotyped. Strikingly, high PAH-DNA adduct levels conferred a dramatically elevated risk of embryonic arrest (OR=18.57, 95% CI: 7.90-43.67, P<0.001). While METTL3 levels remained unchanged, ALKBH5 protein was significantly upregulated in cases (P<0.001). Crucially, the ALKBH5 rs4925144 TT genotype exhibited a strong protective effect against embryonic arrest (aOR=0.35, 95% CI: 0.14-0.87, P=0.024). Generalized multifactor dimensionality reduction (GMDR) revealed a significant synergistic interaction, wherein high PAHs exposure combined with the rs4925144 CC/CT genotypes drastically amplified risk. Structural equation modeling (SEM) confirmed that both PAH-DNA adducts (β=0.480, P<0.001) and ALKBH5 expression (β=0.178, P<0.001) directly drive embryonic arrest pathogenesis. These findings identify a novel gene-environment interaction underlying embryonic arrest and suggest that combining ALKBH5 rs4925144 genotyping with PAHs exposure assessment could serve as a valuable biomarker for early risk stratification, informing targeted intervention to prevent pregnancy loss.

items.title: Lung cancer screening knowledge, attitudes, and practices among primary care providers in Georgia, USA: A survey analysis.
items.abstract: To inform lung cancer screening (LCS) in primary care settings, the study assessed providers' knowledge, attitudes, and practices around LCS and recommended implementation strategies. The online survey was administered from May-August 2025 among primary care providers in Georgia, USA. We ran descriptive analyses for all data and linear regression for predictors of greater knowledge. Providers (N = 112) had an average knowledge score of 3.72/5 (SD = 1.11). Physicians (N = 73) scored significantly higher than nurses/nurse practitioners (β = -1.0, 95% CI: -1.6, -0.44). Overall, participants viewed LCS positively, and about 45% reported offering LCS at their facility while 50% reported referring patients to LCS programs. Most (75.5%) had strategies to follow-up with patients who screened positive, but few (22.6%) offered tobacco cessation services. Top barriers were cost, lack of patient knowledge/interest, and transportation; cost assistance, patient education materials, and patient navigation were the top facilitators. Providers (N = 86) identified 'Distributing patient educational materials' and 'Reminding clinicians' as highly feasible and important implementation strategies. While most providers had sufficient knowledge, positive perceptions, and high availability of LCS services, few engage in patient education or offer smoking cessation resources. Patient education and clinician reminders may be beneficial implementation strategies for primary care-based LCS.

items.title: Clinical and radiographic factors associated with residual low back pain after single-level decompression for lumbar spinal stenosis: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
items.abstract: Residual low back pain (LBP) after decompression for lumbar spinal stenosis (LSS) varies considerably and is likely multifactorial. It remains unclear how residual LBP differs by preoperative severity and which factors are independently associated with it. To examine how postoperative LBP improves across preoperative severity groups and to identify clinical and radiographic factors independently associated with residual LBP. Multicenter retrospective cohort study. A total of 450 patients undergoing primary single-level posterior decompression for LSS at six institutions (2017-2023). The primary outcome was the 1-year postoperative numerical rating scale (NRS) score for LBP. Secondary outcomes were buttock and leg pain NRS, Oswestry Disability Index, EuroQol 5-Dimension, and postoperative satisfaction. Patients were stratified into three predefined preoperative LBP severity groups (Mild 0-3, Moderate 4-7, Severe 8-10). Inverse probability weighting (IPW) was applied for three-group comparisons. Unweighted multivariable linear regression for postoperative LBP NRS included preoperative LBP NRS together with patient, surgical, and radiographic factors as covariates. This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. The authors report no study-specific conflicts of interest. The IPW-adjusted Severe group showed the largest LBP NRS improvement (4.5 points) but the highest residual LBP NRS (4.1). Dissatisfaction did not differ across groups (p=.244). Factors independently associated with residual LBP were preoperative LBP NRS (B=0.381, p 20° (B=0.681, p=.024), and American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status (ASA-PS) ≥3 (B=1.298, p=.017). Greater preoperative LBP severity was associated with both larger improvement and higher residual LBP. Preoperative LBP severity, PI-LL >20°, and ASA-PS ≥3 were independent factors for residual LBP.

items.title: The Evolution of Shiga Toxin-Producing Escherichia coli Characterization and Risk Categorization Strategies.
items.abstract: Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli (STEC) are a group of E. coli that cause food and waterborne enteric illness. STEC are genotypically and phenotypically diverse as they do not have a single evolutionary origin, instead multiple STEC lineages have appeared independently following horizontal gene transfer events. The diversity of STEC is also reflected in an apparent variability in the potential of individual STEC strains to cause severe illness (bloody diarrhea or hemolytic uremic syndrome) or be involved in large foodborne outbreaks. In the context of food safety decision making, the variable characteristics of STEC strains and their potential health outcomes have resulted in an ongoing debate on how STEC should be categorized into risk groups. The aim of this review is to clarify that debate by examining how STEC characterization and risk categorization strategies have evolved over time in response to changes in analytical techniques, understanding of STEC epidemiology, and pathogenicity mechanisms. The origin of established perspectives and practices is explored, from the recognition of STEC O157:H7 as an emerging pathogen in the 1980s, through serotype-based identification and characterization of STEC, to contemporary approaches based on molecular markers for virulence. The evidence for the role of specific virulence factors in STEC pathogenicity is reviewed and their utility in STEC risk categorisation assessed. Finally, a binary categorization scheme is proposed, based on evidence for the correlation of hemolytic uremic syndrome, with the presence of Shiga toxin subtypes Stx2a, Stx2c, Stx2d, and colonisation factors including the Locus of Enterocyte Effacement (intimin/eae) and Enteroaggregative attachment (aggR/aaiC).

items.title: Genomic epidemiology of Salmonella from retail chicken meat in Japan: decline in pESI-like plasmid-harboring S. Infantis ST32 and predominance of S. Schwarzengrund ST241.
items.abstract: Salmonella is a major foodborne pathogen, and chicken meat is an important source of infection. This study investigated Salmonella prevalence, serovar distribution, antimicrobial resistance, and genomic characteristics in 150 retail chicken meat samples collected in Japan in 2023. The predominant serovar was S. Schwarzengrund (42.7%), followed by S. Infantis (7.3%), which has long been the predominant serovar in Japan. The globally expanding S. Infantis sequence type (ST) 32 harboring pESI-like plasmids has declined in Japan. In contrast, S. Schwarzengrund ST241 was isolated more frequently in winter (66%) than in summer (31%, P < 0.001) and more often from chicken meat produced in eastern Japan (47.1%) than in western Japan (29.4%, P = 0.042). Antimicrobial resistance was most common to tetracycline (50.6%) and streptomycin (45.7%), whereas kanamycin resistance (33.3%) had declined compared with 2015 to 2019, consistent with reduced use of this antimicrobial in broiler production. Moreover, the proportion of S. Schwarzengrund isolates lacking antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) increased markedly from summer (19.4%) to winter (45.5%). cgMLST analysis revealed that antimicrobial-susceptible S. Schwarzengrund isolates formed the largest clade and, notably, retained pESI-like plasmids despite apparent loss of ARG-containing regions from these plasmids. These findings demonstrate ongoing genomic shifts in Salmonella populations in Japan and underscore the need for continuous genomic surveillance to mitigate their public health impact.

items.title: Tracking Illnesses Caused by Four Foodborne Pathogens Over Four Decades of the Healthy People Initiative.
items.abstract: The Healthy People (HP) Initiative, a collaboration between the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and various public and private organizations, aims to improve the health and well-being of all Americans. HP consists of national health objectives with 10-year targets to achieve by the end of the decade. Since HP2000, progress toward goals on four foodborne pathogens (Campylobacter, Listeria monocytogenes, Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli, and Salmonella) has been primarily tracked using data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's Foodborne Diseases Active Surveillance Network (FoodNet). The data used to inform the HP food safety goals spans nearly four decades from 1987 (HP2000) to 2024 (the most recent HP2030 data point). Each decade, measuring foodborne pathogen objectives has become more rigorous and target-setting methods have evolved. HP2000 objectives aimed at a reduction in infections to no more than a set value and, most recently, HP2030 objectives were developed to align with key regulations or targeted a percent improvement in foodborne illness infections. Progress toward these targets has been monitored and categorized (getting worse, no detectable change, improving, or met target) for these pathogens. This article details the advancements made to more accurately establish targets, assess the data, and measure progress at the end or most recent data point of each decade. Each decade, measurement of objectives, baseline-setting methods, target-setting methods, and reporting progress methods have evolved. For this reason, caution must be taken when attempting to compare data across decades.

items.title: Interaction patterns of internalized and perceived stigma with antidepressant adverse reactions on medication adherence in major depressive disorder: A prospective cohort study.
items.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a leading global cause of disease burden, and suboptimal medication adherence is a primary driver of treatment failure. Both depression stigma and antidepressant adverse drug reactions (ADRs) are established barriers to adherence, but their interactive effects and temporal dynamics in MDD remain poorly characterized. The subjects of this prospective cohort study were MDD patients from the Depression Cohort in China. Medication adherence, stigma, and ADRs were repeated assessed at baseline and weeks 4, 8, 12, 24, 48, and 72 using the Medication Adherence Rating Scale, Depression Stigma Scale, and Side-effect Rating Scale for Antidepressants, respectively. Generalized additive mixed model (GAMM) was employed to explore the interaction between stigma and ADRs, while analyzing its temporal effect on medication adherence. Among 1770 patients with a mean (SD) age of 28.74 (7.90) years, 68.53% were female. GAMMs showed significant nonlinear interactions between internalized stigma (IS) and ADRs, and between perceived stigma (PS) and ADRs (both P < 0.001; edf = 6.309 and 8.301). IS predominantly impaired adherence when ADRs were severe, whereas PS exerts the strongest negative effect when ADRs were mild. The study found no statistical evidence of temporal heterogeneity (P = 0.175 and 0.673, respectively). Stigma and ADRs jointly influence antidepressant adherence through a stable, nonlinear interaction pattern. The divergent effects of IS and PS across ADRs severity levels support differentiated intervention strategies: prioritizing ADRs management for patients with high IS, and providing early psychosocial support for those with high PS.

items.title: Fatigue, Anxiety and Depression 12 Months After Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Population Based Cohort Study.
items.abstract: To determine the prevalence and factors associated with fatigue, anxiety, and depression 12 months after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA); examine their associations with health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and functional recovery; and compare symptom burden with population norms. This prospective, population-based cohort study included adults (≥18 years) who received EMS-attempted resuscitation and survived to hospital discharge following non-traumatic OHCA in Victoria, Australia, between July 2019 and June 2022. Survivors were identified from a statewide OHCA registry and completed a 12-month telephone interview. Primary outcomes were fatigue (Modified Fatigue Impact Scale), anxiety and depression (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale). Secondary outcomes included HRQoL (EQ-5D, SF-12), functional recovery (GOSE), living arrangement, and return to work. Of 1068 eligible 12-month survivors, 728 (68.2%) completed follow-up (median age 61 years; 555 [76.2%] male). Fatigue was reported by 35.8% (250/699), anxiety by 22.6% (162/716), and depression by 18.0% (129/716). Higher symptom burden was associated with lower EQ-5D and SF-12 scores, worse GOSE outcomes (all p<0.001) and reduced return-to-work rates. Compared with population norms, survivors reported greater fatigue (SMD 0.64; 95%CI, 0.50-0.78;p<0.001), and depression (SMD, 0.12; 95%CI, 0.02,0.21;p=0.02) but lower anxiety (SMD, -0.27; 95%CI, -0.35 to -0.18;p<0.001). In adjusted models, younger age, preexisting anxiety or depression, diabetes and initial non-shockable arrest were associated with higher symptom burden, whereas EMS-witnessed arrests were associated with lower symptom burden. Fatigue, anxiety, and depression were common at 12 months after OHCA and are associated with poorer recovery. Fatigue exceeded population norms and may be an under-recognised component of cardiac arrest survivorship.

items.title: Association Between Capnographic Changes During Pulse Checks of Varying Durations and Clinical Outcomes During Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation: A Multicenter Study From Türkiye (CaPTuRe).
items.abstract: To investigate the association between capnographic changes during pulse checks of different durations and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) outcomes. This multicenter, prospective, controlled, quasi-randomized study categorized patients according to pulse check duration: Group A (≤5 seconds) and Group B (>5 to ≤10 seconds). Five measurements were obtained during the first six CPR cycles. Four capnographic parameters were evaluated for each measurement: Post-CPR end-tidal carbon dioxide (ETCO2), Pre-CPR ETCO2, loss rate (percentage decrease between Post- and Pre-CPR ETCO2), and recovery time (time required to regain the previous cycle's Post-CPR ETCO2). The study included 252 cardiac arrest patients (Group A, n=124; Group B, n=128). In Group A, patients with return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) had markedly lower loss rates and shorter recovery times than non-survivors, together with higher pre- and post-CPR ETCO2 values (all p<0.001). Group A also had a higher ROSC rate than Group B (36.3% vs. 19.5%; p=0.005). Logistic regression identified pulse check duration as an independent predictor of ROSC, with Group A having 2.39-fold higher odds of ROSC than Group B (odds ratio [OR]=2.39, 95% confidence interval [CI]=1.347-4.242; p=0.003). Pre-CPR ETCO2 was strongly negatively correlated with loss rate (ρ=-0.770), whereas Pre- and Post-CPR ETCO2 values (ρ=0.96) and loss rate and recovery time (ρ=0.89) were strongly positively correlated. Pulse checks completed within 5 seconds were associated with more favorable capnographic dynamics and higher ROSC rates than those lasting 6-10 seconds. These findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant prospective validation.

items.title: Next-Generation CRISPR-Based Molecular Diagnostics for Veterinary Parasitology: From Laboratory Innovation to One Health Surveillance.
items.abstract: Veterinary parasitic diseases remain a major threat to livestock production, companion animal health, wildlife conservation, and public health worldwide. Conventional diagnostic methods, including microscopy, serology, and culture-based techniques, often suffer from limited sensitivity, poor specificity, prolonged turnaround time, and dependence on specialized laboratory facilities. Recent advances in Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR)-based diagnostics have introduced highly sensitive, rapid, and field-deployable platforms for parasite detection. This review critically summarizes the principles and recent applications of CRISPR/Cas12, Cas13, and emerging Cas14-based diagnostic approaches in veterinary parasitology, covering protozoan, helminthic, and arthropod-borne parasites. It further compares CRISPR platforms and discusses their integration with isothermal amplification, lateral flow assays, fluorescence detection, and portable biosensors to improve diagnostic performance. Moreover, current challenges, including sample preparation, assay standardization, multiplex detection, regulatory approval, and commercialization, are highlighted. Finally, future perspectives on amplification-free CRISPR assays, artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostics, and point-of-care platforms are discussed. By providing a translational perspective from laboratory innovation to field application, this review highlights the potential of CRISPR-based diagnostics to transform veterinary parasite surveillance and disease control.

items.title: Longitudinal Proteomics Integrated with Multi‑Omics Reveal Molecular Drivers of Responses to Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy in Rectal Cancer.
items.abstract: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) is the standard treatment for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC), yet its molecular determinants of response remain unclear. We conducted longitudinal 4D-DIA proteomic profiling of pre- and post-treatment specimens from 156 patients, including 31 patients with matched pre- and post-treatment specimens, and integrated with bulk RNA sequencing, single-cell transcriptomics, and functional validation. At baseline, responders were enriched in innate and adaptive immune pathways, whereas non-responders showed proliferative and metabolic programs. Pre-treatment RAC2, elevated in responders, was positively associated with immune activation, oxaliplatin sensitivity, and survival, and was validated in GSE139255 and GSE35640 (all P < 0.05). Moreover, RAC2 demonstrated strong predictive performance (training AUC = 0.867; testing AUC = 0.857). During treatment, NAC induced fibrosis-related remodeling across all groups (all P < 0.05), while responders uniquely preserved CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration (P = 0.031). Responders and RAC2-high tumors exhibited concordant pathway dynamics during NAC. Single-cell analysis further revealed that pre-treatment tumor RAC2, higher in responders, transmitted signals to CD8⁺ T cells while receiving inputs from fibroblasts (P < 0.05). In vitro and in vivo, RAC2 knockdown reduced baseline tumor growth but promoted under oxaliplatin (all P < 0.05). Overall, this study offers proteomic insights into NAC in LARC, supports therapeutic decision-making, and identifies potential targets.

items.title: Serum Aflatoxin-Albumin Adduct Profiling and Exposure Predictors Among Gastroenterology Patients of Tertiary Hospitals in Southwestern Nigeria.
items.abstract: Aflatoxin, a potent hepatocarcinogenic mycotoxin, remains a major public health concern in sub-Saharan Africa. Due to its severe health and socio-economic impact, aflatoxin exposure needs to be monitored and mitigated. This cross-sectional study assessed serum aflatoxin-albumin adducts (AF-ALB), an objective biomarker of systemic aflatoxin exposure, among gastroenterology patients in southwestern Nigeria using ELISA. AF-ALB levels were categorized into high and low groups based on interquartile ranges. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify socio-demographic, dietary, and temporal predictors. Of the 573 participants, 405 (70.7%) were male, and 168 (29.3%) were female. Overall median AF-ALB concentration was 3.5 pg/mL. Daily groundnut consumption showed the strongest dietary association (aOR= 9.7, 95% CI: 4.3-21.9, p < 0.001), while the sampling period was also significantly associated with AF-ALB levels (p < 0.001). The association between urban residence and high AF-ALB levels was model-dependent rather than a true independent association. AF-ALB median levels varied significantly across gastroenteric diseases (p < 0.001, Cramer's V = 0.478). Age, sex, education, occupation, marital status, and aflatoxin awareness status were not significantly associated with AF-ALB levels. These findings indicate that dietary practices, particularly frequent groundnut consumption, are important predictors of aflatoxin exposure in this population.

items.title: Urinary Metabolites in Tryptophan-Kynurenine Pathway and Risk of CKD Progression in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes.
items.abstract: Tryptophan-kynurenine pathway is integral for energy metabolism and immune-inflammation regulation. We sought to study the associations between urinary metabolites in tryptophan-kynurenine pathway and risk of chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression in patients with type 2 diabetes. Prospective cohort study. 1,892 participants with type 2 diabetes from Southeast Asia were included in the primary analysis; 951 Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) participants with diabetes at baseline were included in the validation study. Urinary tryptophan, kynurenine, 3-hydroxykynurenine, kynurenic acid, xanthurenic acid and kynurenine-to-tryptophan ratio (KTR). CKD progression defined as a composite of incident end stage kidney disease (sustained eGFR < 15 ml/min/1.73m2, maintenance dialysis, renal death) or doubling of serum creatinine concentration. Cause-specific hazard regression. A total of 224 CKD progression events were identified over a median follow-up of 7.2 years. Each one SD increase in the concentration of urinary kynurenine, 3-hydroxykynurenine, kynurenic acid, and KTR was associated with 1.60 [95% CI 1.16-2.22], 1.64 [1.17-2.31], 1.47 [1.10-1.97] and 1.97 [1.43-2.71] fold higher risk of CKD progression, respectively, after adjustment for known clinical risk factors. These associations were more pronounced in participants with prevalent CKD (eGFR <60 ml/min/1.73m2) compared to those with preserved eGFR. Each one SD increase in urinary tryptophan and kynurenine concentrations was independently associated with 1.60 [1.24-2.06] and 1.35 [1.05-1.73] fold higher risk of CKD progression, respectively, in CRIC participants with diabetes. Observational study with unmeasured confounding. Higher concentrations of urinary metabolites in the tryptophan-kynurenine pathway were associated with higher risk of CKD progression in patients with type 2 diabetes. Future studies are warranted to elucidate the biological mechanisms linking the tryptophan-kynurenine pathway and progression of kidney disease.

items.title: Clinical and Laboratory Predictors for Differentiating Visceral Leishmaniasis from Hematological Malignancies in Adults with Pancytopenia.
items.abstract: Visceral leishmaniasis (VL) is a systemic, life-threatening zoonotic disease. VL and hematological malignancies (HMs) may present with overlapping clinical and laboratory features. The primary endpoint of our study was to identify the clinical and laboratory parameters for differentiating VL from HMs in adult patients with pancytopenia. The secondary endpoint was to evaluate the clinical and laboratory findings in patients with VL. In this 15.5-year retrospective case-control study, adult patients with pancytopenia who were diagnosed with VL or HMs at a tertiary referral hospital in Antalya were included. A total of 53 patients were included (VL, n = 24; HMs, n = 29). The VL group was younger and presented with a significantly longer duration from symptom onset to hospital admission compared to the HMs group (each, p 13.75 cm (AUC: 0.945, sensitivity: 92%, specificity: 93%), followed by CRP >33.5 mg/L (AUC: 0.817, sensitivity: 83%, specificity: 83%) and symptom duration >52.5 days (AUC: 0.799, sensitivity: 67%, specificity: 86%). VL should be considered in the differential diagnosis of adults with pancytopenia, particularly in endemic regions. We believe that our findings may contribute to earlier and more accurate diagnosis of VL. Prolonged symptom duration, hepatosplenomegaly, elevated AST, elevated CRP, hyperproteinemia, hypoalbuminemia, and reversed albumin-globulin ratio necessitate a high index of clinical suspicion for VL compared to HMs.

items.title: Epidemiological comparison of cirrhosis to other long-term health conditions in the United Kingdom.
items.abstract: Although cirrhosis is a serious long-term health condition (LTC), it tends to receive little attention from healthcare policymakers. Here, we sought to describe how cirrhosis compares to other LTCs to inform priority-setting discussions. We analysed data from the Our Future Health (OFH) study, a cohort of ∼1.7 million individuals from England, United Kingdom. Self-reported diagnosis status for cirrhosis and 15 benchmark LTCs (including type 1 diabetes, type 2 diabetes, Parkinson's disease, chronic kidney disease, schizophrenia, and stage 4 cancer) were ascertained from the enrolment questionnaire. Each LTC was profiled with respect to: sociodemographic characteristics; mortality; comorbidity burden; and late diagnosis. Furthermore, information on each LTC's trajectory (i.e., increasing, stable, or decreasing over time) was determined from background mortality data over the last decade. The study cohort included 1,613,777 participants, of whom 2,606 (0.2%) reported a diagnosis of cirrhosis. Mortality elevation for participants with cirrhosis versus without was substantial (HR: 7.46; P<0.001, with adjustment for age/sex) and comparable to dementia (HR:7.60), stage 4 cancer (HR:7.06), whilst higher than schizophrenia (HR:4.46) and heart failure (HR:4.01). People with cirrhosis had more co-existing health conditions/diseases than other LTCs (i.e., elevated prevalence for 58/145 distinct health conditions; second only to stage 4 cancer). Area-based deprivation score was third highest for cirrhosis, behind COPD and schizophrenia. Late diagnosis of cirrhosis was commonplace, with <15% of new-onset liver failure reporting cirrhosis at enrolment. Cirrhosis also exhibited an upward trajectory, with mortality increasing by ∼20% in the last decade. Cirrhosis is an anomaly LTC with respect to its deprivation, comorbidity, mortality, upward trajectory, and late diagnosis profile. Our data provide comparative evidence to inform priority-setting discussions with policymakers. Various levers are available to policy makers for reducing incidence of liver cirrhosis. However, other health conditions are often prioritised by policy makers ahead of cirrhosis; the decision-making process around this is not always transparent nor grounded in evidence. This study explores the characteristics of cirrhosis relative to other long-term conditions through a public-health lens. Our findings may guide priority-setting discussions between policy makers, advocates and other stakeholders and may shift current discourse onto a more empirical footing.

items.title: Reinforcement learning-driven optimal capital allocation for intelligent finance.
items.abstract: Optimal capital allocation in financial markets has long been a challenging task due to the dynamic nature of market conditions, risk factors, and the complexity of financial data. Traditional methods of portfolio management often fail to adapt to market shifts and do not fully leverage potential of modern machine learning techniques. To develop a model that dynamically optimizes capital allocation, leveraging reinforcement learning (RL), with focus on risk management, stability, and adaptability. Proposed model, Dynamic Actor-Critic (DAC)-enriched Clipped Proximal Policy Optimization (DAC-CPPO) model for portfolio optimization. A Dynamic Actor-Critic (DAC)-enriched Clipped Proximal Policy Optimization (DAC-CPPO) model is developed for portfolio optimization. The Dynamic Actor-Critic module learns optimal portfolio policies by evaluating actions and maximizing long-term returns, while the CPPO mechanism ensures stable policy updates and risk-controlled portfolio optimization. The Intelligent Finance Assets dataset contains 7,000 records with 32 features, whereas the Massive Yahoo Finance dataset includes 603k records with 9 features, collected from publicly available Kaggle sources for financial analysis. Normalization and data cleaning techniques for smooth data integration and model readiness, and LDA extracts discriminative financial features to improve portfolio allocation prediction performance. Experimental settings are implemented using Python. Proposed DAC-CPPO model, achieving 97.6% accuracy, 0.074 MAE, 0.081 RMSE, 1.91 Sharpe ratio, 1.12 Cumulative return, and 0.14 Volatility, demonstrates superior risk-adjusted performance, offering higher returns while managing market risks effectively compared to other existing models. The DAC-CPPO model offers a robust solution for practical capital allocation by combining advanced RL techniques, ensuring effective decision-making while managing risks in dynamic financial environments.

items.title: Cerebrospinal fluid and dural accumulation of α-synuclein impairs CNS clearance in Parkinson's disease.
items.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized by the build-up of α-synuclein (α-syn) in the brain, where it drives neurodegeneration. Importantly, aggregated α-syn also accumulates in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) of PD patients, and while increasingly used for diagnosis, its pathological role remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that α-syn accumulation in central nervous system (CNS) border tissues promotes CNS clearance deficits, as observed in PD patients. We find that aggregated α-syn accumulates not only in the CSF but also in the dura mater of individuals with PD, and, using acute and chronic mouse models, show that α-syn deposition in these sites induces immune alterations in CNS borders and disrupts CNS clearance. Mechanistically, we reveal that α-syn at CNS borders elevates CSF TNF and demonstrate that both TNF and α-syn aggregates themselves impair lymphatic endothelial cell function. These findings demonstrate a pathological role for α-syn in the CNS border tissues and position meningeal immunity as a contributor to CNS clearance deficits in PD pathogenesis.

items.title: An integrated human forebrain organoid reveals microglia-mediated CD8<sup>+</sup> T cell recruitment and neuroimmune dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease pathology.
items.abstract: Genetic evidence implicates immune dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet the neuroimmune mechanisms operating in human tissue remain poorly defined. Here, we establish a modular human forebrain organoid platform that systematically integrates human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived microglia and CD8 + T cells to reconstitute multicellular AD pathology. This system enables functional interrogation of both innate and adaptive immune components in a human-relevant context. Using this platform, we demonstrate that microglia mediate amyloid-β clearance and neuronal maturation but also drive inflammatory activation and recruit CD8 + T cells through CCL4/5 signaling via CCR1/5 and CXCR3, establishing a neuroinflammatory feedback loop. Pharmacological targeting of CCR5 or CXCR3 blocks T cell recruitment and modulates autophagy in a microglia-dependent manner. This modular organoid platform provides a versatile tool for dissecting neuron-immune interactions and enables cell-type-specific therapeutic screening in human neuroinflammatory disease models.

items.title: Multiplexed CRISPRi reveals a transcriptional switch between KLF activators and repressors in the maturing neocortex.
items.abstract: A critical phase of mammalian brain development takes place after birth. Neurons of the mouse neocortex undergo dramatic changes in their morphology, physiology, and synaptic connections during the first postnatal month, while properties of immature neurons, such as the capacity for robust axon outgrowth, are lost. The genetic and epigenetic programs controlling prenatal development are well studied, but our understanding of the transcriptional mechanisms that regulate postnatal neuronal maturation is comparatively lacking. By integrating chromatin accessibility and gene expression data from two subtypes of neocortical pyramidal neurons in the neonatal and maturing brain, we predicted a role for the Krüppel-like factor (KLF) family of transcription factors in the developmental regulation of neonatally expressed genes. Using a multiplexed CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) knockdown strategy, we found that a shift in expression from KLF activators (Klf6, Klf7) to repressors (Klf9, Klf13) during early postnatal development functions as a transcriptional 'switch' to first activate, then repress a set of shared targets with cytoskeletal functions including Tubb2b and Dpysl3. We demonstrate that this switch is buffered by redundancy between KLF paralogs, which our multiplexed CRISPRi strategy is equipped to overcome and study. Our results indicate that competition between activators and repressors within the KLF family regulates a conserved component of the postnatal maturation program that may underlie the loss of intrinsic axon growth in maturing neurons. This could facilitate the transition from axon growth to synaptic refinement required to stabilize mature circuits.

items.title: Depth-dependent soil water-salt relationships in the Hetao Irrigation District, arid Northwest China: Implications for sustainable management.
items.abstract: Soil salinization threatens agricultural productivity in arid gravity irrigation systems worldwide, yet the depth-stratified relationships between soil water and salt content remain poorly characterized. We monitored soil moisture and electrical conductivity (EC) at six depths (0-100 cm) across 15 sites in the Hetao Irrigation District, China, during the 2025 growing season. Our results indicate a depth-dependent divergence in water-salt associations. The EC-derived salinity index varied from 0.08 to 42.91 g/kg, exhibiting extreme spatial heterogeneity (coefficient of variation (CV) = 185.2%) across the salinity gradient. However, moisture-salinity relationships showed marked depth dependency. Surface soils (0-20 cm) exhibited non-statistically significant correlations (r = 0.07), whereas deep layers (60-100 cm) showed a statistically significant but weak positive correlation (r = 0.25, p < 0.01, R2 = 0.06), indicating limited explanatory power. This pattern is consistent with a subtle tendency of downward salt redistribution. The EC-derived salinity index showed a 42% increase in deep layers (from 1.59 to 2.26 g/kg) over the season, compared to a 136% fluctuation in surface layers. These results highlight limitations of surface-focused monitoring approaches and indicate patterns consistent with subsurface salt redistribution. Compared with previous studies, this work provides a depth-resolved, multi-site observational dataset combined with a stratified analytical approach, offering additional evidence for interpreting soil salinity dynamics under heterogeneous field conditions.

items.title: Integrating machine learning and geospatial technologies for spatio-temporal analysis of urban expansion and land use transformation in Gambella Town, Ethiopia.
items.abstract: Rapid urbanization and the associated expansion of built-up areas are transforming land resources, ecosystem functions, and the spatial structure of cities. Distinguishing urban growth, urban expansion, and urban sprawl is essential for understanding the processes and patterns of urban transformation and supporting sustainable urban planning. This study integrates machine learning and geospatial technologies to analyze spatio-temporal land use and land cover (LULC) dynamics and urban expansion in Gambella Town, Ethiopia. Multi-temporal Landsat satellite images from 2005, 2015, and 2025 were processed using remote sensing techniques and a supervised machine learning approach based on the Random Forest (RF) classifier. Six major LULC classes were identified: Agricultural Land, Bush with Grass, Built-Up Area, Bare Land, Forest Land, and Water Bodies. The classification achieved overall accuracies of 90%, 90%, and 89% for 2005, 2015, and 2025, respectively. The results revealed substantial land transformation and rapid physical urban expansion, with the built-up area increasing from 93 ha (2.0%) in 2005-1,956 ha (41.3%) in 2025. This expansion was accompanied by major transformations of surrounding land resources, particularly the conversion of Bush with Grass and other open areas to built-up land. Agricultural land increased from 634 ha (13.4%) to 1,750 ha (36.9%), whereas Bush with Grass declined from 3,375 ha (71.1%) to 652 ha (13.7%). Socio-economic information collected from 277 respondents indicated that population growth, rural-urban migration, housing demand, employment opportunities, and infrastructure development were major drivers of urban expansion. The study distinguishes urban expansion, represented by the increase in built-up land, from urban sprawl, which refers to the spatial pattern and form of outward urban development. The integration of Random Forest classification and GIS-based spatial analysis provides valuable evidence of land transformation, vegetation loss, and increasing pressure on urban services, supporting more sustainable urban planning and land management in Gambella Town.

items.title: Evidence-based practice implementation and associated factors among nurses employed at public hospitals in Siltie Zone, South Central Ethiopia: A cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: The use of the best available research evidence in clinical decision-making through the incorporation of clinical experience and patient preferences into the delivery of professional patient care is known as evidence-based practice. The best way to provide high-quality care that is secure and has positive results is through evidence-based practice. To use evidence-based practice. Despite the anticipated advantages of evidence-based practice, nurses have found it challenging to implement. To assess the implementation of evidence-based practice and related factors among nurses working in public hospitals in the Siltie Zone in South Central Ethiopia in 2023. An institution-based cross-sectional study was conducted from March 6 to April 5, 2023, to assess the implementation of evidence-based practice. A sample size was 337 nurses working in Siltie Zone public hospitals; a self-administered, semi-structured questionnaire was used for data collection. Data was cleaned, coded, and entered into EpiData version 4.6 before being exported and analyzed in SPSS (version 26). To ascertain the relationship between the outcome variable and the predictors, binary logistic regression was performed, and those with a p-value of < 0.25 were entered into multivariate analysis. In multivariate analysis, a p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. The Adjusted Odds Ratio (AOR) was calculated to determine the association between the dependent and independent variables at a 95% confidence interval (CI). According to this study, 147 (45.5%) of nurses have good evidence-based practice implementation, and 176 (54.5%) of nurses were found to have poor evidence-based practice implementation. Factors significantly associated with implementation of evidence-based practice were age between 26 and 30 (AOR = 5.247, 95% CI: 1.249, 22.047); educational level, BSc (AOR = 1.956, 95% CI: 1.035, 3.698) and masters (AOR = 4.149, 95% CI: 1.088, 15.817); working unit like emergency (AOR = 3.935, 95% CI: 1.300, 11.914) and inpatient (AOR = 4.684, 95% CI: 1.633, 13.435); ability to formulate a question (AOR = 1.844, 95% CI: 1.062, 3.201); and not relevant to the nursing profession (AOR = 0.459, 95% CI: .236, .878). This study showed that the majority of nurses implement evidence-based practice ineffectively. Age, educational level, working unit, question formulation, and the applicability of evidence-based practice to nursing professions were the main causes of inadequate implementation of evidence-based practice. Therefore, multi-stakeholder approaches are required to address the main contributing variables and promote the implementation of evidence-based practice.
