items.title: Integrating airborne chemical ecology with informed intercropping for sustainable crop protection.
items.abstract: The role of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in plant-insect interactions has been studied in detail in recent decades, especially in the context of environment-friendly integrated pest management (IPM) in agroecosystems. Field-based study and behavioural investigations have shown that specific VOCs (or combinations of VOCs) of companion crops are crucial in diverting phytophagous insects from main food or cash crops, along with attracting beneficial insects which decimate pest species. The functional mechanisms of these olfactory cues, however, are not always clear and distinctive, especially since these ecological interactions are highly variable. The complex 'odourscapes' occurring in mixed cropping systems are determined by species-specific interactions, local climate, prevalent agricultural/landscaping practices, and other environmental factors which need to be examined in localized contexts. This review aims to cover the dynamics and mechanisms of VOCs mediating plant-insect interactions in mixed crop settings, the variables and technical constraints to be considered for implementing these interactions for cost-effective IPM, and potential challenges presented by ecological fine-tuning of such interactions.

items.title: Distribution and potential carcinogenicity of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in beached and pelagic tarballs along the eastern Arabian Sea.
items.abstract: Tarballs, the weathered residues of petroleum hydrocarbons, are a recurring feature along the west coast of India, yet their role as carriers of toxic and carcinogenic compounds remains insufficiently quantified. This study presents a comprehensive assessment of the distribution, composition, abundance and carcinogenic potential of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in pelagic and beached tarballs collected along the Eastern Arabian Sea and the adjacent coastal regions (2018-2024). Results indicate that both pelagic and beached tarballs are dominated by low and medium-molecular-weight(LMW) PAHs, with phenanthrene consistently identified as the most abundant compound. Total PAH concentrations were markedly higher in pelagic tarballs than in beached tarballs. Diagnostic PAH ratios and principal component analysis suggest that the observed differences in PAH composition between pelagic and beached tarballs are consistent with the effects of environmental weathering. Assessment based on benzo[a]pyrene toxic equivalents (BaP-TEQ) and carcinogenic PAH fraction (cPAH%) indicates higher carcinogenic potential in pelagic tarballs, whereas beached tarballs exhibited greater spatial variability in PAH composition. Despite evidence of weathering, carcinogenic PAHs persisted in both tarball types, with some locations exhibiting notably elevated contributions. Overall, the study demonstrates that pelagic tarballs function as mobile vectors of carcinogenic hydrocarbons in the marine environment, while beached tarballs act as persistent secondary sources of contamination.. These findings highlight the potential environmental concern associated with tarball-derived PAHs and underscore the need for sustained monitoring and management of petroleum residues along coastal ecosystems.

items.title: Ontogenetic shifts in the metabolomic profiles of Battus polydamas (Lepidoptera: Papilionidae: Troidini) Feeding on Aristolochia gigantea.
items.abstract: Insect development involves profound physiological reorganization that can alter the assimilation and allocation of metabolites across life stages. In herbivorous insects, these processes are tightly linked to diet-derived chemical exposure, yet how metabolic organization shifts throughout ontogeny remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated ontogenetic metabolomic variation in Battus polydamas feeding on Aristolochia gigantea, a system characterized by a specialized ecological interaction between insect and host plant. We examined how chemical profiles vary across larval, pupal, and adult stages, as well as in the host plant and larval frass, to determine whether metamorphosis is associated with stage-specific reorganization of the insect metabolome. Multivariate analyses revealed clear separation among sample types, and PERMANOVA confirmed significant differences among groups. Pupae and adult bodies showed the greatest similarity, whereas plant and frass formed distinct clusters. Wings exhibited a differentiated metabolomic profile. Molecular networking revealed a diverse set of primary and secondary metabolites, including carbohydrates, amino acids, phenolics, fatty acids, and sterol-related compounds. Nine metabolites differed significantly among plant, insect stages, and frass. Lipid- and sterol-related compounds showed stage-specific variation, particularly in pupae and wings, while phenolic derivatives and fatty acids distinguished insect tissues from plant and frass samples. Frass displayed marked chemical divergence, consistent with differential assimilation and metabolic processing. In summary, the metabolomic profile of B. polydamas is reorganized across ontogeny, reflecting stage-specific patterns of metabolite retention and transformation throughout development.

items.title: An update on the mosquito fauna of Aguascalientes, Mexico: morphological and molecular identifications, host-feeding patterns, and the removal of Aedes idahoensis (Theobald) from Mexico
items.abstract: To better understand taxonomic identity and feeding patterns of mosquitoes in all physiographic regions and sub-regions of Aguascalientes, Mexico, we conducted surveillance followed by morphologic analysis and DNA metabarcoding. We targeted the Sierra Madre Occidental, Central Plateau, and Neo-Volcanic Axis. We sampled natural larval habitat for immature stages and adults were collected using Shannon and CDC light traps, mechanical aspirators, and human landing catch method. In addition, curated specimens from Aguascalientes deposited in a local institution were re-examined. Overall, 5,227 mosquito specimens consisting of 357 larvae, 199 larval exuviae, 373 pupal exuviae, 33 pupae, 3,000 females, 1,264 males, and 1 male genitalia were examined using taxonomic keys. Most immature and adult species (n = 20/34 species representing 58.8% coverage) were barcoded for molecular species designation, and a subsample (n = 64) of engorged female mosquitoes were analyzed for blood feeding patterns. Two subfamilies, four tribes, seven genera, 14 subgenera, and 34 species were identified, which one tribe, three genera, nine subgenera, and 22 species are new records. Phylogenetic analysis of specimens from Aguascalientes identified 20 species. Morphological observation of mosquitoes deposited in entomological collections resulted in the removal of Aedesidahoensis from Mexico, leaving the country with a total of 255 species documented. Bloodmeal metabarcoding was successful in 23 mosquitoes of five species, revealing evidence of feeding on more than a single vertebrate species in 17 individuals. Birds were the most common host with the cattle egret (Ardea ibis) found in 18 out of 23 mosquitoes. This update on the taxonomic identity and mosquito richness and feeding patterns from Aguascalientes affords a better understanding of the ecology of medically important mosquito species.

items.title: Disentangling the effect of maternal mental health on children's academic achievement: A random intercept approach.
items.abstract: A wealth of transactional mother-child effects has been proposed in developmental research, including the potential influence of maternal mental health on children's academic development and vice versa. However, longitudinal multi-informant studies spanning several years remain scarce. In the present study, two birth cohorts were followed from ages 8 to 14 ( N = 747, 49.4% girls) to examine whether maternal anxiety and depression differentially predicted children's academic achievement and vice versa. A cross-lagged random-intercept model was applied to biennially collected data, controlling for stable, unmeasured, time-invariant factors (e.g., shared genetics, parental education) as well as time-varying covariates (e.g., negative life events). Results showed that higher levels of self-reported maternal anxiety and depression consistently predicted-at comparable magnitudes-lower teacher-reported academic achievement across all time points. These effects persisted after adjusting for prior levels of children's emotional problems, school performance, and exposure to negative life events. Moreover, lower academic achievement predicted increased maternal depressive symptoms between ages 10 and 12. The findings underscore the long-term impact of maternal mental health difficulties on children's functioning beyond the immediate family context, likely representing one of several mechanisms contributing to the intergenerational transmission of social marginalization. items.title: An optimized flow cytometry sorting-sequencing workflow reduces storage, sorting, and extraction bias in sorted microbial communities.
items.abstract: Fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) followed by metataxonomics is commonly used to probe the composition of microbial subpopulations with a functionality of interest. Metataxonomic analysis of sorted low-microbial-biomass samples is prone to contamination and bias introduced during sorting and DNA extraction. To improve metataxonomic accuracy, the DNA yield obtained by the DNeasy PowerSoil Pro kit was first maximized. FACS-sequencing using the optimized DNA extraction method distorted the composition of sorted microbiota by introducing sheath fluid contaminants, termed the FACSome. Since FACSome contaminants were experiment-specific, a standardized, applicable in silico decontamination method was developed to characterize and remove FACSome contamination in PacBio and Illumina metataxonomic sequencing data based on carefully selected controls. The optimized DNA extraction and decontamination methods were validated in soil, water, feces, saliva, gut reactor, and mock microbial communities. Metataxonomic profiles of non-selectively sorted and unsorted samples derived from these ecosystems did not perfectly match due to relic DNA depletion during FACS. Effective (97%) relic DNA depletion was confirmed with a spike-in experiment and is desirable since naturally present relic DNA can interfere with function-driven FACS-sequencing. A nuclease-based digest further enhanced relic DNA depletion. Since FACS depleted relic DNA, the preservation of intact cells prior to sorting is essential for activity- or viability-targeted FACS. Intact cells were best preserved during long-term -80°C storage of fecal samples that were not amended with glycerol-1× Tris-EDTA cryoprotectant.IMPORTANCEBulk meta-omics fail to provide sufficient resolution to gain mechanistic insights in microbial ecosystems. Function-driven microbiome research requires high-throughput profiling of active microbial subpopulations. These can be singled out through fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) combined with function-, activity-, or viability-based labeling. The resulting low-biomass sorted samples present a currently overlooked challenge for accurate 16S rRNA gene profiling. We systematically identified all potential sources of interference to enable decontamination of 16S rRNA gene sequences from sorted microbiota. While this study focused on metataxonomic read-outs, our optimized extraction and decontamination workflow can advance other sequencing-based omics analyses of sorted microbial communities. Our optimized FACS-sequencing workflow is thus imperative to unlock the full potential of single-cell labeling and FACS, in turn enabling mode-of-action studies that will broaden our understanding of microbe-environment interactions.

items.title: Seasonal and evolutionary patterns of planktonic Hikarchaeia reveal ecological niches of marine rare biosphere constituents.
items.abstract: Members of Marine Group IV, now termed Hikarchaeia, hold an important transitional evolutionary position among Archaea but remain uncultivated, and their ecology remains uncharacterized. Over a 5-year period, we performed monthly profile sampling in the North Atlantic Subtropical Gyre and sequenced V4 16S rRNA gene amplicons, while also collecting additional size-fractionated and metagenomic samples. Hikarchaeal relative abundance annually peaked at ~1% of prokaryotic amplicons. Their relative abundances were significantly higher after deep winter mixing when thermal stratification isolated exported dissolved organic matter in the twilight zone (TZ), the boundary region between the epipelagic and mesopelagic. A diminutive 1.17 Mbp complete hikarchaeal genome was recovered by sequencing and co-assembling diel TZ metagenomes from 200 m during summer, where their relative abundances were highest. Phylogenomic reconstruction incorporating our new metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) and public MAGs established five clades. Clades I and III were in subtropical and tropical environments, with vertical partitioning: Clade I dominated the TZ, and Clade III detection initiated in the lower mesopelagic and extended into the bathypelagic. Clade V is polar-associated. Data sparsity makes Clade II and IV distributions unclear. All Hikarchaeia recovered thus far appear to be free-living aerobes capable of heterotrophy. Unlike MGI, MGII, and MGIII Archaea, and most marine pelagic bacteria, the Hikarchaeia encode bacterioruberin biosynthesis, except deep Clade III. Hikarchaeia also have nitrile hydratases alongside enzymes for carbon monoxide oxidation and menaquinone biosynthesis, suggesting previously unrecognized roles in nitrogen and carbon cycling. Collectively, our studies reveal niche partitioning of evolutionarily distinct uncultivated Hikarchaeia clades and patterning within the rare biosphere.IMPORTANCEThe ocean and its vertical water-column structure are changing with planetary warming; yet, there are many enigmatic microbes, especially those that inhabit the deep ocean. Here, we illuminate a group of uncultivated Archaea that were discovered over two decades ago but still lack clear distributions and habitat preferences. With the first complete hikarchaeal genome now in hand, we identified distinct lineages within the Hikarchaeia that occupy different marine niches. Strong reoccurring seasonal patterns were observed that closely followed the annual cycle of temperature-driven ocean stratification. Given rapid natural and anthropogenic perturbations at hand, establishing baselines for these Archaea is critical for improving our understanding and modeling of marine microbiomes and their biogeochemical functions.

items.title: Comparative dietary profiling of smoked and non-smoked paprika (Capsicum annuum L.) in Wistar rats: metabolomic, biochemical and gut microbiota responses in a healthy animal model.
items.abstract: Paprika ( Capsicum annuum L.) is a widely consumed spice whose bioactive composition is substantially influenced by processing conditions. Traditional smoking, as applied in the production of PDO Pimentón de la Vera, enriches paprika with wood smoke-derived phenolics while also introducing polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), warranting an integrated evaluation of processing-related biological responses and safety considerations. This study compared physiological, biochemical, metabolomic, and cecal microbiota responses to dietary supplementation with smoked and non-smoked paprika in healthy Wistar rats. Thirty animals of both sexes (16 females and 14 males) received a control diet or diets supplemented with 5% smoked or non-smoked paprika for 30 days. Histological examination revealed no treatment-related alterations in the organs evaluated. Hematological and biochemical analyses showed diet- and sex-associated differences in hematocrit, plasma glucose, total antioxidant capacity, and lipid-related parameters, although all values remained within normal physiological ranges. Untargeted urinary metabolomics, restricted to males because of insufficient urine volume in females, identified features tentatively annotated as phenolic conjugates and other metabolites associated with paprika intake, with several signals showing higher abundance in the smoked paprika group. Cecal metagenomic analyses showed sex-dependent changes across taxon-level abundance, alpha diversity, and beta diversity. In females receiving smoked paprika, lower TC and LDL-C coincided with higher alpha diversity and lower cecal lipid content, suggesting a potential link between intestinal microbial ecology and lipid handling. Overall, paprika processing was associated with distinct biochemical, metabolomic, and cecal microbiota response patterns in this healthy animal model.

items.title: Metal-organic frameworks for photocatalytic CO<sub>2</sub> reduction: recent advances, design principles, and mechanistic insights.
items.abstract: The rising atmospheric CO 2 levels demand sustainable technologies for converting CO 2 into fuels and chemicals. Photocatalytic CO 2 reduction mimics natural photosynthesis but faces great challenges from the inertness of CO 2 , high CO bond energy, slow kinetics, and competing hydrogen evolution. With ultrahigh surface areas, tunable porosity, and modular architectures, metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) serve as a versatile platform, enabling molecular-level integration of light harvesting and catalysis to overcome these limitations. Rational optimization via linker functionalization, heterometal doping, defect engineering, heterojunctions, and morphology control has improved the efficiency and selectivity in CO 2 photoreduction. This review summarizes recent advances in framework engineering and their photophysical mechanisms. Despite progress, there still remain great challenges, such as limited visible-light absorption, low charge mobility, rapid recombination, poor stability, difficulty achieving C 2+ products, and insufficient operando understanding. Future efforts should focus on π-conjugated frameworks, conductive linkers, single-atom/dual-site centers to enable C-C coupling, and in situ / operando spectroscopies combined with theoretical analysis. Moreover, developing sacrificial-agent-free systems using water as an electron donor shows great promise for practical solar-fuel production.

items.title: High-throughput mitochondrial aerobic metabolism measurement: assessing a plate-reader approach using avian blood cells.
items.abstract: Mitochondria power biological processes, driving interest in measuring mitochondrial aerobic metabolism to understand individual variation in performance and fitness. High-resolution respirometry (HRR) is the gold standard because of its sensitivity and versatility, but it is time-consuming and has low throughput, limiting its use in large-scale studies. We assessed the validity of a high-throughput, fluorescence-based plate reader by comparing it to HRR. In a first experiment, we measured mitochondrial respiration in blood cells from two bird species (quails and chickens) across three temperatures (hypothermia, normothermia, and hyperthermia). The two methods were moderately correlated and revealed similar species effects; however, temperature effects differed between approaches, particularly under hyperthermic conditions, indicating that the plate-reader approach is best suited for stable, normothermic conditions. In a second experiment on sex differences in quails at normothermia, the two methods agreed quantitatively for proton leak and oxidative control efficiency and qualitatively for oxidative phosphorylation, although the plate-reader estimate was marginally significant (P=0.060 versus P=0.046 for HRR). The plate reader's main limitation is its lower sensitivity and greater measurement error, which could be offset by increasing sample sizes. Following protocol optimisation for each study system, this approach may offer a useful high-throughput complement to HRR for studies prioritising larger sample sizes.

items.title: Attentional territories: The influence of gaze and interpersonal distance in the navigation of public space.
items.abstract: Human gaze is a potent social signal; it communicates attention, intention and social engagement, and allows observers to infer not only where others are attending but also how they are socially related. Although gaze has been extensively studied in direct social interaction, far less is known about how it shapes the perceptions and actions of uninvolved observers in shared environments. Here, we investigate whether mutual gaze creates an 'attentional territory' that third parties implicitly respect. In a large-scale field study across four university campuses in Europe and Canada (N = 4680 pedestrians), two confederates stood facing one another in a public space. We manipulated gaze direction and reciprocity (mutual, unilateral or no interaction) as well as interpersonal distance (2-6 metres), holding body orientation and spatial arrangement constant. Pedestrians were less likely to cross between individuals engaged in mutual gaze. This effect weakened with increasing distance, but was robust across all locations. Together, the findings demonstrate that gaze does not merely coordinate interaction between individuals but also shapes how uninvolved others perceive and move through shared environments. By isolating gaze reciprocity from spatial arrangement, we demonstrate that mutual gaze functions as a dynamic social boundary organizing the permeability of public space.

items.title: The Japanese Adaptation of the Reading the Mind in Films Test: Differentiating Autism Spectrum Disorder From Depression Using an Ecologically Valid Social Cognitive Task.
items.abstract: Cognitive tests that reflect the complexity of real-world social interactions are essential for autism spectrum disorder (ASD)-related clinical assessment and research. This study developed and adapted a Japanese version of the Reading the Mind in Films (RMF) test, which assesses mind-reading ability through dynamic, multisensory, and context-rich stimuli. Participants included 23 autistic adults, 39 typically developing adults, and 40 adults with depression as a clinical control. RMF scores in the autistic group were significantly lower than in both the typically developing and depression groups. Hierarchical logistic regression analyses showed that RMF performance provided incremental predictive value beyond Reading the Mind in the Eyes test performance in differentiating autistic individuals from typically developing participants and from participants with depression. Receiver operating characteristic analyses further indicated moderate discriminative accuracy of the RMF for differentiating autistic from non-autistic individuals. In contrast, the depression group performed comparably to the typically developing group on the RMF, suggesting that the RMF captures ASD-specific social cognitive difficulties rather than social dysfunction. These findings provide preliminary support for both the construct validity and the potential discriminative utility of the Japanese RMF. This tool has potential applications in future transdiagnostic and cross-cultural studies.

items.title: Mapping mental health complexity in esports: an exploratory psychosocial network approach.
items.abstract: Background The rapid rise in popularity of esports has brought increased attention to the unique mental health challenges faced by esports players, yet research in this area remains in its infancy. Early research suggests a substantial mental health burden and has examined associations between esports-specific stressors, mental health, and sleep disturbances. However, much of this work has relied on traditional methodologies, providing limited insight into how affective, psychosocial, sleep-related, and esports-specific indicators are organised within this competitive performance environment. Methods To address this gap, we developed a bespoke 17-item questionnaire tailored for Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) network analysis, an exploratory approach for mapping the conditional dependency structure of complex multivariate systems such as mental health. Results A total of 1025 esports players from over 60 countries completed the survey. Game-related thought preoccupation, a core feature of gaming disorder, emerged as the most robust structural sink node, downstream of several psychosocial indicators, raising the hypothesis that it represents a compound indicator of broader upstream psychosocial strain. Depressed mood occupied an upstream position within the network, an observation that held more robustly for the psychopathological subnetwork as a whole than for depressed mood as the single source. Mental fatigue occupied an intermediate, connecting position between affective variables and the sleep and fatigue indicators. Its high prevalence, together with a positioning upstream of the sleep indicators, suggests that it may warrant closer examination in future research on training load, recovery, and sleep in esports, though this ordering rested on edges with moderate directional support. Emotion control and a sense of autonomy appeared to connect upstream affective distress with downstream esports-specific indicators such as esports-related stress, though was the least stable of the structural features identified. Conclusions Collectively, these findings provide an exploratory map of how mental health-relevant indicators were organised in this performance environment, and generate concrete, testable hypotheses for future longitudinal, experimental, and intervention research.

items.title: Emotion regulation and its association with subjective memory performance among undergraduate students at port said university.
items.abstract: Background Emotion regulation (ER), particularly through cognitive reappraisal (CR) and expressive suppression (ES), plays an important role in psychological well-being and higher-order cognitive functioning. Both ER and subjective memory performance (SMP), as measured by the Prospective and Retrospective Memory Questionnaire (PRMQ), have been proposed to draw on shared executive control resources. Although memory complaints have been reported among Egyptian university students, the association between ER strategies and SMP remains largely unexplored. This study aimed to assess ER strategies and SMP among undergraduate students at Port Said University and examine the association between these constructs. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional study with an analytical component was conducted among 1,287 undergraduate students from seven randomly selected faculties at Port Said University. Data were collected using a self-administered questionnaire comprising the Emotion Regulation Questionnaire (ERQ) to assess CR and ES and the PRMQ to measure SMP. Data were analyzed using Jamovi version 2.3.28 employing descriptive statistics, nonparametric tests, Spearman's rank correlation, and multiple linear regression. Results Participants had a median total ERQ score of 44 and a median total PRMQ score of 50. Males reported significantly higher ES and total ER scores than females (p Conclusion The findings suggest that greater reported use of ER strategies is associated with fewer self-reported memory complaints among undergraduate students. Although the association was statistically significant, its magnitude was weak, indicating that ER represents only one of several factors associated with SMP. This suggests that effective emotional processing may support the cognitive resources required for daily memory tasks.

items.title: Life's Essential 8 and Psychological Wellbeing in Those with and without Schizophrenia, Schizoaffective Disorder, and Bipolar Disorder.
items.abstract: Background Poor cardiovascular health (CVH) remains a leading cause of early mortality among individuals with serious mental illness (SMI). While psychological well-being (PWB) is linked to CVH in the general population, its role among those with SMI is less understood. Method This cross-sectional study characterized CVH using the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 among those with and without SMI and examined relationships between CVH and PWB. Demographic, clinical, and PWB data were obtained from the electronic health record and a health and wellbeing survey for 156 individuals with SMI and 311 matched controls (2015-2020). CVH and PWB were compared across groups. General linear models examined associations between CVH and PWB factors, and interaction terms tested whether associations differed by SMI status. Results Individuals with SMI had poorer CVH and reported worse PWB in domains of life satisfaction, perceived social support, and gratitude compared to controls. Life satisfaction (b = 1.06, 95% CI [0.35, 1.76], p = 0.004) was positively associated with CVH in the total sample and did not vary by SMI status (p = 0.82). The association of social support with CVH varied by SMI status, such that the positive effect of social support on LE8 was greater among individuals without SMI (b = -11.37, 95% CI [-20.28, -2.48], p = 0.012). Gratitude was not associated with CVH. Conclusion Patients with SMI compared to those without SMI have poorer CVH and PWB. Greater life satisfaction and social support may be protective for CVH, but social support may not have the same association among those with SMI.

items.title: Human-in-the-loop LLM-assisted thematic analysis: A validated, reproducible tutorial for large-scale qualitative research.
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support qualitative research, yet clear methodological frameworks for integrating them into thematic analysis remain limited. A central challenge is how to scale qualitative coding with LLM assistance while preserving methodological rigor and reproducibility. This tutorial presents a structured, human-in-the-loop workflow for conducting large-scale thematic analysis with LLM support. Grounded in inductive and hybrid approaches to thematic analysis (Braun & Clarke, 2006), the workflow proceeds in three phases. First, researchers conduct manual thematic analysis on a subset of data to establish an initial codebook and assess relevance. Second, the same subset is analyzed using an LLM to iteratively refine prompts and evaluate alignment between human and model outputs. Third, the validated approach is applied to the full corpus using a modular four-step pipeline: key-idea extraction, chunk-level thematic coding, theme consolidation, and clustering, with iterative human verification through random sampling of outputs. We demonstrate the workflow using 2,952 publicly available Reddit posts. Structured prompt design and JSON-formatted outputs enable traceability between themes and source data and support reproducible analysis. Prompt engineering is treated as an iterative analytic process rather than a one-time instruction. Under controlled conditions, human and LLM coding showed high agreement (Cohen's κ = 0.91). All prompts, code, and reproducibility materials are openly available via an Open Science Framework repository. By providing detailed implementation guidance, embedded validation procedures, and safeguards against common failure modes such as hallucination and overgeneralization, this tutorial offers a practical and extensible framework for integrating LLMs into qualitative research across domains.

items.title: Generative AI vs. Human Sources for Sexual Health Information: Credibility, Trust, and Behavioral Intentions in a U.S. College Sample.
items.abstract: Limited access to comprehensive sexual health education has prompted a need to consider the utility of alternative strategies, such as generative artificial intelligence (genAI), for delivering accurate and accessible sexual health information. Although genAI tools can generate health information, less is known about how perceptions of the source of information shape evaluations of content (e.g., human vs. genAI). The present study examined whether college students' perceptions of sexual health information differed based on source attribution. Participants (N = 266) were students recruited from a single university in the southeastern USA in 2025. They were randomly assigned to conditions in which they were made to believe that three sexual health passages that were identical across conditions (sexual communication, body image, and sexual pleasure and safety) were written by genAI, an academic expert, a community health professional, or a peer/social media influencer. Across outcomes-including perceived accuracy and clarity, warmth and helpfulness, trustworthiness, self-efficacy, and willingness to act-genAI-attributed information was evaluated less favorably than identical information attributed to human sources. For willingness to act, there were differences in source effects across topics, such that effects were strongest for sexual pleasure/safety and weakest for sexual communication. Findings remained significant after controlling for genAI familiarity/use and attitudes. Findings indicate that evaluations of sexual health information depend not only on informational content but also on perceived source legitimacy, suggesting that AI-based tools may be the most effective when paired with human guidance to support trust and actionability.

items.title: Shared cortical morphometry and molecular signatures across depression and physical diseases.
items.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is highly comorbid with physical diseases, suggesting shared neurobiological mechanisms. However, the common structural and molecular substrates underlying this comorbidity remain poorly understood. We analyzed multimodal MRI data from 577 patients (MDD, asthma, fibromyalgia, gastroesophageal reflux disease, type 2 diabetes) and 275 healthy controls, constructed individual morphometric similarity networks (MSN) to identify shared cortical alterations, and applied principal component analysis with multiscale molecular annotation (transcriptomic, cell-type, neurotransmitter, and cognitive mapping) to characterize underlying mechanisms. All patient groups exhibited regional MSN abnormalities. A shared MSN pattern emerged, featuring increased similarity in visual and somatomotor regions and decreased similarity in ventral attention, limbic, and default mode networks, and was replicated in independent cohorts. This pattern was significantly associated with spatial gene expression enriched for synaptic signaling, membrane potential regulation, and neuronal architecture, with predominant expression in excitatory/inhibitory neurons and astrocytes. It further mapped onto specific neurotransmitter systems, with exploratory cognitive decoding suggesting possible relevance to emotion and social cognition. Related genes overlapped with known risk loci for Alzheimer's disease and bipolar disorder. These findings identify a robust across diseases cortical MSN phenotype linked to convergent molecular and neurochemical correlates, offering a framework for studying shared vulnerability and transdiagnostic mechanisms across depression and physical diseases.

items.title: Motor abstraction training generalizes to the refinement of specific movement patterns.
items.abstract: The ability to abstract the invariant structure of an experience while discarding incidental details underlies generalization across virtually every domain of human cognition, from vision and language to concept learning. Yet whether the motor system generates such abstractions and whether they causally contribute to skilled performance remain open questions. Here we introduce a paradigm in which human participants learned novel movement patterns by precisely copying unfamiliar handwritten characters. To examine the role of motor abstractions in this form of learning, participants were trained on markedly rotated versions of the characters, which recruited substantially different lower-level movements while still maintaining the relevant abstract movement trajectory. Across 11 experiments, abstraction training drove robust performance improvements that were comparable to having repetitive practice on the canonical form of each character. Moreover, this effect was largely motoric in nature: it did not require a visual template, sustained trajectory feedback or mental imagery, and was sensitive to the sequential structure of the movement trajectory. These findings establish a causal role for abstractions in motor learning, revealing that the motor system probably deploys abstractions in the earliest stages of skill acquisition.

items.title: Perceived neighborhood crime and social cohesion trajectories and mental health during COVID-19: Evidence from a 2020-2024 cohort.
items.abstract: We examined longitudinal changes in perceived neighborhood crime and social cohesion from 2020 to 2024 and their associations with depression, anxiety, and loneliness. U.S. adults (N = 895) recruited in spring 2020 completed at least one annual follow-up surveys through 2024. Group-based trajectory modeling identified four perceived-crime trajectories: low (71.7%), increasing (14.9%), decreasing (8.7%), and high (4.8%), and three stable social-cohesion trajectories: high (18.2%), middle (63.9%), and low (17.9%). Multivariable logistic regression showed that, compared with the low-crime trajectory, high and increasing crime were associated with higher odds of depression (OR = 2.61 and 1.82) and anxiety (OR = 3.08 and 1.87), whereas decreasing crime was associated with lower odds of loneliness (OR = 0.55). Compared with high cohesion, low cohesion was associated with higher odds of depression (OR = 6.38), anxiety (OR = 4.81), and loneliness (OR = 4.17). Complementary within-between mixed-effects models showed that within-person increases in perceived crime were associated with higher depression (β = .12), anxiety (β = .15), and loneliness (β = .19), whereas within-person increases in social cohesion were associated with lower symptoms (β = -0.02 to -0.04). Findings indicate consistent longitudinal associations between neighborhood perceptions and mental health across person-centered and variable-centered approaches.

items.title: Lung Restriction From Childhood Is Associated With Obstructive Sleep Apnoea in Middle-Age.
items.abstract: Background and objective Whether lifetime lung function trajectories and spirometry patterns are associated with Obstructive Sleep Apnoea (OSA) is unknown. We aimed to investigate this association to widen the understanding of OSA pathophysiology. Methods We previously identified six FEV 1 /FVC (forced expiratory volume in the first second/forced vital capacity) and five FVC trajectories within a population-based prospective cohort (n = 2422) using spirometry assessed at ages 7, 13, 18, 43, 50, and 53 years. These trajectories were combined into four lifetime spirometry patterns: restrictive-only, obstructive-only, mixed, and reference (normal), which were our exposure variables. Outcomes were medically-confirmed OSA in midlife and probable-OSA defined using the STOP-Bang questionnaire. Associations were assessed using logistic regression models. Results The 'restrictive-only' spirometry pattern was associated with medically-confirmed OSA (OR = 2.5; 95% CI 1.5, 4.3). In addition, restriction-confirmatory low total lung capacity and reduced functional residual capacity were associated with increased odds of medically-confirmed OSA (OR = 1.4; 0.9, 2.1 and OR = 1.7; 1.1, 2.6, respectively, per one SD reduction in volume). The results were similar for probable OSA. These associations held when controlled for BMI and central obesity and were independent of childhood lung function. Neither transfer factor for carbon monoxide (T L co) nor transfer coefficient (Kco) was associated with OSA. Conclusion We provide first evidence that lifetime lung restriction is related to middle-age OSA. While this information may be used to incidentally flag middle-age OSA risk and vice versa, further research is encouraged to confirm the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms.

items.title: Identification of individual animals from position, orientation, and movement sequences in the Morris water task with machine learning: implications for spatial learning.
items.abstract: The Morris water task (MWT) has been the gold standard assessment of place learning and memory for over four decades, yet the processes that contribute to successful navigation are not completely understood. It is generally posited that rats learn to navigate directly to a place; however, navigation is not perfectly direct but contains variation in swim speed and trajectory, resulting in efficient, yet suboptimal paths. Recently, our lab demonstrated that path topography is quantitatively similar across trials within individual rats for a given start location, and dissimilar between rats and different start locations within rat. This suggests rats may take unique paths to the platform from each release point. If the sequences of position and heading changes in the MWT are reinforced based on individual experience, it should be possible to objectively classify (identify) individual rats using machine learning. In the present study, a recurrent neural network was trained to classify 15 rats based on trial-level time-series data of path coordinates, velocity, and orientation. Testing on unseen coordinates or combined features from the same starting locations yielded classification accuracies that were 5.93- to 7.26-fold greater than chance and significantly greater than data from different start locations. Classification using scalar metrics with support vector machines was unable to match these outcomes. Collectively, these observations support the hypothesis that navigation in the MWT involves learning to perform behavioral sequences.

items.title: Cardiorespiratory Fitness in Young Adulthood and Depressive Symptoms Later in Life Among Swedish Men.
items.abstract: ObjectivesThis study investigated whether cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) in young adulthood is associated with depressive symptoms several decades later and if later-life physical activity and self-rated health mediate this association.MethodsThe sample comprised 690 Swedish men completing a CRF test at age 18 and self-reported depressive symptoms around age 61. Unadjusted and adjusted logistic and linear regression models and Bayesian mediation analyses were estimated.ResultsMedium and high CRF at age 18, compared with low CRF, were associated with lower odds of clinically significant depressive symptoms in late adulthood. The odds ratios of clinically significant depressive symptoms were 0.329 (95% CI [0.157, 0.687]) for men with medium and 0.383 (95% CI [0.157, 0.939]) for men with high CRF compared with those with low CRF. No credible mediated associations were observed.ConclusionThese findings suggest that promoting fitness early in life may represent a useful preventive strategy for mental health resilience across the life course.

items.title: Learning to become a tutor: Experiences of adults with intellectual disabilities in peer tutoring for digital skills.
items.abstract: Societies are digitalizing services with a rapid speed. As a result, people, such as adults with disabilities, are at risk of being excluded if they lack appropriate digital skills and have few possibilities to get support in learning these skills. Peer tutoring is seen as an effective way to learn these skills according to research done on peer tutoring with older adults and immigrants, but there remains a gap in research with adults with intellectual disabilities and their preferences for digital skills learning. This article focuses on the experiences of Finnish adults with intellectual disabilities in digital skills peer tutoring courses they attended. The data were collected by conducting semi-structured interviews via Teams with ten participants. The results indicate that digital skills training activities supported the peer-tutor trainees' learning, their skills to support others with technology use, and their social inclusion in Finland's digitalized society.

items.title: Neural Response to Monetary and Social Feedback in Childhood: Processing Reward and Loss in Relation to Peer Outcomes and Anxiety Symptoms.
items.abstract: Anxiety disorders are the most prevalent psychiatric conditions in childhood and are associated with social functioning impairment. How youth process rewards may contribute to the development of social impairment in childhood anxiety. Although aberrant reward processing is a well-established mechanism of psychopathology, associations with anxiety remain inconsistent and limited, especially in childhood. This study investigated neural response to monetary and social reward feedback in relation to anxiety and peer functioning in children. Children (N=106; Age=8.12±.68 years) completed the Doors Task and the Island Getaway Task while electroencephalogram (EEG) recordings assessed event-related potentials (ERPs) to wins and losses. Parents completed questionnaires assessing child anxiety, depression, and peer relations. Contrary to pre-registered hypotheses, we found a significant Valence (reward versus loss) by Condition (monetary versus social) interaction. Specifically, children exhibited greater neural response to monetary loss than reward, but showed the opposite pattern in the social condition, with greater neural response to social reward than loss. Higher child- and parent-reported total and generalized anxiety predicted significantly greater neural response to monetary reward, but not monetary loss or social feedback. As hypothesized, anxiety symptoms significantly moderated the association between neural response and peer relations, demonstrating that for highly anxious children, a greater neural response to social loss predicted worse peer relations. Findings demonstrate differences in neural response to monetary and social feedback processing. Moreover, the distinct vulnerability to social rejection might impair peer functioning in anxious children, suggesting that clinical interventions targeting social rejection processing may effectively improve peer outcomes in childhood anxiety.

items.title: Subjective emotional ratings dissociate brain activation and network patterns during counterfactual outcome processing.
items.abstract: Human decision-making integrates outcome evaluation, counterfactual comparison, and individual traits. We investigated the neural processing of outcome-related emotions during economic decision-making by classifying feedback according to participants' subjective emotional ratings rather than objective gain-loss categories. Participants completed a Wheel of Fortune gambling task during fMRI scanning and provided emotional ratings for feedback outcomes, enabling identification of regret, relief, disappointment, and elation. We also assessed individual differences in regret proneness, maximization tendencies, alternative search, high standards, and decision difficulty. Behaviorally, emotional ratings increased with larger obtained outcomes and decreased as reference outcomes increased, indicating robust modulation of outcome evaluation by counterfactual information Whole-brain analyses revealed greater activation for low-rating than high-rating outcomes, indicating stronger neural responses to negative than positive emotions across feedback types. Complete feedback also elicited greater activation than partial feedback within the same emotional valence. Network-level analyses revealed partially dissociable neural profiles for positive and negative emotions. Positive emotions, including elation and relief, predominantly recruited the somatomotor network, whereas negative emotions, including disappointment and regret, engaged broader distributions across the default mode, dorsal attention, and other large-scale networks. Regret elicited the largest activation extent, whereas elation elicited the smallest. Region-of-interest analyses showed that bilateral orbitofrontal cortex (OFC) responses were significantly greater for negative than positive emotions and for complete than partial feedback conditions. Across all four emotions, right OFC activation was negatively associated with maximization. For elation, relief, and disappointment, right OFC activation was also negatively associated with alternative search and decision difficulty, whereas these associations were absent for regret. Together, these findings demonstrate that subjective emotional evaluation, counterfactual context, and decision-related traits jointly shape the neural processing of decision outcomes, while suggesting relatively trait-independent neural processing of regret.

items.title: Systematic, contextual, and individual influences drive trialists' behaviour relating to greener trial design and delivery - A qualitative study.
items.abstract: Objectives To identify the key behavioural determinants that influence how people working in clinical trials ('trialists') design and deliver greener trials. Study design and setting We conducted semi-structured focus groups and interviews with trialists involved in the design and conduct of clinical trials in the UK. Participants were recruited from a preceding survey, supplemented by purposive sampling through established trial networks and professional groups. Data collection was guided by the Theoretical Domains Framework (TDF) where analysis combined deductive TDF coding with inductive thematic development. Results Three focus groups and nine interviews with a total of 23 participants including diverse roles, such as Clinical Trials Unit (CTU) directors, trial managers, statisticians, Quality Assurance staff, and researchers, were conducted. We identified 34 belief statements across all 14 TDF domains which were synthesised into five overarching themes: 1. Developing and promoting a culture for greener trials; 2. Weighing up the anticipated benefits against the unknowns; 3. Tensions between intrinsic and extrinsic priorities; 4. Degree of control over the enablement of greener trials; and 5. Negotiating gaps to address individual uncertainties. The study found that trialists' actions were shaped by a range of behavioural mechanisms. Cultural and contextual constraints, competing priorities, and limited organisational support were key challenges; while leadership, funders' expectations, and existing sustainability practices were identified as potential opportunities. Conclusion This study provides an in-depth theory-informed behavioural analysis of the challenges and opportunities for making clinical trials greener. These findings provide a basis for designing behaviour change strategies to support trialists' adoption of greener trials.

items.title: Toward a Psychology of Science: A Dynamic Cognitive Model of the Evolution of Scientific Theories.
items.abstract: Responding to a recent call for the development of a psychology of science, we examine how scientists manage empirical anomalies, a routine yet consequential challenge in scientific practice, and how their responses shape theory development. We argue that defensive anomaly-reduction strategies, which allow researchers to preserve an initial theoretical claim, can generate important secondary benefits. During the emergence phase of a theory, they foster auxiliary revisions that may reduce underfitting and place a fragile theory on a growth trajectory. During the exploitation phase of established theories, they help sustain attention to problems derived from the theory and support cumulative research. However, their accumulation may also increase the risk of overfitting, reduce predictive power, and set the theory on a degenerative trajectory. We illustrate these dynamics primarily through examples drawn from psychological theories, with a focus on responses to replication failures. Last, we derive several implications for peer review aimed at fostering scientific innovation. In particular, we propose shifting evaluation away from the consistency of findings, which may penalize emerging research programs and hinder innovation, and toward how inconsistencies are managed, thereby fostering growth trajectories, including for mature programs confronted with anomalies.

items.title: Long-term episodic memory alterations and the role of perceived stress in post-COVID-19 condition.
items.abstract: Post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) is frequently associated with cognitive impairments, but the integrity of long-term episodic memory remains poorly understood. This study examined immediate, short-term, and very long-term episodic memory in individuals with PCC and evaluated whether emotional disturbances predict long-term recognition outcomes. Forty-one participants (30 PCC; 11 non-PCC) completed a verbal cued-recall task and an immersive virtual reality free-recall object-location memory (OLM) task immediately after learning and the following day. Nine months later, three recognition tasks (verbal, word-list of objects, and visuospatial recognition) and questionnaires assessing anxiety, depression, and perceived stress were administered. PCC participants required significantly longer retrieval times than non-PCC participants in the immediate and delayed OLM trials. Nine months later, PCC participants exhibited significant impairments in verbal cued-recall compared to the immediate and one-day recall trials. Performance on the word-list task was poorer in the PCC group, whereas scores in verbal and visuospatial recognition tasks remained comparable between groups. Emotional symptoms were significantly higher in the PCC group. Exploratory regression analyses suggested a negative association between perceived stress and nine-month visuospatial recognition performance in PCC participants. These preliminary findings suggest a potential vulnerability of very long-term verbal episodic memory in PCC, alongside slowed retrieval processes and heightened emotional distress. The observed association between chronic perceived stress and visuospatial recognition suggests a potential role of stress in very long-term memory performance. Overall, the results highlight the need for long-term cognitive follow-up in PCC and identify perceived stress as a potential factor relevant for long-term recognition of visuospatial information.

items.title: Metacognitive monitoring in Kenyan, Chinese, and U.S. children.
items.abstract: Theories of cognitive development propose that cultural values shape metacognitive skills. However, cross-cultural research on metacognition remains limited and often relies on verbal assessments that may lack validity across cultural contexts. The present study examined metacognitive monitoring in Kenyan, Chinese, and U.S. children (N = 95; 6-10-year-olds; 46% female) using a non-verbal problem-solving task in which children assembled objects according to a model. Across all three cultural contexts, children exhibited various monitoring behaviors (e.g., checking the model), and the frequency of these behaviors increased with age. Cross-cultural differences emerged in the specific monitoring strategies children used: Chinese children engaged in more thorough monitoring than Kenyan and U.S. children. These findings highlight both culturally-recurrent and culturally-variable patterns in children's metacognitive monitoring.

items.title: Silhouette-based body dissatisfaction and positive psychological functioning in Uruguayan adults.
items.abstract: Objective This study aimed to analyze the relationship between silhouette-based body dissatisfaction and positive psychological functioning (PPF) in Uruguayan adults, and to explore differences according to sex, body mass index (BMI), and body satisfaction status. Method A cross-sectional study was conducted with 202 adults (M age = 35.44, SD = 12.69; 73.8% women). Participants completed the Stunkard Figure Rating Scale (SFRS), the Positive Psychological Functioning Scale (PPFS), the General Health Questionnaire-28 (GHQ-28), the Dutch Eating Behavior Questionnaire (DEBQ), and a sociodemographic survey. Results Body dissatisfaction was negatively correlated with PPF total score (r = -0.28, p Conclusions Silhouette-based body satisfaction status was associated with higher positive psychological functioning and lower psychological distress. When age, sex, living situation, BMI, psychological distress, subjective socioeconomic level, and PPF were considered simultaneously, PPF remained independently associated with body dissatisfaction. These findings suggest that silhouette-based body satisfaction status is associated with psychological resources and may be relevant for understanding broader psychological functioning. Longitudinal research is needed to confirm causal directions.

items.title: Growing into the groove: Developmental changes in the pleasurable urge to move to music.
items.abstract: Groove - the pleasurable urge to move to music - provides a behavioral index of how perceptual, motor, and reward systems are engaged and coupled by rhythm. Although groove has been widely studied in adults, little is known about its developmental trajectory. We examined how groove evolves across early to mid-adolescence using a cross-sectional (N = 290) and longitudinal design (N = 105). Participants aged 11-15 rated their urge to move to music stimuli varying in low, moderate, and high levels of rhythmic and harmonic complexity. Across both studies, groove showed the well-established inverted U-shaped relationship with rhythmic complexity, peaking at moderate levels; however, this pattern varied by age. In the cross-sectional study, groove declined with age selectively at high levels of rhythmic complexity. The longitudinal study revealed a comparable decline over time for high rhythmic as well as harmonic complexity levels. These findings indicate that adult-like groove patterns emerge during early adolescence. More broadly, they suggest two complementary developmental processes: broader predictive priors that drive curiosity for highly complex structures in early adolescence, and increasing engagement with moderately complex structures that facilitate sensorimotor coupling and social coordination in mid adolescence.

items.title: Cognitively demanding motor exercise and subsequent inhibitory control: Behavioral and ERP Evidence.
items.abstract: Purpose Acute exercise can influence executive function, yet conventional exercise prescriptions primarily characterize its physical dose and rarely specify the cognitive operations embedded within the exercise bout. Using a Motor-Cognitive Integrated Task (MCIT) with conditions differing in cognitive demand while involving comparable physical demands, this study examined whether cognitively demanding motor exercise was associated with differences in subsequent behavioral and neurophysiological indices of inhibitory control. Methods Forty healthy young adults completed two counterbalanced sessions separated by at least 24 h. In the experimental session, participants performed the MCIT, which required whole-body responses to flanker stimuli. In the control session, participants performed the same motor task in response to predictable single-arrow stimuli. Heart rate (HR), physical rating of perceived exertion (RPE), cognitive RPE, response time (RT), movement time (MT), and overall response time (RMT) were assessed during the MCIT. Immediately afterward, participants completed a computerized flanker task while electroencephalography was recorded. Results Cognitive RPE, RT and RMT of the MCIT were higher in the experimental session than in the control session, whereas HR, physical RPE, and MT of the MCIT were comparable across sessions. Following the MCIT, participants showed a smaller flanker interference in the experimental than in the control session, accompanied by differences in conflict-related modulation of the N2 and smaller overall P3 amplitude, with no between-session difference in accuracy. Conclusions Cognitive demand may represent a manipulable characteristic of acute exercise prescription beyond physical intensity alone. Motor exercise incorporating greater cognitive demands was associated with reduced subsequent behavioral interference and differences in N2 and P3 modulation. Although these effects cannot be attributed exclusively to any specific cognitive operation, the findings highlight the potential importance of considering the cognitive characteristics of exercise when examining its acute neurocognitive effects.

items.title: Cognitive forecasting: How intuitive theories of attention shape anticipated risk preferences.
items.abstract: How do people forecast their own and others' risk preferences? Although it is well established that affective forecasts shape decision-making, less is known about where these forecasts come from. Five studies demonstrate that people rely on intuitive theories of attention when forecasting future affect-such as dread and savoring while waiting for a risk to be resolved-with these affective forecasts in turn shaping willingness to take such risks. In Study 1, forecasts of the participant's own expectations and attention were systematically related to forecasts of positive and negative affect during a waiting period, which in turn predicted risk preferences. Studies 2a and 2b demonstrate substantial heterogeneity in intuitive attention-affect theories: some participants believed attention amplifies the emotional consequences of expectations, whereas others believed attention is uniformly affectively negative. These differences led to sharply divergent predictions about when attention should increase or decrease risk-taking. Study 3 shows that attention is also informative about expectations: participants differed in whether they believed attention signals optimism or pessimism, producing downstream consequences for affective forecasts and risk-taking. Finally, Study 4 reveals that many people endorse asymmetric causal models, viewing optimism as a cause of risk-taking, but risk-taking as a cause of attention. Together, these findings show that forecasts of risk preferences depend critically on people's intuitive theories about how cognition shapes affect and how affective utility is generated over time. By integrating affective forecasting, attention, and decision-making under uncertainty, this work highlights the role of metacognitive beliefs in shaping economic preferences.

items.title: Mind wandering and executive functions: A conceptual replication of Kam & Handy (2014).
items.abstract: Mind wandering - a spontaneous shift in attention away from a task - has been consistently associated with impaired cognitive task performance, often attributed to disruptions in executive functioning. In this study, we conducted three experiments to replicate and extend previous work (Kam & Handy, 2014) by examining how mind wandering interacts with three core executive functions: Inhibition (Experiment 1: Sustained Attention to Response Task, n = 54), updating (Experiment 2: Random n-back Task, n = 52) and shifting (Experiment 3: Number-Letter Task, n = 54). If mind wandering is closely related to executive functioning, it was expected that mind wandering would impair performance on trials requiring these functions, reflected in lower accuracy and increased reaction time variability. Our findings did not confirm this: Mind wandering was associated with a general negative effect on performance, rather than specifically impairing executive functioning. Accuracy was lower on executive than non-executive trials in the inhibition and shifting tasks, but these effects were not attenuated by mind wandering. In the updating task, where executive and non-executive trials were matched in difficulty, mind wandering reduced accuracy in both executive and non-executive trials. Variability in reaction time was found to be higher during mind wandering in the inhibition and updating tasks, with evidence against such an effect in the shifting task. These findings suggest that the observed performance decrements may be more closely tied to task demands than to executive functions per se.

items.title: Virtual Reality for Enhancing Self-Compassion and Reducing Burnout Among Mental Health Care Professionals: Protocol for a Pilot Feasibility Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.abstract: Background Mental health care professionals working in high-demand clinical environments are frequently exposed to patient suffering and trauma, placing them at increased risk for burnout and secondary traumatic stress. Compassion-focused cognitive behavioral therapy (CF-CBT) has shown promise in reducing psychological distress and enhancing self-compassion; however, traditional delivery methods may be limited by time, accessibility, and resource constraints. Virtual reality (VR) may provide an immersive and accessible approach for delivering compassion-focused interventions. Objective The primary objective is to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of a self-administered VR-enhanced CF-CBT (VR-CF-CBT) intervention for mental health care professionals. Secondary exploratory objectives are to estimate changes in self-compassion, burnout, and secondary traumatic stress (STS), as well as between-group differences that can inform the design of a future definitive trial. Methods A 2-arm randomized controlled pilot trial will be conducted among mental health care professionals. Participants will be randomized to either a VR-CF-CBT intervention or an active comparison condition consisting of self-guided CF-CBT delivered via digital booklets. Participants will complete 8 brief sessions (approximately 10 minutes each) over a 4- to 6-week period. Exploratory clinical outcomes will include changes in self-compassion, burnout, and STS measured using validated self-report instruments. Primary feasibility and acceptability outcomes will include recruitment, retention, intervention adherence, session completion, participant satisfaction, and scores on the Acceptability of Intervention Measure, Intervention Appropriateness Measure, and Feasibility of Intervention Measure. Results The study was funded in April 2026. As of October 2026, 38 participants had provided consent and enrolled. Recruitment for a second wave of participants is ongoing, and data collection is in progress. Enrollment and data collection are expected to continue through 2026, with data analysis and dissemination of findings anticipated by spring 2027. Conclusions This pilot study will provide information on the feasibility and acceptability of delivering CF-CBT through immersive VR to mental health care professionals. Findings will help identify whether modifications are needed before a larger trial and provide preliminary estimates to inform the design of future efficacy testing. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07666867; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07666867. International registered report identifier (irrid) DERR1-10.2196/105754.

items.title: Beyond the silo: Single-disorder ADHD clinics and the case for more integrated care.
items.abstract: ObjectiveThe rapid growth of ADHD assessment and prescribing in Australia reflects a gap between demand and service availability. Workforce shortages, restrictive stimulant regulations and limited adult ADHD care within public mental health services have contributed to this gap. ADHD-focused clinics have emerged in response. Using two de-identified clinical scenarios, this paper examines the drivers of this model and its potential harms.ConclusionFocused clinics can improve access and provide expertise. However, a narrow scope and fee-for-service model may also encourage transactional and fragmented care. We describe this risk as organisational iatrogenesis. Potential harms include incomplete formulation, uncoordinated prescribing and missed psychiatric, neurodevelopmental or neurocognitive comorbidity. Broader concerns include inequity, cost, discontinuity of care and erosion of generalist skills. The solution is not to restrict focused practice, but to integrate it more effectively with mainstream care. Priorities include nationally consistent prescribing rules, stronger shared-care arrangements with general practitioners, greater adult ADHD capacity within public services and clearer standards for scope-restricted practice. These issues are also relevant to other single-disorder models of psychiatric care.

items.title: Characterizing Heat Health Hazards and Receptivity of Cooling Interventions Among Indoor Lumber Mill Workers in Southern Thailand.
items.abstract: Objective To evaluate the effectiveness and feasibility of two workplace cooling strategies and identify priorities for future mixed-methods research and practical solutions. Methods A pilot randomized crossover field trial was conducted among 12 sawmill workers in southern Thailand under three conditions: no cooling (CON), a phase change cooling vest (VEST), and a combined cooling oasis (OASIS: hydration, fans, water dousing, cooling towels). Core temperature and heart rate were continuously monitored. Worker perceptions were explored through post-intervention focus group discussions. Results Compared with CON, OASIS reduced core temperature (-0.24°C; 95% CI: 0.23, 0.25) and heart rate (-7 bpm; 95% CI: 6, 9), while VEST reduced core temperature (-0.17°C; 95% CI: 0.17, 0.18) and heart rate (-5 bpm; 95% CI: 4, 6). Despite greater physiological benefits from OASIS, most workers preferred VEST due to ease of use and caused minimal disruption to workflow. OASIS was perceived as effective but interruptive. Conclusions Combined cooling strategies can reduce heat strain in indoor industrial settings; however, the adoption of interventions is strongly influenced by practicality and economic considerations. Hybrid approaches and structural improvements are recommended. A full mixed-methods study is needed to evaluate effectiveness, productivity, and cost-effectiveness to inform scalable occupational heat policies.

items.title: Developing scenario-based, near-term iterative forecasts to inform water management
items.abstract: Near-term, iterative ecosystem forecasts with scenarios representing alternate management decisions have high potential for providing valuable insights on how decisions may impact future ecological conditions. Scenario-based forecasts may be particularly useful for informing the decision-making around freshwater ecosystems managed for multiple objectives. We applied a near-term, iterative forecasting system at Lake Alexandrina, Australia, which is located at the nexus of one of the world’s largest catchments and a protected coastal wetland. Lake Alexandrina is highly managed through multi-gate barrages to optimize catchment, lake, and outflow targets, providing an unparalleled opportunity to investigate the value of scenario-based probabilistic forecasting for decision-makers. We co-developed the forecasting system with managers to generate automated 1-30 day-ahead barrage operation scenario forecasts. Over ~2 years, forecasts accurately predicted lake water level, water temperature, and salinity and outperformed null baseline models up to 10-30 days ahead. Alternative barrage scenarios were particularly important during drier hydrological conditions and resulted in substantive changes to lake level and salt export from the lake. Lake temperatures and salinity were less sensitive to barrage operations and generally more dependent on variability in lake inflow discharge. Overall, our study provides a framework for forecasting lake water quantity and quality variables for anticipatory decision-making.

items.title: Functional diversity complements taxonomical diversity in productivity-biodiversity relationships in freshwaters
items.abstract: Abstract Productivity is widely considered a key driver of biodiversity, yet whether taxonomic and functional diversity respond similarly to productivity gradients remains unclear. Using phosphorus as an indicator for productivity gradient, we compiled 78 freshwater datasets spanning > 30,000 sites globally to test how productivity–biodiversity relationships (PBRs) vary across diversity dimensions, trophic groups, and ecosystems. We show that PBRs are predominantly unimodal across taxonomic and functional dimensions, with slightly weaker curvature for functional diversity. Unimodal PBRs are more pronounced in producers than in consumers and show stronger curvature in lakes than in rivers. Functional reorganization also varies along the phosphorus gradient, with the clearest contraction in resource-related trait space and marked shifts in community functional centroids. Climatic, geographic and human land-use gradients further modify PBR shape. These findings indicate that predicting biodiversity responses to productivity benefits from considering functional diversity, ecological context, and broad-scale environmental gradients.

items.title: Lattice Boltzmann Methods for Compressible Magnetohydrodynamics
items.abstract: Abstract Compressible, magnetised plasma flows pervade astrophysics, from stellar winds to planetary magnetospheres and the interstellar medium. Their high-fidelity simulation at scale is limited by the non-local operations that conventional solvers require for flux reconstruction, gradient and stress evaluation, and magnetic-divergence control, which bottleneck communication on heterogeneous supercomputers. We present a novel class of fully local Lattice Boltzmann Method (LBM) schemes for compressible magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) in which all nonlinear operations are point-wise. The approach exploits the kinetic structure to transport each state variable of the Strang-split conservation laws alongside its characteristics, recovering the compressible macroscopic fluxes, gradients, and viscous stresses through local relaxation rather than finite-difference stencils. Divergence control enters as a local source term within the same kinetic update, with no separate global solve. The formulation is partial-differential-equation agnostic and encompasses hydrodynamic limits such as the compressible Euler and incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. We discretise both ideal compressible and resistive incompressible MHD, and validate the scheme across multiple resolutions against the canonical astrophysical MHD test suite: the Brio-Wu shock tube resolves compound waves and slow-fast shocks, the MHD rotor captures strong torsional Alfvén waves, and the Orszag-Tang vortex reproduces current-sheet formation and the transition to MHD turbulence. Implemented in the performance-portable framework OpenLB, the scheme reaches up to 98.9 per cent of the hardware roofline on GPU. Finally, as a capability demonstration, we simulate a rotating, surface-resolved magnetised body modelled after 16 Psyche in a supersonic early solar wind, yielding an emergent bow shock, flux-rope magnetosheath, and reconnecting magnetotail.

items.title: Spectator axions in string inflation and primordial black holes
items.abstract: A bstract We study the impact of light spectator axions on the seeding of primordial black holes (PBHs) during inflation in string theory. Primordial black holes exhibit unique and novel phenomenology, and may constitute the observed dark matter. Cosmic inflation provides a mechanism for producing them, but such inflation models typically feature Planckian field excursions, necessitating an ultraviolet completion into quantum gravity. String theory provides a natural framework for doing so, and indeed Fibre Inflation has been shown to produce PBHs while satisfying constraints from cosmic microwave background data. In this work we study the dynamics of axions during Fibre Inflation, and find a diverse and rich set of possibilities, including turns in field space and enhancement of primordial perturbations. We find that across most of parameter space, notably an axion with a far sub-Planckian decay constant f ≪ M Pl , there is a negligible impact on the power spectrum of curvature perturbations, indicating an overall robustness of the model. On the other hand, an axion with a larger but still sub-Planckian decay constant, f ≳ 𝒪(0 . 1) M Pl , and an exponentially small prefactor of its non-perturbative potential, can enhance the growth of perturbations, making it easier to achieve the amplification needed to seed PBHs, effectively realizing axion-assisted PBHs in string theory.

items.title: Constraining lunar lower-mantle attenuation using ScSH-SH amplitude ratios
items.abstract: Summary Seismic attenuation in lunar lower mantle can provide critical constraints on thermal state and composition of the deep interior; however, previous estimates based on path-integrated amplitudes are strongly influenced by near-surface scattering, especially for narrow-band waveforms recorded by Apollo’s sparse seismic stations. Here we show that the amplitude ratio between ScSH and SH from the same station can mitigate this limitation. We measure these ratios from narrow-band records and invert for lower-mantle Q by matching them with synthetic predictions that account for geometric spreading, source radiation, and interface transmission. Synthetic tests verify that the method recovers Q within 10 per cent for SNR ≥ 10 and remains robust to scattering and source mechanism uncertainties. Application to a terrestrial deep earthquake recovers Q = 308 (IQR: 280–340), consistent with the PREM reference value (Q ≈ 312), confirming its feasibility on real data. Application to Apollo deep moonquake records (10 stacked records) shows that the amplitude ratios exhibit the expected single-peak distance trend and yield broadly consistent Q estimates across narrow bands, though the limited data warrant interpreting these results as a feasibility demonstration. This framework provides a practical and complementary constraint on lunar lower-mantle attenuation and is transferable to other planetary datasets with similar data limitations.
