items.title: Chemogenetic inhibition of the ventrolateral orbitofrontal cortex disrupts novelty-guided updating of spatial memories and alters hippocampal engram reactivation
items.abstract: Abstract Rationale Adaptive behavior requires revising memories when outcomes deviate from expectations. The orbitofrontal cortex (OFC) is implicated in representing outcome expectancies, but its role in memory-updating, beyond value-based learning, remains unclear. Objectives We tested whether the ventrolateral OFC (VLO) contributes to hippocampal-dependent memory-updating in the Objects in Updated Locations (OUL) task, where novelty-driven exploration provides a behavioral readout consistent with successful updating of spatial information Methods Using inhibitory DREADDs, in male and female (Swiss Webster and C57BL/6) mice, we suppressed VLO activity during the Updating session, when new object-location information was introduced. Results Control mice preferentially explored the updated object-location configuration during Updating and discriminated between updated and novel object-location configurations at Test, whereas VLO-inhibited mice did not. VLO inhibition when no updating demand was present did not alter exploration of novel object-location configurations or memory for the original spatial configuration at Test. Conclusions These results indicate that VLO activity is selectively required when novelty must be interpreted relative to prior experience, implicating this region in evaluating change rather than detecting it. To assess hippocampal ensemble dynamics, we tagged neuronal ensembles, in the dorsal dentate gyrus (dDG) recruited during Updating, followed by quantification of overlap between Updating-tagged cells and ensembles reactivated at Test. We found that VLO inhibition reduced reactivation of Updating-tagged dDG ensembles, paralleling the behavioral impairments observed in the OUL task. These findings support a role for the VLO in hippocampal-dependent memory-updating and extend OFC models beyond reward contexts to include predictive updating of spatial memory representations. Significance Statement Using a spatial paradigm that distinguishes detection of changed information from incorporation of that information into an updated hippocampal representation, we found that ventrolateral orbitofrontal cortex (VLO) activity is required for memory-updating when new information is present. We found behavioral deficits accompanied by impairments in hippocampal ensemble representations, indicating VLO activity is necessary for memory-updating at the hippocampal engram level. Through this mechanism, the OFC supports the flexible updating of expected outcomes when environmental conditions shift, allowing for the re-evaluation of previously learned associations. These findings extend models of orbitofrontal cortex function beyond reward-guided behavior and identify a cortical contribution to predictive spatial memory processes. Disruption of this computation may contribute to the cognitive rigidity observed in neuropsychiatric disorders.

items.title: The Influence of Perception of Career Opportunities on Students' Interest in Working in the MICE Industry
items.abstract: Background. The Meeting, Incentive, Convention, and Exhibition (MICE) industry is a growing tourism sector and offers a variety of career opportunities for tourism education graduates. However, the availability of job opportunities does not necessarily translate into high student interest in choosing the MICE industry as a career destination, because these decisions can be influenced by perceptions of available career prospects. Objectives. This study aims to analyze how perceptions of career opportunities influence students' interest in working in the MICE industry. Methods. This study used a quantitative approach involving 40 students in the D4 Convention and Event Management Study Program at Prima Turismo Polytechnic International, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through a Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, determination coefficients, and simple linear regression using SPSS. Results. The results showed that students had a positive perception of career opportunities and high interest in working in the MICE industry. The perception of career opportunities had a positive and strong relationship with interest in working in the MICE industry (r = 0.772; p < 0.05). The coefficient of determination (R² = 0.596) showed that the perception of career opportunities explained 59.6% of the variation in students' interest, while the remaining 40.4% was related to factors outside the research model. Regression analysis also showed that the perception of career opportunities had a positive and significant effect on students' interest in working in the MICE industry (β = 0.641; t = 7.480; p < 0.05). Conclusion. These findings confirm that students' perceptions of job prospects, career development opportunities, and professional opportunities are important factors in forming career interest in the MICE industry. This study strengthens the relevance of the Social Cognitive Career Theory perspective in explaining the relationship between perception of the environment and career opportunities and the formation of career interests. Implementation. Practically, universities and the MICE industry need to strengthen their career exposure through internships, training, involvement in event organizing, career mentoring, and education-industry collaboration to increase students' readiness and interest in careers in the MICE sector.

items.title: From Emotion to Expression: The AL–DL–CL Framework for Understanding Communication in the Age of AI and Digital Media
items.abstract: Rapid progress in digital media and artificial intelligence is transforming human communication, facilitating the rapid exchange of messages and minimizing the chances of reflective interpretation. Existing theories in linguistics, psychology, and cultural studies address the structural, cognitive, or social aspects of language, yet fail to explain how emotional processing, internal linguistic structuring, and culturally mediated communication function as a coherent, dynamic system. Through this model, the authors present the AL–DL–CL framework that explores how three layers are engaged in a process that results in communication, through a recursive interaction between the Automatic Layer (AL), the Deliberate Layer (DL), and the Cultural Language Layer (CL). In such a process, the affective or unconscious processes in AL are consistently reframed into structured internal representations via DL, and through CL, and translated back into culturally-expressed language serves as a feedback mechanism, with a tendency to modify cognition and emotional response. Based on a multi-method exploratory approach of sequential cultural transmission, clinical case study analysis, and group-based validation, the results indicate that language is not so much a static container for meaning as a process of reconstruction that is molded by the dynamic interaction between emotion, cognition, and culture. This model also demonstrates how digitally mediated communication can amplify AL-directed reaction and limit DL-level thinking, which increases the potential for misinterpretation, polarization, or misinformation. The AL–DL–CL framework provides guidance in a unified theoretical perspective around language emergence, responsible AI design and digital literacy and intercultural discourse based on the continuous transformation system of communication, and not on the linear encoding.

items.title: Neurophysiological Effects of Pranayama on Brain-Wave Modulation: An EEG-Based Analytical Study of Alpha, Beta, Theta, and Delta Activity
items.abstract: Background: Pranayama is usually defined as slow nasal breathing and involves the control of the breathing rate, route, and timing, accompanied by a high degree of concentration.It is still not clear how this type of breathing exercise influences the autonomic system and respiration-coupled neural activity, and little research has been done to measure the effects of pranayama on the four major brain wave frequencies -alpha, beta, theta, and delta -in a controlled setting.The objective of this work is to provide the basis of an analytic framework based on electroencephalography (EEG) to assess the short-term effects of Nadi Shodhana pranayama in a highly regulated experiment as compared to quiet seated rest.The example synthetic demonstration data used in this work included a sample of 60 healthy adults who participated in one of the two conditions of either 20 minutes of pranayama or seated rest.Baseline (T0) and resting, eyes-closed EEG were collected post-condition (T1) and post a 10-minute recovery period (T2).Change in relative spectral power for the 4 frequency bands (delta, theta, alpha, beta) was computed.A 2 (condition) by 3 (time) mixed analysis of variance (ANOVA) was performed, and each of the group, time, and group-by-time effects were analyzed.The primary analysis was augmented with effect sizes, Holm-adjusted contrasts, correlations, and multiple regression.Findings: A significant interaction effect for group and time was found for alpha power, F(1.48, 85.56) = 7.13, p = 0.004, partial η² = 0.110.In the pranayama group, alpha power increased (adjusted mean: 2.48) compared to the control group (adjusted mean: 0.37) with an approximate 95% confidence interval of 0.64 to 1.74 for Hedges g = 1.19.A clear interaction was found for beta power, while effects for delta and theta were much smaller and interpreted based on p-values and intervals.The pranayama condition resulted in more favorable outcomes for breathing rate, heartIn this synthetic analytical demonstration, it was found that pranayama brought about a considerable increase in alpha power and brought about a reduction of beta power when compared to quiet rest.The differences seen in theta and delta of the groups were small and of no statistical significance.The framework shows how upcoming preregistered studies can capture the integration of EEG quality control, repeated-measures modelling, effect-size estimation and open data practices.

items.title: Bridging the disaster awareness-preparedness gap in a heritage-sensitive built environment: A case study of İznik
items.abstract: This study explores the asymmetric relationship between household disaster awareness and structural preparedness actions in İznik (Türkiye), a region characterized by its vulnerability to multiple hazards and its high sensitivity to cultural heritage damage. The present study examines the "awareness-preparedness gap" paradox within the extant literature. To this end, the study analyzes cross-sectional survey data obtained from 515 households employing binary logistic regression models. The empirical findings indicate that risk perception varies significantly depending on the hazard typology: While the perception of seismic risk is notably high (77.9%), structural retrofitting rates remain marginal (7.0%). Conversely, flood risk is largely neglected both perceptually and behaviorally. Multivariate analyses indicate that, when controlled for sociodemographic and cognitive variables, housing ownership status (homeowners are approximately three times more likely to prepare compared to tenants; OR = 3.031) and self-efficacy constitute the most robust predictors of protective behavior. The analysis demonstrates that fatalism, institutional trust, and mere risk perception, which are frequently emphasized in the literature, do not independently catalyze disaster mitigation actions. Moreover, the factors constraining structural interventions were identified as bureaucratic obstacles rather than concerns regarding the preservation of cultural heritage. Consequently, this study advocates for transcending conventional information-deficit models in disaster risk reduction (DRR) strategies. The study proposes the adoption of an integrated "awareness-capacity-action" framework that centers on ownership-related constraints, institutional barriers, and individual self-efficacy.

items.title: Young children prefer to learn from and befriend strivers rather than endowed individuals
items.abstract: Do children reason about the unequal means to success when making future learning decisions? Here we show that children preferred to learn from a striver than from an endowed informant. In Study 1 (N = 100, Mage = 7.58, 45 girls), children compared between a striver and an endowed informant who achieved the same outcome when making future learning decisions. In Study 2 (N = 120, Mage = 7.30, 65 girls), they compared between informants who achieved different outcomes when making future learning and interpersonal decisions. With increasing age, children attributed more competence and preferred to learn from the striver over the endowed informant (Study 1). Children’s preference to learn from the striver was replicated in Study 2 even when the informants’ outcomes differed in success, with this pattern extending to their preference from whom to seek future information and their interpersonal choices. Moreover, children referenced both epistemic cues (e.g., “she knows more”) and effort (e.g., “because she worked hard”) to explain their choices. Taken together, children assign epistemic value to effort, and view effort as an indicator of future informant reliability. Broadly, our findings demonstrate that children’s learning and interpersonal preferences are not solely based on successful outcomes, but also the process through which that success is attained. Across two studies, 5- to 9-year-old children selected between a striver and an endowed informant when making epistemic and social decisions. This study found that children preferred the striver as a source of information and social partner even when both individuals differed in their outcomes of success.

items.title: Brain Structure and Differential Response to Family-Centered Prevention: Evidence for Anterior Cingulate Cortex Moderation in a Randomized Controlled Trial
items.abstract: Family-centered prevention programs improve youth self-regulation, yet intervention effects are heterogeneous, and the mechanisms underlying differential response remain poorly understood. Identifying neural metrics that shape responsiveness to prevention may advance theory and inform program refinement. This study examined whether baseline brain structure moderated response to a telehealth adaptation of the Strong African American Families program (T-SAAF), a prevention intervention targeting self-regulation among Black preadolescents. Youth ages 11-12 and their caregivers (N = 170 families) were recruited in North Georgia and randomly assigned to T-SAAF or a no-treatment control condition. Allocation was 1:1 in a two-group parallel design evaluated within a superiority framework, and we generated the allocation sequence using statistical software. Because randomization followed the pretest assessment, allocation was concealed from participants and from pretest assessors, and condition was revealed only after pretest data collection was complete. Thereafter, families, facilitators, and posttest assessors could not be masked to condition, as T-SAAF is a group-based family program delivered by facilitators. We conducted no interim analyses and used no stopping guidelines; the trial completed as planned. They were assessed at baseline and approximately nine months later. A neuroimaging subsample completed structural MRI prior to intervention exposure. Analyses focused on whether cortical and subcortical structural metrics moderated changes in parent-reported youth self-control. To account for differential engagement, the intervention main effect was tested in a propensity score-matched sample of youth who received the intervention and comparable controls (n = 130); brain by intervention interactions were tested in the neuroimaging subsample (n = 105). Assignment to T-SAAF was associated with a modest increase in self-control (F[1,124] = 4.28, p = .04). Baseline anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) structure moderated this effect. The clearest and most consistent evidence was for rostral ACC thickness and caudal ACC thickness; caudal ACC volume showed the same pattern with weaker but convergent support. Across these metrics, thinner or smaller ACC at baseline was associated with greater intervention-related gains in self-control, whereas youth with higher ACC structural values showed little differential benefit. No moderation was observed for rostral ACC volume, amygdala volume, or nucleus accumbens volume. Findings provide preliminary evidence that individual differences in neural structure, particularly within the ACC, may shape responsiveness to family-centered preventive intervention during preadolescence. By extending neural prediction approaches from adult treatment to developmental prevention, this study indicates that neurodevelopmental markers can clarify mechanisms of differential response and inform program refinement. Confirmation in adequately powered, preregistered research is needed. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05253235 ( https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05253235 ); registered February 22, 2022.

items.title: Beyond Task Delegation: Reconceptualising Instructional Design to Measure Competence in the Age of Generative AI
items.abstract: The rapid proliferation of Large Language Models (LLMs) has invalidated traditional content-recall assessments, acting as a catalyst for a systemic transition towards Competence-Based Education (CBE). This paper contends that the role of faculty must transcend content dissemination, focusing instead on observable human competencies associated with Metacognition and Self-Regulated Learning (SRL). Drawing upon Behaviourism and Bloom's Taxonomy, we propose the Reverse-Flipped Model. This conceptual framework, supported by illustrative disciplinary cases in History, Computer Science, Digital Photography, and Composition, utilises generative tools for low-stakes production to repurpose pedagogical time for high-stakes human intervention. Prompt Literacy is conceptualised as an observable instructional competency that externalises planning, monitoring, evaluation, and strategic intervention behaviours during human-AI collaboration. Implementation necessitates the use of Analytic Rubrics and Automated Process Portfolios (APP) to document observable demonstrations of Prompt Literacy and strategic engagement over final product quality. The framework addresses institutional sustainability and the moral imperative of digital equity. The primary contribution of this framework is a structural shift that enhances assessment validity by ensuring student success is defined by verifiable mastery of human-led strategic intervention rather than machine-generated output.

items.title: A dataset on radical and extremist attitudes in Europe
items.abstract: This dataset introduces the first cross-nationally validated measurement scales for left-wing and right-wing radicalism, and general political extremism, along with an implicit association test (IAT) for implicit political extremism in the Western world. It includes data from more than 18,000 participants collected through ten surveys conducted between 2022 and 2024 in France, Germany, Great Britain, Greece, Hungary, the Netherlands, and the United States. The dataset facilitates comparative analyses of the origins and consequences of radical and extremist attitudes across different political systems. Moreover, by linking attitudinal measures with behavioral indicators such as party support, it provides a foundation for examining how latent forms of extremism are translated into political action. Beyond extremism research, the dataset contributes to the broader study of democratic resilience, political polarization, and ideological belief structures.

items.title: Use of Visual Aids as a Communication Channel in the Field of Learning in Secondary Schools
items.abstract: Visual learning aids that involve the use of photographs, drawings or interactive video are typically intended to promote learning and have a positive impact on learning for the students. Visual aids have become the very instrument in effective academic learning in the modern century. It is pertinent to understand and know the psychological manifestations of the use of visual aids in imparting knowledge in the children especially those in the formative stage; the secondary school students. However, this study, sought to investigate the use of visual aids as a communication channel in the field of learning in secondary schools. The quantitative approach was used on a multi-stage sampling of the population. The population was composed of all students of Emmanuel Anglican Secondary School and Union Secondary School, Awkunanaw. The paper was anchored on Gestalt and Constructivism theories. Findings from the study show that majority of the respondents are aware of visual aids in teaching and are in support of the use of visual aids for teaching in secondary schools. Also findings from the study indicated that majority of the respondents affirmed the use of power points slides in class rooms while teaching although other visual aids were revealed such as mnemonics, audio or video clips, and use of mind pictures/mind maps as it enable them to retain what they have learnt in their long term memory. The recommendations suggest that Teachers should make greater and more consistent use of appropriate visual aids such as charts, diagrams, pictures, maps, models, posters, videos, and PowerPoint presentations during classroom instruction and proprietors and school management should provide adequate and functional visual aid facilities.

items.title: When extremes sound like the majority: Social signal and norm misperception
items.abstract: Abstract Societies often misperceive their own normative center. Individuals may believe that distinctive, conservative, or ideologically committed positions are more widely shared than they actually are, sustaining pluralistic ignorance even when private attitudes are moderate. Yet little is known about how perceived norms become systematically organized under conditions of uncertainty. We propose that norm perceptions are structured around socially salient reference points, including identity-defining or ideologically committed subgroups, and only partially calibrated by individuals’ private attitudes. Across two preregistered studies, we test this representational account of norm perception in distinct social ecologies. Study 1 examines norm inference among 550 adults from Israel’s ultra-Orthodox community, a context characterized by strong social norms and hierarchies. Study 2 extends the analysis cross-nationally using survey data from 21,233 respondents in 57 countries on perceived gender norms. Using theory-constrained regression models, we fixed the intercept to alternative candidate reference points and estimated adjustment from these anchors as a function of respondents’ private attitudes. Across studies, perceived norms were better represented relative to contextually salient subgroup anchors or, in some domains, the response-scale midpoint, than by population averages alone. These findings suggest that pluralistic ignorance may reflect a predictable structure in how normative perceptions are formed under uncertainty: perceived norms are organized around salient reference points and only partially adjusted in relation to individuals’ private attitudes.

items.title: Streptomyces chodovensis sp. nov.: a novel candidate for plant growth-promoting actinomycete from bare soil developing on Miocene lacustrine sediment of the Sokolov Coal Basin, Czech Republic
items.abstract: Abstract A novel actinomycete, designated as BCCO 10_0861 T , was isolated from overburden Miocene clay sediments undergoing primary succession in Northwest Czechia and characterized by the polyphasic approach. According to 16S rRNA gene sequence similarity, the strain was closely related to Streptomyces turgidiscabies DSM 41838 T (99.00%), Streptomyces reticuliscabiei DSM 41804 T (98.93%), Streptomyces lacrimifluminis DSM 111125 T (98.15%), and Streptomyces geranii JCM 32177 T (98.08%). Morphological and chemotaxonomic characteristics supported the assignment to the genus Streptomyces . Diagnostic diamino acid in the cell-wall peptidoglycan was LL -diaminopimelic acid and the dominant menaquinone was MK-9(H 6 ). The major cellular fatty acids (> 10%) were anteiso -C 15:0 , iso -C 16:0 , C 16:1 ω7c, and C 16:0 . The polar lipid profile comprised of aminophospholipids, diphosphatidylglycerol, glycophospholipids, phosphatidylethanolamine, phosphatidylinositol, and three unidentified phospholipids. The whole cell sugars were galactose, glucose, mannose, ribose, and traces of rhamnose. The genome size of the strain BCCO 10_0861 T was 10.6 Mb with G+C content of 70.05%. Bioinformatic analysis suggested several biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) with medium-to-high similarity confidence to already known BGCs, having ethylenediaminesuccinic acid hydroxyarginine (EDHA), humidimycin, inthomycin B, and triascin C unique to BCCO 10_0861 T . Similarly, predicted plant-growth promoting trait (PGPT) genes differed between genomes, when the one of BCCO 10_0861 T showed the highest number of unique PGPT genes (2,255). In addition, no association with potato pathogenicity was predicted in the genome of BCCO 10_0861 T . The digital DNA-DNA hybridization (ranged from 34.7 to 37.5%), average nucleotide identity values (ranged from 86.26 to 87.24%) and phenotype distinguish strain BCCO 10_0861 T from closely related strains. Based on the polyphasic approach and genomic content, the strain represents a novel species of the genus Streptomyces , for which we propose the name Streptomyces chodovensis sp. nov. for BCCO 10_0861 T (= DSM 117345 T ).

items.title: Isolation, Phenotypic Screening, and Extracellular Serotonin-Like Immunoreactivity of Presumptive Lactic Acid Bacteria from Butterfly Pea Flower (Clitoria ternatea L.) Kombucha
items.abstract: Background: Major depressive disorder is a leading cause of disability, and interest in the microbiota-gut-brain axis has stimulated bioprospecting of food-derived lactic acid bacteria (LAB) for neuroactive metabolite production. Objective: To isolate and phenotypically screen acidogenic bacteria from butterfly pea flower (Clitoria ternatea L.) kombucha and to evaluate their cell-free supernatants for extracellular serotonin-like immunoreactivity. Methods: Colonies were isolated from day-14 kombucha on MRS agar supplemented with 1.0% CaCO3 and characterised by Gram staining, catalase testing and broth acidification in MRS broth (24 h, 37 °C). Serotonin-like immunoreactivity in cell-free supernatants was quantified by a competitive enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) calibrated with a four-parameter logistic (4-PL) model. Results: Three isolates (Isolates 3, 6 and 8) were presumptive LAB (Gram-positive, catalase-negative bacilli), dissolved CaCO3 (clear zones 14.8–18.4 mm) and reduced broth pH from 7.00 to 3.94–4.15. The 4-PL model returned R2 = 0.9993 and back-calculated the standards to within 0.1% of nominal. Cell-free supernatants gave serotonin-like immunoreactivity averaging 18.11 ± 4.54 ng/mL (Isolate 3 highest, 23.13 ng/mL) versus 1.28 ± 0.67 ng/mL in sterile media (exploratory Welch's t = 6.34, df = 2.09, p = 0.022). Conclusion: Presumptive lactic acid bacteria from butterfly pea flower kombucha yielded a measurable serotonin-like immunoreactivity signal in culture broth. These preliminary in vitro findings warrant 16S rRNA gene sequencing, chromatographic confirmation of analyte identity (HPLC/LC-MS) and in vivo evaluation.

items.title: Synergy between Universities and Local Communities in Empowering Elementary School Teachers to Design Sustainable Environmental Education Projects
items.abstract: Environmental education in elementary schools is constrained by limited contextual resources, predominantly theoretical instruction, and insufficient teacher capacity to design sustainable environmental projects. This study examines how collaboration between higher education institutions and local communities can support teachers in developing contextual and sustainable environmental education projects. A community-based empowerment approach combined with participatory action research (PAR) was employed, involving elementary school teachers in Cluster 3, Pasir Penyu District, Indragiri Hulu Regency, Riau Province. Activities comprised preparation, needs identification, pedagogical training, project design, learning media development, mentoring, and evaluation. Data from observations, interviews, documentation, and activity evaluations were analyzed descriptively. The findings highlight collaborative partnerships as a foundation for integrating local environmental resources, community knowledge, and project-based learning into environmental education. Proposed projects included waste sorting, composting, school greening, water conservation, and school garden development. A hybrid strategy combining printed materials, digital pocketbooks, and resources accessed through QR codes was identified to support learning accessibility and program continuity. The study presents a collaborative framework for strengthening teachers’ capacity to design locally relevant environmental education projects and advancing sustainable development. Its effectiveness in improving teacher competence and students’ environmental awareness, however, requires further empirical evaluation.

items.title: Türkiye Yeşil Taksonomisi Yönetmeliğinde Döngüsel Ekonomi ve Sürdürülebilir Finansın Yeri ve Önemi
items.abstract: Türkiye Yeşil Taksonomisi Yönetmeliği (TYTY), çevresel sürdürülebilirliği ekonomik faaliyet düzeyinde tanımlayan ve sürdürülebilir yatırımlara finansman akışını desteklemeyi amaçlayan yeni bir düzenleyici altyapı kurmaktadır. Bu bölüm, Yönetmeliği özellikle döngüsel ekonomi ve sürdürülebilir finans arasındaki ilişki bakımından incelemektedir. Analiz, 24 Eylül 2026 tarihli TYTY Yönetmeliği ve Ek-1’in sistematiği esas alınarak; Avrupa Birliği Taksonomi Tüzüğü (ABTT) ve ilgili ikincil mevzuat ile güncel akademik literatür çerçevesinde geliştirilmiştir. Yönetmelikte döngüsel ekonomiye geçiş, altı çevresel hedeften biri olarak kabul edilmekte; Ek-1’de plastik ambalaj, elektrikli ve elektronik ekipman, atık toplama ve işleme, fosfor geri kazanımı, inşaat ve yenileme, onarım, yenileme, yeniden imalat, ikinci el faaliyetleri ve ürün-hizmet modelleri gibi kaynak değerini koruyan faaliyetler taksonomi kapsamına alınmaktadır. Sürdürülebilir finans boyutunda ise hasılat, yatırım harcamaları ve işletme giderlerine dayalı anahtar performans göstergeleri ile finansal kuruluşlara özgü raporlama mantığı, taksonomi verisini sermaye tahsisiyle ilişkilendirmektedir. Bölümde, Türkiye modelinin AB Taksonomi Tüzüğü’nün altı hedef, önemli ölçüde katkı, önemli zarar vermeme, asgari sosyal koruma ve teknik tarama kriterleri yaklaşımıyla güçlü yapısal benzerlik taşıdığı; buna karşılık faaliyet-özel teknik eşiklerin, doğrulama usullerinin, geçiş planı içeriğinin ve finansal kuruluşlara özgü ayrıntılı metodolojilerin henüz tamamlanmamış olması nedeniyle uygulama düzeyinde önemli belirsizliklerin sürdüğü sonucuna ulaşılmaktadır. Döngüsel ekonominin finansmanı bakımından temel mesele, taksonominin yalnızca geri dönüşümü değil; ürün ömrünün uzatılması, onarım, yeniden kullanım, yeniden imalat, ikincil hammadde kullanımı ve ürün-hizmet sistemleri gibi daha yüksek değer koruma stratejilerini ölçülebilir ve doğrulanabilir biçimde finansal karar süreçlerine aktarabilmesidir.

items.title: Güncel Finans Araştırmaları II
items.abstract: Finansal piyasalar; artan küresel bağlantılılık, sürdürülebilirlik beklentileri ve finansal teknolojilerin yükselişiyle yeni bir döneme girmektedir. Güncel Finans Araştırmaları II, bu dönüşümü sermaye piyasaları, sürdürülebilir finans ve finansal yenilik ekseninde ele alan yedi bölümden oluşmaktadır. Kitapta E7 ülkelerinin gösterge borsaları arasındaki bağlantılılık ilişkileri, Borsa İstanbul menkul kıymet yatırım ortaklıklarında piyasa fiyatı ile net aktif değer arasındaki ayrışma ve pay geri alımı ile likidite sağlayıcılığının karşılaştırması incelenmektedir. Çevresel, sosyal ve yönetişimsel (ESG) faktörlerin varlık fiyatlamasındaki rolü, biyoçeşitlilik finansmanının kaynakları, araçları ve güçlükleri, finansal yenilik, finansal teknoloji ve finansal kapsayıcılık arasındaki ilişki ile Türkiye'de İngilizce yazılmış muhasebe ve finans doktora tezlerinde nedensellik ifadelerinin derlem tabanlı analizi de kitabın konuları arasındadır. Kuram ile uygulamayı bir araya getiren bu çalışma; araştırmacılar, finans uzmanları, portföy yöneticileri, karar alıcılar ve piyasa profesyonelleri için bir başvuru kaynağı niteliği taşımaktadır.

items.title: Seed persistence of nine weed species in silage, manure, and slurry and implications for dispersal through organic fertilizers
items.abstract: Weed seed contamination of cattle feed can contribute to weed dispersal within crop–livestock systems when viable seeds survive digestion and are returned to fields through manure or slurry applications. However, the persistence of weed seeds from feed preservation to waste recycling remains poorly understood. This study aimed to evaluate the viability of common agricultural weed seeds after exposure to silage fermentation, simulated rumen digestion, and storage in cattle manure and slurry. Seeds of nine weed species ( Abutilon theophrasti , Alopecurus myosuroides , Amaranthus retroflexus , Avena sterilis , Chenopodium album , Datura stramonium , Echinochloa crus-galli , Lolium multiflorum , and Sorghum halepense ) were incubated for one, four, and six months in three silage types (maize, sorghum, and grass) and subsequently incubated in cattle manure and slurry following simulated rumen digestion. Silage fermentation significantly reduced seed viability, although the response varied among weed species and silage types. During storage in cattle waste, seed viability declined progressively, with slurry degrading seeds faster than manure. Nevertheless, seeds of C. album , D. stramonium , A. retroflexus , and E. crus-galli remained viable after six months in manure. These findings suggest that cattle manure may be an important pathway for weed seed persistence and dispersal in agricultural soils, whereas slurry may pose a much lower risk. The results provide practical guidance for manure management strategies aimed at reducing weed spread while supporting sustainable crop–livestock production systems.

items.title: From fear to coexistence: citizen science and environmental education to increase urban snake awareness and appreciation
items.abstract: Abstract As urbanization intensifies, encounters between people and wildlife are increasing, often generating fear and conflict. A key example is interactions with snakes, which face strong cultural stigmas that hinder their conservation despite their fundamental ecological role in regulating prey populations. The Serpentes do Distrito Federal Project , implemented in Brasília, Brazil, a city where 70% of the territory still retains remnants of the Cerrado, provides a case study of how citizen science and environmental education can increase appreciation and awareness of these animals, fostering better human–snake coexistence in urban landscapes. Through participatory monitoring, structured data validation, interactive workshops, social media dialogue, and survey-based activities, the project combines data collection with emotional and cognitive learning processes. Over two years, the increase in voluntary record submissions, participant feedback during exhibitions, and inquiries from institutions indicate changes in people’s engagement with the project and in their perceptions of coexistence with snakes. Drawing on our experiences, we propose five recommendations to integrate biodiversity monitoring with public engagement within an ecology-with-cities framework. Together, these recommendations offer a replicable approach for increasing urban biodiversity awareness and promoting sustainable human–wildlife coexistence, particularly with species that may evoke fear or generate conflict.

items.title: Historical dynamics of social adaptation strategies under natural hazard characteristics in the Hengduan Mountains, Southwest China
items.abstract: The nexus between natural hazard events and regional societal responses constitutes a critical link in the chain of climate change impacts on human social systems. China’s extensive historical documentary resources remain underutilized for reconstructing spatiotemporal patterns of natural hazard events, characterizing impacts, and identifying adaptation features. This study systematically compiles a dataset of natural hazard events in the Hengduan Mountains region (HMR) during the Little Ice Age (LIA), and delineates their spatiotemporal patterns across climatic fluctuations. An examination of societal adaptation across ten stages reveals the transformation of traditional mountain societies from infrastructure restoration to integrated hazard-relief systems. Results indicate that natural hazard events in the HMR exhibit phased clustering, with one primary peak and four secondary peaks. These clusters are concentrated in land-water ecotones, forming three coupled hazard zones: tectonic-dominated, agroecologically vulnerable, and monsoon-sensitive hydrological zones. Temporal analyses demonstrate the dominance of hydro-meteorological hazard events and their strong association with climate. Seismic geological hazard events show strong spatial congruence with active fault zones. In contrast, hot-spots of biological hazard events exhibit strong spatial coupling with food-security events. The Driving forces-Pressures-State-Impacts-Responses (DPSIR) framework reveals that the combined effects of climate transitions and mountain development exert environmental pressures on regional systems, thereby contributing to cascading hazard-chain effects and livelihood disruption. In traditional societies, dynamic adaptation strategies evolved through sophisticated spatiotemporally tailored measures, localized knowledge transmission, and the establishment of synergies between institutions and culture. This research advances understanding of social adaptation strategies to natural hazards, thereby providing historical references for environmental decision-making and hazard prevention.

items.title: Colonial Alien: House Crows, Disposability and Necropolitics in Urban Tanzania
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Which lives are allowed to flourish in the city, and which are rendered excessive, alien, or disposable? This article examines kunguru (a Swahili term for crows/ravens, commonly referring to the house crow, Corvus splendens , in urban Tanzania) in Dar es Salaam as a lens through which to analyze colonial afterlives, urban waste infrastructures, and the biopolitics of multispecies life in a postcolonial African city. Kunguru in urban East Africa were initially introduced to Zanzibar Island by the British colonial administration as scavengers and were incorporated into urban hygiene projects. Over time, however, their ecological success exceeded the narrow functions assigned to them, leading to their reclassification as invasive aliens and subsequent targets of eradication. Kunguru introduced in Tanzania through colonial ecological interventions are presently proliferating by fragmented waste infrastructures and governed as unwanted excess in the contemporary postcolonial cities of Tanzania. Analyzing kunguru eradication as a necropolitical practice, the article argues that these programs displace accountability for the city's infrastructural failures onto the urban poor and the crows themselves. By foregrounding the concept of the colonial alien, the article develops an analytic for tracing how colonial and postcolonial governance incorporate particular forms of life into their projects, only to later revoke that incorporation and recast them as excess, unwanted, or disposable.

items.title: Genomic diversity, population structure, and relatedness of critically endangered Philippine eagles under conservation management
items.abstract: The critically endangered Philippine eagle ( Pithecophaga jefferyi ) faces severe threats to its population from habitat loss, naturally slow reproduction cycles, and human encroachment. Thus, 38 years ago, the Philippine Eagle Foundation (PEF) was established for the conservation of the endangered Philippine eagle and its rainforest habitat. To support the PEF’s captive-breeding and rehabilitation efforts, this study investigates the genome-wide single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) profiles of 20 wild-captive and 15 captive-bred individuals under the foundation’s care. Sequence reads were quality-filtered and aligned to a previously generated Philippine eagle reference genome. Identified SNPs across the 35 individuals were then further analyzed to assess population structure, isolation by distance (IBD), inbreeding, and relatedness. Population structure analysis revealed that genetic distance tended to increase with geographic distance, suggesting that the wild-captive eagles follow an pattern. Inbreeding analysis meanwhile showed significantly higher levels among wild-captive eagles compared to those bred in captivity, suggesting limited access to genetically diverse mates in the wild, and highlighting the success of the foundation’s breeding strategy in minimizing inbreeding. Finally, kinship analysis confirmed known first-degree relationships among captive-bred eagles and uncovered novel kinships among wild-captive individuals that reinforce the IBD model. These results represent the first comprehensive conservation genomics study on the Philippine eagle, providing insights into the diversity of its captive and wild populations, as well as valuable information that can guide future breeding and conservation efforts.

items.title: First record of Syringophiloidus glandarii (Fritsch) in Türkiye, with an updated overview of the quill mites (Acari: Syringophilidae) of Türkiye
items.abstract: Quill mites (Acari: Syringophilidae) are obligatory and permanent ectoparasites of birds inhabiting the inner part of the quill (calamus) of various types of feathers. These mites spend their entire life cycle inside the feather quills and are widely distributed among various bird groups. Currently, the family Syringophilidae comprises hundreds of species reported from numerous avian orders worldwide, and recent taxonomic studies have demonstrated that the biodiversity of this group is considerably higher than previously assumed. In the present study, quill mites recovered from the calamus of contour feathers of the Eurasian Jay (Garrulus glandarius Linnaeus) and the Eurasian Magpie (Pica pica Linnaeus) were examined, resulting in the first record of Syringophiloidus glandarii (Fritsch) in Türkiye. The present record increases the number of syringophilid mite species known from Türkiye to 10, representing seven genera. In addition, an updated checklist of the Syringophilidae species reported from Türkiye is provided. The present findings not only expand the known geographical distribution of S. glandarii but also contribute to the knowledge of the quill mite fauna of Türkiye. Furthermore, the available data indicate that the fauna of quill mites in Türkiye remains insufficiently investigated. Detailed studies focusing on different bird orders and geographical regions are expected to reveal new records of species, host associations, and distributions.

items.title: Multiple dimensions of taxonomic tree diversity reveal complementary effects of environmental filtering and land-use legacy in an urban Atlantic Forest
items.abstract: Abstract The Brazilian Atlantic Forest is a highly diverse ecosystem that has been extensively fragmented by human activities, making secondary urban forests important for biodiversity conservation. However, the influence of environmental filtering and land-use legacies on taxonomic diversity during forest regeneration remains poorly understood. We evaluated tree community diversity along environmental gradients under contrasting management histories in an urban secondary forest in Juiz de Fora, Brazil. Three regenerating communities with a common origin as shaded coffee agroforestry systems were sampled: second-growth forest after silvicultural management (SGAM), second-growth forest after enrichment with Euterpe edulis (SGAE), and second-growth forest under natural regeneration (SGA). Phytosociological, topographic, soil, and litter data were analyzed using Hill numbers (q = 0, 1, 2) through iNEXT.3D and iNEXT.beta3D, Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Non-metric Multidimensional Scaling (NMDS), and Generalized Linear Mixed Models. PCA revealed edaphic and elevation gradients, whereas NMDS showed significant differences in species composition. Species richness (q = 0) was highest in SGAE and SGA, while dominance-weighted diversity (q = 1 and 2) was greater in SGAE and SGAM. Species richness increased with elevation, effective cation exchange capacity, sand content, and litter carbon-to-nitrogen ratio, but decreased with clay content, whereas management history showed little influence. In contrast, abundance-weighted diversity was primarily driven by management history, but also increased with litter carbon-to-nitrogen ratio and elevation. These findings indicate that environmental filtering shapes species richness, whereas land-use legacies have persistent effects on community structure, highlighting the importance of multidimensional approaches for evaluating and restoring secondary urban tropical forests.

Urban agriculture encompasses various practices, from community gardens and rooftop farms to vertical farming and aquaponics, transforming urban spaces into productive landscapes. By integrating food production into urban planning, cities can pave the way for a more resilient and sustainable food system that meets the needs of their residents. items.title: Traditional Ethnic Beverages as Sources of Phenolic Compounds: Antioxidant and Anti-inflammatory Properties—A Narrative Review
items.abstract: Indigenous groups have been consuming traditional ethnic beverages for generations, and they play a significant role in their dietary customs, cultural legacy, and traditional medical systems.These drinks are typically made using naturally occurring fermentation processes that improve the nutritional content and bioactive composition of cereals, fruits, herbs, and other locally accessible plant materials.Traditional fermented drinks are rich in phenolic compounds, flavonoids, organic acids, bioactive peptides, and beneficial microbes, which together support a variety of biological activities, according to mounting scientific data.Because of their ability to avoid oxidative stress and chronic inflammatory illnesses, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory capabilities have garnered significant interest.Fermentation increases the bioavailability and biological effectiveness of phytochemicals by facilitating their release and biotransformation.In experimental studies, a number of traditional beverages, such as Haria, Kanji, Pakhoi, Chubitchi, Makgeolli, Judima, and other native fermented drinks, have shown notable free radical scavenging activity, inhibition of lipid peroxidation, modulation of inflammatory cytokines, and regulation of oxidative stress pathways.However, due to variations in raw ingredients, fermentation techniques, microbial variety, and geographic origin, there is a great deal of variation in their phytochemical content and biological activities.The present understanding of the phenolic composition, antioxidant capacity, and anti-inflammatory potential of traditional ethnic beverages is summarized in this narrative review, with a focus on beverages that the Khasi population of Meghalaya, India, typically consumes.Furthermore, it highlights the underlying mechanisms responsible for their biofunctional properties, discusses existing research gaps, and outlines future perspectives for the scientific validation and development of traditional ethnic beverages as evidence-based functional foods.

items.title: Spatial and temporal patterns of human-elephant conflict and compensation in Nagaon District, Assam, India
items.abstract: Human-elephant conflict (HEC) threatens both biodiversity and rural livelihoods. Forest departments in affected districts hold decades of compensation-claim records, but these archives are seldom analyzed for the spatial and temporal insights they contain. This study analyses twenty-one years of compensation-claim records from Nagaon District, Assam, India (1999–2020) to identify the spatial, seasonal, and institutional structure of conflict, and to assess whether compensation is allocated in proportion to the burden it addresses. Getis-Ord Gi* and Local Moran’s I statistics were applied to 1,915 georeferenced incidents across 1,032 villages, and 1,788 records with complete financial data were examined using non-parametric correlation, Theil-Sen regression, and segmentation by policy regime. Conflict was reported in 241 villages (23.35%), with hotspots concentrated along the Karbi Anglong foothills and human casualty clusters localized in the northeastern part of the district. Incidents peaked in December (23.29%), coinciding with the Sali rice harvest. Property and crop damage together accounted for over 88% of claims but under 28% of disbursed funds, while human fatalities represented 6.26% of claims and 68.37% of funds. Claim volume explained only 31.8% of the variation in payouts, with compensation rate revisions accounting for most of the remainder. Mitigation should be spatially targeted and seasonally adaptive, and compensation restructured into a tiered, need-based model that recognizes chronic livelihood loss alongside catastrophic outcomes.

items.title: Teredinid ecosystem engineering in Indonesian mangrove forests: biodiversity, functional diversity and habitat complexity datasets
items.abstract: This dataset accompanies the manuscript “Teredinid ecosystem engineering transforms fallen mangrove wood into biodiversity-rich habitat”, submitted to Ecology Letters. The data describe macrofaunal biodiversity, assemblage composition, functional feeding groups, trophic groups and habitat complexity across five mangrove forests in southeastern Sulawesi, Indonesia: Langira, Kaluku, Loho, Onitu and Gili. Sampling encompassed teredinid-bored large woody debris (LWD), Rhizophora prop roots and mangrove sediments. Additional measurements characterise vacant teredinid tunnel area and its associations with macrofaunal richness, abundance and occupancy. The deposit includes supporting datasets, statistical outputs and methodological documentation. These materials support examination and reuse of the ecological patterns reported in the accompanying manuscript.

items.title: Genetic isolation and loss of diversity in the broadcast spawning coral, Acropora kenti at Yunbenun (Magnetic Island) on the Great Barrier Reef
items.abstract: Abstract Coral populations on inshore reefs of the Great Barrier Reef (GBR) face increasing pressures from environmental stressors. Genetic diversity and connectivity are key determinants of coral adaptive capacity. Acropora kenti forms at least four genetically distinct clusters distributed across hundreds of kilometres along the GBR. One cluster which is potentially vulnerable due to restricted geographic distribution is found at Yunbenun (Magnetic Island). Here, we conducted a genetic assessment of A. kenti populations from seven reefs around Yunbenun and eight adjacent inshore and mid-shelf reefs in the central GBR to identify their population structure, genetic diversity and connectivity. Using single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) we demonstrate that a genetically distinct (F st >0.33) lineage dominates at all bays around Yunbenun but is rarely found on adjacent reefs. Fine-scale analysis within the Yunbenun lineage revealed a pattern of isolation by distance, driven by limited gene flow. Admixture analysis supported by hydrodynamic modelling shows that larval dispersal is occurring between Yunbenun and surrounding reefs, but gene flow remains limited. Populations at Yunbenun have lower allelic richness ( p < 0.001) and much lower effective population sizes (N e = 1348 (northern bays), N e = 91 (southern bays)) compared with adjacent reefs (N e = 9494). These findings demonstrate that although the genetic diversity of A. kenti across the GBR remains high, isolated and potentially locally adapted populations such as those at Yunbenun may be at risk of genetic decline, undermining their adaptive potential and increasing their conservation concern.

items.title: Exports of technologically related environmental goods are associated with higher environmental performance in OECD countries
items.abstract: In this study, the impact of trade in technologically related environmental goods on environmental quality in OECD countries is examined for the period 2000–2023 using the MMQR method. To further address potential reverse causality concerns, the empirical analysis is complemented by the Dumitrescu–Hurlin panel Granger causality test. The study highlights how trade in these goods promotes the diffusion of environmentally friendly technologies, thereby supporting sustainable energy transitions and improvements in environmental performance. Empirical findings show that exports of technologically related environmental goods have a positive and significant impact across all quantiles, indicating that exports contribute consistently to technology diffusion. In contrast, the effect of imports becomes significant only in countries with relatively high environmental performance levels. The Dumitrescu–Hurlin test results further indicate a unidirectional predictive relationship running from both exports and imports of technologically related environmental goods to environmental performance, while no statistically significant feedback from environmental performance to trade variables is detected. The results further reveal that economic growth initially harms environmental quality, but as development progresses, its effect turns positive, confirming the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis. Renewable energy consumption provides limited short-term support for environmental performance, whereas urbanization generally exerts positive effects. Overall, the findings suggest that sustainable development policies should be tailored to country-specific structural characteristics. To maximize the benefits of trade in technologically related environmental goods, it is recommended that countries prioritize tax incentives encouraging the export of environmentally friendly products and invest in infrastructure that facilitates the effective domestic use of imported environmental technologies.

items.title: Microplastic contamination in commercially important marine fishes from the Sohar Coast, Sea of Oman: occurrence, characterization, and polymer composition
items.abstract: Microplastic (MP) pollution is an increasing concern in marine environments because of its persistence, bioavailability, and potential implications for marine ecosystem health and seafood safety. Despite growing global attention, information on MP contamination in commercially important marine fish from the Sea of Oman remains limited. This study assessed the occurrence, abundance, and characteristics of MPs in four commercially important fish species from the Sohar coast and tested whether MP contamination differed among species and tissues and was associated with habitat group, sex, and biometric characteristics. A total of 120 fish representing Epinephelus areolatus , Lethrinus microdon , Nematalosa arabica , and Rastrelliger kanagurta were examined for MPs in the gastrointestinal tract (GIT) and gills. Microplastics were extracted using alkaline digestion and visually identified under a stereomicroscope. All 316 recovered particles were subjected to ATR-FTIR spectroscopy; 313 (99.1%) met the ≥ 70% spectral-match criterion and were successfully assigned to polymer types. Microplastics were detected in 79.2% of the examined fish, with a mean total abundance of 2.63 ± 2.60 items individual⁻1. Frequency of occurrence ranged from 66.7% to 90.0% among species. Total MP abundance did not differ significantly among species, whereas GIT MP concentration differed significantly among species. GIT–gill differences were significant only in E. areolatus and R. kanagurta . No significant associations were detected between total MP abundance and habitat group, sex, total length, body weight, or condition factor. Fibers were the dominant particle type, most particles measured < 2 mm, and polyester was the predominant identified polymer, followed by polypropylene and ethylene-propylene diene polymer (EPDM). The predominance of fibers and polyester indicates that fibrous synthetic materials constitute an important component of MP exposure in these commercially important fishes. However, specific environmental sources cannot be determined from polymer identity alone, highlighting the need for integrated assessment of fish alongside seawater, sediments, and other potential environmental sources.

items.title: Constructing community economies: a pathway toward just agri-food transitions?
items.abstract: Exploring pathways toward just agri-food transitions has attracted increasing attention in political discourse and civic action. Community economies focus on alternative economic practices, reciprocity, and ethical commitments, aligning with the just transition goal of preventing new or intensified injustices in agri-food systems. This article develops a conceptual framework for analyzing the construction of community economies in agri-food systems and critically examines how economic alterity, performative interventions, and everyday practices can contribute to just transitions. Drawing on an in-depth case study of Mui Wo, an agricultural community in Hong Kong, this study investigates how a community economy model emerges, is constituted, and interacts with powerful actors and wider structural forces. The findings show that Mui Wo’s community economy has generated meaningful openings for a just agri-food transition, especially through recognition, community value chains, and capacity-building. However, government indifference to agriculture, structural constraints such as land ownership, insufficient support systems, and the absence of formal mechanisms for stakeholder participation in land-use decisions undermine the effectiveness of community economies in transforming agri-food systems. These findings highlight the need for transition interventions to re-examine policy frameworks and confront structural determinants, thereby empowering community economy pathways to advance just and sustainable transitions.

items.title: An asteroseismic age estimate for the Pleiades using a neural-network emulator of rotating δ Scuti pulsation models
items.abstract: Asteroseismology of δ Sct stars has strong potential for determining the ages of young stars through individual mode fitting. We present a neural-network emulator trained on approximately 46 million rotating pulsation models. From stellar mass, metallicity, age, and equatorial rotation velocity, it predicts 12 classical observables, two asteroseismic scalars, and the p mode, f mode and low-order g mode frequencies for degrees ℓ=0-3, including the individual m components of rotationally split multiplets. We couple the emulator to nested sampling through a multivariate likelihood that propagates correlated emulator residuals, making full Bayesian posterior exploration practical. Applied to five δ Sct stars in the Pleiades observed by TESS, the framework gives mutually consistent individual asteroseismic ages of 107-117 Myr. Combining their age posteriors gives a cluster age of 113.3±4.5 Myr (statistical), consistent with the 112±5 Myr lithium-depletion-boundary age and the 110-160 Myr range from rotating-isochrone fitting. Together with spectroscopic vsini, the inferred equatorial velocities also provide post-fit inclination estimates. Separate perturbed-grid tests using 100 matched synthetic pairs per input-physics variation give median absolute age shifts of 2.1, 2.3, and 5.2 Myr for |Δf_ov|=0.005, |Δα_MLT|=0.1, and |ΔY|=0.02, respectively; the corresponding 90th percentile shifts are 6.5, 7.6, and 16.2 Myr. These tests describe conditional population sensitivities, not a systematic uncertainty on the Pleiades age. Together, the cluster-age agreement and the scale of these input-physics sensitivities support δ Sct asteroseismology as a complementary age estimation method for young stars.

items.title: A chemically etched D-band waveguide orthomode transducer for CMB measurements
items.abstract: Abstract This study presents a prototype D-band waveguide orthomode transducer (OMT) fabricated using chemically etched brass platelets. This method offers a fast, cost-effective, and scalable approach for producing such devices above 100 GHz, making it well-suited for current and future Cosmic Microwave Background polarization experiments, where large focal planes with thousands of receivers are required to detect the faint primordial B -modes. Chemical etching has already demonstrated its effectiveness in manufacturing corrugated feedhorn arrays with state-of-the-art performance up to 150 GHz. Here, we evaluate its applicability to more complex structures, such as OMTs. We designed a single OMT prototype operating in the 130–170 GHz range, fabricated by chemically etching 0.15 mm-thick brass plates, which were then stacked, aligned, and mechanically clamped. Simulations based on metrological measurements of the OMT profile predict reflected power below −10 dB, cross-polarization better than −30 dB, and transmission around −0.5 dB in the 140−170 GHz band. Measurements yield transmisison around −1.5/−2 dB and cross-polarization $$<-$$ 20 dB. Further simulations show that the degradation in the transmission is related to defects and roughness along the etched profile ( $$\textrm{RMS}\simeq $$ 3 $$\mu $$ m), which is a typical and unavoidable effect of chemical etching. The discrepancy in cross-polarization, instead, could arise from a $$\sim $$ 1.5 $$^{\circ }$$ rotation of the polarization angle within the measurement chain. Our results show that chemical etching is a fast, low-cost, and scalable technique for producing waveguide OMTs with state-of-the-art performance in terms of reflected power and cross-polarization. However, at frequencies above 100 GHz our results show that the mechanical precision limitations of the chemical etching process degrade the transmission coefficient.

items.title: How Much Did the Moon-Forming Impact Change Earth's Core Fraction?
items.abstract: Earth's core, made mostly of iron, makes up about 32% of the planet's mass. In the giant-impact theory of the Moon's origin, a roughly Mars-sized planet, often called Theia, struck the young Earth and placed iron-poor rocky debris, mostly from the impactor, into orbit, where the Moon formed. The Moon has only a small iron core. What that impact did to the share of Earth's mass held in its own core depends on more than the impact itself, because two processes, each supported by published work, push in opposite directions. Collisions between bodies that already have iron cores can knock away rock more easily than iron, which raises the core's share. But models of Earth's core formation suggest that, as the planet grew, more of its iron combined with oxygen and stayed in the rocky mantle, which, this Commentary argues, lowers the core's share. Earth's iron-to-magnesium ratio is about 10% above the solar value, which has been interpreted as a net loss of about 10% of rock relative to metal over Earth's whole growth. A simple estimate suggests that the rock removed to form the Moon would raise Earth's core share by only a few percent of its value at most. Because the two processes oppose each other and other factors are unknown, the net change caused by the Moon-forming impact cannot yet be stated with confidence.

items.title: Contribution of Cosmic Alphas to Generation of Albedo Neutrons and Gammas in Lunar Regolith
items.abstract: The lunar surface is constantly and directly exposed to Galactic Cosmic Rays (GCRs) due to the lack of the atmosphere and the magnetic field around it. The high-energetic alpha particles subsequently contribute to the generation of the secondary neutrons through either the spallation reaction or the low-energetic (alpha, n) process along with the cosmic protons. In this study, the contribution of the alpha particles to the production of the albedo neutrons as well as the albedo gamma rays in the lunar regolith is studied by using the Monte Carlo simulations based on the GEANT4 toolkit. The incident alpha particles are referenced from the PAMELA spectrometer over the interval between 0.14 and 52 GeV and executed as a probability-based primary particle source. The present simulations demonstrate the production of the albedo neutrons and gamma rays upon the process of cosmic alpha irradiation in the lunar regolith. The albedo neutron production is predominantly situated within the near-surface region of the lunar regolith and progressively diminishes with the increasing depth. The population of the secondary neutrons is primarily distributed over the low-energy region and reduces towards the high energies. These results imply that the cosmic alpha particles have also quantifiable contribution in the generation of the secondary radiation at the lunar surface together with the cosmic protons, and this study demonstrates a computational framework in the evaluation of the lunar albedo, the radiation transport, the surface composition, and the radiation environment for the further lunar exploration missions.

items.title: Evidence-informed dynamic modelling and intervention prioritisation in diabetic bone marrow
items.abstract: Aims. Fragmented understanding of how diabetes disrupts interconnected bone marrow niches has hindered integrated strategies to restore function. Building on a previous static network, we developed a dynamic model to simulate intervention responses. Methods. The investigator and ChatGPT dialogued to extract evidence from a frozen corpus and develop the model. A Python implementation extended Boolean logic to three ordinal levels (0, 1 and 2) representing biological states and, where applicable, intervention strength. Under high metabolic stress, 15 interventions were assessed at three strengths and four with binary settings; 171 pairs were tested at maximal strength. A domain balanced score (0 to100) integrated favourable and adverse changes. Staged simulations assessed withdrawal; regulatory constraints on recovery after metabolic stress reduction were examined separately. Results. Endothelial reactive oxygen species (ROS) suppression achieved the highest score among 19 single interventions (24.2), improving three functional domains. Endothelial protein kinase B (Akt) augmentation scored 15.2 (two domains); oncostatin M (OSM) blockade and haematopoietic 66 kDa SHC transforming protein 1 (p66Shc) loss each scored 13.6 (two domains). ROS suppression combined with either OSM blockade or p66Shc loss scored 37.9, (five domains). No pair restored all functions under high stress. Benefits of ROS suppression, Akt augmentation and ROS and OSM blockade disappeared after withdrawal. Reducing metabolic stress led to variable scores (range 4.5 to 100), increasing mainly with restored endothelial function, followed by progenitor recovery and interruption of inflammatory and adipocyte stromal signalling. Conclusions. These simulations offer a rule based framework for investigating diabetic marrow recovery. Experimental studies must establish whether it can guide targeted therapy.

items.title: Longitudinal fMRI reveals multi-network reconfiguration and a recurrent frontoparietal shift across rest and task states during adult aging
items.abstract: Functional connectivity changes across adult aging, but most evidence is cross-sectional, and covariance-based connectivity depends on blood oxygenation level dependent (BOLD) fluctuation amplitude. Covariance decline can reflect changing fluctuation amplitude, and its interpretation may depend on whether normalization uses signal amplitude or includes estimated noise. It is also unclear which longitudinal changes recur across brain states. We analyzed 852 adults (baseline age 36-89 years) from the Aging Adult Brain Connectome with repeated functional MRI (fMRI) during rest, inhibitory control, associative memory, and visual-motor processing (2,220 sessions; median follow-up 5.5 years). Baseline age and elapsed follow-up were modeled separately. Ten cortical networks were tested jointly across states, and covariance was normalized either by released signal amplitude or by a candidate total amplitude reconstructed from released signal and noise amplitudes. Native common covariance declined by 7-11% per 5 years, while signal pair amplitude declined by 9% on average across states, significantly more than estimated noise pair amplitude. Under signal normalization, the relative balance among networks reconfigured over follow-up and differed across states, and the frontoparietal network shifted positively relative to the other nine networks in all four states, by 5-8% per 5 years. The estimated common trajectory was near zero under signal normalization but declined by 4-7% per 5 years under candidate total normalization. The network reconfiguration and the positive frontoparietal-relative direction persisted under both. Within-person coupling between the frontoparietal shift and fluid cognition was not detected. Adult aging thus combines normalization-dependent overall change with a state-dependent redistribution among networks that includes a recurrent frontoparietal shift.

items.title: Global stability of Michaelis-Menten networks
items.abstract: In a very nice paper, Blanchini, Breda, Giordano and Liessi studied networks of species coupled through Michaelis-Menten interactions. Under standard assumptions of strong connectedness and non-degeneracy, they show that there is a unique equilibrium, which is (locally) asymptotically stable. This note shows that global stability, which was stated there as an open problem, holds as well. In fact, whenever a positive equilibrium exists, it attracts every solution with positive initial condition, with no connectedness or non-degeneracy hypothesis at all; those assumptions are needed only in order to guarantee existence and to cover solutions starting on the boundary of the orthant. The key is to note that the system is contractive with respect to the Thompson part metric.

items.title: A general mechanism for collective foraging: percolating recruitment cascades coupled to a maximum-entropy
items.abstract: Foraging recruitment is a contagion: an agent finding a resource triggers a linear-threshold cascade -- the model for rumour and adoption spread on social networks -- embedded in space. Because activation is degree-normalized, the same rule that spreads the cascade also stifles it as neighbourhoods crowd (density-dependent blocking), so the swarm aggregates on a resource, then releases to explore again. The cascade runs on the communication network, but acting on it moves agents in physical space, and that motion rewires the network: network and physical space are one coupled system, and this feedback -- not tuning -- makes the coordination self-limiting. Because recruitment chains along the graph rather than near neighbours alone, whether a discovery stays local or spans the swarm is a matter of percolation, and past a critical connectivity the swarm holds itself in a cascade window -- locally near-critical though globally subcritical, a self-organized, sandpile-like drive-avalanche cycle. Nothing is tuned, yet behaviours foraging biology documents separately emerge together -- recruitment, marginal-value patch-leaving, and Levy search with a switch to local exploitation. These are not coincidences but one least-committal principle: the resource field and the search both follow from maximum entropy -- Levy search matched to the field's sparsity, recruitment to its clustering, so active-matter order and optimal foraging are one system in two domains. The gains are real but conditional: up to 7.6x the harvest of solitary search when resources are sparse and clustered, shrinking to nothing when search is already easy. Percolating cascades yield a large return on minimal communication. And that sparse, clustered field is the generic one -- resources almost inevitably aggregate, and maximum entropy makes it the least-committal one once they do -- so one untuned rule should recur widely.

items.title: Modeling the Coevolution of Human Skills and AI Adoption
items.abstract: The value of relying on generative AI depends on two quantities that evolve with its use: users' unaided skill, which may decline without practice, and the originality of AI-assisted work, which may decline as more people rely on similar tools. We model this process as a coevolutionary game in which individuals choose between autonomous and AI-assisted work, with autonomous practice strengthening their skills while reliance on AI gradually erodes them. When the reinforcing effect of skill erosion outweighs the crowding cost of lost originality, the population exhibits two alternative stable states: low AI adoption with high average skill, and high AI adoption with low average skill. Because skill is individual, autonomous workers remain more skilled than AI users, making autonomous work less vulnerable to population-wide skill decline. The strength of this effect is governed by a timescale ratio: the rate at which skills adapt relative to the rate at which individuals change strategy. The same ratio determines the full distribution of skills, which we derive analytically. Populations with identical AI adoption and average skill can differ sharply: when strategies change frequently, skills remain homogeneous and collective lock-in to high AI adoption is stronger; when strategies persist, lock-in weakens but the population can polarize into highly skilled autonomous workers and AI-dependent individuals. Modeling output overlap further shows that more diverse AI outputs can make widespread adoption harder to reverse. Together, these results expose tradeoffs between the benefits of widespread AI adoption and its long-run risks, making collective lock-in and skill polarization distinct intervention targets.

items.title: Strategic Origins of Network Structure
items.abstract: The structure and dynamics of complex networks are intimately linked. Despite immense progress in statistically characterizing these systems, a generalized mechanistic framework explaining why specific mesoscale structures emerge remains elusive. Here we introduce the game-graph equilibrium, the stable rest point of a payoff-driven partner-choice dynamic, analogous to a Nash equilibrium. This reveals network structure as the fossilized record of strategic interaction. We prove analytically that two-type games have exactly four network topologies, which are their exhaustive thermodynamic phases: assortative, disassortative, and two core-peripheries. This result generalizes to $K^K$ topological classes for $K$-type interactions. Furthermore, four distinct Nash equilibria produce core-periphery topologies, yet their payoffs reveal whether the underlying dynamic is cooperative or exploitative. To recover the generating dynamics from observed networks, we develop mechanistic inference by constraining a block model to lie on a low-dimensional, game-theoretic manifold. Applied to real-world networks, the model yields interpretable quantities, distinguishes states that look identical to conventional methods, predicts network topologies it has never seen without retraining, and controls its own complexity without hand-tuned penalties. Networks such as international trade are well described by the model despite the hard constraint, suggesting that real-world systems are organized by payoff-driven partner choice. Our framework resolves a foundational ambiguity by offering a precise, mechanistic definition of communities: strategic equivalence.

items.title: Mid-infrared Imaging of SR 12 c with JWST/MIRI: Grain Growth in an Evolved Circumplanetary Disk
items.abstract: The physical properties of circumplanetary disks offer insights into the formation of giant planets and their satellites. The circumbinary planetary-mass companion SR 12 c (1200 au from SR 12 AB) hosts an isolated dust disk directly detected with ALMA. We present JWST/MIRI imaging of SR 12 c from 5.6 to 21 $μ$m and analyze its spectral energy distribution from infrared to submillimeter wavelengths. Phenomenologically, the dust disk can be described by a two-component blackbody with large contrasts in characteristic temperatures and radii. Physically motivated models with varied geometries and heating mechanisms suggest a predominantly flat, irradiation-heated disk with a smaller contribution from viscous dissipation. The disk is inferred to be compact, with an inner radius of ~3 $R_{\rm Jup}$. The outer radius is only loosely constrained, with a characteristic value of ~3 au. The lack of strong 10 $μ$m excess emission suggests significant grain growth and dust settling. We also find that SR 12 c is broadly consistent with the empirical star-disk scaling relations, providing context for its possible formation pathway. These results demonstrate the power of combining mid-infrared and submillimeter observations with disk modeling to better understand the physical properties of circumplanetary disks.

items.title: Linear Approximations Provide Rigorous Conditions for Phase Locking in Oscillator Networks and Power Grids
items.abstract: Synchronization is a fundamental collective phenomenon in many natural and engineered networks. The stable operation of oscillator networks, such as electric power grids, requires phase locking with phase differences across edges below a given threshold. A central question is whether a given network supports such a state. In this contribution, we extend a convex optimization formulation of the nonlinear fixed point equations of the Kuramoto model, that also describe lossless power grids. Based on this formulation, we derive rigorous and tight bounds on the error introduced by an arbitrary approximation of the original model, in particular linear approximations. The bounds yield edge-wise regions of trust around the approximation, within which the true nonlinear solution must lie. They further provide sufficient and necessary conditions for phase locking under prescribed phase difference limits. Numerical experiments show that the bounds are tight over a broad range of parameters.
