items.title: Smart Piezoelectric Hybrid Ceramic Membrane With the Capacity of Pulsed Responsive Self-Cleaning and Anti-Fouling Functions.
items.abstract: Organic fouling remains a major challenge for ceramic membrane filtration because of the strong adsorption of organic foulants on membrane surfaces. Herein, a novel design strategy is proposed for smart piezoelectric hybrid ceramic membranes featuring self-powered nano-brushes. Specifically, a self-powered nano-brush smart piezoelectric hybrid ceramic membrane (ATPAA--PBM) with the pulsed pressure responsiveness and self-cleaning capability was prepared by grafting negatively charged sodium PAA polymer chain (PAA-) on the surface of BaTiO3 (BTO) piezoelectric ceramic membrane. Under the pulsed pressure, alternating piezoelectric charges induced reversible conformational oscillations of the self-powered nano-brushes, promoting the detachment of the foulant layer by the flowing water and thereby enabling in situ self-cleaning. Meanwhile, the grafted PAA- nano-brushes strongly associated with water molecules to establish a 462 nm-thick hydration layer, while generating electrostatic repulsion toward humic acid (HA), jointly preventing foulant adhesion and enabling nearly complete rejection. The membrane exhibited outstanding retention, anti-fouling ability, and remarkable flux retention ratio (FRR = 92.3%, 10 d) during a long-term filtration process. Consequently, a novel excellent rejection and anti-fouling mechanism of "self-powered nano-brush dynamic oscillation self-cleaning & hydration barrier" was proposed. This study provides a new perspective for the fabrication of self-cleaning smart piezoelectric hybrid ceramic membranes.

items.title: Molecular evidence of Bartonella spp. in wild felids from Brazil.
items.abstract: Among Felidae, domestic cats play a role as reservoirs for Bartonella henselae, Bartonella clarridgeiae, and Bartonella koehlerae. Despite the well-known relationship between Bartonella spp. and domestic cats, to date, there is still a paucity of reports on Bartonella spp. in wild felids. The aim of this study was to molecularly detect and characterize Bartonella spp. in blood and tissue samples from wild felids sampled in Brazil. Among 291 DNA samples (211 blood, 77 spleens and three livers), 3.09% (9/291) were positive in the Quantitative Real-Time PCR (qPCR) assay for Bartonella spp. based on the nuoG gene: 1/44 Leopardus pardalis, 3/61 Leopardus geoffroyi, 1/66 Panthera onca, 1/3 Herpailurus yagouaroundi, and 3/32 Leopardus wiedii. In the phylogenetic analyses, while the gltA sequence detected in L. wiedii grouped with Bartonella henselae, the gltA and ftsZ sequences detected in L. geoffroyi clustered within the same subclade as Bartonella sp. sequences previously identified in wild rodents and associated fleas. These findings reinforce that besides harboring Bartonella species associated with cats, wild felids also may act as accidental hosts for Bartonella species associated with wild small mammals, possibly as a consequence of predation.

items.title: Compatibility among Bacillus strains is linked to synthetic communities function, rhizosphere microbiome assembly and plant performance.
items.abstract: Microbial compatibility is an important consideration for synthetic communities (SynCom) function, but its ecological and physiological consequences for plant-microbe interactions remain insufficiently understood. We investigated compatible and incompatible Bacillus-based SynComs and their effects on tomato growth, rhizosphere microbiome assembly, and microbial network organization. Compatible co-cultures exhibited enhanced co-culture phenotypes, including merged colony morphology, enhanced biofilm formation, and altered growth dynamics, whereas incompatible combinations formed demarcation zones, indicative of antagonism. The compatible pair NMCN6+LNXM12 showed higher attached biomass and relative indole-3-acetic acid production compared with most incompatible or single-strain inoculations. Greenhouse experiments revealed that compatible SynComs significantly promoted tomato growth, increased plant height, root length, photosynthesis, and stomatal conductance, while incompatible combinations showed distinct soluble sugar responses rather than consistent evidence of plant stress. Amplicon sequencing revealed treatment-associated variation in rhizosphere bacterial community composition. Compatible SynComs were associated with enrichment of specific bacterial taxa and produced more interconnected and stable co-occurrence networks, whereas incompatible combinations showed distinct taxonomic profiles and comparatively fragmented microbial associations. Community composition differed significantly among individual treatments but not among broader compatibility categories with unequal within-group dispersion. Collectively, the observed co-culture, plant, and microbiome responses highlight differences among the selected Bacillus combinations that cannot be attributed to compatibility alone. These findings may provide the selection of Bacillus strain combinations for further evaluation as plant inoculants.

items.title: Cell wall polymer interactions, rather than polysaccharide fine structure, underlie recalcitrance in energy cane varieties.
items.abstract: Second-generation bioethanol production from lignocellulosic biomass has driven the development of high-fiber sugarcane varieties known as energy canes, which combine high tillering, high biomass accumulation, lower sucrose, and improved agronomic performance. However, energy canes have been reported to be more recalcitrant to enzymatic saccharification. We compared biomass and cell wall composition, non-cellulosic polysaccharide extractability, and saccharification efficiency in two energy cane varieties, Vertix V2 and Vertix V3, and sugarcane. Sugarcane contained three times as much sucrose and less fiber than energy canes. After removing soluble sugars from the biomass, reduced digestibility became evident in the two energy cane varieties, particularly in V2. Saccharification increased with alkali and doubled after acidic sodium chlorite treatments. Although the main polysaccharides and linkage structures were broadly conserved across genotypes, minor changes were observed in their relative abundance and extractability. Glucuronoarabinoxylans (GAX) were the predominant wall polysaccharides (72%), while pectins [homogalacturonan (HG) and rhamnogalacturonan I (RG-I), each 1%], arabinan side-groups (4-6%), glucomannans (1%), and xyloglucan (2-4%) occurred in smaller proportions. Sugarcane contained higher abundances of xyloglucan, β-glucan, glucomannan, and arabinan, whereas energy canes had higher HG and RG-I. Chlorite oxidation solubilized GAX and RG-I, indicating that polymers are associated with phenylpropanoids and contribute to wall recalcitrance. The contrasting saccharification behavior of the sugarcane and energy cane varieties examined here appears to arise not from major changes in polysaccharide fine structure, but from differences in biomass allocation, phenylpropanoid abundance, extractability, and molecular interactions among cellulose, matrix polysaccharides, and phenylpropanoids within the cell wall. Understanding these properties in relation to enzyme-mediated disassembly is fundamental to accessing grass walls and improving biomass saccharification.

items.title: Decentring artistic practice beyond national narratives. An analysis of the European pavilion as a post-national model
items.abstract: Background: The national pavilion model, epitomised by the Venice Biennale, functions as an internal cultural border that aligns artistic production with state sovereignty and Eurocentric universality. This representational framework fails to accommodate contemporary, mobile, and post-national artistic practices. To explore an alternative paradigm, this article evaluates Liquid Becomings, a 2024 waterborne project commissioned by the European Cultural Foundation. Navigating four major European rivers—the Danube, Rhine, Vistula, and Tagus—this itinerant civic laboratory sought to test how a post-national community might be lived through fluid, non-extractive practices. Methods This study employs a qualitative, interdisciplinary methodology bridging contemporary curatorial critique with decolonial theory and political geography. Utilizing the framework of the institutional archive versus the embodied repertoire, the empirical analysis juxtaposes official curatorial materials, manifestoes, and video documentation from the four river routes against ex-post reflective accounts of the project’s final transition to a land-bound festival in Lisbon. Results The river residencies successfully disrupted state-centric visual regimes by shifting the locus of enunciation onto mobile platforms. The routes reconceptualized European borders through decolonial delinking, relational opacity, hydrofeminist ecology, and human-powered navigation. However, translating these slow, somatic, and non-representational practices into an urban festival in Lisbon generated significant structural friction, revealing a fundamental disconnect between the transient embodied repertoire of the river journeys and the spectacle-driven expectations of land-based cultural institutions. Conclusions The study concludes that the material absence, insularity, and spatial diffusion observed at the Lisbon festival do not represent operational failures. Synthesising participatory aesthetics, the distribution of the sensible, and agonistic pluralism, the article demonstrates that these frictions constitute a radical aesthetic of withdrawal that evades institutional capture and resists state-sanctioned narratives of European identity.

items.title: Contextual Stress Exposure and Longitudinal Change in Mental Health and Sleep Among US Latino/a Adolescents.
items.abstract: This research examines how contextual stress exposure within the immigration environment predicts sleep problems and internalizing symptoms for Latino/a adolescents. Participants included N = 547 adolescents listed as "Hispanic" on 2017-18 middle school enrollment lists in a suburban Atlanta, GA, school district. Using three time (T) points of survey data (2021-23), structural equation models tested paths from immigration-related stressors to changes in sleep problems and internalizing symptoms. Missing data were addressed using multiply imputed datasets and full information maximum likelihood. At T1, the 244 (44.6%) male and 303 (55.4%) female participants had a mean (SD) age of 16.2 (.91) years. Across time, 28.8%-40.3% of youth reported <7 hours of sleep on average. The prevalence of clinical internalizing symptoms ranged from 31.1% to 35.9% for female participants and from 29.9% to 44.3% for male participants. T1 immigration-related stressors predicted T1 to T2 increases in sleep problems (ß = .12 [95% CI = .03-.20]) and internalizing symptoms (ß = .09 [95% CI = .01-.17]). T2 sleep problems mediated associations between T1 immigration-related stressors and T2 to T3 increases in internalizing symptoms (indirect effect: ß = .01 [95% CI = .00-.03]) and sleep problems (indirect effect: ß = .07 [95% CI = .02-.12]). Sleep problems and internalizing symptoms were reciprocally associated from T1 to T2 (sleep to internalizing: ß = .11 [95% CI = .02-.20]; internalizing to sleep: ß = .14 [95% CI = .04-.25]) and from T2 to T3 (sleep to internalizing: ß = .11 [95% CI = .03-.20]; internalizing to sleep: ß = .10 [95% CI = .00-.20]). For Latino/a adolescents, immigration-related stressors may harm mental health through increased sleep problems.

items.title: Moral distress and moral injury among nurses in German acute inpatient care - a cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Moral suffering in health care is increasingly a focus of research. The extent of and relationship between two distinct forms of moral suffering, namely, moral injury (MI) and moral distress (MD), has not yet been studied in nurses in acute inpatient care in Germany. This study aims to examine the severity of MI and MD in the context of organizational support, the correlation between the two constructs, and the variables associated with the extent of MD and MI. We conducted a cross-sectional study including 1323 nurses employed in German hospitals. The data were collected in March and April 2023 in an online survey using the German version of the Moral Distress Scale (MDS), the German Moral Injury Symptom Scale for Health Professionals (G-MISS-HP), the Perceived Organizational Support Scale (POS-s) and an additional questionnaire on the individual perception of ethical and structural conditions in the institution. The data were analyzed descriptively. Partial credit Rasch models were fitted to the item-level responses of the G-MISS-HP and the MDS to obtain interval-level measures of moral injury and moral distress for subsequent analyses. Median regressions with backward variable selection were performed for MD- and MI-Rasch scores to identify variables associated with the level of moral distress/injury. The associations between the MD and MI-Rasch scores were tested using Spearman's correlation test. A total of 68.6% (n = 907; 95% CI: 66.1%-71.1%) of the respondents scored above the validated G-MISS-HP screening threshold (≥ 29), which has previously been associated with impairment in family, social, and occupational functioning. Spearman's correlation analysis revealed statistically significant positive associations between the MD-Rasch score and the MI-Rasch subscores (guilt/shame subscore: r = 0.57, 95% CI [0.53; 0.61]; spiritual troubles subscore: r = 0.22, 95% CI [0.16; 0.27]; condemnation subscore: r = 0.39, 95% CI [0.34; 0.43], all p < 0.001). Median regression analyses revealed significant associations of both MD and MI with perceived organizational support (POS-s), satisfaction with the treatment team's consideration of own perspective, responsibility for staff, and participation in interprofessional case discussions. Manifestations of moral suffering are common. Our findings highlight the importance of measures to promote an ethical climate and to address the negative consequences of moral suffering, particularly at the management level. German Clinical Trials Register ( https://www.drks.de/ ): DRKS00030785 (date: 06 February 2023).

items.title: Ketamine administration reduced conditioned defensive behaviour and upregulated protein expression associated with neuroplasticity in a planarian model of aversive memory reactivation.
items.abstract: Traumatic memories that are resistant to modification or extinction are a characteristic feature of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). The process of fear memory reconsolidation has been identified as a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of PTSD. Ketamine, an NMDA receptor antagonist with dissociative properties, has been identified as a drug with high therapeutic potential for this target, as it destabilises traumatic memory while enabling rapid modification and update of the memory to no longer be threatening. However, its exact mechanisms of action on reducing the impact of aversive memory remains poorly understood. To better understand these mechanisms, a conditioned aversive memory reactivation model using ketamine was carried out in brown planaria (Girardia dorotocephala), an invertebrate model that shows a high degree of conservation in neural anatomy, receptors, neurotransmitters, and learning behaviours, while being comparatively simpler than standard mammalian models. In this study, 15 planaria were randomly assigned to three treatment groups (10 μM ketamine, 1 μM ketamine, vehicle control) and underwent a classical aversive memory reactivation paradigm. Whole planaria were processed for an exploratory proteomic analysis to analyse changes in protein expression associated with the effects of ketamine on the aversive memory reactivation process. Behavioural data showed a significant reduction in defensive behaviours, including scrunching movements F(2,12) = 11.85, p = 0.0014, ƞ2 = 0.66, C-shape movements F(2,12) = 6.59, p = 0.012, ƞ2 = 0.52, and head turns F(2,12) = 9.59, p = 0.0032, ƞ2 = 0.61, in the 10 μM ketamine group on the final test day compared to vehicle controls. Proteomic analysis showed that these behavioural changes were accompanied by a high degree of enrichment in molecular pathways associated with rapid neuronal growth and synaptic plasticity, and changes in cellular mRNA, all markers of learning. These preliminary findings in an invertebrate model improve understanding of how ketamine may facilitate disruption of conditioned aversive memory via rapid neuronal restructuring and augmenting synaptic plasticity.

items.title: Pain in the media: A content analysis of pain-related events in 'Made for Kids' YouTube videos.
items.abstract: During childhood, children are presented with ample opportunities to learn about pain, including through their own experiences and interactions with others. Another possible source of influence is the media they consume. Portrayals of pain in children's television, movies and picture books have previously been examined; however, less is known about other mediums, like YouTube, that reach millions of children. This study aimed to investigate how pain-related events are portrayed in popular children's YouTube videos. Videos from 15 popular 'Made for Kids' YouTube channels (30 videos/channel) were screened for pain-related events. Channels were selected based on popularity (highest subscribers and views). Videos that included pain-related events were analysed using codes adapted from previous studies of pain in children's media. Pain-related events were commonly represented and present in 174 videos, with impact portrayals (i.e., where pain and or injury would be expected in real life, but no evidence of either was present) being the most frequent, followed by minor pain/injury. Boy characters experienced pain-related events more frequently than girl characters, but girls demonstrated more prosocial behaviours in response to sufferers than boys. Characters/presenters with racialized identities were underrepresented in pain-related events, yet racial stereotypes of violence were present. Findings of this study align with previous work investigating portrayals of pain in children's popular television, movies and picture books; demonstrating that sociocultural messaging about pain is consistent across different types of children's media. Future research should consider children's perspectives on pain-related events in popular children's media. PERSPECTIVE: This article describes the frequency and characteristics of pain-related events in popular 'Made for Kids' YouTube videos. Understanding the characteristics of this content is an essential step in understanding how pain may be socialised to children in their everyday media engagement.

items.title: A tablet-based cognitive and physical training intervention to improve postural control for older adults with subjective cognitive decline - a feasibility study.
items.abstract: Previous research suggests that adding cognitive training to balance training may improve fall-prevention interventions. This study examined the feasibility and potential effects of a tablet-based intervention comprising balance and strength training alone or combined with cognitive training. Twenty older adults with subjective cognitive decline who were able to stand and walk unassisted were recruited via social media and senior organizations; 18 completed the study. Participants were allocated to an eight-week tablet-based intervention comprising balance and strength training (BT) or balance and strength training plus cognitive functions (BT + CT). Feasibility outcomes were recruitment, adherence, adverse events, participant experiences and perceived effects. Potential effects on fall-related concerns, cognitive function and postural control were analyzed descriptively. Recruitment met the prespecifies succession criterion. In the BT group, median adherence to balance training and the walking protocol was 75% and 100%, respectively. In the BT + CT group, median adherence was 83% for cognitive training, 54% for balance and strength training, and 170,5% for walking. The interventions were generally well perceived, although the balance training was considered too easy. Descriptive findings indicated that dual-task costs for gait parameters tended to increase in the BT group but decrease in the BT + CT group. Tablet-based interventions targeting cognition and postural control were feasible in several respects among older adults with subjective cognitive decline. Digital tools should be flexible enough to accommodate individual needs, interactive to promote motivation and sufficiently challenging to elicit positive adaptations. Measures of gait variability may be sensitive to subtle changes in postural control.

items.title: Identifying the behavioural determinants of trialists for the design and delivery of greener trials - A cross-sectional survey study.
items.abstract: To understand the behavioural determinants of people working in clinical trials ('trialists') to support greener trials which, in this survey, refer to those being designed and delivered without unnecessary, disproportionate, or unexamined carbon emissions. AND SETTING: We conducted an online cross-sectional survey of trialists involved in the design, conduct, analysis, or reporting of clinical trials. Recruitment targeted established trial networks in the UK and Ireland supplemented by social media and snowball sampling. Data collected included demographics, attitudes to climate change risk (ACCRs), perceived capability, opportunity and motivation in relation to design and delivery of greener trials through application of the 'Capabilities, Opportunities, Motivations - Behaviour' (COM-B) model, and self-reported behavioural specification for greener trials. We received 88 responses mainly from the UK and Ireland. Respondents, on average, were concerned about climate change. Most respondents considered the carbon impact of their professional activities at least sometimes. Most respondents reported high levels of psychological capability and reflective motivation, but less agreement on social opportunity, physical opportunity, and automatic motivation when considering the design and delivery of greener trials. Several key actors (e.g., trial staff, funders) and actions (e.g., institutional incentives, green technologies) were proposed by respondents as important targets for change. This study investigated trialists' perspectives on the design and delivery of greener trials through a behavioural lens. Our findings highlight key behavioural determinants that could be targets for future intervention development. In addition, our results demonstrate the range of actors and actions that are important in the clinical trial ecosystem to ensure greener trials become routine. Behavioural models offer valuable insights for guiding the development of relevant strategies for change.

items.title: Decreased function of fatty acid desaturase 1 is associated with placental foetal vascular malperfusion and highlights the key role of the maternal-foetal interface.
items.abstract: Placental foetal vascular malperfusion (PFVM) is a chronic disorder characterised by impaired blood flow and abnormal vascular development, inducing adverse neonatal outcomes. Long chain polyunsaturated fatty acids (LC-PUFAs) play a crucial role in placenta health. We aimed to explore the role of genetic variation in LC-PUFA metabolism in PFVM risk as well as underlying mechanisms. Associations were examined between two functional polymorphisms (rs174538 and rs174556) of the fatty acid desaturase 1 (FADS1) gene encoding the rate-limiting enzyme for LC-PUFA metabolism and PFVM among pregnant women (n = 646). Placental transcriptomes were correlated with PFVM and FADS1 genotypes. Various assays were performed in human umbilical vein endothelial cells and trophoblasts with FADS1 inhibitor and LC-PUFA interventions to characterise their function changes. Low-function alleles of both polymorphisms were significantly associated with increased PFVM risk and decreased placental FADS1 transcription level. In placenta tissue, lower FADS1 expression is also associated with PFVM. PFVM-associated genes are enriched to pathways related to immune responses, apoptosis, and angiogenesis, which overlap with the genes and pathways associated with the risk alleles and demonstrate a cell-type enrichment to endothelial cells. In vitro, FADS1 inhibition impairs multiple functions of and interactions between endothelial and trophoblast cells. These impairments are reversed by LC-PUFA supplementation. These findings highlight the impact of maternal LC-PUFA homoeostasis in placenta health and suggest that maternal FADS1 variants can potentially be an early diagnostic marker for PFVM. Our data supports PUFA metabolism as a precision therapeutic or preventive target to reduce placental dysfunction risk. NIH, Wayne State University and Michigan State University.

items.title: Building creative momentum: Social and psychological factors associated with flow in Chinese artists.
items.abstract: Flow is a deeply immersive psychological state characterized by intense concentration, intrinsic motivation, and a perceived balance between challenge and skill. Although prior research has examined flow in contexts such as sports, education, and workplace performance, limited attention has been paid to how social, cognitive, and motivational factors are associated with flow experiences among practicing artists. This study examined the relationships among perceived social support, the positive mindset dimension, creative process, expected self/life, and flow among practicing artists in China. Drawing on a sample of 962 artists, the study employed Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to assess theoretically informed associations among social support from friends, family, and significant others, internal psychological factors, and flow experiences. The findings showed that creative process and expected self/life were positively associated with flow-related experiences, whereas the positive mindset dimension was not directly associated with flow. Social support was also associated with internal psychological factors relevant to creative engagement. Mediation analyses indicated that creative process and expected self/life were significant indirect pathways linking the positive mindset dimension and flow. The model demonstrated satisfactory explanatory and predictive relevance, supporting the integration of social and psychological correlates in understanding flow among artistic populations. These findings highlight the relevance of supportive social environments and internal psychological resources in relation to creative engagement and flow, while acknowledging that the cross-sectional and self-report design does not permit causal or temporal conclusions.

items.title: Is it really about historical interest? Configurational pathways to museum "check-in" intention among Chinese young adults.
items.abstract: As digital media become embedded in everyday life, museum "check-in" has become an increasingly visible form of cultural participation among Chinese young adults. This practice foregrounds social self-presentation, raising questions about whether engagement with historical and cultural contexts coexists with visually oriented and potentially superficial consumption. Guided by the theory of planned behavior, this study examined the configurations associated with museum "check-in" intention among Chinese young adults. Grounded theory-informed coding and constant comparison were first used to identify empirical categories, followed by fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA). The analysis identified four configurational pathways: multiconditional synergy, convenience-enabled, contextual convergence, and positive appraisal. High intention did not depend uniformly on stable historical and cultural identification. Instead, several pathways involved different combinations of platform-mediated visibility, peer-based normative pressure, and low practical barriers. Psychological judgments were therefore closely intertwined with external contexts, while the pathway centered on cultural interest and experiential appraisal showed relatively limited empirical coverage. These findings provide a configurational account of digitally mediated cultural participation and clarify how evaluative, normative, informational, and practical conditions jointly shape museum "check-in" intention. More broadly, they suggest that youth museum participation cannot be reduced either to renewed cultural identification or to media-driven conformity.

items.title: Polygenic risk for schizophrenia predicting age-specific fluctuations in depressive symptoms: Findings from the Young Finns Study.
items.abstract: A well-established connection exists between psychoses and depression, with one presentation being depressive symptoms before psychosis. However, the predictive power of preceding affective symptoms is reported to be low, raising the question whether depressive symptoms could reflect intermediary phenotypes associated with high polygenic risk for schizophrenia (PRSscz). We examined whether PRSscz is associated with depressive symptoms from adolescence to middle age in those who did not develop a non-affective psychosis. We used the population-based Young Finns Study (n = 2291). Depressive symptoms were measured with the Beck Depression Inventory-II and its modified version (suitable for non-clinical symptoms) between ages 15 and 56. Covariates included age, sex, childhood family environment, and adulthood education and income. The Care Register for Health Care was used to exclude participants with non-affective psychoses until middle age. High PRSscz was associated with higher performance difficulties from adolescence to early adulthood and higher depressive cognitions when approaching middle age. These associations were sustained in the fully adjusted models. PRSscz did not show consistent associations with the total amount of depressive symptoms or somatic/affective symptoms. First, PRSscz appears to explain age-specific fluctuations in depressive symptoms. Second, PRSscz may not predict the full symptom profile of major depression (i.e., it was not associated with affective/somatic symptoms). Third, high PRSscz explains depressive symptoms during periods typical for prodromal syndromes, even among those who do not develop psychosis. Thus, depressive symptoms in adolescence may represent intermediary phenotypes or transdiagnostic susceptibilities related to high PRSscz.

items.title: "I'm much more ok with my body just being mine and treating it well": women's experiences of empowerment after completing a holistic health programme.
items.abstract: Women are often disempowered by dominant discourses that narrowly define health in terms of weight, exercise, and diet. This study explored women's experiences of empowerment after completing Next Level Health (NLH), a holistic health programme that supported women to make small, achievable behaviour change across health domains including physical activity, sleep, nutrition, eating behaviour, self-care, and stress management. Fifty-six women living in New Zealand completed evaluation forms that asked about their experiences of NLH and any outcomes they experienced at programme-end (6 months) and follow-up (12 months). Four themes were identified through reflexive thematic analysis. Women were empowered through (1) embedded health routines, (2) adopting a holistic perspective, (3) health literacy in daily life, and (4) reframing success. Collectively, these themes reveal the expansive and personal ways empowerment was realised and the context sensitivity it required. These findings highlight how women gained greater agency over their health by shifting away from rigid norms towards context-sensitive and self-directed health practices. There is compelling evidence that future health interventions should embed holistic, women-centred approaches, with reflexive practice playing a key role in women's empowerment.

items.title: Pulpotomy of deciduous molars with deep caries using three different hydraulic calcium silicate cements: a short-term pilot randomized controlled split-mouth study.
items.abstract: This randomized, controlled split-mouth study evaluated the short-term clinical survival of three hydraulic calcium silicate cements for pulp capping after pulpotomy in primary molars under general anesthesia. Thirty-three children aged 2 to 6 years, each with three carious primary molars (ICDAS 4-6), were recruited for treatment under general anesthesia. Following pulpotomy, the pulp was randomly covered with one of the materials: ProRoot MTA (Dentsply Sirona), Biodentine (Septodont), or TotalFill BC RRM Putty (FKG). The teeth were restored with steel crowns. Clinical survival rate at 5 and 10 months, application time, treatment costs and oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL) were evaluated using the ECOHIS-G questionnaire. Data analysis was performed using non-parametric methods (α = 0.05). All 84 treated teeth remained in situ for up to 10 months without clinical symptoms. TotalFill BC RRM Putty had the significantly shortest application time (median 75.5 s; p ≤ 0.001) compared to Biodentine (259 s) and ProRoot MTA (200.5 s). Biodentine resulted in the significantly lowest treatment cost (median €42.45; p ≤ 0.001), ProRoot MTA in the highest (€74.37; TotalFill BC RRM Putty: €60.01). The treatments generally led to improved OHRQoL (Median ECOHIS-G score: initial 5, after 5 months 4, after 10 months 2.5). All investigated hydraulic calcium silicate cements showed no differences in short-term clinical outcomes after pulpotomy in primary molars. Material selection may therefore be guided by practical factors such as handling time and treatment costs, while long-term outcomes, which require further investigations, should be considered. items.title: The Power of Stereotypes: A Thematic Analysis of How Social Attitudes and Beliefs Shape Perceived Stalking Threat.
items.abstract: Stalking is a behavior that negatively impacts individuals of all gender identities, and yet public threat perceptions often revolve around cisheteronormative relationship stereotypes. The present qualitative study aimed to explore how observers construct threat perceptions associated with stalking, focusing on perpetrator and victim gender (man, woman, nonbinary) and relationship type (stranger, ex-intimate). Undergraduate psychology students (N = 243) completed an online vignette survey, answering four exploratory open-ended questions that detail concerns related to the perpetrator's and victim's behavior and their relationship. Reflexive thematic analysis generated four themes: Perceptions of Escalation and Dangerous Behavior; Normalization, Minimization, and Justification of Stalking Behavior; Relational Dynamics and Misconceptions of Consent; and Victim Blame and Protection Strategies. Findings suggest that gendered stereotypes and victim-blaming narratives persist among young adults. Greater public awareness of the prevalence, nature, diversity, and harms associated with stalking may lead to better protection for gender diverse victims and ensure their experiences are recognized and sincerely appreciated in social, clinical, and legal contexts.

items.title: The role of spiritual well-being in the association between perceived social support and psychological resilience in women with gynecologic cancer.
items.abstract: Women with gynecologic cancer may rely on both interpersonal and internal resources to adapt to illness. This study examined whether spiritual well-being may be involved in the association between perceived social support and psychological resilience. In this cross-sectional study, 161 women with gynecologic cancer in Ankara, Türkiye, completed measures of spiritual well-being, perceived social support, and psychological resilience. Psychological resilience was positively associated with both perceived social support and spiritual well-being, and the mediation analysis produced a pattern consistent with partial mediation. These findings suggest that spiritual well-being may represent one possible pathway within the association between perceived social support and resilience in women with gynecologic cancer. The findings are consistent with Reed's Self-Transcendence Theory by suggesting that spiritual well-being may be one self-transcendent resource associated with both perceived social support and psychological resilience.

items.title: Efficacy of measurement-based care (MBC) in routine child and youth behavioral therapy: A pragmatic randomized controlled trial.
items.abstract: Objective : This pragmatic randomized trial evaluated a low-frequency measurement-based care (MBC) approach in children and youth. Method: In the modified intention-to-treat sample (mITT), 317 children (6-10) and youth (11-17) were randomized to behavioral therapy with or without MBC; 169 completed the trial per protocol (PP). Outcomes were assessed by masked raters, therapists, caregivers, and youth. Results: Average MBC participation ranged from 69% to 87% across informants, while therapists discussed the report at least once in only 29.3% of cases. In the mITT analysis, masked ratings of total symptoms (SFSS-I) showed no effect, d = 0.00, 95% CI [-0.22, 0.22], while caregiver-rated externalizing symptoms (FBB-SCREEN) showed a small reduction, d = -0.17, [-0.33, -0.01]. In the PP analysis, masked ratings (SFSS-I) remained nonsignificant, d = -0.29, [-0.59, 0.01], but caregiver ratings showed significant reductions in externalizing (FBB-SCREEN), d = -0.29, [-0.53, -0.05], and internalizing symptoms (CBCL), d = -0.32, [-0.61, -0.03]. Conclusions: Low-frequency MBC may offer practical advantages for child and youth therapy, such as good participation, but its efficacy remained insufficient, likely reflecting implementation challenges. Differences between caregiver and masked outcomes may indicate a risk of overestimating treatment effects when assessments are unblinded. Trial registration: German Clinical Trials Register identifier: DRKS00016737.

items.title: Associations of Depressive Symptoms With Quit Motivation and Quit Efficacy Among Korean Adults: Findings From the 2023 ITC Korea Survey.
items.abstract: We examined the relationship between depressive symptoms and 2 key predictors of smoking cessation-quit motivation and quit efficacy-among 1608 South Korean adults (aged ≥19) who smoked cigarettes regularly (≥weekly) and participated in the 2023 International Tobacco Control (ITC) Korea Survey. Overall, 19.0% reported depressive symptoms, which were significantly associated with sociodemographic factors, nicotine dependence, alcohol use, quit motivation, and quit efficacy. Those with depressive symptoms showed greater quit motivation (89.7% vs 81.4%, P = .004) and quit efficacy (41.1% vs 29.9%, P = .002) than those without symptoms. In adjusted logistic regression models, depressive symptoms remained significantly associated with quit motivation (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 1.89; 95% CI, 1.13-3.17) and quit efficacy (aOR = 1.42; 95% CI, 1.01-2.01). Although Koreans who smoke with depressive symptoms had greater motivation to quit and had higher quit efficacy, they were not more likely to have attempted to quit.

items.title: Reward sensitivity is negatively associated with future self-continuity: the mediation role of functional connectivity between the dorsomedial prefrontal cortex and ventrolateral prefrontal cortex.
items.abstract: Reward Sensitivity refers to individual differences in the perception, evaluation, and emotional response to potential or acquired rewarding stimuli. Future self-continuity refers to the degree of psychological connection, identification, and consistency that individuals perceive between their present self and future self. Although both constructs are known to critically influence intertemporal decision-making and self-control, the shared neurobiological mechanisms linking them remain largely unexplored. To address this question, we used voxel-based morphometry and resting-state functional connectivity analyses to investigate the neural basis underlying the association between reward sensitivity and future self-continuity. Behavioral results showed reward sensitivity exhibited a significant negative correlation with future self-continuity. Moreover, voxel-based morphometry (VBM) revealed that reward sensitivity was negatively associated with gray matter volume in the dorsomedial prefrontal cortex (dmPFC). Furthermore, resting-state functional connectivity (RSFC) analysis demonstrated that the functional connectivity between the dmPFC and the ventrolateral prefrontal cortex (vlPFC) was positively correlated with reward sensitivity. Ultimately, mediation analysis revealed a positive indirect effect, indicating that this dmPFC-vlPFC connectivity acted as a protective neural factor in the negative relationship between reward sensitivity and future self-continuity. In conclusion, the current research offered novel insights into the impact of reward sensitivity on future self-continuity, advancing our understanding of this behavioral connection from a neurobiological perspective.

items.title: Multilingual Brain Decoding Reveals Shared Cortical Semantic Geometry
items.abstract: Human languages differ markedly in lexical and syntactic form yet can convey similar semantic content. The neural basis of this cross-language semantic commonality remains unclear. Here we developed a multilingual brain decoding framework and analysed brain recordings from 227 participants spanning Chinese, English and French. We found that cortical semantic representations exhibited consistent semantic geometry relationships across languages and individuals, revealing a shared cortical semantic geometry. Importantly, the cross-language consistency of cortical semantic geometry increased from sensorimotor to higher-order association cortex, forming a shared semantic geometry gradient closely aligned with the principal cortical functional gradient. Our work establishes generalizable multilingual brain decoding and identifies stable cortical semantic geometry as a neural basis for semantic commonality across languages.

items.title: A mechanism for collective foraging: percolating recruitment cascades coupled to a maximum-entropy
items.abstract: Foraging recruitment is a contagion: an agent that finds a resource triggers a linear-threshold cascade, the model built for rumour and adoption spread on social networks, now embedded in space. Because activation is degree-normalized, the same rule that spreads the cascade also stifles it as neighbourhoods crowd, so the swarm aggregates on a resource and then releases to explore again. The cascade runs on the communication network, but acting on it moves agents in physical space, and that motion rewires the network: network and space are one coupled system, and this feedback, not any tuning, makes the coordination self-limiting. Because recruitment chains along the graph rather than reaching near neighbours alone, whether a discovery stays local or spans the swarm is a question of percolation. The swarm holds itself in a cascade window that is locally near-critical though globally subcritical, a self-organized, self-limiting drive-release cycle, sandpile-like but non-conservative. Nothing is tuned, yet behaviours that foraging biology documents separately emerge together: recruitment to discoveries, marginal-value patch-leaving, and Levy search with a switch to local exploitation. These follow from one least-committal principle, the resource field and the search both as maximum entropy, with Levy search matched to the field's sparsity and recruitment to its clustering, so active-matter order and optimal foraging appear as one system seen in two domains. The gains are real but conditional: up to 7.6x the harvest of solitary search when resources are sparse and clustered, shrinking to nothing when search is already easy. That sparse, clustered field is also the generic one, because resources almost inevitably aggregate, so one untuned rule should recur widely.

items.title: Quantum metrology of spin sensing with free space electrons
items.abstract: Abstract Recent advances in transmission electron microscopy (TEM) have opened the path toward spin resonance spectroscopy with single-spin sensitivity. To assess this potential, we investigate the quantum precision limits for sensing magnetic moments with free-electron probes. Using a scattering model where an electron wavepacket interacts with a localized spin, we study two metrological tasks: estimating the magnitude of the magnetic moment and discriminating the presence of a spin. The sensitivity for a given measurement setting is generally determined by the classical Fisher information, which we benchmark against the quantum bound optimized over all measurements. We find that conventional TEM imaging can saturate the quantum bound when backaction of the probe electron onto the spin state is negligible. We also find that, when backaction is relevant, one could do better by realizing a measurement of the electron's orbital angular momentum state. These results establish the quantum limits of spin sensing in TEM and guide the development of future experiments probing individual electron spins or nanoscale ensembles of nuclear spins.

items.title: General orbital perturbation theory in Schwarzschild space-time
items.abstract: Abstract We derive general relativistic Gaussian equations for osculating elements for orbits under the influence of a perturbing force without any restrictions in an underlying Schwarzschild space-time. Such a formulation provides a way to describe the evolution of orbital parameters in strong gravity relativistic settings. As examples of external forces we considered Kerr and q-metric space-times generated forces, for which we solve equations for osculating elements in linear approximation. For the Kerr space-time in the post-Newtonian limit, our result reproduces the well-known Lense-Thirring precession of the longitude of the ascending node.

items.title: Exploring gas thermodynamics around galaxies from the Sunyaev-Zel’dovich effects: Impact of galaxy-halo connection, 2D projection, and velocity field
items.abstract: A complete picture of the gas thermodynamics around galaxies is imprinted on the cosmic microwave background (CMB). Indeed, the thermal, kinematic, and relativistic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effects (tSZ, kSZ, rSZ) measure the gas density, temperature, pressure of baryonic feedback and bulk velocity around galaxies, along with the gravitational potential it sits in. This full thermodynamic picture promises to constrain galaxy formation models and gas related uncertainties in the impact on galaxy lensing. Recent kSZ measurements around galaxies suggest that the gas may be more extended than anticipated, pointing to powerful feedback processes and large baryonic corrections to lensing. How robust are these conclusions about the galaxy-halo connection, including satellite fraction and high-mass outliers, or to 2D projection effects and large-scale velocity modes? In this paper, we give estimates for these effects using a simulated sample of DESI-like luminous red galaxies within the IllustrisTNG hydrodynamical simulation and the Abacus N-body simulation. We show that analyzing projected 2D profiles can lead to biases when computing quantities like the gas fraction. We also find that in the absence of spatial filtering, the 2-halo term is non-negligible for kSZ even at the smaller radii where the 1-halo term dominates. We show that a 1% uncertainty in the satellite fraction of galaxies can propagate into uncertainties of $\pm$1%, $\pm$3% and $\pm$5% in the 1-halo terms of the kSZ, tSZ, and rSZ signals, respectively. We show that masking the 2% most massive objects in the sample reduces the profile amplitudes by up to 10%, 40%, and 75% for the kSZ, tSZ, and rSZ signals, respectively. Finally, we show that naive simulations of the kSZ effect can be biased by an artificial Doppler term, which is automatically removed when high-pass or compensated aperture filtering is applied.

items.title: Inflationary magnetogenesis from nonminimal coupling in large- and small-field potentials
items.abstract: We investigate inflationary magnetogenesis in a scenario where conformal invariance of electromagnetism is broken through a \emph{non-minimal Yukawa-like coupling between the inflaton and the Ricci scalar}. We account for electromagnetic backreaction and the Schwinger effect, analyzing both standard single-field inflation and a generalized K-essence framework, \emph{dubbed quasi-quintessence}. We consider inflationary potentials compatible with Planck satellite constraints, including Starobinsky and $α$-attractor models for large fields, as well as hilltop scenarios for small fields. Moreover, we explore very different functional electromagnetic couplings, introducing a novel ansatz modeled for small-fields. We show that the non-minimal coupling plays a central role in controlling the dynamics, \emph{acting as a timing parameter that regulates the onset of electric backreaction and the Schwinger regime}. This leads to a deep modification of the magnetogenesis process. Indeed, the amplitude of the generated magnetic fields can be enhanced by several orders of magnitude with respect to the minimally coupled case, reaching present-day values up to $B_0 \sim 10^{-13}\,\mathrm{G}$ in large-field scenarios, \emph{which appear as the only ones compatible with observational bounds}. Conversely, small-field models yield negligible magnetic amplitudes and appear non-predictive within our non-minimal framework.

items.title: A 4200-hour HyperFlash and ÉCLAT campaign on the hyperactive FRB 20240114A: constraining energetics with the most brilliant bursts
items.abstract: Abstract Hyperactive repeaters provide a unique window into the evolving environments and energy budgets of fast radio burst (FRB) sources, though they may not be representative of the FRB population in general. High-cadence observations are key to capturing the rarest and most energetic bursts, which occur only once per hundreds to thousands of hours. Here we present an unprecedented 4, 200-hour observing campaign targeting FRB 20240114A as part of the HyperFlash and ÉCLAT FRB monitoring programs. Over 806 days, we detected 178 high-energy (∼1040 − 42 erg) bursts with HyperFlash, which together amount to 4.4 × 1042 erg of released radio energy (assuming isotropic emission and 1-GHz emission bandwidth). The cumulative energy of the HyperFlash bursts is about twice that of ∼11, 000 lower-energy bursts detected with FAST, emphasising the significant role that the highest-energy bursts play in depleting the central engine’s stored energy. In fact, the single most brilliant burst from our sample, which we term the STROOP, contributes roughly 1/3 of all the energy we measure, and is at the maximum energy seen in studies of both repeating and apparently one-off FRBs alike. We also find a break in the burst energy distribution at ∼2 × 1040 erg and a linear dispersion measure (DM) increase of +0.96 ± 0.06 pc cm−3 over a period of 318 days. We discuss these findings in the context of a magnetar source model and highlight comparisons with the energetics of intermediate and giant X-ray/γ-ray flares from Galactic sources.

items.title: Black hole photon rings saturate the quantum chaos bound
items.abstract: A bstract We study the quantum chaos bound in the photon ring region surrounding black holes. By evaluating the Lyapunov exponent associated with unstable null geodesics in a broad class of generalized Kerr geometries, as well as the temperature induced by a string probe, we show that the quantum chaos bound is exactly saturated on equatorial circular orbits of the photon ring. We confirm our result by deriving the same exponent from out-of-time-order correlators in the near ring region. As a byproduct, we show that the photon ring saturation of the quantum chaos bound implies the saturation of the Bekenstein bound on the rate of information emission from the ringdown phase through the quasinormal modes in the eikonal limit. Our results extend the known correspondence between black hole thermodynamics and chaotic dynamics, highlighting the role of the photon ring as a probe of the fundamental limits on thermalization and information scrambling in black holes.

items.title: Gravitational-wave astronomy with a space-based optical clock network
items.abstract: Since the first detection of a merging binary black hole system a decade ago, gravitational-wave astronomy has emerged as a powerful tool for astrophysics. Future space-based observatories, such as the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA), will unlock the millihertz (mHz) band, which remains entirely inaccessible to ground-based detectors due to terrestrial noise. In parallel, proposed atom-based gravitational-wave detectors, specifically those based on space-based optical clocks and atom interferometers, offer capabilities that are unique and complementary to traditional optical interferometers. Their highly tunable character enables sensitive measurements across a broad frequency band extending from the mHz up to and possibly even above the Hz regime. In this work, we investigate the use of one-way Doppler tracking in space-based atomic clock networks operating in concert with detectors like LISA. We analyze the dominant noise sources and develop dedicated measurement protocols, which operate in a targeted mode, using an externally supplied signal model to track the response coherently as the source chirps. Performing preliminary parameter estimation on simulated signals, we demonstrate how these detectors could be used to extract critical astrophysical information about binary gravitational-wave sources. We further show that the same instrument retains sensitivity in a search mode, where no prior on the source is assumed.

items.title: Searching for extra dimensions with gravitational waves: Dark-siren constraints from GWTC-4
items.abstract: Higher-dimensional theories of gravity predict that gravitational waves (GWs) can propagate into extra spatial dimensions, leading to modified amplitude damping over cosmological distances. Measurements of GW luminosity distances therefore provide a unique probe of the dimensionality of spacetime. In this work, we constrain higher-dimensional GW propagation using the dark-siren method with the Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog 4.0 (GWTC-4). We adopt a phenomenological parameterization motivated by braneworld scenarios, in which deviations from General Relativity are characterized by the spacetime dimension number $D$ and a crossover scale $R_c$ governing the transition between four- and higher-dimensional gravity. We perform a hierarchical Bayesian analysis combining 141 compact binary coalescences from GWTC-4 with line-of-sight galaxy information from the GLADE+ catalog. For a prior $H_0 \in [65,77]\ {\rm km~s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$ and $\log(R_c/{\rm Mpc}) \in [2.7,4.0]$, we obtain $D = 4.38^{+1.91}_{-1.01}$ (68\% credible interval). We also find that the inferred posterior distribution of $R_c$ accumulates near the upper prior boundary, indicating that the crossover scale remains poorly constrained by current observations. We further show that the inferred constraint on $D$ depends sensitively on the assumed prior range of $R_c$, which determines the characteristic distance scale at which deviations from General Relativity become significant. Our results provide the first GWTC-4 dark-siren constraints on higher-dimensional GW propagation and demonstrate that current observations remain consistent with four-dimensional General Relativity.

items.title: Stellar wind driven Alfvén wing dynamics in planetary and exoplanetary magnetospheres
items.abstract: Magnetized obstacles embedded within a plasma flow generate magnetohydrodynamic structures known as Alfvén wings, which act as primary conduits for the transfer of momentum and energy between the body and the surrounding medium. This study employs three-dimensional resistive magnetohydrodynamic simulations to explore how these wings and the magnetosphere respond to diverse stellar wind conditions. Our results, gleaned from a large number of simulations spanning a wide range of stellar wind speed and magnetic field–and planetary dipole field–show that the global magnetospheric configuration is highly sensitive to the upstream Alfvén Mach number. We find that increasing stellar wind speed leads to a systematic closure and narrowing of Alfvén wing structures, while stronger stellar magnetic fields facilitate their opening. Analysis of the Alfvén wing morphology demonstrates a distinct dependence of wing opening angle on stellar wind speed, with internal wing analysis showing a reduction in plasma velocity and significant magnetic-flux accumulation. Our results exhibit a clear interdependence between the day-side magnetopause stand-off distance and the night-side magnetotail current sheet length. We find a linear scaling between the magnetotail dynamics and upstream forcing parameters. This study bridges the gap between solar system observations and (exo)planetary systems by demonstrating how Earth-like magnetospheres might transform into wing-dominated configurations during extreme stellar events or within the sub-Alfvénic regimes of close-in (exo)planets. Our findings can aid the interpretation of Alfvén wing signatures in observational data and enhance our understanding of how (exo)planetary magnetospheres respond to dynamic stellar wind forcing.

items.title: Dark matter energy exchange in stars orbiting supermassive black holes
items.abstract: Stars on tight orbits around the supermassive black hole at the Galactic Center pass through regions where the dark matter~(DM) density may be strongly enhanced. We compute the orbit-averaged DM-induced energy exchange for S4714 as an example. It is a star on an exceptionally close and relativistic orbit around Sagittarius~A*. For a spiked dark matter profile, the exchange reaches the stellar luminosity at $σ_{χp} \sim 10^{-36}~\mathrm{cm}^2$ for MeV-GeV masses and $σ_{χe} \sim 5\times10^{-38}~\mathrm{cm}^2$ for sub-MeV masses, opening a new annihilation-free route toward dark-star phases. These cross sections lie within the range predicted by freeze-in scenarios and are consistent with cosmic-ray--boosted and solar-reflection dark matter constraints.

items.title: Probing quadratically coupled ultralight dark matter with the laser interferometer space antenna
items.abstract: Ultralight dark matter can interact with Standard Model particles via gravitational and non-gravitational interactions. Through such interactions, it can leave distinctive signals in gravitational-wave experiments. In this work, we investigate signals induced by ultralight dark matter quadratically coupled to the Standard Model in the future space-borne gravitational-wave detector, the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). Due to the quadratic nature of the coupling, dark matter signals appear at two distinct frequencies: the frequency corresponding to twice the dark matter mass, and frequencies below the typical dark matter kinetic energy. We analyze both contributions and show that LISA can surpass current constraints from terrestrial and astrophysical probes in certain mass ranges. We also find that dark matter signals in LISA are free from screening effects which significantly limit the sensitivity of terrestrial experiments.

items.title: Weyl gauge symmetry at LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA
items.abstract: With current advances in gravitational wave (GW) detection made by the worldwide LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) network of detectors, ever-more sensitive tests of gravity in the strong-field regime are now possible. This enables one to test gauge theories beyond Einstein-Hilbert action, such as Weyl gauge theories of gravity. The only anomaly-free (quantum) gauge theory of a space-time symmetry beyond Poincaré is based on Weyl gauge group (of dilatations and Poincaré symmetry) with Weyl conformal geometry as its natural underlying geometry. This gauge theory has spontaneous breaking of Weyl gauge symmetry to Einstein-Hilbert and Proca actions, plus a positive cosmological constant. We investigate the GW polarisation modes of Weyl (quadratic) gauge theory of gravity in Weyl geometry and compare our findings to the most recent experimental data. We show how the geodesic deviation equation from Riemannian geometry translates to Weyl geometry, and explain why it is crucial to perform the analysis around de Sitter background, which is the correct low-energy limit of Weyl quadratic gravity, to not alter the GW content, and then compute the polarisation modes. In addition to the two transverse-traceless tensor modes predicted by Einstein-Hilbert action, we find two additional vector modes induced by the transverse fluctuations of the Weyl gauge field. If detected, these vectors modes would be important evidence for Weyl gauge symmetry.

items.title: Post-Newtonian Global Conservation Laws in the Presence of Sensitive Bodies
items.abstract: Abstract The parameterized post-Newtonian (PPN) approach is the state of the art formalism for performing theory independent tests of weak-field gravity, and for constraining possible deviations from Einstein's theory. Within this framework, global conservation laws are useful for the calculation of dynamics and for giving meaning to parameters. In this paper we extend the concept of semi-conservative and fullyconservative theories of gravity to include situations in which compact astrophysical bodies are modeled as masses that are sensitive to their local environment, as relevant for theories that violate the strong equivalence principle. We find that globally conserved quantities can still exist in the presence of such sensitivities, and find their explicit forms when they do. We identify new ways of writing the coefficients that enter into the PPN metric when a theory of gravity admits conserved quantities in the presence of a sensitive body, and demonstrate the applicability of our approach by comparing it to known results in scalar-tensor theories of gravity.

items.title: Growth–recovery decoupling in the timing of geomagnetic disturbances across five solar cycles
items.abstract: The timing of geomagnetic disturbances depends on energy accumulation and releases within the 8 magnetosphere, and shows how that balance is organized by solar cycle. We decompose every 9 negative excursion of the 1-min SYM-H index over 1981–2026 (78,096 events at the median 10 threshold, spanning solar cycles 21 through 25) into a growth lifetime τg, from downward threshold 11 crossing to the first attainment of its minimum, and a recovery lifetime τr, from minimum to recovery 12 crossing. Both durations follow finite-range power laws with distinct exponents, μg = 1.079 ± 0.005 13 and μr = 1.305 ± 0.004. The recovery exponent is larger at every threshold and in every yearly 14 window. Under the standard first-attainment convention the exponents respond oppositely to solar 15 activity: μg rises with sunspot number (r = +0.59, p = 7 × 10-5 in independent windows) but μr is 16 statistically flat. The solar cycle influences the temporal width over which the scaling law extends. 17 The solar cycle is therefore imprinted on low-latitude disturbance timing selectively: through the 18 growth exponent and through the temporal cutoff scales of both channels, but not through the 19 recovery exponent. The exponent ordering survives alternative estimators, independence treatments, 20 and an agnostic treatment of tied minima, and the undivided excursion recovers the single threshold-21 robust burst-lifetime law reported previously (Wanliss and Weygand, 2007). The apparent invariance 22 of bursts arises because the recovery channel controls the tail. Growth and recovery timing are 23 therefore decoupled. 24

items.title: Prospects for direct detection of ultralight dark matter candidates in deci-Hz band with IndIGO-D
items.abstract: We investigate the sensitivity of IndIGO-D, a proposed space-based decihertz gravitational-wave interferometer, to different classes of ultralight dark matter. IndIGO-D will probe the $\sim0.01$--$10~\mathrm{Hz}$ frequency band between those accessible to current ground- and future space-based gravitational-wave interferometers, providing access to ultralight dark-matter masses beyond the reach of existing instruments. We consider two complementary signatures: interferometric displacements induced by coherently oscillating scalar (dilaton), vector (dark-photon, $U(1)_B$ and $U(1)_{B-L}$ gauge groups), and tensor fields with masses $m_{\rm DM}\sim10^{-17}$--$10^{-14}~\mathrm{eV}$; and changes in laser polarization induced by pseudoscalar axion dark matter at higher masses, around $m_a\sim10^{-12}~\mathrm{eV}$. For the dilatons, dark photons and tensors, we compute the expected sensitivities using two pipelines -- cross-correlation and BSD excess-power -- assuming L-shaped and triangular interferometer layouts and three representative noise power spectral densities (S1, S2, S3), each for two years of continuous observation. We find that the projected sensitivities agree to within a factor of order unity across the search pipelines and interferometer geometries. In particular, we show that IndIGO-D could open previously unconstrained coupling parameter space for vector and tensor dark matter across $m_{\rm DM}\sim10^{-16}$--$10^{-14}~\mathrm{eV}$, bridging the sensitivity of space- and ground-based experiments. For axion dark matter, we demonstrate that a complementary detection for laser light polarization shifts, limited primarily by photon shot noise, could probe the axion-photon coupling $g_{aγ}$ at masses around $m_a\sim10^{-12}~\mathrm{eV}$ at a level potentially better than that of other future experiments without degrading sensitivity to gravitational waves.

items.title: Studying the Intermittency of the Magnetized Interstellar Medium by Synchrotron Polarization Intensity and Its Gradient
items.abstract: Abstract Based on synthetic polarization observations, we qualitatively investigate the intermittency of the magnetized interstellar medium (ISM) through synchrotron polarization intensity (SPI) and synchrotron polarization gradient (SPG). Three principal findings emerge from our analysis: (1) The intermittency of the magnetized ISM is strongly modulated by magnetization and compressibility, with pronounced modulation effects predominantly observed in regimes characterized by strong magnetization and high compressibility. (2) The characterized intermittency of the magnetized ISM demonstrates a dependence on the electron spectral index under conditions where the random magnetic field dominates. (3) SPG enables the identification of finer three-dimensional fractal structures in the case of strong Faraday depolarization. The synergistic application of SPI and SPG substantially enhances the reliability of probing magnetized ISM intermittency from real observations.

items.title: Disk winds from T Tauri stars - physics and observables
items.abstract: Magnetically driven disk winds are fundamental to protoplanetary disk evolution, regulating angular momentum transport, stellar accretion, disk dispersal, and the environment in which planets form. Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) models provide the theoretical framework for understanding how large-scale magnetic fields launch, accelerate, and collimate these outflows, while establishing direct links between the underlying physics and observable diagnostics. This review presents an overview of analytical magnetized disk-wind models developed primarily for T Tauri stars. We summarize the physical foundations of magnetized outflows, from early magnetized wind theories to self-consistent accretion–ejection solutions, emphasizing the roles of magnetic geometry, angular momentum extraction, magnetic lever arms, mass loading, and non-ideal MHD effects in determining wind structure and efficiency. We review the observational diagnostics predicted by analytical models, including spectroscopic, kinematic, thermo-chemical, and molecular signatures that constrain the wind-launching region, acceleration, collimation, and angular momentum transport. We also briefly discuss how modern numerical simulations extend analytical theory by incorporating non-ideal MHD, realistic thermodynamics, radiative transfer, chemistry, dust evolution, and time-dependent processes that cannot be treated self-consistently within the assumptions of analytical models. By linking MHD theory, analytical solutions, observations, and numerical simulations, this review emphasizes the enduring importance of analytical disk-wind models as the conceptual framework for interpreting magnetized outflows from protoplanetary disks and their role in the evolution of young planetary systems.

items.title: Regimes of truth in postmodern novels: the atlas of misty continents in the context of modernity and Ottoman epistemology
items.abstract: This study aims to analyze the epistemological transformation concerning the nature and legitimacy of knowledge in the context of modernity and postmodernity through İhsan Oktay Anar’s The Atlas of Misty Continents. While modernity conceptualizes knowledge as a universal structure grounded in reason and empirical verification, postmodern thought challenges these assumptions by arguing that knowledge is produced within historical, cultural, and discursive processes. Accordingly, truth is not treated as a fixed entity but rather as a contextual and pluralized construction. The study examines the core concepts of postmodern epistemology through Jean-François Lyotard’s critique of “grand narratives” and his notion of “language games,” as well as Michel Foucault’s framework of the knowledge–power relationship. Although these perspectives do not entirely deny the possibility of objective reality, they emphasize that knowledge gains legitimacy through specific discursive and institutional formations. By extending this theoretical framework into the field of literature, the article discusses how the postmodern novel represents regimes of knowledge. In this respect, it argues that in The Atlas of Misty Continents, knowledge is constructed in multiple forms, drawing not only on scientific rationality but also on sources such as rumor, intuition, tradition, and dreams. The novel is analyzed through categories including narrative reliability, the representation of knowledge sources, the pluralization of truth claims, and the distribution of epistemic authority. The study contends that Anar does not merely juxtapose modern and postmodern epistemologies but instead incorporates them simultaneously and equivalently within fiction. Consequently, this article argues that The Atlas of Misty Continents is not merely an aesthetic work of fiction; rather, it constructs a mode of thinking that simultaneously draws on postmodern epistemology and the Ottoman epistemic framework.

items.title: WALLABY pilot survey: accurate and automated linewidth measurements from global H i profiles
items.abstract: Abstract Current-generation 21-cm surveys of extragalactic neutral hydrogen (H i) with instruments such as FAST and ASKAP are providing detailed spectral and spatial information for over 105 galaxies. Future H i surveys with next-generation radio telescopes could provide sample sizes larger by orders of magnitude. There is therefore a need for accurate, automated, and reliable parameterisation of the H i emission from galaxies. We have developed an automated estimator for H i global profile widths to better enable studies of, for example, dynamical masses and Tully-Fisher distances. Our estimator is based on an implementation of the BusyFit profile-fitting algorithm, and converges for 95 % of global profiles in the WALLABY pilot survey. Probability density functions are calculated for all profile parameters using Monte Carlo techniques, and example error parameterisations are given. We confirm that linewidth uncertainties depend primarily on the integrated signal-to-noise ratio, profile steepness, and the linewidth, consistent with previous studies. We compare several common linewidth definitions, and the width at 50 % of the mean flux density (Wm50) is found to be the most robust measure of linewidth. We provide examples of the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation drawn from the WALLABY pilot survey.

items.title: Classification of chiral domain-wall dynamics through symmetry analysis
items.abstract: We report the discovery of a previously unreported type of chiral domain-wall (DW) dynamics and establish a symmetry-based framework for classifying the observed types of chiral DW dynamics. In this newly identified type, the symmetric component of the DW speed exhibits a concave-down curvature, in sharp contrast to the conventional concave-up response associated with the equilibrium DW-energy contribution. Sample-specific micromagnetic calculations reproduce only the conventional response and fail to account for this reversed curvature, indicating an additional even contribution beyond the conventional equilibrium DW-energy picture. By incorporating this new response, we show that the chiral DW dynamics observed to date can be classified into three distinct types, all of which are quantitatively described by symmetric and antisymmetric components having the same respective functional forms. This classification provides a systematic framework for investigating diverse chiral DW dynamics and their underlying physics.

items.title: A 13CO Detection in a Massive Molecular Gas Flow in Abell 1795’s Central Galaxy
items.abstract: Abstract We present new ALMA 13CO(2-1) observations of the central galaxy in the cool-core cluster Abell 1795, targeting the origin of extended molecular filaments. The filaments extend for 5–7 kpc and are closely drawn up around large radio bubbles inflated by jets from the central active galactic nucleus (AGN). Smooth velocity gradients along their lengths are consistent with entrained flows lifted by the expanding bubbles. Here we detect the northern molecular filament in the low-opacity molecular tracer 13CO(2-1) , which can provide a more reliable measure of the molecular gas mass and conditions than 12CO . The velocity structure in 13CO(2-1) is consistent with that of the 12CO (2-1) emission. Using a range of plausible excitation temperatures and covering fractions, we thereby determine a filament molecular gas mass of (0.1–2) × 109 M⊙, or down to an order of magnitude below previous estimates. This implies a CO-to-H2 conversion factor of αCO = 0.4–5 M⊙ (K km s−1 pc2)−1 in the filament, or ∼ 0.1–1 times the standard assumption of the Milky Way value. Direct entrainment by the N radio bubble is now plausible, as it can provide sufficient mechanical energy and buoyant support for the molecular gas flow. Similarly, measured X-ray cooling rates are also now consistent with in-situ condensation of uplifted, low-entropy hot gas. Both formation mechanisms require multiple generations of bubbles at higher filament masses.

items.title: Conditional Derivative GANs for Parameter-Conditioned Synthesis of Gravitational Waves from Core-Collapse Supernovae
items.abstract: Abstract Gravitational wave signals from core-collapse supernovae encode critical astrophysical information, including key astrophysical parameters such as the ratio of rotational kinetic to gravitational potential energy at bounce, pre-collapse differential rotation, and the nuclear equation of state. However, the limited number of observed core-collapse supernovae events makes it challenging to build robust data-driven models. The generation of synthetic gravitational wave signals from core-collapse supernovae can therefore provide a valuable tool for data augmentation in machine learning pipelines, particularly for the training and testing of detection and parameter estimation algorithms. Although recent efforts have explored the use of generative models to synthesize waveform-like data, existing approaches lack the ability to condition outputs on specific astrophysical parameters. To address this, we propose a model capable of generating gravitational wave signals conditioned on astrophysical parameters of core-collapse supernovae rotation. The proposed conditional derivative generative adversarial network is trained on the Richers et al. catalog, which contains 1,824 simulated time-series gravitational wave waveforms and their corresponding physical parameters. Quantitative evaluation using time-domain similarity and distributional metrics shows that the generated signals reproduce the key statistical and morphological features of the original dataset. This work introduces a conditional generative framework for rotating core-collapse supernovae gravitational wave signals, that enables fast, low-cost data augmentation and parameterized modeling, improving ML-based detection and parameter estimation.

items.title: DIGITAL ELECTORAL RECAPITULATION SYSTEMS AND GOVERNANCE MODELS: COMPARATIVE INTERNATIONAL EVIDENCE
items.abstract: This study compares the management of election recapitulation information systems in Indonesia with those implemented in the Philippines, Brazil, Estonia, and Kyrgyzstan to examine differences in governance, system design, security mechanisms, digital infrastructure, transparency, and public trust. Although these countries have adopted various election technologies, ranging from optical scanning and Electronic Voting Machines (EVM) to Internet voting (i-voting) and optical tabulation, comprehensive comparative studies that position Indonesia within this international context remain limited. This study employed a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Data were collected from the Scopus database and supported by credible reports, while CiteSpace was used to map research trends and identify knowledge gaps. The findings reveal significant differences in the maturity of election recapitulation systems. Estonia and Brazil have achieved advanced digital election management through integrated digital governance, secure verification mechanisms, and high public trust. The Philippines applies a hybrid model combining paper ballots with automated vote counting, whereas Kyrgyzstan continues to rely largely on manual procedures. Indonesia's Sirekap represents an intermediate stage of digital transformation but continues to face challenges related to security, OCR accuracy, infrastructure readiness, and public trust. The theoretical contribution of this study is the development of a Comparative Governance Framework for Election Recapitulation Information Systems, demonstrating that system maturity is determined not only by technological adoption but also by the interaction among governance, security, digital infrastructure, transparency, and public trust. This framework provides a foundation for evaluating and improving election recapitulation systems in emerging digital democracies.
